cards.title: Defects found proving #3271: Close the CBOR semantic profile against selected breadth
cards.body:
Defects found while proving #3271 (Close the CBOR semantic profile against selected breadth) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3271.

1. Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer02/cbor_err_min.jet: `a :: cbor.parse([U8]{247}) ?? { print("rejected: {err.reason}"); return }`
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: prints `rejected: unsupported CBOR simple value 23` then `internal compiler error: JIT drop `CBORErrorKind` enum discriminant is invalid`, exit 101 (interpreter exit 0)
   Expected: clean exit after printing the rejection

2. Repro: cbor_probe.jet (any cbor.parse error path) with safe-jet.sh build
   Tiers: AOT
   Observed: generated Rust fails: `error[E0425]: cannot find type `CBORError` in module `jet_std`` / `CBORErrorKind` not in jet_std
   Expected: builds and runs

3. Repro: cbor.parse error typing: checker types `err` as CBORError/CBORErrorKind(Syntax|Truncated|Unsupported) (Core.jet:86) while host returns jet_std::EncodingError (EncodingCodecs.rs:478-505); spec :918-921 says CBORErrorKind has 7 variants
   Tiers: checker (all)
   Observed: matching err.kind against EncodingErrorKind is E0112; matching CBORErrorKind -> interp `E0956 MIR reached an unreachable terminator`
   Expected: one error type per spec: CBORError{kind: 7-variant CBORErrorKind, byte_offset, path, reason}

4. Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer02/cbor_nan.jet: cbor.parse([U8]{251,127,248,0,0,0,0,0,0}) then print
   Tiers: JIT, interpreter
   Observed: internal compiler error: JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float (crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/JSONInterp.rs:365)
   Expected: accepted NaN Float (or a typed rejection)

5. Repro: cbor_typed.jet: `back :: cbor.decode<Blob>(wire) ?? panic("decode")`
   Tiers: JIT, interpreter, AOT
   Observed: ICE: checked Core call `core.encoding.cbor.decode` has no canonical TIR record (Unknown)
   Expected: typed decode per spec :860-862
cards.plan: Fix each listed defect at its root on every tier (Jet compiler first where it is language policy; host runtime otherwise). Add or complete the golden or UI proof per defect. Then re-prove the source card.

cards.title: Defects found proving #3272: Close TOML version and typed round-trip coverage
cards.body:
Defects found while proving #3272 (Close TOML version and typed round-trip coverage) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3272.

1. Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer02/toml_min.jet: `toml.parse("a = 1\n")`
   Tiers: JIT, interpreter, AOT
   Observed: internal compiler error: checked TIR cannot lower to MIR at 1458..1459: __jet_parse_toml: missing checked function target `...toml.jet::TomlParser::fail`
   Expected: Ok(DataTree {a: 1})

2. Repro: toml_typed.jet: toml.decode<One>("n = 1\nn = 2\n"), ("n = 012"), ("n = 1__0"), ("n = 10_"), ("[t]\nn = 1\n[s]\n[t]\nm = 2\n"), ("n = \"7\"")
   Tiers: JIT, AOT
   Observed: duplicate key accepted; 012->12, 1__0->10, 10_->10 accepted; table redefinition not detected (reports missing field); string "7" coerced to Int 7
   Expected: TOML 1.0: reject duplicate key, leading zero, bad underscores, table redefinition (with line/column); typed Int rejects a string

3. Repro: toml_typed.jet case "[t]\nn = 1\n[s]\n[t]\nm = 2\n"
   Tiers: JIT vs AOT
   Observed: JIT: `[at `n`: missing field `n`]`; AOT: `[at `n`: expected Int, found null]`
   Expected: identical error on all tiers (I9)

4. Repro: any toml.decode<T> under run --interpret
   Tiers: interpreter
   Observed: E0956 core.encoding.toml.decode() isn't supported by the current evaluator yet
   Expected: same output as JIT

5. Repro: `struct TypedDate { ld: Date }` (core.time) then toml.decode<TypedDate>("ld = 1979-05-27\n")
   Tiers: checker
   Observed: E2411 `TypedDate` can't be decoded
   Expected: typed TOML dates/times decode into core.time types (card plan change 2)

cards.title: Defects found proving #3273: Close YAML version, trailing input and resource behavior
cards.body:
Defects found while proving #3273 (Close YAML version, trailing input and resource behavior) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3273.

1. Repro: yaml.parse("hello\nworld: 1\n"), ("a:\n  b: 1\n c: 2\n"), ("---\na: 1\n"), ("%YAML 1.2\n---\na: 1\n")
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: "hello"; {"a":{"b":1}}; "---"; "%YAML 1.2" (rest of input silently dropped)
   Expected: reject trailing/misindented content with its line; accept leading --- as document start

2. Repro: yaml.parse("a: &x 1\nb: *x\n"), ("a: !!int 3\n"), ("a: {{b: 1}}\n")
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: accepted as Text "&x 1", "*x", "!!int 3", "{b: 1}"
   Expected: EncodingError Unsupported naming the feature with true line/column (yaml.jet:20-21 claims fail-closed)

3. Repro: yaml.parse("a: 1\nb: 2\na: 3\n")
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: rejected line 1 col 1 @0: duplicate YAML map key
   Expected: line 3 col 1

4. Repro: yaml.parse of 257-deep block map (yaml_probe.jet nested_map(257))
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: internal compiler error: typed drop value recursion limit exceeded
   Expected: Limit error at max_depth

5. Repro: any program calling yaml.parse
   Tiers: interpreter, AOT
   Observed: interp: E0956 core.collections.slice_list_range() unsupported; AOT: rustc E0308 jet_std::DataEvent::Int(..) expected i64, found JetInt
   Expected: runs on all tiers

6. Repro: perf/yaml_parse_{125,250,500}.jet and yaml_parse.jet (flat n-entry map)
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: 0.089s/0.337s/2.148s/12.08s for 3/6/12/25 KB (superlinear); program then ICEs `typed drop `Int` field 0 is unavailable`
   Expected: linear parse; no ICE

Defects found while proving #3113 (Close dev reload state and side-effect semantics) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3113.

1. Repro: python3 ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer07/devreload/drive3.py; inspect /__jet_dev_status while the invalid edit is pending
   Tiers: jet dev --target=web (snapshot14)
   Observed: {"version":2,"state":"error","code":"E0003","diagnostic":"..."}: no candidate/diagnostic_revision/last_good_revision/accepted_revision
   Expected: diagnostic_revision = rejected candidate; last_good_revision = accepted_revision = /__jet_dev_version (2)

2. Repro: safe-jet.sh dev --watch=on --json --target=web --port=P run.jet, then save an invalid edit
   Tiers: jet dev
   Observed: stdout holds only 'App preview: http://...'; no jet.status/v1 or jet.report/v3 record for watch-cycle builds; E0003 goes to stderr as human text
   Expected: --json emits machine diagnostics for watch-cycle builds (as it does for the startup failure)

3. Repro: python3 ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer07/devreload/drive2.py (in-place truncate+write saves)
   Tiers: jet dev --target=web
   Observed: 2/2 runs: the first good in-place save after ready never triggered a rebuild (version stayed 1, status ready, 180s). Run 1 also compiled a truncated empty file (E0003 at run.jet:1:1). With atomic os.replace saves (drive3.py) the good edit rebuilt in 12.4s.
   Expected: an in-place save is rebuilt once its content is complete; no lost edit

4. Repro: Tools/gauntlet/axes/live-reload/jet/run.jet under safe-jet.sh dev --target=web
   Tiers: snapshot14 embedded Core
   Observed: E0769 `viewport` is a label-only parameter of `preview`/`playground` at <corelib>/Core/ui/ui.jet:104,109
   Expected: Core compiles (tree Core/ui/ui.jet:104,109 now pass viewport: viewport; needs a new snapshot)
cards.plan: Fix each listed defect at its root on every tier (Jet compiler first where it is language policy; host runtime otherwise). Add or complete the golden or UI proof per defect. Then re-prove the source card.

cards.title: Defects found proving #3158: Prove enum rename, navigation and case completion
cards.body:
Defects found while proving #3158 (Prove enum rename, navigation and case completion) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3158.

1. Repro: dir with modes.jet `pub enum Mode { Fast Slow }` + `pub fn fast() -> Mode { Mode.Fast }`; run.jet `use "modes"` fn run() { m :: modes.fast(); if m == .Fast -> print("x") }
   Tiers: check (run)
   Observed: E0305 Pattern `Fast` doesn't match this value's type. Why: `.::modes.jet::Mode` is a struct, not an enum
   Expected: the leading-dot pattern resolves against the sibling module's enum

2. Repro: same fixture; `modes.Mode.Fast` in expression or pattern position
   Tiers: check
   Observed: E0107 Nothing named `modes` exists here
   Expected: a qualified variant through the file-module alias resolves (or a documented import form exists)

3. Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer07/lsp/probe2: speeds.jet `pub enum Speed { Fast Slow }` + fast() + speed_label(); run.jet `use "speeds"`, print(speeds.speed_label(speeds.fast()))
   Tiers: run and run --interpret
   Observed: ICE: checked TIR cannot lower to MIR at 13196..14575: duplicate checked type definition `.::speeds.jet::Speed`. Renaming Speed->Velocity compiles and prints Fast
   Expected: compiles; the type name Speed is not special

4. Repro: drive.py rename response
   Tiers: self lsp
   Observed: semantic_ops [{kind:rename, from:Fast, to:Quick, targets:[], files:[]}] while documentChanges edits modes.jet
   Expected: semantic_ops targets/files reflect the edited file (minor)

   Tiers: LSP
   Observed: only the declaration model.jet 8:7; prepareCallHierarchy -> []; prepareTypeHierarchy(struct Item) -> null
   Expected: includes the service.jet:4 call (as `jet inspect impact` reports); a hierarchy or an explicit unsupported status

cards.title: Defects found proving #3095: Prove local timer and cron scheduling without durable-job claims
cards.body:
Defects found while proving #3095 (Prove local timer and cron scheduling without durable-job claims) on 2026-09-29 (evidence-closer, snapshots 14-17). Each needs a root-cause fix and a golden/UI proof; then re-prove #3095.

1. Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/Closer07/sched/cancel_after.jet: c :: tasks.after(60000ms, 9); c2 :: tasks.cancel(c); print(c2.receive() ?? -1)
   Tiers: jet run (JIT)
   Observed: prints -1, done, then Stop [E3013] parked task 'time sleep', exit 70
   Expected: cancel stops the producer; clean exit 0

2. Repro: sched/cancel_interval.jet: a :: tasks.interval(1ms); a.receive(); a2 :: tasks.cancel(a); a2.receive()
   Tiers: JIT
   Observed: post-cancel receive returns 2
   Expected: None after cancel (or a documented buffered drain)

3. Repro: sched/cancel_after.jet and cancel_interval.jet
   Tiers: --interpret
   Observed: E0956 `core.tasks.after()`/`core.tasks.interval()` isn't supported by the current evaluator
   Expected: same behaviour as JIT (I9)

4. Repro: safe-jet.sh build sched/cancel_after.jet
   Tiers: AOT
   Observed: ICE: MIR nominal type "time.Duration" has no declaration row
   Expected: builds

5. Repro: sched/sleep_ice.jet: use core.tasks as tasks; fn run() { tasks.sleep(1); print("slept") }
   Tiers: JIT and --interpret
   Observed: ICE: __jet_core_core_tasks::__jet_host_sleep_ms: missing checked MIR owner type
   Expected: sleeps and prints

cards.title: Shared storage with copy on first write, and shared sliceable text
cards.body: D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A. Parent #3741. When two owners need the same heap value, share it; copy only on first write. Text is shared and sliceable so `.trim()` stored into a field never copies.
cards.plan:
1. Counted buffers for heap values not proven unique; statically unique values carry no counter/check.
2. Counter becomes thread-safe only when crossing tasks (D-MEMREF-TASK1).
3. Text slices share buffer; compact small slices of large buffers on long-lived store.
4. `jet audit copies` + hover report possible first-write copies; lint for first-write copies inside loops.
5. Paired perf cells vs eager copy and vs Rust/Swift.

cards.title: core.time dual types: source structs and host handles disagree; Instant.unix_ns silently reads 0
cards.body:
Found by WaveSemaHoles3840 on snapshot20. core.time types exist twice: host dispatcher rows (Core.jet: core.time instant -> jet_time_instant_now, start -> jet_std_time_start; JetInstant{start_ns private}, Stopwatch{start: std::time::Instant}) and source structs in Core/time/time.jet (pub struct Instant{unix_ns}, Stopwatch{start_ns}) plus sema core_constructable_fields rows that claim those fields. Period, Zone, DateTime, LocalDate and LocalTime have the same dual ownership.
Observed: `time.instant().unix_ns` prints 0, `time.start().start_ns` prints 0 (silently wrong); `i :: time.instant(); i.unix_ns` ICEs 'typed drop Int field 0 is unavailable'. Core/time/time.jet itself reads the fake field (host_unix_ns feeds sleep_until/elapsed).
Separate: `time.duration_ms(3).ns` ICEs 'missing checked MIR owner type' in TIR/mir.rs field_id_for (no type_defs row for the constructable core Duration).
cards.plan: I8: one owner per type. Jet source is canonical: make each core.time type a Core/time source struct whose fields are real, with the host providing only primitive kernels (e.g. a host monotonic/unix ns read returning Int). Delete the host handle carriers and stale sema core_constructable_fields rows; route jet_time_* rows to construct the source structs on every tier. Register constructable core types in MIR type_defs (Duration). Goldens: time.instant().unix_ns > 0 and monotonic; Stopwatch elapsed; Duration .ns; on run, --interpret, AOT. Mirror in Compiler/ where the Jet compiler has core-type rows.

cards.title: SECURITY: compile-time fold baked random draws into programs
cards.body: Found by WaveRV20bBugs on snapshot21 (#3748 d3). Sema's implicit immutable-binding fold evaluated `draw :: next_bits63()` inside Core/math/random bounded() at compile time, because core.math.random.getrandbits (the only host draw) was missing from is_nondeterministic_core and had no Rand effect row. `jet emit --rust` shows the draw as a literal (JetInt::from_i64(6825273360077706433)): random.int returns 211148 on run/--interpret for every seed and 171622 on AOT. Any Core helper built on that draw (tokens, ids, keys) may have produced constants.
cards.plan: 1) Fixed in source: getrandbits gets the Rand effect row and is non-foldable (Effects.rs, core_calls.rs, Compiler/JetFoundation CoreCalls.jet). 2) Root: the fold must derive foldability from effect rows (a Core call with a non-empty or missing effect row is never folded), not from an allowlist. 3) Audit every Core host row for missing Rand/Time/IO rows. 4) Proof: math/random_seeded_sequence golden on 3 tiers; a test that two jet runs of random_bytes/uuid.v4 differ and that emit --rust contains no folded draw. 5) Assess the exposure window (which commits shipped it) for the security record per Docs/spec/contributing/security-closure.md.

log.text: 2026-10-23 Main: Main rerun at fc382a23cd (discovery jet), $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/cv/r42.jet: seed(1); a :: int(0,1000000); seed(2); b, c :: draws -> '778340 594364 282315 same? false' on jet run and on the jet build binary, so the draws follow the runtime seed and successive draws differ (a folded literal would ignore the seed). Unseeded r0.jet gives 171622 211148 624618 on both tiers and on every run, which is the documented ambient deterministic stream (core-library.md: random.seed seeds the ambient deterministic stream), now identical across tiers (the defect gave different constants per tier). Found closable by CardVerify.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: re-phased (no building work logged since before 2026-10-20).
Board prep 2026-10-01 (D-EXEC1, #4013): SECURITY root fix and test landed; add the positive purity list for rows with no effect entry, add criteria, then close.

WaveRV20bBugs (source; cargo check clean): root fixed. is_nondeterministic_core now derives from the effect row (Time|Rand), no allowlist; comptime eval refuses any Core call with a non-empty effect row other than Mem/Panic (E3410). Audit found two more rows with no effect: core.crypto.__x25519_generate and core.crypto.__signing_generate (OS key generation) now carry Rand. Before this, key generation could be folded into the binary as constants. Test tests/determinism.rs ambient_draws_are_never_folded_into_the_build (two runs of uuid.v4 differ; emit --rust contains no drawn value; seeded draws differ). Remaining: rows with no effect entry are still treated as pure by the fold (needs a positive purity bit per row); exposure-window assessment.

cards.title: Interpreter read_place clones the whole base value before projecting
cards.body: Found by WaveRV20dBugs: the MIR interpreter's read_place clones the entire base value before applying the projection, so `out.len()` or `s.field` on a growing list/struct costs O(size). A nested-loop data join became quadratic: 10x10 took 19.3 s, 100x100 hit the 300 s timeout under --interpret (Core/data join was rewritten to avoid it, but every other loop that reads a projection of a large local pays the same cost).
cards.plan: Make read_place project through a borrowed reference to the base (clone only the projected leaf) in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs; keep copy semantics (D-COPY-DEFAULT1) by cloning at the use site only when the value escapes. Perf proof: a paired cell (list.len() inside a 1e5 loop on a 1e5-element list) under --interpret before/after; goldens unchanged. Check other interpreter hot paths (field writes, index reads) for the same whole-value clone.

cards.title: #Memo memoization is not implemented on any tier
cards.body: Found by RocDefects (roc-skip research D4): MirFunction.memo_bound is set during lowering, but no backend reads it; MIRRust, the JIT and MIREval have no memo call-site code. cards.title: Concurrent query engine: declaration-granular reverse dependencies, signature diff, immutable published facts
cards.body: Hack's typechecker scaled to tens of millions of lines by recording reads at declaration/function granularity, diffing old/new declarations, and sharing immutable facts across parallel workers (talk J31LlAUtoos 12:57-26:08; hphp/hack/src/server/server_type_check.ml). Jet today: `jet_queries::QueryEngine` is an in-memory, single-threaded (`&mut self`) memo with recorded deps and item-level re-verdicts (crates/jet-queries/src/lib.rs:94-208; crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs:33-61). Compiler-speed law requires query incrementality and parallel-by-construction (Docs/spec/reference/compiler-speed.md:79-83).
cards.plan:
1. Key queries by declaration/function identity; record reads as reverse edges (dependency -> consumers) in a compact, lock-free table.
2. On edit: re-parse dirty files, diff old/new declaration signatures; invalidate only consumers of changed signatures; body-only edits recheck that body.
3. Publish facts as immutable, interned values shared by parallel workers; bucket work per phase (parse/file, declare/symbol, check/function).
4. Eager name/declaration index; lazy bodies checked on demand, open files first.
5. Measure with #666 corpus: time-to-first-diagnostic, total fanout time, heap bytes.

cards.title: Saved compiler state: persist name, dependency, and declaration tables across runs and from CI
cards.body: Hack loads a saved state (naming table, dependency table, declarations) and rechecks only dirty files plus fanout (talk J31LlAUtoos 74:35-78:17, 90:42; hphp/hack/src/server/server_lazy_init.ml). Jet persists run/build artifacts (Source/RunCache.rs, Source/BuildCache.rs, Source/ReceiptStore.rs) but not front-end query state; D-JPK-NODAEMON1 forbids a background daemon, so cold starts must be fast without one.
cards.plan:
1. Serialize the query engine's published facts and reverse edges, keyed by compiler, profile, target, and source hashes (compiler-speed invariant 5).
2. `jet check`/`jet run` load the newest matching state, re-parse dirty files, recompute fanout.
3. CI can publish a state for a commit; local runs reuse it.
4. Verifier: loaded-state result equals clean result (hh_saved_state_verifier style).

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #3852; criteria carried there as [#3853]. Saved compiler state persists the same query tables.

Opus 5.5 adversarial pass (2026-09-30, AdvCompileSpeed) found: CI-published state as written is a safety bypass: verdicts/TIR/diagnostics from a remote state skip sema, the only gatekeeper (cache-poisoning class). Rescope: remote state carries only naming table, declaration signatures and edges, each tied to a source hash; verdicts/TIR/diagnostics only from the local store; signed provenance from trusted branches (key pinned in lock); local sampling re-verify. Key = engine-recorded manifest of every input read; BLAKE3 >=128-bit, never DefaultHasher; timing includes fetch+deserialize+validate.

cards.title: Unified plan: reason-first, magic-by-default Jet (learnability research + Roc/Skip mining)
cards.body:
## Destination
Jet reads clearly, reasons locally, and writes with almost no ceremony: the compiler infers what is obvious (moves, copies, failure sets, effects, honesty), shows every inference where readers look, and lets experts pin any choice with a sigil or marker. Compile feedback stays sub-second on huge projects.

## Notes (order of work)
1. Performance foundation: copy model #3836 #3837 (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A); infallible lowering #3740/#3708; compiler speed #3852 (concurrent decl-granular query engine) -> #3853 (saved state) -> #2529 (opt-in session) + #2531 (incremental == clean) + #3851 (affected tests).
2. Failure and absence: #3838 three states (D-OUTCOME-SHAPE1=A), #3713 failure path report; open ballots D-FAIL-VISIBLE1, D-FAIL-PUBSIG1, D-FAIL-INFER-UNION1, D-ERR-CASES1, D-DISCARD1, D-DBG1, D-PAT-NAMED-NEST1, D-HONEST-SIG2.
3. Reading surface: fact sigil family on #3662 (D-COMPILER-NS1 glyph, D-META-ROOT3 path, D-BUILD-FACT3 roots, D-NAME-SPLICE1 names, D-DECL-META1 metadata); #3727 remove ++/--; #3725 &&/|| parens; #3739 Type{expr}; #3743 retired binding form; #3714 (rescoped pins).
4. Beginner loop: #3722 scaffold, #3721 quiet check, #3724 help order, #3723 glyph explain, #3718 authority, #3719 brackets, #3715 E0121, #3716 else lint, #3717 pure drops (see D-DISCARD1), #3720 diagnostic sweep.
5. Measure: dogfood rerun #2393.

## Decisions so far
D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A, D-OUTCOME-SHAPE1=A, D-BIND-TYPE2=A, D-HELP-SORT1=A (--sort az/za), D-NEW-TEMPLATE1=A, D-ERR-TRAIT1=A (+manual impl), D-SYSSCHED1=A.

## Fog
Fact sigil glyph; whether failures carry text marks by default; exact inferred failure unions; resident session defaults within D-JPK-NODAEMON1.

## Out of scope
Inferring parameter types on signatures (S4 keeps signatures written); a background daemon (D-JPK-NODAEMON1).

cards.title: Core incremental == clean oracle: random revision replay across tiers
cards.body: Split out of #2531 by the Opus 5.5 adversarial pass (2026-09-30): the query-engine rewrite (#3852) and saved state (#3853) must not land without an oracle, and #2531 is blocked on five cards. Hack verified incremental state against clean initialization across random revision jumps (talk J31LlAUtoos 27:48-30:19; hh_saved_state_verifier.ml).
cards.plan:
1. Harness: pick a corpus and a list of revisions; for each random walk, check incrementally and from clean; compare diagnostic bytes, TIR hash, and per-tier binary/output SHA (AOT, jet run, interpreter).
2. No dependency on sealed objects, ThinLTO, or the #2529 session.
3. Cases: body edit flipping an inferred failure/effect/ownership fact; line insert mid-file; glob gains a file; comptime env read; #Impure; new impl joins a reflection enumeration; clock/random during prep; same-content rename; case-insensitive filesystem; symlink swap; injected hash collision; foreign saved state; worker schedule seeds.
4. Resource caps: bounded revisions per run, memory-capped wrapper, nightly full matrix.

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #3852; criteria carried there as [#3860]. Incremental==clean oracle is the engine's required verifier.

Build Systems à la Carte (JFP 2020, section 3.6) gives a crisp correctness definition usable as this oracle: after a build, inputs are unchanged and every non-input equals its recomputation from the final store. The Verse team ran about 100 million QuickCheck cases on their rewrite rules before proving confluence (Verse calculus, ICFP 2023, section 3.9), a model for the random-replay volume. Report: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.

cards.title: Agent verification loop: jet try re-checks and runs affected tests in one verdict (Skipper-style)
cards.body: Owner (2026-09-30): wants Skipper's loop in Jet. Talk J31LlAUtoos 131:50-139:45: spec -> coding agent -> immediate sound incremental analysis -> reachability -> affected tests -> self-correction, target under one second (caption-only, partly unbuilt). Jet already has the pieces: `jet try <plan.json>` applies edits in an overlay, re-verdicts, rolls back by default (#2122, D-DEVR-TRY1=A); `jet inspect impact <file> <symbol>`; `jet review` semantic diff; `jet inspect digest` LLM surface; affected-test selection #3851; fast re-verdict #3852; proofs #3188/#3191. Missing: one command that returns checks + impact + affected test results as one machine-readable verdict for an agent to iterate on. Ballot D-TRY-TESTS1.
cards.plan:
1. `jet try` (per ballot) runs affected tests inside the overlay after a clean re-verdict.
2. One JSON verdict: diagnostics (stable codes, spans, fixes), impact set, selected/skipped/stale test counts, test results, timings, rollback state.
3. Latency budget: time-to-first-verdict recorded; skipped tests never reported as passing (#3851 rules).
4. Agent workload proof: a scripted agent fixes a seeded bug through repeated `jet try` calls in the dogfood harness (#2393).

cards.title: Check the self-hosted compiler as a module graph, not one assembled unit
cards.body: Compiler/ is 223 files and ~170k lines written as one flat namespace (only 4 files have `use`). Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh and the slice tooling assemble it into a single compiler.jet unit, which is the worst case for jet check: no module boundary, so the per-module interface-fingerprint incrementality (D-INCR-UNIT1, #1026) and any persisted module cache (#2517) can never apply, every edit re-checks everything, and the sema slice exceeds 6 GB. Owner direction 2026-09-30: prioritize making the tools we use to bootstrap/dogfood the self-hosted compiler fast; checking must never happen as one giant unit.
cards.plan: 1. Inventory cross-file references in Compiler/ with a script (Tools/compiler-modules/): for every top-level item, which files use it; propose module boundaries = one module per file inside each package (JetFoundation, JetLexer, JetParser, JetAst, JetSema, JetEval, JetOptimizer, JetCodegen, JetDriver), packages as real Jet packages with package.jet and explicit dependencies. 2. Mechanical migration per package in dependency order: add `use` imports and `pub` on exported items (formatter-checked), keep names unchanged; the migration script is idempotent and reviewable. 3. Replace assemble.mjs/check.sh with checking the package graph (`jet check Compiler/<Pkg>` or one workspace check that walks modules), so D-INCR-UNIT1 dirtying applies and #2517 can persist per-module results. 4. Measure: cold check of each package and of the whole graph; a body-only edit in JetSema re-checks one module; an interface edit re-checks importers only. 5. Keep tests/selfhost_* and Bootstrap/Tests.rs working against the new layout (greenfield cutover: remove the assembled-unit path).

cards.title: Cognitive-complexity score ignores nesting depth, contradicting its documented rule
cards.body:
Found while mining Jonathan Blow's code-visualizer clip (PbVHBToltXk, 2026-09-30). The planned code map reuses nesting depth, so the current score must be right first.

## Evidence

The scorer's header (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CognitiveComplexity.rs:3-7) says each branch, loop, or dispatch adds `1 + enclosing-structure-depth`. The live binary never adds the depth term.

Probe (binary ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/jet-debug-snapshot27, via ~/.cache/jet-luna/safe-jet.sh, 2026-09-30):

```
fn two_loops(n: Int) -> Int { total := 0
    loop i in 0..<n { loop j in 0..<n { total += i * j } }
    return total }
fn nested_if(n: Int) -> Int { if n > 100 { if n > 1000 { return 3 } return 2 } return 1 }
fn if_in_loop(n: Int) -> Int { total := 0
    loop i in 0..<n { if i > 2 { total += i } }
    return total }

$ jet lint --complexity nest.jet
nest.jet:1 fn two_loops — score 2
nest.jet:11 fn nested_if — score 2
nest.jet:21 fn if_in_loop — score 2
```

The documented rule gives 3 for each. The UI goldens bless the wrong numbers: tests/ui/lint_cognitive_complexity.stderr pins `tangled` at 4 (rule: 1 + 2 + 3 + 1 mixed boolean = 7), and the refactored golden pins `add_if_match` at 3 (rule: 4).

The likely cause is the strict span containment test at CognitiveComplexity.rs:110-112 or the spans recorded for loop and `if` nodes. This is not confirmed.

## Why it matters

`jet lint --complexity --max` is an agent self-check (#2033). An agent that flattens nesting sees no score change today. The code-map card reuses this nesting walker.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make the reported score follow the documented rule, then re-derive both UI fixtures by hand.

## Steps
1. Add the three-function reproduction above as a fixture with hand-derived scores (3, 3, 3).
2. Find why `contains` never matches an enclosing loop or `if`; fix the span or the containment test at the root.
3. Re-derive `tangled` (7) and `add_if_match` (4) by hand. The refactored fixture must still pass its budget: change its refactor or its budget, never the rule.
4. Regenerate the two UI snapshots and confirm the architecture-advice test is unchanged.

## Not in scope
No new metric, flag, or diagnostic code.

cards.title: Per-function code metrics from the checked program, in one inspect view
cards.body:
Owner request (2026-09-30): support every mode in Jonathan Blow's code visualizer, then show them visually (the visual is a separate card). Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PbVHBToltXk (clip of https://youtube.com/watch?v=IdpD5QIVOKQ), captured 2026-09-30.

## Modes seen in the source

Metric menu (frames at 05:12 and 06:40): 'if' Density, Maximum 'if' Depth, Maximum Loop Depth, Assignments, Global Reads, Global Writes, Heap Allocations, Heap Frees, Call Locality (module), Call Locality (file), Call Constancy, Blend. Every leaf is one procedure, sized by expression count (02:41-03:04). Borders: 'Modules and Files'. The talk also uses the map to spot polymorphic copies (07:57-08:49) and macro-expansion bloat (08:49-09:57). View Mode showed only Treemap; the other View Mode, Borders, and sidebar (Settings, Info, Graphs, Allocs) choices were never opened, so they are not specified here.

## What Jet has today

- `jet lint --complexity FILE` prints one control-flow score per function from the parsed file (Source/CmdDevTools.rs:8545). Its nesting term is broken (#3866).
- Sema records allocation and retain/release events with spans (MemoryFacts.rs:30-46) and dispatch sites with no known callee (`open_dispatches`, MemoryFacts.rs:61-72).
- The semantic index has call edges and resolved references with module paths (Source/CmdDevTools.rs:8793-8840).
- Nothing counts checked nodes, assignments, branch or loop depth, per-function allocation sites, call locality, dynamic calls, or generic instantiations.
- Jet has no mutable global item and no manual free, so three source modes need a Jet meaning (ballot D-CODEMAP-MEANING1).

## Mode mapping

| Source mode | Jet row |
|---|---|
| size (expression count) | checked expression nodes in the function |
| macro bloat | checked nodes minus written nodes (expansion) |
| 'if' density | branch count / size |
| max 'if' depth, max loop depth | deepest branch nesting, deepest loop nesting |
| assignments | assignment and compound-assignment count |
| heap allocations | allocation events |
| global reads/writes, heap frees | per D-CODEMAP-MEANING1 |
| call locality (module/file) | resolved calls leaving the module / file |
| call constancy | calls through a function value or trait object |
| polymorphic copies | distinct checked type-argument sets per generic function |
| blend | viewer-side weighted sum (visual card) |
cards.plan:
## Goal
One typed row per function, derived from the checked program, projected by the CLI surface chosen in D-CODEMAP-CLI1 with `--json`.

## Steps
1. Wait for D-CODEMAP-CLI1 and D-CODEMAP-MEANING1; build only the ratified surface and meanings.
2. Build rows from the existing checked projection (CheckProjection and its semantic index); do not reparse or run a second analyzer.
3. Share one nesting walker with `jet lint --complexity` (fixed in #3866).
4. Row identity: package, module, file, function, span. Each metric is a number or an explicit `unavailable` with a reason (for example an unresolved callee), never a silent zero.
5. Compute only when the view is requested; `jet check`, `jet build`, and `jet run` do no extra work.
6. Migrate CLI registry, help, completions, and man goldens in the same change.

## Tiers
These are compile-time facts about source. No execution tier runs them, so I9 has nothing to compare; the same facts must feed CLI and visual hosts.

cards.title: Visual code map: every function as a rectangle, coloured by a chosen metric
cards.body:
Owner request (2026-09-30): a visual tool, not only the CLI, to see usage hotspots across a codebase, covering every mode in Jonathan Blow's visualizer (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PbVHBToltXk).

## What the source shows

- A treemap: each leaf is one procedure, area proportional to its size (02:17-03:04).
- Colour from a chosen metric, blue (cold) to orange (hot), normalized within this program only; there is no absolute scale (04:37-05:00).
- Blend: a weighted sum of all metrics with the author's own weights (07:19-07:41).
- Borders around modules and files; the standard library appears as its own region (07:41-08:03).
- Hover shows the name, file:line, and values; in Blend mode it lists every metric (frame 02:24). Click opens the function in the editor; the map zooms (03:04-03:51).
- The map loads a saved metrics file that can live in source control (01:54-02:17).

## What Jet has today

- Canvas (`jet dev --canvas`, crates/jet-canvas) is Jet's browser IDE with source navigation and live rebuilds.
- The devtools catalog has a Structure panel and a Profiler panel (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/DevtoolsPanelCatalog.rs:8-28).
- `jet perf view` renders a runtime flamegraph in HTML (Source/CmdPerf.rs:2437).
- No code treemap exists anywhere in the tree (searched crates, Source, Core, Tools/editors on 2026-09-30).

## Where Jet can beat the source

The source needs a recompile and a file reload to refresh. Jet can refresh the map on every save, because the dev loop already re-checks the program. Runtime hotness from `jet perf` (#2997) can be a later colour source on the same map; it is not in this card.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Build the map in the host chosen by D-CODEMAP-VIEW1, reading only the rows from #3867.

## Steps
1. Wait for D-CODEMAP-VIEW1.
2. Layout: squarified treemap. Leaf area = checked size. Group by package, module, and file.
3. Controls: metric picker listing every #3867 metric plus Blend; border choice (none, modules, files, modules and files); Blend weights visible and adjustable in the view.
4. Colour: normalized within the loaded program, with a legend that says so. Hover shows absolute values for every metric.
5. Navigation: click opens the function's source location; zoom into a module or file and back.
6. Refresh: in the dev loop, a saved edit updates the map without restarting.
7. Snapshots: open a saved `--json` output from #3867 in the same view.
8. Measure first render and hover latency on the Compiler/ Jet sources and record them on this card.

## Not in scope
Runtime hotness colouring, and any View Mode or sidebar tool the source never showed.

cards.title: Core crypto hashes run on big integers: port SHA-512, BLAKE2b and Argon2id to U64
cards.body: Found by CryptoFinish: Core/crypto/expert.jet implements SHA-512, BLAKE2b and Argon2id on exact Int with a 64-bit mask (C_MASK64). Every word at or above 2^63 spills into big-integer arithmetic, so each G-mix, xor, rotate and add is a bignum op; block fills also allocate fresh 128-element lists (argon2_read_block, argon2_fill_block) and 16-element lists per permute pass. password_hash (m=65536, t=3) is ~196k block fills per call; crypto/primitive_matrix hits the 300 s cap on every tier and crypto_suite stalls after password_hash.
cards.plan: Port the 64-bit primitives to U64 with wrapping ops (wrapping_add, rotate_right, xor) and fixed-size in-place block buffers ([U64#128] or a reused list) in Core/crypto (one implementation shared by crypto.jet and expert.jet). Keep outputs byte-identical: prove with the FIPS 180-4, BLAKE2b and RFC 9106 vectors already in the goldens. Perf cell: Argon2id m=65536 t=3 vs the Rust argon2 crate and libsodium, per the performance gate (Jet/Rust <= 1.05). Goldens crypto/primitive_matrix and crypto/crypto_suite on run/--interpret/AOT (interpreter subject to D-INTERP-BUDGET1).

cards.title: JIT segfaults storing fixed-width integers into lists (exact-Int retention on U64 words)
cards.body: Found by CryptoU64 (#3870) on snapshot28: jet-rt JetArena::list_push_int / list_set_int call retain_exact_raw on every word. A U64 (or I64) value in [2^62, 2^63) whose low bits match JET_INT_POINTER_TAG is treated as an exact-Int heap pointer and dereferenced. Repro: `b := [U64]{U64{0}}; b[0] = (U64{0x6a09e667} << 32) | U64{0xf3bcc908}` -> SIGSEGV on jet run. Hits ~1.5% of stores in hash code; any user list of fixed-width integers is exposed (I1 memory safety).
cards.plan: Route fixed-width-element list operations (index write, push, insert, constant lists, extend, adapter results, sort, copy/clone, drop) by MIR element type to host routes that never apply exact-Int retention (jet-rt lib.rs, jet-jit Collections.rs host table, functions_compile.rs sites). Golden storing values across the full U64/I64 range incl. [2^62, 2^63) with tag-aligned low bits on run/--interpret/AOT; a fuzz test over random 64-bit words. Owner: CryptoU64.

EmitterViews, 2026-10-01: the Jet Rust emitter now emits reducible MIR CFGs as structured Rust (labeled loop/block/break/continue nested by dominators, explicit work stack, flat branch chains); irreducible CFGs keep the dispatch loop. This removes the view-lifetime E0502/E0506 class for release builds through the Jet compiler (option a over re-sliced triples or an unsafe lifetime erase; rationale in Docs/research/jet-backend-design-2026-10-01.md). isocheck clean; rustc proof on the Jet emitter's own output pending (~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/EmitterViews/PROOF.md). Separate defect: passing a view to a String read parameter emits &&str where &String is expected (E0308), MIRRust and probably the Jet emitter.

BootFixes, 2026-10-01: MIRRust emits each function as one dispatch loop ('mir_dispatch: loop { match pc }) with Option<&str>/Option<&[T]> view locals; rustc assumes any arm can follow any arm, so a later take/rebind of the view's base local (scope-end drop, loop variable) is E0502/E0506. Pre-existing since at least r89 (view_copy test failures). Bootstrap workaround: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Direct.jet:180 now takes an explicit copy (the only local/loop-base view binding in Compiler/). Core/app/app.jet:52,196 and Jetpack/Environment still have loop-base views. Real fix belongs in the Jet emitter before user release builds depend on it: options A (vetted lifetime-erase helper, relies on the Jet view checker) or B (owned copies for view locals, O(n) per binding). Other s170 test failures (core_files typed-drop on resource partial moves, view_copy JIT nested copies, mir_const stale fixtures) are pre-existing and frozen under the Rust freeze.

EmitParity4, 2026-10-01: Jet Emit reaches 166/166 goldens by runtime name: storage constants as JetPersistCell statics with get/set/take, folded constants as inline functions, persistent live-value reports, the __jet_ associated-type lane, wide casts. debug_trace waits on #3888 (front-end trace). Not behaviour-proven until jetc0 exists. isocheck clean 09:14.

EmitParity2, 2026-09-30 night: Jet Emit now bridges Encode/Decode impls (jet_encode/jet_decode), maps every Core native type as MIRRust does (JetIter, JetRange, Decimal/Fraction, date/time, Regex, DataTree, host handles) without re-declaring them, converts native enum payloads and host record fields, ports the special Core calls, shared-guard deref, NaN/infinity constants and per-function stack frames (the #3940 gap; entry/jobs/harness already matched). 158 of 166 goldens covered by runtime name; history capture and compute AD fail closed (excluded with reasons in ~/.cache/jet-luna/status/EmitParity-coverage.md). Full-unit check after the last edits still owed (unitcheck.sh).

Coverage table ~/.cache/jet-luna/status/EmitParity-coverage.md. Remaining: jet_panic_rich, Core native type mapping, special-cased Core calls, host record/enum conversion, shared-guard Deref, NaN/inf spellings (EmitParity2).

cards.title: AOT: rustc takes >650 s on a 30-variant #Comparable enum program (13.8 MB generated main.rs)
cards.body: After #3871 (dee9a5fe4), jet lowers fast, but the AOT Rust for a 30-variant named-payload #Comparable enum with a match, == and compare (the original Examples/features/types/enum_many_variants, 30 variants) makes rustc run >650 s; an unused 30-variant enum (same 13.7 MB main.rs size) compiles in 52 s, and 12 variants take 157 s. Likely the emitted derived compare/equal/Debug shapes (per-variant pairs) or a rustc-hostile match. Jetpack enums reach 30+ variants, so AOT builds of Jetpack will hit this. Find which emitted items dominate rustc time (rustc -Z time-passes / self-profile on the generated crate) and emit a linear shape (e.g. compare by discriminant first, then per-variant payload).

JetDriver verb surface: Jet has only compile and check. The compiler-facing verbs (test, doc, fuzz, lint, expand, explain, inspect, emit, fix, graph/query/explain-build, semindex, repl, eval, debug, try, jobs, generate, bind) have no Jet entry

jet update versus jet self update: help text should say which changes project pins and which installs a release; consider jet self update applying the current channel by default, like rustup update (claim learning-compilers:OZ9; APICompLearn `jet help update`/`jet help self` on dev-05ea86f65).

Distill 2026-10-05, compiler-cost report rows (carried #3867 rows; also cite on #2528 explain-build). Jon Blow's Jai `-perf` report (youtube A2U_GMWl9l4): one flag on an ordinary build answers 'why is my compile slow?' for a program author, not a compiler author. It lists (a) every compile-time execution in order, which exposed two metaprograms both instrumenting every function, an unknown duplicate; (b) total time spent in compile-time execution that blocks compilation; (c) phase times; (d) a polymorphism report: calls needing overload/polymorph resolution, solver runs, and per generic function the calls that reused an existing instantiation (table_add: 515 calls, 427 reused) versus each new instantiation with its type arguments. The author wants timestamps on the comptime list (gap). Code-map talk (youtube PbVHBToltXk): metrics computed at compile time are saved to a binary file viewable offline; an expanded-size map revealed a 300-line function holding 50-60 macro expansions and one generated copy of table_add per key type; normalised colour weights are subjective (users may want their own weights; evidence gap). Rows to carry: instantiation reuse vs new (with type arguments), comptime execution list with timings, expanded-size per function. The same facts feed #4272's code map.

cards.title: #SingleUse duty is lost when the value is stored in a list or an optional
cards.body: A `#SingleUse` value must be consumed on every path (D-LIN1: E0140/E0141/E0142). The duty disappears when the value is wrapped. `leases :: [Lease{name: "a"}, Lease{name: "b"}]` followed by no use runs and exits 0 with no diagnostic. `held :: maybe_lease(1)` (returns `Lease?`) only gets the L0101 unused-binding warning. A single bare `lease :: Lease{…}` correctly gets E0140. Linear Haskell (POPL 2018, §6.1) names this exact consequence of putting linearity on types: a container that holds a linear value must itself become linear. Probed on target/debug/jet built 2026-09-30 12:12 from a dirty working tree (44 modified files under crates/jet-sema); reproduce on clean HEAD first. The fix direction is ballot D-LIN-CONTAINER1 on this card. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.

cards.title: An unannotated parameter is misread as a multi-head variant: three cascading errors, none names the missing type
cards.body: `fn twice(x) -> Int { x * 2 }` called as `twice(4)` reports E0305 "Multi-head variant `x` is not an enum variant", then E0107 "Nothing named `x` exists here", then E0104 "`twice` expects 0 arguments, got 1". A beginner coming from Python or JavaScript meant a parameter without a type. None of the three messages says so, and two are cascades of the first. This is the error-localization lesson from Diagnosing Type Errors with Class (PLDI 2015) and SHErrLoc: blame the likely mistake, not the first rule that failed. Probed on target/debug/jet built 2026-09-30 12:12 (dirty tree). Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.
cards.plan:
1. When a multi-head head is a bare lowercase name that is not a variant of any enum in scope, and the function has no other head, report one diagnostic: the parameter needs a type (fix: `x: Int`, using the body's use when it pins a type, otherwise a placeholder).
2. Suppress the E0107 and E0104 cascade that follows from the misparse.
3. Add a UI snapshot and keep E0305 for genuine multi-head typos.

questions.text: I dont see why this would basically ever be the case. You would just fuse the two tables together unless there is additional logic separating them. I think tables should be complete units
questions.answer: Agreed. I revised the ballot. Option A is now "Complete tables, with a fuse hint": every table names every variant, whatever checks came before it. The existing lint L0514 (card #2395) already suggests one table when three or more adjacent checks test the same value. It gains one more shape: a single early check followed directly by a table on the same value suggests folding the check into the table, with a one-click fix. When other logic sits between them, no hint fires, and the table stays complete on its own. My earlier recommendation (let earlier checks shrink the table) is now option B, recommended against.

questions.text: For A, I understand that code is copied but if it is copied and has already been processed, then it should be cached/incrementally handled with the compiler and therefore should have minimal/no impact, yes? Effectivelly just linking?
questions.answer: Partly. Checking is not affected at all: inlining runs after sema, on MIR, and the helper itself is checked and lowered once. But it is not just linking. Each caller that receives a copy is optimized and turned into machine code with the helper's body inside it, so that work grows with the copied size. Only small bodies get copied, which keeps it small. Caching covers the rest: each caller's optimized result is keyed on its own body plus the bodies copied into it. An unchanged program reuses everything, and editing a helper re-optimizes only the callers that hold a copy of it, not the whole program. That is the one real cost, and I reworded the ballot's loss to say exactly that. For context, rustc already does this for jet build today; the ballot brings it to jet run and the interpreter.

questions.text: For A, I understand that code is copied but if it is copied and has already been processed, then it should be cached/incrementally handled with the compiler and therefore should have minimal/no impact, yes? Effectivelly just linking?
questions.answer: Duplicate of the question just before it on D-OPT-INLINE1; answered there. Short version: checking is unaffected, the helper is compiled once, unchanged callers come from cache, and only callers holding a copy of an edited helper are rebuilt.

questions.text: Can we build something alongside/into sema so we dont have duplicates that allow us to have a sherrloc like system for better lint/error detection?
questions.answer: Yes, and it is better than the separate engine. I revised the ballot so option A is "Blame ranking built into sema". Sema already records where effect and failure facts come from (RightsProvenance and FailureCallProvenance). The change adds the same source record to the few places sema infers types: locals, lambdas, literals, and inferred failures and effects. When a check fails, sema ranks the facts involved by how many conflicts each explains and how many agreeing facts it would break. The top one becomes the error's main location; the rest become notes. It uses sema's own facts, so there is no second solver to drift, and it runs only after a check has failed, so correct programs pay nothing. A corpus of seeded mistakes measures first-error accuracy and gates each change. The separate SHErrLoc-style engine is now option B, and case-by-case fixes are C, both recommended against.

cards.title: Guarded dispatch tables: E0003 parse error without else, while L0303 says to delete the else
cards.body: In a value table on an enum, a guarded arm (`.Rect(w, h) && w == h -> …`) makes the table fail to parse when there is no `else`: two E0003 errors ("Expected a call, binding, assignment, or `return`, found a piece of quoted text"). Adding `else` makes it parse, but when unguarded arms already cover every variant, `jet check` reports L0303 "This `else` can never run … Delete the `else` arm". The user follows the Fix and gets the parse error again. The comment in Examples/features/patterns/nested_payload_safety.jet:26-27 says guards need an else. Whichever rule wins, E0003 is the wrong diagnostic: coverage must be reported by sema (E0307/L0303) in words about coverage. The rule itself is ballot D-MATCH-GUARD1 on this card (owner: exhaustive pure enum tables must not carry an else, so a new variant forces handling). Probed on target/debug/jet built 2026-09-30 12:12 from a dirty tree; Tower #3587 is building nearby. Related history: #1440. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.

cards.title: Performance: Jet-compiled byte loops run 2-120x slower than equivalent Rust kernels (AOT release)
cards.body:
DedupCore2 measured on 2026-09-30, 1 MB x 10, AOT --release, Jet Core body vs the Rust Prelude kernel for the same function:

| Function | Jet body | Rust kernel |
|---|---|---|
| hex.encode | 470 ms | 225 ms |
| base64.encode | 334 ms | 10 ms |
| base32.encode | 530 ms | 14 ms |
| hex.decode | 1240 ms | 19 ms |
| base64.decode | 2450 ms | ~20 ms |

Core now forwards these functions to the Rust kernels (one implementation, I9), so end users don't pay the gap there. But any user code written like these bodies (byte loops, string building, table lookups) pays it, and that fails the performance gate against Rust (parity band 1.05). Profile the emitted Rust for one of these bodies (jet emit --rust), find the causes (bounds checks, per-byte String/list growth, boxed values, checked arithmetic, clones), fix them in the emitter/optimizer in both compilers, and add a paired perf cell per AGENTS.md.

cards.title: Package path policy treats a path dependency inside the project folder as the app's own code
cards.body: `package_policy_source_path` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Effects.rs:296-307) says it returns `None` for a dependency module so package path policy cannot leak across package boundaries. It only strips `bundle.project_root` and never consults `bundle.dep_roots`. A path dependency whose source root sits under the project folder (for example `libs/util`), or a package store configured under it, therefore gets a project-relative path. The root package's `policy.unsafe` (UnsafeObligations.rs:87-123), `policy.effects` (Effects.rs:248-294), and `policy.expert` then apply to the dependency's code as if the app wrote it. Other passes already attribute modules by longest `dep_roots` match (BudgetSpecs.rs:168-172, Pipeline.rs:634-644, GenericModules/Identity.rs:342-346). Found by the adversarial reviewer of ballot D-UNSAFE-DEPS1 on 2026-09-30 from code reading; not yet reproduced with a program. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.
cards.plan:
1. Reproduce: a package with `policy.unsafe: .Deny` and a path dependency under `libs/` that contains `#Unsafe`; record today's verdict.
2. Make `package_policy_source_path` return None when the module's path falls under any `dep_roots` entry (longest match, the same rule the other passes use); keep one shared helper for module-to-package attribution.
3. Add UI tests for effects, unsafe, and expert policy with an in-tree path dependency.

cards.title: #Transact rollback misses locals changed through method calls (list.push, &self methods)
cards.body: D-TXN-ROLLBACK layer 1 promises that every value a `#Transact` block mutates is snapshotted and restored on a `?`-failure (Examples/features/errors/transact.jet:3-4). `collect_txn_mut_roots` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/env.rs:419-431) collects only assignment targets (`x = …`, `x += …`, `x.f = …`, `x[i] = …`). Mutation reached only through a `&self` method call such as `log.push(entry)`, or through a deep alias, is not snapshotted; the code comment calls it a documented deferred corner. So after a failed transaction, such a local keeps the change while assigned locals are restored. This also blocks D-CONC-STM2 option A (re-run on conflict), which needs every local change undone between attempts. Found by the adversarial reviewer of D-TXN-WAIT1 on 2026-09-30 from code reading; not yet reproduced with a program. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.
cards.plan:
1. Reproduce: a local list, `log.push(1)` inside #Transact, then `return Err(…)`; print the list after the call.
2. Extend root collection to receivers of mutating calls (exclusive `&` access, including `&self` methods) using sema's access facts, not method names.
3. For deep aliases sema cannot attribute to a root, choose one checked outcome: snapshot the alias target or reject the mutation inside #Transact with a registered diagnostic.
4. Prove on AOT, jet run, and the interpreter.

cards.title: Parity: the Jet compiler loads no Core/*.jet source modules (Core calls become host rows; Core source bodies, types and errors never reach Jet programs)
cards.body: MirrorPrune, 2026-09-30, from reading both compilers: Compiler/JetDriver Loader.jet (1730-1869) loads only authorized package roots, and Bootstrap/Host/Native.rs requires a package.jet per root, which Core/ lacks. JetSema Calls/Core.jet sema_call_core_source_target needs a graph module named core.* and so always returns None; every Core call becomes a registry/host CoreCall row. The Rust compiler loads Core source modules, checks and lowers the reachable Core bodies, and exposes Core types. Behavior difference today: Jet types core.perf.override_fidelity as failing with a String (CorePlatformSignatures.jet:332), so a Jet program can't match .Err(.OutOfRange(x)) on PerfError. Load Core source modules into the Jet graph the same way Rust does (canonical <corelib>/ identities), resolve Core calls to source bodies where Rust does, and keep host rows only where Rust does. Blocks #3980 (Core-body pruning) and relates to #3908 (packages).

cards.title: Effect vocabulary lives in five homes, breaking D-META-ONE1=A
cards.body:
Effect names live in five homes, though the header of `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Effects.jet` states ratified D-META-ONE1=A: "an effect exists exactly when it is written here".

Evidence (commit d382af63b plus the working tree at audit time):
- `Effects.jet:8-22`: 13 roots and 2 leaves.
- `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/effects_surface.rs:37-67` (`BUILTIN_EFFECT_LEAVES`): 29 leaves, 27 of them absent from `Effects.jet` (`Time.Wait`, `Exec.Args`, `Exec.Exit`, `DB.Read`, `DB.Write`, `Rand.Draw`, 21 `FFI.*`).
- `crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs:549-581` (`effect_action`): the roots `Mem` and `Panic`, and the leaf `Mem.Alloc`.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/TargetMachine.rs:320-335`: `Time.Sleep`.
- `Core/compiler/lang.jet:25-38` (`core.compiler.lang.Effect`): 12 names, including `Crypto`, `Random`, and `Proc`, which exist nowhere else; it lacks `Log`, `GPU`, `FFI`, `Mem`, and `Panic`. Markers use it in qualified form (`tests/marker_rule_signatures.rs:108-115`).
- `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:448-655`: a hard-coded Core module → effect-leaf table.

Probe: `fn crypto() -[Crypto]> Int { 2 }` fails with `E0119` "`Crypto` isn't a known effect", although `lang.Effect.Crypto` is public. `fn waits() -[Time.Wait]> Int { 1 }` is accepted.

Source: Docs/audits/elegance-audit-2026-09-30.md §3.3. The owner choice for the reflective enum is ballot D-EFFECT-ENUM1 on this card.

cards.title: `core.tasks` blocking calls declare the `Time` root instead of `Time.Wait`
cards.body:
Seven blocking calls in `Core/tasks/tasks.jet` declare `-[Time]>`: `recv` (:121), `get` (:127), `result` (:129), `wait` (:131), `waitall` (:93), `waitany` (:99), and `timeout` (:154). Across Core, 119 other blocking declarations use the `Time.Wait` leaf, and `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:448-655` infers `Time.Wait` for blocking Core calls. The root covers the leaf, so this is coarser, not unsafe. But it tells readers that waiting on a task is the same as reading the clock. A fresh reader also answered `Time` for a blocking receive in the audit's prediction test.

Source: Docs/audits/elegance-audit-2026-09-30.md §3.3.

cards.title: Core module map: one owner per job, singular names, nested overlaps
cards.body:
Owner-requested elegance audit, dive 3.4. `Session` is exported by `app`, `web`, and `auth`. The working directory, environment, and pid live in `sys`, `process`, `files`, and `files.path`. `core.sync` holds CRDTs, while locks live in `core.tasks`. `term` and `tui` split terminal presentation. Seven root names are plurals. A closed-book prediction test of the proposed map scored 7 hit, 0 near, 3 miss; the misses showed that `process` must own per-process state and that `Session` belongs in `auth`.

The owner choices are D-CORE-MODULE-MAP1 and D-CORE-MODULE-ABBREV1 on this card.

cards.title: Memory regression: jet run of the 108k-line PackageModel unit reaches 24G in 18 s (pre-dee9a5fe4 binary ran at ~3.9G)
cards.body: Split from #3871 on closure. dee9a5fe4 (the #3871 fix for exponential named-payload enum lowering) regresses memory on large units: ~/.cache/jet-luna/IceFix/3676/unit/run/project under jet run reaches 10G in 12 s and 24G in 18 s (cgroup OOM), while the pre-fix binary ran it for 3500 s at ~3.9G. cards.title: Dev-loop speed: paused at 2026-09-30 state; resume after Jet-Rust parity
cards.body:
Owner, 2026-09-30 night: the dev loop needed to stop taking ~20 minutes per test/recheck/recompile; that is done enough, and further speed work resumes once the Jet compiler has full parity. State when paused (release jet unless noted):
- jet build hello: 117 ms cold / 68 ms warm (Go 140/80, Zig 420/350). First build on a fresh system: ~1.0 s (prebuilt runtime rlibs, Tools/packaging/prebuild-runtime.sh). jet check hello warm 0.07 s; jet run hello 0.21 s.
- 5,135-line program (~/.cache/jetbench2/big): jet build 5.86 s cold / 0.16 s warm (was 96 s); jet check 1.28 s; jet run 6.4 s.
- 116k-line check slice: ~36-55 s release; one-line-edit warm re-check 54 s debug (item reuse + stored compile-time values, #2517).
- Cranelift dev backend (#3953, D-AOT-CRANELIFT1): prebuilt jet-aot-rt runner + verified appended image; release builds stay rustc/LLVM.
Resume list, in order:
1. #3953 DevBuildFast2 levers: stored compiled functions by MIR digest (Core compiles once per jet version), parallel Cranelift, pruning unreachable Core before lowering; then re-profile (cold 5.9 s was Cranelift 2.9 s, TIR->MIR 1.9 s, MIR optimize 0.8 s, front end 0.8 s).
2. #2517 IncrStage step 4: marker-rule product evaluation (~9%), failure-union probe, web partition and derive into item reuse; record subsystem in the Jet driver (#3948).
3. Fast-compiler architecture stages 1-5 in Jet (Docs/research/fast-compiler-architecture-2026-09-30.md): arenas and interning, comptime lowered once with runtime values, parallel checking, Jai-class throughput target.
4. #3999 memory regression on large units; Jet optimizer dev/verify switch (skip per-pass legality re-checks like Rust release).
Scripts: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/{DevBuildFast,DevBuildFast2,CraneliftAOT3,IncrStage6}/, benchmarks ~/.cache/jetbench2/.

Frozen until the bootstrap finishes and the Rust front end retires (D-EXEC1, #4013). Owner 2026-09-30: dev-loop speed paused until Jet-Rust parity; card holds the resume list. Paused work: the sweep reopens this card when that step lands.

Speed note 2026-10-01: Rust emission of the 170k-line Jet compiler went from ~85 min to ~2 min by replacing per-query linear scans with indexes (type defs, user impls by trait) and memoizing type_derive_capability (Stage0Rustc, Stage0c); whole-compiler build sweep 90 min -> 5:51 at 21.6G peak. Memory is the remaining large-program cost.

Finding (ParserParity2, 2026-09-30 night): jet run of a 3.1 MB unit spends ~10 of its 11.7 minutes lowering and JIT-compiling the whole unit before running anything, including functions the program cannot reach; jet check of the same unit takes ~90 s. Reachability pruning before lowering on jet run is a large dev-loop lever.

DevBuildFast2 final (paused): parallel Cranelift + per-function compiled-code cache landed. 5,135-line program cold 6.52 -> 4.73 s (machine under load; old jet re-measured alongside); one CPU: 7.24 s cold vs 5.0 s with every function from the store. Executables byte-identical across cold / fully stored / one CPU; output equals jet run. Correction to resume item 1: Core functions are never compiled into images (Core calls are runner hosts) and Core pruning before lowering already existed, so those two levers are void. Real next levers: TIR->MIR lowering 1.82 s, MIR passes 0.82 s, serial Cranelift IR building ~0.65 s, Cranelift verifier 28% of compile CPU (off in release?). Proofs owed: cargo test --test build_entry dev_build_; --test ice_report_codegen_rejection; -p jet-store; cargo metadata --locked.

cards.title: String.slice(a, b) includes the end index; byte and list .slice exclude it
cards.body: Found by JetExec on snapshot117 (2026-09-30 night): String.slice(a, b) returns the text through index b inclusive, while [U8].slice(a, b) and [T].slice(a, b) stop before b. Two meanings for one spelling breaks I8 (one mechanism per meaning) and has already caused panics in the Jet compiler's own parser (Items.jet:660, Modules.jet:81, fixed by ParserParity2). Needs: the spec's rule for .slice (check Docs/spec and Core), one meaning across String/bytes/lists on every tier, a golden pinning it, and a sweep of Compiler/, Core/ and Examples/ call sites. If the spec does not decide it, ballot it for the owner.

Unbuilt; proof on the next snapshot. List/bytes slices excluded already; --interpret lacks list_slice (frozen tier).

Owner ruling 2026-10-01 (asked in chat): "End excluded everywhere": .slice(a, b) excludes the end for String, lists and bytes (slice(1, 3) = items 1 and 2), matching a..<b; String changes to match; migrate every in-repo caller (Compiler/, Core/, Examples/) in one cutover; golden on all tiers.

More evidence 2026-10-01 (JetCli2, MirLint2): the shipping runtime's String.slice(a, b) treats the end as inclusive (RangeBounds.rs) while Compiler/ code (ForeignProviders.jet, FactReads.jet) calls x.slice(n, x.len()) as exclusive and panics at run time. Needs the ruling this card asks for.

Retargeted to the Jet compiler under the Rust freeze, 2026-10-01 (owner): the Rust compiler only gets stage-zero blockers, deletions and C-ABI runtime exports. String.slice end-index semantics are fixed in Core and the Jet compiler only.

cards.title: JIT resolves folded prep constants by bare type name: a user enum named like a Core enum gets Core's discriminants (silent wrong output on jet run/dev builds)
cards.body: Found by JetExec2 (2026-10-01). crates/jet-jit/src/jit/functions_compile.rs enum_discriminant (~11332) and declared_constant_fields look types up by bare name, so with a user enum Effect the Core core.compiler.lang Effect wins. Symptoms: 'MIR enum variant Effect::Rand is missing' (falls back to rustc), and variants shared by both enums (FS, Net) silently get Core's discriminants under jet run and Cranelift dev builds. Repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/JetExec2/effenum. Fix: resolve by checked type identity (MIR type id), never by name; golden with a user enum shadowing a Core enum name, proven on jet run, --interpret, jet build and the dev build. Jet mirror: check JetEval/JetCodegen for the same name lookup.

cards.title: Parity: JetSema has no inline-module subsystem (module bodies never registered or checked)
cards.body: Found by SemaParity6 (2026-10-01). In the Jet compiler, CodeModule bodies (module X { ... }) are never registered or checked: no sibling-call mangling, no alias.fn resolution, no member-type hoisting. Any program that declares an inline module checks wrong in the Jet compiler, and generic modules (#3894) have no consumer for their expansion. Port the Rust inline-module path (registration, checking, name resolution, lowering) so both compilers give the same results; then #3894 expansion lands on top. Fixtures: tests/ui and Examples/features using module bodies (live jet check is the oracle).

Open: templates nested in templates, Core-importing modules keep functions in their body, value folding limits. Fixtures listed for the runner.

InlineModules, 2026-10-01: new Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/InlineModules.jet lowers inline module x { ... } as the Rust checker does: member types lifted under Rust's module_type_name, top-level member functions lifted under Rust's member names with sibling calls renamed, x.f(...) calls and use x.[f] imports resolved with E0608/E0609/E0611/E0105 Rust text; body diagnostics name the source function. unitcheck 04:49 clean. cards.title: Parity: JetSema has no String builtin-method surface (s.trim(), s.after(), to_upper, replace, starts_with ... all E0311)
cards.body: Found by MemParity3 (2026-10-01). JetSema resolves no String builtin methods: s.after(sep), s.trim(), s.before(sep), to_upper, replace, starts_with and the rest find no candidate and report E0311 (Methods.jet sema_call_resolve_method_with_inference); no sema site emits TBuiltinOp.Trim/After/StringIndexOf; Core/text/string.jet carries only len. Nearly every real program calls String methods, so the Jet compiler rejects them. Port the whole Rust builtin-method surface for String (crates/jet-sema Collections.rs builtin_method_return rows and the TBuiltinOp lowering), then audit the other builtin receivers (lists, maps, sets, bytes, numbers) for the same gap. MemParity3 adds only trim/after/before for #4004; the rest is this card.

cards.body: Seen on the 2026-09-30 tier sweep and again by JetFront3 (2026-10-01). cards.title: Rust builtin-method defects found by the Jet port: wrong output, ICEs, unchecked arguments, len meaning
cards.body:
Found by BuiltinMethods (2026-10-01) while porting the builtin-method surface to JetSema. Each is a Rust-compiler defect; the Jet port must match the fixed behavior, not the bug.
1. Silent wrong output: [4, 8, 15].lazy().to_set().len() prints 0 instead of 3.
2. ICE: String.to_string() and Bool.to_string() crash MIR lowering ('builtin method ToString requires structural MIR lowering').
3. Map.replace(k, v): Rust treats it as a read (E0225 on &m.replace) and an unmarked call crashes in lowering; it writes the map, so it needs write access like other mutating methods.
4. Rust does not type-check the arguments of String center, ljust, rjust, zfill, compare, matches, match, last_index_of, after and before (JetSema does, E0108).
5. "héllo".len() returns 5 (characters) but the docs say len is byte length (6). Code and spec disagree: find the ratified rule (Docs/spec, Core docs, decision log); if unratified, ballot it for the owner with both options; do not change behavior before that.
6. View.index_of: Rust's table says T? but the lowering returns Int?.
Each fix: golden or UI test on every tier, both compilers.

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #3983; criteria carried there as [#4009]. Builtin-method semantics found by the port; Jet must match the fixed behavior. Triage evidence: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs:17587 maps title; :15344-15350 documents missing Euclidean call location; Jet emission builtin-method regression proof remains incomplete.

Proof and Rust-freeze retarget 2026-10-01 (TowerCloser). Proof batch s170 (snapshot170 tree, rustc golden harness): text/string_len_scalars ok (1 passed, ~/.cache/jet-luna/proof-s170/tc_4009b.log); text/string_method_surface FAILED (tc_4009a.log: rustc E0308 jet_int_to_radix JetInt vs i64 at generated :395, E0061 jet_int_owned_div_euclid/rem_euclid take 4 args, 2 given, at :399/:404); collections/receiver_method_surface FAILED (tc_4009c.log: E0506 local assigned while borrowed by jet_view_new_range at :313); collections/index_of_by_value (D-INDEXOF1, card #4010 frozen) FAILED (tc_4010.log: E0506/E0502, same view-borrow shape). The CLI tiers are fine: on jet-debug-snapshot170, jet run, --interpret and jet build (Cranelift debug) MATCH expected for all four files. So c1 (shipping compiler fixes) is met; the rustc-emission defects go to the Jet emitter only under the Rust freeze (c2), and c3 covers the Jet compiler mirror. Note for screens: jet build without --release uses Cranelift, so an 'AOT match' from screen.sh is not the rustc path.

MethodBugs, 2026-10-01: all 6 fixed in both compilers. (1) lazy().to_set() read the Iter handle as a list: now drained with IterToList (prints 3 on run, --interpret, AOT). (2) ToString lowers through the Display string path (no ICE). (3) Map.replace and Set.replace now mutate (E0224 when unmarked). (4) String after/before/last_index_of/compare/equal/matches/match/zfill/center/ljust/rjust arguments are type-checked (E0108). (5) Per ratified S41, String.len() counts scalars everywhere: Core/text/string.jet len fixed (with use core.text it gave 6), core-library.md corrected (count_bytes/text.byte_count for bytes). (6) View.index_of returns Int?. Goldens text/string_method_surface, text/string_len_scalars, collections/receiver_method_surface pass run+AOT on snapshot142; 2 fail --interpret on pre-existing evaluator gaps (card #4010). UI tests receiver_mark_collection_replace and string_method_arg_types need blessing.

cards.title: MIR Lint: independent typed check of MIR in the Jet compiler (always-on final pass; per-pass in tests/CI/--verify)
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-01 (SPJ Core Lint idea). An independent type-and-ownership checker over MIR, separate from the checker's code: every operand type against its operation, every call against the callee signature by ID (never by name), enum variants and payloads against declarations, ownership state (moved/borrowed/initialized), effect rows. Runs once after the last pass on every compile (target cost 2-5% of compile time; linear dataflow over bitsets, no per-block clones) and after every pass in tests, CI and --verify, reporting an ICE that names the pass. Same rules in Rust (crates/jet-foundation) and Jet (Compiler/JetOptimizer or JetFoundation). Rule-by-rule tests with a planted bug per rule. Then a TIR Lint.

cards.title: Markers `#allow` and `#wire` break the PascalCase marker law
cards.body:
The executable naming table says markers are PascalCase (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:764`, `("marker", NameCase::Pascal)`), and 81 of 83 active markers follow it. Two do not: `marker allow(...)` and `marker wire(...)` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Markers.jet:207,211`).

The comment at `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs:99-107` calls lowercase `allow` deliberate and cites D-LINTPOLICY1. That decision does not ratify a lowercase spelling; it quotes the old Rust attribute `#[allow(lint)]` only as a current-state example. No decision ratifies lowercase `wire`. The owner directed on 2026-10-01 that both be fixed.

Spelling sites: `MARKER_ALLOW` (`markers.rs:107`), a hard-coded `"allow"` in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Numeric.rs:200`, the parser (`crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs:363`), sema (`CheckerCore/statements.rs:1168-1181`, `stdlib_lints/loop_lints.rs:300`), and the `wire` row in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs:2044`.

Source: Docs/audits/elegance-audit-2026-09-30.md, syntax ledger.
cards.plan:
The Jet compiler builds marker names from the embedded Prelude/Markers.jet and hard-codes no `allow`/`wire` (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ScopeMembers.jet:162-176). The fix is the shared Markers.jet rows plus examples and tests. The frozen Rust compiler hard-codes `allow` (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs:107; Numeric.rs:200), so renaming the shared row breaks Rust lint suppression: owner chooses the timing.

Owner 2026-10-01: the Rust compiler (crates/, Source/) is frozen; implement only in the Jet compiler (Compiler/). Shared canonical sources (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/*.jet, Core/, Docs/) are read by BOTH compilers, so edits there need owner timing; never hand-edit generated Compiler files (DiagnosticRows.jet, CoreCallRows.jet, CoreSources.jet) — regenerate them.

cards.title: Active keyword `yield` is missing from `JET_KEYWORD_LIST`
cards.body:
`yield` is an active keyword (D-STREAMYIELD1): the lexer maps it to `TokKind::KwYield` (`crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/mod.rs:79`; constant `KW_YIELD` at `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_surface.rs:514`). `JET_KEYWORD_LIST` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/package_files.rs:459-551`) is documented as the canonical list of real keywords, and it omits `yield`.

Consumers of that list therefore miss it:
- `keyword_spelling(&TokKind::KwYield)` returns `None` (`Lexer/mod.rs:44-48`).
- LSP completion and keyword tokens (`Source/LSP/Completion.rs:102`, `Source/LSP/Server.rs:3343`).
- Generated-name reservation (`Syntax/predicates.rs:463`).
- The foreign binders' reserved-name checks (`crates/jet-pkg-model/src/*Bind.rs`), so a binder can emit a Jet identifier named `yield`.
- The `jet inspect` keyword digest (`Source/CmdInspect.rs:1874`).

criteria.text: [from #2859 c1] From #666 c2: The canonical production run `scripts/agent/jet-env sh tools/perf/dashboard.sh --json` covers every `tools/perf/corpus.tsv` program in all six states: jit-clean, jit-no-change, jit-representative-edit, aot-release-clean, aot-release-no-change, and aot-release-representative-edit. Each row contains latency, peak memory, output/stderr hashes, phases, stage/profile/backend, and machine/tool identities. Apply the AGENTS.md comparator separately to every cell and metric: Rust runtime rows may be at most 1.05x and every non-Rust peer must be below 1.00x. Missing, mismatched, unavailable, or inconclusive evidence fails; no average can pass.

criteria.text: [from #2859 c2] From #666 c5: Focused production-output checks over the affected golden and diagnostic fixtures compare emitted behavior, output/stderr hashes, docs examples, and audit rows. Run `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden --test diagnostic_snapshots` with the dashboard receipt and source/golden hashes; update documentation and audit output only after the command evidence exists. Full-suite proof remains epoch closeout.
criteria.evidence: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #2859; criteria carried there as [#4050]. Part 1/7 split of #2859 (criteria are #2859 c1-c4 verbatim).

The receipt names this card as the sole owner; no sibling evidence substitutes for it.
criteria.evidence: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #2859; criteria carried there as [#4050]. Part 1/7 split of #2859 (criteria are #2859 c1-c4 verbatim).

criteria.text: [from #2859 c4] From #676 c5: Every passing row runs the same source through the named JIT, dev, and optimized-AOT paths and records profile/backend, output, diagnostics, effects, and tier parity. cards.title: Lint suppression `#allow(lint)` never reaches the gate ledger, against D-LINTPOLICY1=A
cards.body:
Ratified D-LINTPOLICY1=A: "every bypass is spelled at the site or on the command line, never in hidden config, and lands in the audit record". Its lesson lists `#[allow(lint)]` among the bypasses the law binds.

Today `#allow(name)` only filters diagnostics: sema collects names into `statement_lint_allows` and drops matching diagnostics (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:620-643,1181-1183`). `GateKind` has 13 kinds and none for lint suppression (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs:660-676`), and `GateLedger` collects no `#allow` row (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/GateLedger.rs`). So `jet inspect gates` cannot show a project's lint suppressions, while it does show `#Unsafe`, `#Impure`, `#Nondeterministic`, `assume_deterministic`, scrubs, duty drops, and precision demotions.

Related: #4016 renames the marker to `#Allow`.

Source: Docs/audits/elegance-audit-2026-09-30.md (principle hunt, 2026-10-01).

cards.title: Principle: one law for every gate (written, reasoned, ledgered, refusable)
cards.body:
Elegance principle hunt, 2026-10-01. Jet already has one gate mechanism: `GateKind` (13 kinds) and `GateLedger`, shown by `jet inspect gates` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs:660-676`; `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/GateLedger.rs`). The surface does not show that unity. Lint suppressions are not gates (#4078). Only `unsafe`, `impure`, and `nondeterministic` can be refused by policy (`PolicyKey`, `crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy.rs:9-30`). Determinism has two spellings, `assume_deterministic { }` and `#Nondeterministic("…")`, which are already the same ledger kind (`GateLedger.rs:355-359,670-671`).

Three ratified decisions state the law in separate domains: D-AUTHORITY-MODEL1=A, D-FACT-LAW1=B, and D-LINTPOLICY1=A.

Closed-book prediction test: 5 hit, 0 near, 1 miss; the miss led to the sentence "the outermost refusal wins".

Owner choice: ballot D-GATE-LAW1.
cards.plan: After ratification: make every gate kind a policy key with forbid / per-site / reason-required values; give the lint-suppression marker a reason slot; retire `assume_deterministic` into `#Nondeterministic("…")`; update `jet inspect gates` and the spec.

cards.title: Principle: sigils mean ownership and outcomes; arithmetic uses words
cards.body:
Elegance principle hunt, 2026-10-01. Jet's sigils mostly carry ownership and outcome meanings: `^` take (614 uses in 265 files), `&` write (3,888 uses in 515 files), `~` copy, `?` success or present side, `!` failure or denial, `|` alternatives (D-MEM1, D-RESULT-DECON2, D-FAIL-CARRIER1, D-SHAPE-PIPE1). The same marks also do arithmetic: `^` power (13 uses in 2 files), and bitwise `&`, `|`, `~|`, and integer `!` (about 440 uses, mostly in about 30 crypto, archive, and math files).
