cards.title: Close Prelude admission and language-enum ownership
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Prelude policy and the safe additions; Contested prelude entries: files and random; Where the prelude lives; Marker argument types become real prelude enums; Name of the reserved namespace for the language's own declarations

**Decision IDs:** D-CORE-PRELUDE1, D-CORE-PRELUDE2, D-NAME-ALIAS1, D-RULEARG-TYPES1, D-LANGNS-NAME1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-CORE-PRELUDE1:** The seven criteria become law: measured frequency, total and safe, names never semantics, no better home, first-hour coverage, one fixed set, collision-conscious names. Shadowing lets the user win with a compiler warning.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Readable core.prelude source exists (Core/prelude/prelude.jet:1-15), but it declares a small set of scalar helpers (:17-49), not the complete ratified ambient alias inventory. Jet/Rust ambient names still have compiler registry ownership; the complete alias-opening, shadow warning, gated additions and NoPrelude behavior were not established.
- **D-CORE-PRELUDE2:** read_file, write_file, and file_exists join the prelude. Random stays in core.math.random.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Readable core.prelude source exists (Core/prelude/prelude.jet:1-15), but it declares a small set of scalar helpers (:17-49), not the complete ratified ambient alias inventory. Jet/Rust ambient names still have compiler registry ownership; the complete alias-opening, shadow warning, gated additions and NoPrelude behavior were not established.
- **D-LANGNS-NAME1:** The reserved namespace for language declarations is core.lang, including marker argument types and dimensions. D-EFFECT-ENUM1 later explicitly places Effect at core.compiler.lang.Effect; no general relocation ruling was found in the supplied corpus. Exclude Effect, explicitly relocated by D-EFFECT-ENUM1; resolve remaining enum locations without inventing a blanket supersession.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — Core/compiler/lang.jet:8-21,40-91 locates ABI/ArithmeticMode/FFILanguage/etc under core.compiler.lang, not the ratified core.lang. Jet Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1825 exports that namespace; Rust and Jet use the same source. D-EFFECT-ENUM1 approves only the later Effect location explicitly; a general namespace replacement could not be found.
- **D-NAME-ALIAS1:** Core ships one short prelude module: the ambient basics are declared there, and the rest are pub use aliases into the ratified Core tree. The compiler opens it for every file.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Readable core.prelude source exists (Core/prelude/prelude.jet:1-15), but it declares a small set of scalar helpers (:17-49), not the complete ratified ambient alias inventory. Jet/Rust ambient names still have compiler registry ownership; the complete alias-opening, shadow warning, gated additions and NoPrelude behavior were not established.
- **D-RULEARG-TYPES1:** The 14 marker argument menus become ordinary public enum declarations generated from the canonical registry, not hidden compiler-only type categories. The working core.lang location is subsequently nested under core.compiler.lang by the Core tree ruling.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Shared ordinary marker-argument enum declarations exist under core.compiler.lang (Core/compiler/lang.jet:8-130). However the chosen 14-menu registry-generation and every enum semantic/consumer contract were not proved in both compilers. The working namespace core.lang is not treated as a fixed-name contradiction: D-CORE-TREE1 subsequently nests it under compiler.


Effective-scope corrections:
D-RULEARG-TYPES1: Generate all fourteen ordinary public argument enums from their canonical menus. Resolve the source report's historical namespace sentence using its precedence register: core.lang for non-Effect declarations and core.compiler.lang.Effect only for Effect; do not invent blanket relocation.

All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

Also covers V40 (D-LANGNS-NAME1):
Decision IDs: D-LANGNS-NAME1

Active contract: The reserved namespace for language declarations is core.lang, including marker argument types and dimensions. D-EFFECT-ENUM1 later explicitly places Effect at core.compiler.lang.Effect; no general relocation ruling was found in the supplied corpus.

Gap evidence (static source witness, not a passing test): Core/compiler/lang.jet:8-21,40-91 locates ABI/ArithmeticMode/FFILanguage/etc under core.compiler.lang, not the ratified core.lang. Jet Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1825 exports that namespace; Rust and Jet use the same source. D-EFFECT-ENUM1 approves only the later Effect location explicitly; a general namespace replacement could not be found.

Coverage disposition: Same contract boundary is already assigned to P03.json; this amendment adds violation-specific regression evidence and criteria to that draft, not another implementation card.

All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Close checked text, schema and provenance boundaries
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Libraries declare their own checked text types; jet bind reads data schemas, not only language headers; Dependency provenance gets a read surface and a default posture; Who may declare a text block language

**Decision IDs:** D-BOUND-SINK1, D-BOUND-BIND1, D-BOUND-PROV1, D-META-DSL1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BOUND-BIND1:** jet bind json sample.json --type Repo writes bindings/repo.jet: an ordinary #Codable struct with the sample's hash in its header; Same verb for csv, sql DDL, xml, and proto; The file is committed and owned like any source; regeneration is explicit, and drift from a new sample shows as a normal diff; Gain: transcription errors die, and the FFI and data worlds share one verb; Loss: a generated file can go stale until someone reruns the command.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-BOUND-PROV1:** jet inspect provenance prints each dependency's chain: locked hash, transparency-log entry, publisher identity, build attestation — each line marked enforced, verified, or recorded; Integrity stays enforced always; Everything above it is verified and shown when present, and required only when the manifest's authority block says so; The same row is the refusal switch; Gain: the chain becomes readable today and enforceable per project; Loss: an unattested dependency still resolves by default.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production inspect seam exists at Source/main.rs:3389-3406; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-BOUND-SINK1:** A library declares a checked text head with a compile-time checker and hole encoder on the marker/text target mechanism. Users invoke Selector{"..."} with final dotless checked-head syntax, like the built-in checked SQL/URL heads; library ownership does not bypass checked-input refusal.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Marker text/block declaration rails exist in Rust parser and Jet Declarations/Markers.jet, but no source-owned user Selector text checker plus hole encoder/sink witness was established in either side. Builtin checked heads do not prove openness.
- **D-META-DSL1:** Libraries may define a text-block rule with Jet-owned block boundaries, handing the interior text to a checked library implementation. The grammar itself stays closed; the current declaration metadata uses $sites, not trailing on.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Parser/Items/states_protocols.rs:505-520 directly parses checked item templates. Jet Registration/UserTemplates.jet:1-6,165-184 expands parsed templates and re-registers items without relexing, but current marker-origin law/provider migration remains missing (derive selection :219-290); complete library text checking/encoding and rejection powers were not established.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Close ecosystem activation, secret graph and trust policy
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Shell auto-activation for jet env; Upstream build and install hook approval; New-release maturity default; Compose secret values from named inputs; Define secret metadata and activation rules; Trust model for the community package channel

**Decision IDs:** D-ENVHOOK1, D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1, D-JPK-FRESHNESS1, D-JPK-SECRETCOMPOSE1, D-JPK-SECRETMETA1, D-REGCURATE1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-ENVHOOK1:** jet env hook <shell> prints a hook the user adds to their shell config once; After that, entering a directory with env.jet activates it, and leaving deactivates; The first activation of an untrusted env uses the same trust prompt as the rest of Jet; JET_ENV_DISABLE turns it off anywhere.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production env seam exists at Source/main.rs:3947-3950; crates/jetpack/src/CLI/parse.rs:574-575; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-JPK-BUILDSCRIPT1:** Metadata probing never executes upstream code; unreviewed hooks are held, not run. Interactive `jet add` shows package identity, provider/source, script digest, and requested capabilities, and one confirmation drafts an exact `policy.trust` grant binding all four; any digest or capability change re-prompts with a diff of what changed.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust jetpack/CLI/realize.rs:551-554 gates Cargo upstream executable hooks on an externally approved exact source/recipe/capability identity. Jetpack CLI/Realize/RealizeRefs.jet:298-302 carries the matching approval seam. Complete all-provider build-hook identity and tamper/approval consumer evidence were not established, so no blanket sandbox certification.
- **D-JPK-FRESHNESS1:** New direct and transitive third-party versions wait 24 hours from first immutable inclusion in trusted monotonic signed registry/transparency metadata — never publisher, mirror, or local timestamps; existing exact locks and realized environments are untouched (D-JPK-OFFLINE1). Workspace policy may raise or lower the window per registry or source class; first-party and workspace-internal sources default to zero.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Source/Publish/Advisory.rs:865-868 checks all locked registry/git/foreign packages against the verified maturity feed, excluding only root/path packages. Equivalent Jet ecosystem maturity intersection and all overridden/host-policy boundary consumer evidence were not established.
- **D-JPK-SECRETCOMPOSE1:** Extend the environment secret declaration with a named template and its input names. Code still calls core.crypto.vault.get for DB_URL, so beginners get one named secret and experts can inspect the dependency list.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust jetpack/CLI/services_secrets_config.rs:18-100 and Jetpack CLI/Services/ServicesCommand.jet:46-123 enforce allowed environments, required secret presence, max-age rotation and named composition graph checking. Jetpack EnvModel/ModuleEval/SecretSpecs.jet:1-4 owns typed declarations. Complete per-profile defaults/generator schema and no-value-leak/read-time recomputation consumer proof were not established; these activation paths do not by themselves certify the vault boundary.
- **D-JPK-SECRETMETA1:** Make each secret a typed declaration in env source. Carry description, required or optional status, allowed environments, rotation policy, per-profile default, and generator recipe.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust jetpack/CLI/services_secrets_config.rs:18-100 and Jetpack CLI/Services/ServicesCommand.jet:46-123 enforce allowed environments, required secret presence, max-age rotation and named composition graph checking. Jetpack EnvModel/ModuleEval/SecretSpecs.jet:1-4 owns typed declarations. Complete per-profile defaults/generator schema and no-value-leak/read-time recomputation consumer proof were not established; these activation paths do not by themselves certify the vault boundary.
- **D-REGCURATE1:** One registry, two labeled tiers. The core tier is a small set with human review on top of every machine gate.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Source/Publish/Index.rs:39-43 stores core/community tier and gate status; Tier.rs:1 and :181-229 implements registry review receipt gates. Equivalent Jet registry producer/service admission and full machine-gate plus human-review consumer evidence were not established; ported package fetching is not server governance proof.

Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Close executable entry, debugger and job discovery surfaces
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Typed CLI entry becomes the canonical input recipe; Debugger diagnostics, exits, and recovery; VS Code and Zed debugger discovery and launch experience; Native debugger backends, provisioning, and supported hosts; Bare command entry precedence; Whether jet env lists integration checks as jobs

**Decision IDs:** D-CLI-RECIPE1, D-DBG-DIAG1, D-DBG-EDITOR1, D-DBG-NATIVE1, D-DX-ENTRY1, D-JOB-NAME2

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-CLI-RECIPE1:** Docs, first-contact examples, scaffolds, and dogfood show the #CLI entry for every fixed-shape program; The core.args builder stays as the expert floor for irregular or dynamic grammars; Raw process.argv() stays for true passthrough; The ratified flag-only rule for defaulted fields stands, so the parser has one binding rule and wrong invocations become teaching errors.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DBG-DIAG1:** Recommended; Assign one stable Jet code per recoverable debugger failure family, preserve NATIVE/AUTH ownership, translate one typed record across terminal/JSON/DAP/editors, and require proof-driven recovery; Users get direct fixes; automation gets stable classes and exits without parsing backend text; Timeout-read replay happens internally before any diagnostic; an emitted timeout is final and retryable=false; Acceptance proves exactly two total backend attempts after a timeout; A replay path that makes a third attempt fails the test.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production debug seam exists at Source/main.rs:4328-4331; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DBG-EDITOR1:** Recommended; Register Jet as a real zero-config debugger in VS Code with active-file/package discovery and expert launch/conditional-attach configuration; Disable Zed integration under API 0.7.0 until a pinned released trust/auth API can satisfy AUTH; do not promise parity through a broken button.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production debug seam exists at Source/main.rs:4328-4331; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DBG-NATIVE1:** Recommended; Linux uses locked upstream LLDB >=18.1.0, macOS uses Apple LLDB from Xcode CLT >=16.0, and Windows uses CDB from Windows Debugging Tools >=10.0.26100; Jetpack realizes or verifies each tool, Jet records exact identity, and A never searches or falls through to PATH. Every supported CI row executes real native sessions; This gives each host its maintained process/debug-info engine while preserving one Jet-facing debugger.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production debug seam exists at Source/main.rs:4328-4331; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DX-ENTRY1:** C keeps the shipped override order, adds one shallow inference path, and makes duplicate choices visible; It checks a non-empty role home, one matching root file, then one matching `src/` file; no deeper directory counts; If no override exists, written stock facts and canonical files choose the entry; A proposed `jet fix` writes one candidate into `package.jet`.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-JOB-NAME2:** The heading becomes `jobs` for the project's own entries, and environment checks get their own heading; Gain: a reader sees which entries they wrote and which the environment supplies; Loss: two headings to read, and any script reading the machine key must handle both.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production env seam exists at Source/main.rs:3947-3950; crates/jetpack/src/CLI/parse.rs:574-575; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Close loop, dispatch and return source laws
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** A search that finds nothing takes a written route; Multi-head functions: one coverage proof, and how far to unify; Body-first loops: add a `do` keyword or teach one shape; Compact act-on-error form for Result and Optional; May formatter rewrite branch shape?; Comprehension guard spelling in the loop head; One loop header shape carries two different meanings; Source-loop binding keyword: loop x in xs; Arrow loop bodies in statement position; Bindingless loops with an implicit subject; When does a function block return its final expression?

**Decision IDs:** D-CHOOSE-FIND1, D-CHOOSE-HEADS1, D-DO1, D-ERR-DECON1, D-BRANCH-FMT1, D-LOOP-GUARD1, D-LOOP-HEADER3, D-LOOP-IN1, D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1, D-LOOP-SUBJECT1, D-TAIL-RETURN1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BRANCH-FMT1:** Spaces, arrows, and indent settle; No If to table rewrite; Matches today.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production fmt seam exists at Source/main.rs:3604-3607; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-CHOOSE-FIND1:** A finite loop in value position may exit with `break v`, and the `??` route is required, not optional. The loop's type is the break value's type, and the written route answers exhaustion — so the reader never infers what running out means.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Both parsers recognize value loops; Jet Statements.jet:1109-1112 detects search payload and Expressions/Control.jet:294 keeps exhaustion route. Registered diagnostic exists, but port rejection of immediate ?? next/break and finite exhaustion semantics was not established.
- **D-CHOOSE-HEADS1:** Coverage and overlap of multi-heads are checked by the table's proofs: E0307 for a hole, the unreachable-arm lint for a shadowed head. One error copy instead of two.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Bundle.rs:118-121 lowers heads to one ordinary enum pattern table with common coverage. Jet Coverage.jet:294 has multi_head mode but complete head lowering/overlap parity was not established.
- **D-DO1:** Keep `loop` as the only loop word. The body-first loop is `loop { … if <stop> { break } }`.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Both control parsers keep loop and existing loop/break examples establish body-first iteration; foreign do/repeat/until diagnostics, safe rewrite and constant-true/unreachable lints on both sides were not established.
- **D-ERR-DECON1:** The `??` fallback block keeps its statements and its ambient `err`. Its last line becomes either a plain value or a real exit: `return`, `return expr`, `break`, `next`, or `panic(…)`.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust fallback real-exit lowering has current errors/qq_block_deconstruction.jet and qq_control.jet. Jet Parser/Expressions.jet:2007-2029 does not preserve all labeled break/continue/Panic carrier routes and treats every leading brace as a block. Common fallback works; complete exit/value contract is missing.
- **D-LOOP-GUARD1:** A source comprehension guard follows the source directly: loop x in xs if condition -> value. A comma before if is rejected, not read as a stride.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Syntax.rs:314-339 states the current source/guard/header laws. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:945-947,982-997 has in source bindings and rejects the three-slot counter; callable-tail parsing :264-268 distinguishes yielding arrows. Jet State.jet:320-339 accepts arbitrary TOKEN_IDENT while Rust Parser/mod.rs:1144-1174 rejects reserved in as a name; complete reserved-word and header/statement-expression distinctions are not equivalent.
- **D-LOOP-HEADER3:** The counter dissolves into data. Slot three accepts a whole number — today's every-Nth stride — or a step rule like `s => s * 2` that computes the next value from the current one, with a range giving the start and the stop bound.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Syntax.rs:314-339 states the current source/guard/header laws. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:945-947,982-997 has in source bindings and rejects the three-slot counter; callable-tail parsing :264-268 distinguishes yielding arrows. Jet State.jet:320-339 accepts arbitrary TOKEN_IDENT while Rust Parser/mod.rs:1144-1174 rejects reserved in as a name; complete reserved-word and header/statement-expression distinctions are not equivalent.
- **D-LOOP-IN1:** Source bindings use loop item in source, including loop (key, value) in source; commas separate only later clauses. Bare in is reserved, not a membership expression operator.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Syntax.rs:314-339 states the current source/guard/header laws. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:945-947,982-997 has in source bindings and rejects the three-slot counter; callable-tail parsing :264-268 distinguishes yielding arrows. Jet State.jet:320-339 accepts arbitrary TOKEN_IDENT while Rust Parser/mod.rs:1144-1174 rejects reserved in as a name; complete reserved-word and header/statement-expression distinctions are not equivalent.
- **D-LOOP-STMT-ARROW1:** Every loop-header kind permits a -> body in statement position, performing one statement per iteration. In expression position a finite yielding source loop still produces an eager List.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Syntax.rs:314-339 states the current source/guard/header laws. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:945-947,982-997 has in source bindings and rejects the three-slot counter; callable-tail parsing :264-268 distinguishes yielding arrows. Jet State.jet:320-339 accepts arbitrary TOKEN_IDENT while Rust Parser/mod.rs:1144-1174 rejects reserved in as a name; complete reserved-word and header/statement-expression distinctions are not equivalent.
- **D-LOOP-SUBJECT1:** A bindingless source loop gives each item an implicit subject; .member and .method(...) read that subject. Named scalar and tuple bindings keep their ordinary meaning.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Syntax.rs:314-339 states the current source/guard/header laws. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:945-947,982-997 has in source bindings and rejects the three-slot counter; callable-tail parsing :264-268 distinguishes yielding arrows. Jet State.jet:320-339 accepts arbitrary TOKEN_IDENT while Rust Parser/mod.rs:1144-1174 rejects reserved in as a name; complete reserved-word and header/statement-expression distinctions are not equivalent.
- **D-TAIL-RETURN1:** Every value-expected block yields its final unadorned expression, including functions, methods, lambdas and fallback/nested blocks. A statement tail yields unit; explicit return exits early, and explicit semicolons remain rejected by D-SEMI1.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust grammar tail representation is exercised by tests/grammar.rs:657-660 and tier corpus tests/tail_return_parity.rs. Jet Parser/Statements.jet:264-268 and Expressions.jet:1229-1232 preserve callable tails; complete nested/fallback expected-value semantics and lower/eval parity were not established.


Effective-scope corrections:
D-LOOP-HEADER3: Numeric every-Nth stride and a next-state callable over bounded range follow the current arrow spelling. Do not revive the historical => specimen.

All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Close matched measurement and scale acceptance
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Benchmarks are measured tests — one marker, one verb; keep(x): a benchmark sink the optimizer must respect; Where should Jet expose reproducible comparison between two implementations?; Megaproject scale canary: which program anchors it

**Decision IDs:** D-CLAIM-BENCH1, D-BENCH-KEEP1, D-TEST-COMPARE1, D-MEGAPROJ1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BENCH-KEEP1:** keep(x) is a tiny Prelude function that returns its argument and forces the optimizer to treat the value as used. It works anywhere: inside a measured region, in warm-up code, in every execution tier.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust shared Prelude jet_keep uses std::hint::black_box (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Keep.rs:3-4). Jet has Core/prelude/prelude.jet:15 and a keep route in Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/Prelude.jet:816-819, but the inspected checker also contains an erased-identity helper (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Core.jet:596-605); preservation of an optimizer-resistant use barrier through the new native backend was not established. Helper presence is not asserted to be a reachable contradiction.
- **D-CLAIM-BENCH1:** #Test with a .measure member replaces #Bench; plain jet test runs it once for correctness and jet test --measure does warmup/autoscaled optimized measurement with tier labels and typed budgets. Retired jet bench/#Bench teach the new spelling.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust measurement seam uses the test harness (Source/CmdDevTools.rs:9139-9141), and .measure vocabulary/retired bench rejection exist (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/math_layout.rs:813-815; crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1860-1862). Jet front door has retired bench metadata (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Registry.jet:37) but does not execute test (Front.jet:491-506); actual Jet-hosted measurement is missing.
- **D-MEGAPROJ1:** A real web product the owner uses every day: HTTP service, live board UI, persistence, validation, SSE updates. Exercises services, concurrency, web UI, and long-lived state — the shapes professional teams build.
  - **Gap witness:** NOT-IMPLEMENTED — The repository's Tower implementation remains Tools/tower/tower.mjs and Tools/tower/app/ui/tower.js; no Jet Tower shadow program, tower-jet build, or read-only snapshot parity witness was found by source/name search. The approved 20-50k-line Jet canary therefore is not present in the audited repository; no matching open card found.
- **D-TEST-COMPARE1:** Add comparison to the existing Core Testing API. Ordinary tests and foreign adapters share one contract.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Shared Core/testing/testing.jet:26 exposes compare<E> over cases and two callbacks. Its exact ordered-effect/typed-failure/replay/shrinking/outcome contract and a foreign-adapter consumer proof on Rust and Jet were not completely established.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

Core/, Docs/ and canonical Prelude/*.jet are shared inputs to the frozen reference: coordinate owner timing before editing them. Regenerate generated Compiler registries; never hand-edit DiagnosticRows.jet, CoreCallRows.jet or CoreSources.jet. Historical Rust file:line witnesses diagnose the gap; they do not authorize a Rust repair.
2. Implement only the missing consumer boundary identified by each cited gap witness, preserving working behavior; reuse the owning source, checker, registry and provider seam rather than introduce a parallel mechanism.
3. [D-BENCH-KEEP1] keep(x) is a tiny Prelude function that returns its argument and forces the optimizer to treat the value as used. 4. Retired jet bench/#Bench teach the new spelling. 5. [D-MEGAPROJ1] A real web product the owner uses every day: HTTP service, live board UI, persistence, validation, SSE updates. Exercises services, concurrency, web UI, and long-lived state — the shapes professional teams build. Owning evidence: NOT-IMPLEMENTED — The repository's Tower implementation remains Tools/tower/tower.mjs and Tools/tower/app/ui/tower.js; no Jet Tower shadow program, tower-jet build, or read-only snapshot parity witness was found by source/name search. The approved 20-50k-line Jet canary therefore is not present in the audited repository; no matching open card found.

Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Shared Core/testing/testing.jet:26 exposes compare<E> over cases and two callbacks. Its exact ordered-effect/typed-failure/replay/shrinking/outcome contract and a foreign-adapter consumer proof on Rust and Jet were not completely established.
7. Migrate every affected public caller, example, test and existing doc/changelog section in the same clean cutover. Coordinate overlapping scopes; P23 owns module names, P03 non-Effect enums, #3986 Effect, P12 marker generation, P19 diagnostic templates and P27 fact-query lifetime separation.
8. D-EXEC1 staging: finish stage zero and semantic/output parity on current engines first; unify the compiled runtime and shared low-level ABI/drop representation next; build Jet O0/O1 x86-64 then aarch64, require whole-example-corpus parity and O0 live function replacement, and only then retire Cranelift/MIREval/--interpret in one cutover. Frozen engine-specific work stays frozen until its step lands. Before retirement retain applicable current-engine proof; after retirement retarget durable tests to O0/O1/O2/web. No early engine deletion or declaration that a surviving old engine is itself a violation.
9. Deliver the named Jet-side tests/goldens and real consumer receipts in criteria. Main runs verification once on the integrated snapshot; performance/process requirements require their real receipts, not fabricated code.

cards.title: Close storage, hot migration and hardened memory guarantees
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Keep live state when a type changes; Where a bounded arena limit lives after memory keys leave #Policy; Shipping runtime checks for unsafe islands and foreign edges; Safe address-stable values; Worst-case stack and heap per entry point

**Decision IDs:** D-HOTSTATE1, D-AUTHORITY-MEM2, D-MEM-HARDEN1, D-PIN1, D-STACKBOUND1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-AUTHORITY-MEM2:** A memory denial may carry a bound: -[!Mem.Alloc(above: 65536)]> or the manifest equivalent. The bound is checked transitively and does not grant memory authority.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust Effects.rs:119 canonicalizes parameterized memory rows and uses bounded memory proof; Jet Effects/Checks.jet:1465-1479 parses signed Int bounds and its arena traversal skips unavailable node keys rather than failing closed (see parity/SemaOwnershipEffects.md E1/E5). Package memory-floor projection also remains incomplete relative to Rust. These are enforcement gaps, not only rendering differences.
- **D-HOTSTATE1:** Added fields use defaults and removed fields are dropped; migration blocks adapt renamed/changed types, otherwise dev restarts and names the blocking field.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust checked hot-swap facts carry canonical PublishedSchema migration plans for resident adapters (crates/jet-foundation/src/HotSwap.rs:89-93,130-139). Jet sema reconstructs canonical historical shapes and migration helper functions (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Migrations.jet:73-115), but Jet CLI refuses dev (JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506), so the live retention/restart consumer is unavailable there; complete Rust field adaptation/restart behavior was not established.
- **D-MEM-HARDEN1:** Use the existing named-profile selector on `jet build` and `jet test`. The built-in name turns on sentries for every `#Unsafe` operation and uses the existing all-foreign-dependency fence.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust unsafe/hardening code and tests/hardening.rs exist. Jet unsafe obligations have no equivalent sema inspector/discharger/stripper or runtime evidence producer located; Parser/Statements.jet:1447 only creates assertion syntax (parity/SemaOwnershipEffects.md U1). Whole-foreign fences, honest per-component guarantee levels and default-development/hardened instrumentation are not proved by that syntax.
- **D-PIN1:** mem.pin(&place) provides an address-stable tracked write view that prevents movement or replacement while live. D-MEMREF1 replaces historical Pin<T> spelling with the ordinary &!T! form; specialized field projection follows the current reference law.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL — Rust CheckerOwnership.rs:495-577 handles publication overlap and nested-pin/pin-arena exemptions. Jet Ownership/Checks.jet:916-961 only records view facts at this seam, so the same overlap/stability proof is missing. Existing borrow/split/read methods are not full proof of atomic pre-lending disjoint checks or pin movement barriers.

cards.title: Deliver checked development, review and receipt projections
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** Keep a review attached to its exact checked inputs; Debugging is a query over a recorded run; Claims leave receipts; ledgers render; Discovery by contract: jet find; #Todo is a typed goal; jet fill proposes candidates; Production runs leave receipts; Review as a product: meaning, authority, evidence; Refactors carry their meaning; One project truth surface; Witnesses: whose receipts count, and what CI is; How should ordinary editors reveal deeper reasoning about code?; When should Jet retain the reasons behind a checked claim?; Typed sections on the one receipt

**Decision IDs:** D-BIG-REVIEWORIGIN1, D-DEVR-CAUSE1, D-DEVR-CLAIM1, D-DEVR-FIND1, D-DEVR-HOLE1, D-DEVR-PROD1, D-DEVR-REVIEW1, D-DEVR-SEMID1, D-DEVR-STATUS1, D-DEVR-WITNESS1, D-EXPLAIN-VIEW1, D-EXPLANATION-RECORD1, D-FOUND-RECEIPT1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-BIG-REVIEWORIGIN1:** Add the concrete paired snapshot projection shown to proposed jet.review/v2; Each side has entry, known canonical input path/digest rows, optional existing claim_key, closure and optional proof_receipt; Do not duplicate the entry hash outside its input row or manufacture a claim key.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust emits paired snapshots under jet.review/v2 (Source/CmdReview.rs:2051-2055,2204-2213; tests/review.rs:1053-1057). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-CAUSE1:** Any recorded run — local, test, or crash receipt — answers `why <expr>` (the backward slice of writes and decisions that produced a value) and `when <place>` (the write timeline). This is a named amendment: `when` sits inside the per-variable-history territory D-TIMETRAVEL1=C deferred to Epoch 6 and D-RUN-RECORD1=A re-affirmed as deferred; Option A pulls the query surface over existing recordings forward; reverse-step execution and the standalone always-on history engine stay on the Epoch 6 schedule.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production debug seam exists at Source/main.rs:4328-4331; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-CLAIM1:** Test runs, golden blessings, budget baselines, API snapshots, and schema snapshots become receipt kinds in one store; The parity ledger and the feature manifest become rendered views, byte-compared in CI like llms.text; A hand-written second copy fails the guard.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production inspect seam exists at Source/main.rs:3389-3406; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-FIND1:** `jet find "String -> Path"` unifies against every visible signature; `--effect FS.Read` filters by the typed effect rows; `--example '"a,b" -> ["a","b"]'` runs pure candidates at comptime against the example and returns the ones that reproduce it; One read-only verb, human and `--json` output.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production find seam exists at Source/main.rs:3777-3779; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-HOLE1:** `jet check` prints a goal card per `#Todo`: expected type, allowed effects, in-scope values; Goal cards are advisory rows: the exit code never changes, they summarize past a handful, and a project switch silences them; `jet fill` proposes ranked candidates found by signature search over the prelude and deps; every candidate already passes checking before it is shown; Runtime behavior is untouched — programs with goals still run and stop on reach.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production fill seam exists at Source/main.rs:3440; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-PROD1:** A crashing release binary writes a crash receipt: the report frame, the closure digest, and a replay capture; `jet report --attach` ships it in the support bundle; Long-running services may opt into periodic observed-run receipts; Everything stays on the machine unless the operator ships it, and a project can refuse recording entirely with one typed setting.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust prepares shared redacted receipt context (Source/ProductionReceipt.rs:1-3; CmdCompile.rs:3657-3660,4915-4917); no end-to-end release-crash replay/observed service proof was established. Jet CLI does not run programs (Front.jet:491-506).
- **D-DEVR-REVIEW1:** One verdict over a base ref: meaning (semantic diff with blast radius), authority (gate and effect delta), claims (receipt diff: new, stale, held). Human-readable screen and one JSON object; Works project-wide, not per file.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production review seam exists at Source/main.rs:3456-3457; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-SEMID1:** Every toolchain-executed refactor (jet fix, codemod plan, LSP rename) records its semantic op beside the text change; Diff, merge, review, and blame consume ops plus stable definition IDs: a rename renders as one line, merges clean against body edits, and blame follows the definition; Hand edits stay plain text forever; every surface keeps a --text view.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production inspect seam exists at Source/main.rs:3389-3406; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-STATUS1:** One daily-frequency verb, no arguments, one screen: the closure, then each claim family with its grade, freshness, and receipt; Never runs work; only reads; `--json` emits one machine line per row.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production status seam exists at Source/main.rs:3420-3422; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-DEVR-WITNESS1:** Every receipt names and signs its witness; `jet verify --cold` replays every act from the lock with no reuse and countersigns — that command is CI, on any machine you choose; Receipts share over existing cache bindings; acceptance is trust policy; the default is local-only.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-EXPLAIN-VIEW1:** Show a concise source hint and open details on demand; Source stays readable by default; Experts can pin the complete relationship view; Text and keyboard routes preserve the same evidence.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production inspect seam exists at Source/main.rs:3389-3406; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-EXPLANATION-RECORD1:** Retain compact reason links with existing evidence; Every consumer uses the same checked reason; Old claims retain inspectable source-bound premises; Retained reason links occupy storage.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: production inspect seam exists at Source/main.rs:3389-3406; its complete decision contract was not established by this static read (dispatch is not semantic proof). Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-FOUND-RECEIPT1:** A #Receipt record attaches as a named typed section of the program's existing receipt; status, compare and diff read it without changing identity or fixed fields.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust stores normalized typed sections and exposes query/diff projection (Source/ReceiptStore.rs:6-18,130-136; Source/ReceiptSections.rs:174-177 identifies checked receipt.attach schema digests). Jet declaration registration exists (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet:1802-1803), but the Jet CLI cannot execute status/compare/diff/recorded runs (JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); end-to-end attachment and reading on the Jet-hosted product path remains unestablished.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

cards.title: Deliver honest web application serving and native run admission
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** web.app must serve, or stop claiming full-stack; What jet run does with a web-targeted program on the native tier

**Decision IDs:** D-WEBAPP-SERVE1, D-WEBRUN1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-WEBAPP-SERVE1:** Matches the existing jet dev convention; When the entry builds a web.app and the file defines no fn dev(), jet dev serves the graph on a local port with live reload and prints the address. jet run serves the same graph without dev extras — for a server app the running server IS the program, which is also the deployment path. fn dev() and an explicit app.serve(port) remain the expert overrides.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.
- **D-WEBRUN1:** Native jet run on web-targeted source stops with a registered error naming the target and the two real paths: jet dev for the live loop, or jet build --target=web; Nothing silently executes against a null backend; Dual-target programs keep native runs by declaring a native target explicitly.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust: full ruled behavior could not be established; source search and checked front-door inventory are not an executed feature receipt. Jet port: the executable front door dispatches only help, explain, check and build (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:491-506); this decision's command path is refused by jet_cli_not_ported at :94-102, not implemented by its help/registry row.

Source/Publish/Tier.rs is the registry-side gate. Equivalent Jet registry publish enforcement and a consumer proof for all confusable/tier cases were not established; Compiler/ alone does not implement a registry service.

Registration/metadata ownership is implemented, single text-home ownership is not. No open card specifically plans eliminating the second emitter-text home; #4019 repairs registry placeholder wording but does not name this cutover.

cards.title: Finish one-operation Core naming and caller cutover
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** One name per Core operation; foreign names are taught, never aliased; One English spelling for Core names; What list remove takes: a position or a value; The print family: which spellings survive; One verb per job in Core collections; Variadic newline print

**Decision IDs:** D-CORE-ONE-NAME1, D-CORE-SPELLING1, D-LISTREMOVE1, D-ONCE-PRINT1, D-ONCE-VERB1, D-VERDICT-1321-1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-CORE-ONE-NAME1:** Core retains one canonical callable name; compatibility aliases such as loads are deleted. Removed foreign spellings produce registered teaching errors naming the Jet operation.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — Core/encoding/json.jet:92,95 still exports callable loads/load aliases; shared Core registry admits them. Jet reactive API also keeps computed/derived twins (Calls/ReactiveHandles.jet:221). These are executable aliases, not teaching errors.
- **D-CORE-SPELLING1:** Core public names use American spelling, including meters/kilometers; British spellings such as metres are teaching errors that name the canonical Jet operation. User identifiers are not policed by this rule.
  - **Gap witness:** CONTRADICTED — Core/units/units.jet:74-75,92-94 deliberately preserves callable metres/kilometres aliases and METRE. Shared Core admission still exposes those names rather than the ratified American-spelling teaching errors in the Rust reference and Jet port.
- **D-LISTREMOVE1:** `remove(x)` deletes the first item equal to `x`, because that is what most code does. `remove(i, .Slot)` deletes a slot instead. `remove(x, .Val)` says the default out loud when a reader needs it. The short call stays short, the rare case names itself, and a Python author is right by default.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Jet shared collection registry distinguishes ListRemove/MapMerge and mutation laws (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:148-150,233-234), and codegen selects RemoveList mode (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:496). Existing consumer collection iterator tools documents remove-as-value (Examples/features/collections/iter_tools.jet:27-31); exact value/Slot/Val overloads, pop/replace/add and every retired verb/constructor cutover in Rust and Jet were not completely established.
- **D-ONCE-PRINT1:** Keep newline-ending ambient print and its no-prelude twin; retire println/sprint/repr, using interpolation/repr selectors instead. D-CORE-IO-BUF1 places the former io.print owner under core.term and removes core.io.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust consumer migration test checks the three retired print-family spellings (tests/cli_parts/runtime.rs:99-101), and Jet handles ambient printing (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Direct.jet). Complete variadic newline behavior, canonical no-prelude twin after core.io retirement and removal of every legacy public alias in the Jet port were not established.
- **D-ONCE-VERB1:** One table fixes the family. The verb pop means remove-and-return on every collection, matching the verb beginners arrive knowing.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Jet shared collection registry distinguishes ListRemove/MapMerge and mutation laws (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:148-150,233-234), and codegen selects RemoveList mode (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:496). Existing consumer collection iterator tools documents remove-as-value (Examples/features/collections/iter_tools.jet:27-31); exact value/Slot/Val overloads, pop/replace/add and every retired verb/constructor cutover in Rust and Jet were not completely established.
- **D-VERDICT-1321-1:** print is variadic and newline-ending. D-ONCE-PRINT1 keeps ambient print plus its no-prelude twin, and retires println/sprint/repr aliases.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust consumer migration test checks the three retired print-family spellings (tests/cli_parts/runtime.rs:99-101), and Jet handles ambient printing (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Direct.jet). Complete variadic newline behavior, canonical no-prelude twin after core.io retirement and removal of every legacy public alias in the Jet port were not established.

cards.title: Finish remaining source and error-value cutovers
cards.body:
Ratified contract scope; no new ballot or default is authorized.


**Scope:** The default error is a real value — its name and constructor

**Decision IDs:** D-FAIL-ERROR1

**Acceptance criteria / missing boundary:**

- **D-FAIL-ERROR1:** `Err("msg")` builds the default error — the line beginners already write becomes the constructor, with nothing new to learn. Labels add the rest: `Err("msg", code: "CFG404")` and `Err("msg", cause: e)`.
  - **Gap witness:** PARTIAL: Rust shared JetErr stores message/code/cause (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/PortableAlloc.rs:550-553), while Jet default error conversion recognizes the Core error family (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/FailureLaw.jet:37-45). Exact labeled Err constructor/default-domain/field behavior and source-owned counterpart on both compilers were not completely established.


Effective-scope corrections:


All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.
cards.plan:
1. Rust freeze: do not change Source/, crates/ Rust implementations or add Rust tests. Implement in the Jet compiler, Jet-hosted tooling and owning Jet packages. Core/, Docs/ and canonical Prelude/*.jet are shared inputs to the frozen reference: coordinate owner timing before editing them. Regenerate generated Compiler registries; never hand-edit DiagnosticRows.jet, CoreCallRows.jet or CoreSources.jet. Historical Rust file:line witnesses diagnose the gap; they do not authorize a Rust repair.
2. Implement only the missing consumer boundary identified by each cited gap witness, preserving working behavior; reuse the owning source, checker, registry and provider seam rather than introduce a parallel mechanism.
3. [D-FAIL-ERROR1] `Err("msg")` builds the default error — the line beginners already write becomes the constructor, with nothing new to learn. Labels add the rest: `Err("msg", code: "CFG404")` and `Err("msg", cause: e)`. Owning evidence: PARTIAL: Rust shared JetErr stores message/code/cause (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/PortableAlloc.rs:550-553), while Jet default error conversion recognizes the Core error family (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/FailureLaw.jet:37-45). Exact labeled Err constructor/default-domain/field behavior and source-owned counterpart on both compilers were not completely established.
4. Migrate every affected public caller, example, test and existing doc/changelog section in the same clean cutover. Coordinate overlapping scopes; P23 owns module names, P03 non-Effect enums, #3986 Effect, P12 marker generation, P19 diagnostic templates and P27 fact-query lifetime separation.
5. D-EXEC1 staging: finish stage zero and semantic/output parity on current engines first; unify the compiled runtime and shared low-level ABI/drop representation next; build Jet O0/O1 x86-64 then aarch64, require whole-example-corpus parity and O0 live function replacement, and only then retire Cranelift/MIREval/--interpret in one cutover. Frozen engine-specific work stays frozen until its step lands. Before retirement retain applicable current-engine proof; after retirement retarget durable tests to O0/O1/O2/web. No early engine deletion or declaration that a surviving old engine is itself a violation.
6. Deliver the named Jet-side tests/goldens and real consumer receipts in criteria. Main runs verification once on the integrated snapshot; performance/process requirements require their real receipts, not fabricated code.

**Decision IDs:** D-FANOUT3

cards.title: Emitted Rust fails to compile (E0308 &str vs &String) when a borrowed .trim() result is passed to a String parameter
cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 by the CLI port (PortW2-CLI-16, via PortLead-2) on the night release jet (Rust emitter). Repro: Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Authority.jet:88 `trimmed :: right.trim()` followed by `authority_parse_root(trimmed)` where the parameter is a read String. The generated Rust passes a &str where &String is expected (rustc E0308), which is an internal compiler error under I2 (rustc must never reject emitted code). Root: the trim route returns a borrowed str view carrier while the read String parameter ABI expects &String; the emitter needs one canonical adapter (owned conversion or &str parameter ABI) for borrowed text results flowing into String parameters. Fix in both emitters (MIRRust.rs and Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit), add a golden with trim/split/slice results passed to String parameters. Details: history://PortW2-CLI-16 (unit.rs:207085).

cards.title: Closures capturing a mutable loop-local share one cell across iterations (both compilers)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 (S2 fix spec Semantics-Ownership §6, confirmed by S2Lead-3 on the night release jet): three closures each capturing a mutable `:=` local declared inside a loop body print 4,5,6,7,8,9 instead of 2,3,4,3,4,5, because every iteration shares one captured cell. Root: neither MIR carries a declaration-lifetime event; Rust MIRRust::emit_slots allocates one Rc per MirLocal at function entry and the Jet emitter mirrors that. Fix design (S2Lead-3 option A): a MIR StorageLive{local} op emitted by bind_local for mutable locals declared inside a loop body; shared-capture slots become reassignable and StorageLive allocates a fresh cell; no-op arms in every other MIR consumer (optimizer place-use/inline, digest, evaluator, native backend). Deferred until after stage 2 to avoid wide Rust churn during the bootstrap (decision by Pip); then implement in the Jet compiler with the Rust tandem as required. Golden: Examples/features/callable/s2_loop_mutable_captures (parked outside the active corpus by S2Lead-2).

cards.title: Compile cost: hello must build and run faster and smaller than C, Rust, Go, Zig and Odin
cards.body: Evidence: Docs/audits/compile-cost-hello-2026-10-02.md (measured today; harness Tools/perf/hello-compile/). Jet loses every hello cell: jet build 7.0 s cold / 1.3 s warm, 179 MB, 58.8 MB binary, 7.9 ms start-up; jet build --release 41 s cold, 2.4 GB; the Jet-written compiler jetc0 64.6 s and 11.6 GB for hello (18 s and 11 GB of it restoring the embedded compiler image), versus gcc 0.12 s / 35 MB / 14 KB / 0.36 ms. Root causes (audit section 'Root causes'): whole compiler-image restore for header facts; JetInt hot paths not inlined; copy-on-every-read codegen; fixed 6.3 MB runtime prefix per program; runtime compiled per profile instead of shipped prebuilt.
cards.plan: 1. Restore only the compiler-image header; decode the full image lazily where used (in progress: ImageLazy). 2. Inline JetInt small-integer clone/drop/compare; native integers where the checker proves the range. 3. Remove remaining inspection-only copies (constants, indexed reads, projections, whole-program AST rebuilds). 4. Prune the runtime prefix to reachable code; tables as binary data (Runtime-Prefix-Plan). 5. Ship the shared runtime prebuilt (D-EXEC1) and generate code with the Jet backend. After each step re-run Tools/perf/hello-compile/bench.py and log the numbers here.

questions.text: what are the downsides of the recommended option/a?
questions.answer:
A keeps your one-String design, but “no remaining downside” is too strong.

[INFERENCE] The biggest issue is earlier visible output. A explicitly allows large output to escape its buffer before formatting finishes. If a later calculation stops the program—or a loop never finishes—the destination can contain a prefix where today no outer output would have started. This matters most for long records/files. It also needs protection against changed argument/output ordering and interleaved concurrent prints. A’s exclusion of input/output actions does not exclude calculation failures or endless loops. Buffering small output mitigates this, but does not remove it. Partial output from an actual failed physical write already exists; that is not a new downside.

[INFERENCE] Performance is not automatically better. Tiny strings, many small pieces, indirect function calls, and saved strings can pay extra destination-selection/buffering costs. Existing concatenation can reserve exact space; A forbids formatting twice to calculate length. Buffering prevents repeated physical writes, not every extra instruction or storage cost. These risks affect performance-sensitive code and need measurements, not assurances.

The allocation guarantee also has boundaries: saving a value, inspecting/replacing the builder, effectful formatting, input/destination overlap, and large padded holes still need stored text. Ordinary code remains legal; only people pursuing allocation-free output must learn those rules. A already prevents double formatting and preserves stored-string getters.

[INFERENCE] Compiler/library work is substantial: shared formatting, interpolation, output adapters, separately compiled functions, function-value/trait entries, debugger views, and parity across AOT, JIT, interpreter and web. Existing Display methods, callers and examples need no signature migration; implementation tests and documentation do. Caller-handled print errors are unfinished today and shared by all options. Display/Debug, redaction and existing formatting rules must remain unchanged.

A therefore does not yet meet the bar. Smallest repair: retain ordinary result-building whenever completion/output ordering cannot be preserved, explicitly narrowing guaranteed streaming; require paired performance and all-tier evidence before claiming no practical downside.

cards.title: Generated codec decoders are huge: 154 decode bodies are 15.9 MB of jetc0's 158 MB Rust (TExprKind.decode alone 2.5 MB)
cards.body: Sol scan of jetc0's emitted Rust (2026-10-02, ~/.cache/jet-luna/sol/rusthot/05-matches-carriers-bloat.md): 154 generated decode bodies account for 15.9 MB; the largest, TExprKind.decode, is 2,501,158 bytes, 48,748 lines and 13,806 MIR value slots in one function. Fix: generate table-driven or per-variant out-of-line decoders (one small function per variant, shared field readers) in both codegen paths, keep the byte format identical, and measure emitted size and build time before and after. Related: 228 Box<Vec<T>> declarations created by recursive-layout analysis traversing already-indirect List/Map edges (unnecessary double indirection).

cards.title: Structural: superlinear compile work fails a scaling gate instead of being found one hotspot at a time
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-02: superlinear compile work must be prevented structurally rather than found one hotspot at a time. Evidence (sol/rusthot/03-superlinear-loops.md): 118 linear catalog lookups inside loops, at least 118 quadratic string-building sites, 76 list-membership tests in loops, and growing map buckets copied on append, on top of the roughly 18 scaling items ScaleLead found one by one.

Work: (1) A scaling gate: a deterministic generator emits synthetic Jet programs at N, 2N and 4N (functions, declarations, expression depth, module count, match arms, string sizes); each compiler phase reports deterministic work counters (visits, lookups, allocations, bytes copied) and peak memory; the gate fails when any counter grows more than about 2.2x per doubling. It runs on every compiler build (both compilers while the Rust exists) and inside the performance gate (#4308). (2) Data-structure law for the compiler: catalogs and indexes are maps or arrays keyed by U64 IDs, membership uses sets, strings are built with one builder, and `s = s + x` with `s` at its last use appends in place under the copy-fact law. (3) Expert override: an intentionally superlinear function (for example a bounded small-N search) carries a gate exemption row naming the reason and the bound, reviewed like an #Unsafe audit.

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #4551; criteria carried there as [#4319]. Compile-cost gate: scaling (N/2N/4N) per phase. Triage evidence: Tools/perf/scaling/harness.mjs:12-20 defines axes/limits and :30-52 parses phase counters; default match-arm ladder still48, required universal compiler-build gate unproved.

Absorbs #4147 (merge): Keep #4319; carry #4147 audit findings, N/2N/4N/8N histories/nested-closure/generic/huge-program axes and release guard into it. Evidence: #4319 deterministic work-counter scaling gate and data-structure law; #4147 scaling audit log

jetc vs Rust benchmark (SolJetcBench, 2026-10-02, generated functions axis): Rust emit 0.12 s / 0.19 s at 256 / 512 functions; jetc0 19.8 s / 58.1 s (165x / 306x). jetc has a ~7 s fixed floor (empty program 8.0 s, 5.3 GB); its marginal cost grows 12.8 s -> 51 s per doubling (4x): quadratic in function count in the Jet compiler, linear in the Rust reference. Profiling the culprit now. Also jetc rejects a time example the Rust reference accepts (52 reports, ~/.cache/jet-luna/sol/jetc-bench/divergence-time.md).

Same class found and fixed in the native backend (BackendLead-3, 2026-10-02): Compiler/JetBackend X64/RegAlloc.jet x64_liveness kept blocks x values [[Bool]] matrices read as live_in[succ][value] per value; replaced with sparse per-block value lists plus epoch marks. The iter fixture went from an OOM kill at 5 GB to lowering, compiling and running (3.6 GB peak, the unit type-check itself). Native-backend worktree; integrates after stage 1.

Gate update (SolScaleGate): harness now gates baseline-subtracted marginal ratios (medians of 3; non-positive marginals fail closed as unmeasurable); default ladders functions/declarations/interpolation/fan-in/generics 256/512/1024, modules 64/128/256, depth 16/32/64, match arms 48/96/192 (E1403, #4327), strings 1/2/4 MiB; node --test 4/4. Night12 results (receipt ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/sol/SolScaleGate/prebuilt-marginal-combined.json): modules quadratic (Rust only, #4330); declarations superlinear: check wall 2.48x/2.55x, RSS 3.76x/2.62x per doubling, build RSS 3.22x/2.60x; other axes mostly noise at these sizes (single-digit milliseconds of marginal cost), so the gate needs the deterministic phase counters (JET_PHASE_COUNTERS) to be decisive. Fix spec for the module axis: Tools/perf/scaling/trait-facts-fix.json.

Marginal-cost sweep (SolScaleGate, night12, receipt ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/sol/SolScaleGate/prebuilt-marginal-large.json): module count is quadratic: marginal wall time grows 4.13x then 4.09x, CPU 3.87x then 4.09x, and peak RSS 8.64x then 4.49x per doubling (64/128/256 modules), in jet check. Allocation sites being traced with heaptrack. Other axes show no measurable superlinear growth at these sizes.

Scaling gate first cut (SolScaleGate): Tools/perf/scaling/{generate.mjs,harness.mjs,scaling.test.mjs,README.md}; nine axes (functions, declarations, depth, modules, match arms, string literals, interpolation, fan-in, generics), 2.2x gate, exemption table with reason and bound; node --test passes (4). First measurement on night12 at N=32/64/128: module count fails: peak RSS grows 3.2x per doubling (64 to 128 files) for both check and build; all other axes stayed under 2.2x, but fixed start-up time hides growth at these sizes, so the gate is moving to marginal cost and a larger ladder. Root cause of the module-axis memory growth is being traced.

cards.title: Structural: releasing plain memory after last use is one step, not a per-node destructor walk; no teardown at exit
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-02: once a value's last use has happened, its memory should just be released, not cleaned up piece by piece. Evidence: in the stage-1 self-compile profile, about 25% of all CPU time is in the allocator's free path (_int_free_chunk), almost all of it drop glue walking Vec<Expr> and Box<Vec<...>> trees node by node (stage1/run-loop5b/selfcheck/compile.log.cg+2791s.txt).

Law: dropping plain memory is O(1) at the point of last use. (1) Values whose memory is plain data (no resource, Close or consume duty, no #Scrub tag) do not run a per-node destructor walk: trees and lists of plain data are allocated from a region owned by their root (or the phase), and releasing the root releases the region in one step. (2) At process exit the program does not tear down plain memory at all; only resources with duties (files, locks, connections, flush and commit protocols) still close, in their ratified order (S63/D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1). (3) #Scrub-tagged data keeps its zeroing, because that is its contract. (4) Last-use analysis (D-COPY-DEFAULT1 moves) decides when the release happens; no extra marks for users. Applies to the compiler's own data first (phase arenas for AST, TIR, MIR and image data, released at phase end), then to generated user programs through the shared runtime, both compilers while the Rust exists, and the native backend. Proof: the same profile shows the free path below 2%, and the paired performance cell beats the per-node drop it replaces.

Triage evidence: MIRRust.rs:5078-5081 still boxes recursive edges; Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet and shared runtime still emit ordinary owned aggregates.

Absorbs #4177 (merge): Keep #4320; carry #4177 immediate-after-read release, RSS measurement, full golden parity and Close/single-use/task/file ordering exclusions. Evidence: #4320 plain-memory regions released at last use; Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/LastUse.jet:144-157

Design: ~/.cache/jet-luna/structural/DROP-REGIONS.md (SolDropDesign, 2026-10-02). Profiles: free path 18-28% inclusive after lexing; top release sites Vec<Expr> under Box<Vec<Expr>> 11%, Box<Expr> 1.9%, Box<Result<Expr,..>> 1.9%, Vec<SwitchArm> 1.7%, String 1%. Much of it frees hidden clones, so implementation is sequenced after #4318 lands and the profile is retaken; the first step is terminal-request no-teardown in Compiler/Bootstrap/Tests.rs (not batch mode), then a Plain class with request regions in both emitters.

Owner clarification 2026-10-02: the owner's point was narrower: freed memory needs no wiping, because the next owner initializes it. Checked the runtime: Jet already never zeroes freed memory; the only wipes are the crypto secret types (jet_crypto_zeroize, D-CRYPTO-RNG1 and D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1), where wiping is the contract. This card's remaining scope is Pip's own performance finding (25% of self-compile CPU in per-node free walks), not an owner direction.

cards.title: Tail-position match leaks the function's return type into its scrutinee (E0311 on a valid call chain)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 by JetpackLead-2 (night12). In a function whose return is `Bool Never!`, a tail-position `if <expr> == { ... }` match takes the function's return type as the expected type of its scrutinee: `fn f(t: String) -[Exec, Time.Wait]> Bool Never! { if process.cmd([String]{t}).run() == { .Ok(r) -> r.success  .Err(_) -> false } }` reports E0311 "`run` isn't a method on this value: this `ProcessSpec Never!` value...". Binding the same match first (`ok :: if ... ; ok`) passes. Repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/JetpackLead-2/probe/main.jet. The expected type must flow to the match result (its arms), never into the scrutinee. Fix in both compilers; UI snapshot for the real E0311 and a golden for the tail match.

cards.title: A flat match with 256 arms counts as 257 nesting levels (E1403)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 by the scaling gate (SolScaleGate, Tools/perf/scaling): a single match whose 256 arms are siblings fails with E1403 '257 nesting levels exceeds the limit of 256' on night12. Arms of one match are not nested; the nesting counter (or the parser/AST shape, e.g. arms folded into a right-nested chain) treats each arm as a level. That also implies recursion depth proportional to arm count in later passes (stack risk for large generated matches such as codec decoders). Fix the representation or the counter in both compilers so sibling arms add no depth; scaling-gate axis 'match-arms' at 1024 arms must pass.

cards.title: Rust reference: per-module copies of the whole auto-derive trait union make checking quadratic in module count
cards.body: Root cause of the scaling gate's quadratic module axis (#4319; SolScaleGate heaptrack, 2026-10-02), Rust reference only: crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs:341-365 (TraitRegistry merge_auto_derives / bundle_auto_derives) publishes every registry's synthetic builtin names under each module's nominal identity and clones the union into every module; Names.rs:433-435 nominal_identity qualifies arbitrary names, so empty modules fabricate builtin identities; Traits.rs:369-378 clones six HashSet<String>s and CheckInner.rs:1630-1634 copies them again into every ModuleState. From 64 to 128 modules the two leading HashSet allocation sites each grow 26.6 MB to 105.7 MB and the paired string clones 14.3 MB to 57.0 MB (about 4x). The Jet compiler does not have this pattern (Registration/TypeMetadata.jet:108-126, Derives.jet:1705-1786, Items.jet:492-517 and 1995-2006 build from actual declarations and inject builtins once). Fix (Rust, matching the Jet structure): publish only actual local nominal declarations; keep canonical trait facts once per bundle, shared; keep only local facts per module. Proof: the scaling gate's module axis under 2.2x per doubling.

cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 by BallotRev4 on night12 through laneS: `fmt.decimal(Float{1.5}, 1)` exits 139 (segmentation fault), and so does a division followed by fmt.decimal. A safe-code crash is an I1 violation. Also on night12, `fmt.bytes(1500000)` prints `1.430511474609375 MiB`: binary units with no rounding, against the ratified D-HUMANFMT1 decimal contract (ballot D-FMT-BYTES1 pending for the binary companion). Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/sol/BallotRev4/. Rounding law (Main, applying D-FMT-BYTES1's exact wide-Int requirement; recorded for owner visibility): scaled values under 10 use exact decimal round-half-to-even on the rational value (Int div/rem), so 1250 B -> 1.2 kB, 1150 B -> 1.2 kB, 1050 B -> 1.0 kB; values of 10 and above round half away from zero on the exact rational (matching the frozen f64 round for representable ties). The frozen Rust Fmt.rs:317-333 uses f64 {:.1} below 10 and so differs at 1150 (1.1) and 1050 (1.1): the Rust moves to the exact law in the tandem batch.
