cards.title: Six active diagnostics can never be the primary report: an earlier, more generic check always fires first
cards.body:
Found 2026-10-02 by CW2-UI-C (CardLead-2 batch, night12 release jet via laneS) while writing UI fixtures for #4260. For each code below, the audit trigger recipe (~/.cache/jet-luna/sol/review/Diagnostics-I4.md, section "Every registered code without a UI/report snapshot") reaches the intended mistake, but a broader check reports first, so the specific registered row is never the primary diagnostic and no UI snapshot can show it. For each row decide: either the specific check is a defect (it must run before, or replace, the generic one, so the user sees the precise teaching), or the row is dead and must be removed from the registry in one cutover (greenfield, no dead active rows).
- E0342 (`#Off`/`#DebugOnly` written on an item) and E0343 (in expression position): the generic marker wrong-site gate reports E0355 (`#Off` cannot attach at the Function/Expression site) first; crates/jet-parser primary.rs:73-84 returns before the E0343 branch at :105-111. Note D-OFF-RELEASE1 (#4298) also retires #DebugOnly.
- E0345 (`#Meta` unknown field): typed marker-signature validation reports E0930 (`#Meta` arguments do not match `Meta(category:, tunable:, maturity:)`) before the field check in bindings.rs:1210.
- E1404 (devtools publication needs explicit field/value labels): `devtools.publish(.count, 1)` reports E0769 (`field` is a label-only parameter of `publish`) from the call binder (core_call.rs:3097-3103) before the publication gate at :3116.
- E1410 (devtools panel identity registered twice): a doubled `#DevPanel` reports E0999 (marker already applied) as primary; two `panel` functions report E0105 (defined twice) as primary; E1410 appears only as a secondary report. Cross-module panels never collide because identities include the module path (AST/devtools.rs:105-108).
- L0527 (expression value is discarded): the ordinary discarded-expression program is rejected by the parser with E0003 (control.rs:3068-3117) before the sema lint; loop_lints.rs:131-139 excludes normal calls and lost tails, so no reachable program yields L0527.

Repro:  the probes in CW2-UI-C's report (cleaned scratch; one-liners reproduced from Diagnostics-I4.md recipes for these codes).

Title: `if f() == .Ok(v)` is rejected as unhandled (E0403/E2402) although spec.md:790-791 makes the pattern test a handler
Kind: bug · Track: sidequest · Priority: P2 · Tags: failure-law, I9
Body: Found 2026-10-03 (CW3-DSL). Repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CW3-DSL/single_pattern.jet: `fn optional_number(t: String) -> Int? { if Int.parse(t) == .Ok(v) -> return Val(v); return None }` and `fn is_number(t: String) -> Bool { if Int.parse(t) == .Ok(_) -> return true; return false }`. `P.sh check` -> E0403 at :2:12 ("This fallible call only works inside a function that returns a fallible result"), E0107 at :2:45 (`v` unbound), E2402 at :7:12 ("can't convert ParseError into Err"). spec.md:790-791 says `.Ok(value)` in a pattern test matches the success side (example `result == .Ok(n)`), and spec.md:2333-2334 lists "a pattern test" beside `??` as a way to handle a fallible call. The full two-arm match `if Int.parse(t) == { .Ok(v) -> … .Err(_) -> … }` is accepted (Examples/features/text/hex_decode_policy.jet:8-21), so only the single-pattern form is refused, and it does not bind `v`.
Criteria:
1. The repro checks clean and prints 2 / false; `v` is bound in the true branch.
2. Both checkers agree; a UI or golden fixture covers the single-pattern handling form.
3. If the law changes instead (single-pattern tests no longer handle failure), spec.md:790-791 and :2333-2334 are corrected in the same change and a registered diagnostic teaches the two-arm form.

cards.title: DataTree exact Int: CBOR rejects major-type-0 2^63 as "outside Jet Int", and two equal 2^128+1 trees compare unequal
cards.body:
Title: DataTree exact Int: CBOR rejects major-type-0 2^63 as "outside Jet Int", and two equal 2^128+1 trees compare unequal
Kind: bug · Track: sidequest · Priority: P2 · Tags: core, encoding, I9 · Related: #3271 (C2 dynamic fidelity), #3255, #4306 (Dyn cutover)
Body: Found 2026-10-03 (CW3-DTLOSS, night12). (1) `P.sh run ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CW3-DTLOSS/cbor_uint63.jet` decodes `1b 80 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` -> `rejected: Unsupported: CBOR integer is outside Jet Int`. Jet Int is arbitrary-precision (encoding-decisions.md:718-721), and the CBOR law rejects only bignum tags and values outside Int (:881-885), so a representable major-0 value must decode to Int(9223372036854775808). Core/encoding/cbor.jet:230-236 reads the full 8-byte argument; the host route crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:3665 narrows with i64::try_from. (2) `P.sh run …/bigint_equal.jet` prints `340282366920938463463374607431768211457` twice (DataTree.Int(2^128+1) and json.parse of the same digits), then `false` for equal_unordered. Public numeric variants are Int and Float only (encoding-decisions.md:22-24, core-library.md:2168-2169), so an internal big-Int carrier must not change equality. [INFERENCE] root: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DataTree.rs:352/356/392 compares within one internal carrier and rejects mixed carriers.
Criteria:
1. CBOR major-type-0/1 values that fit an arbitrary-precision Int decode as Int on every tier; only bignum tags stay rejected by the profile.
2. Equal public Int values compare equal through equal_unordered (and `==` where defined), whatever the internal carrier.
3. The two cells marked "defect" in the encoding-decisions.md losslessness table become golden lines in serde/datatree_losslessness.

Title: Typed CBOR codec: `cbor.to_bytes([U8]{…})` fails and then ICEs in typed drop; `cbor.decode<[U8]>` has no canonical TIR record
Kind: bug · Track: sidequest · Priority: P1 · Tags: I1, encoding, compiler · Related: #3271 (C2 typed fidelity), #3255
Body: Found 2026-10-03 (CW3-DTLOSS, night12). `P.sh run ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CW3-DTLOSS/typed_encode.jet` -> prints `typed encode rejected: Syntax: typed_encode.jet`, then exit 101 "internal compiler error: typed drop CBORErrorKind field 0 is unavailable". `P.sh run …/typed_cbor.jet` (`cbor.to_bytes([U8]{0,127,128,255})` then `cbor.decode<[U8]>(wire)`) -> exit 101 "checked TIR cannot lower to MIR at 185..191: core.encoding.cbor.decode has no canonical TIR record (Unknown)" (Source/lib.rs:263:33). Law: a Codable `[U8]` encodes as a CBOR byte string (bstr `44 00 7f 80 ff`) and decodes back to the same bytes (encoding-decisions.md:860-862, 876-881). The checker accepts both programs. A third ICE of the same kind: interpolating an EncodingErrorKind with `:Debug` stops with "MIR debug type EncodingErrorKind<> has no checked debug carrier".
Criteria:
1. Typed CBOR encodes `[U8]` as bstr and decodes it back on the default tier and AOT; the two typed CBOR cells of the losslessness table become golden lines.
2. A failed typed encode returns its CBORError value, never a typed-drop ICE; EncodingErrorKind renders with `:Debug`.

cards.body:
Title: Operator registration keys methods only by name, so lawful same-owner hooks with different RHS report E0105
Kind: bug · Track: sidequest · Priority: P2 · Tags: compiler, operators, I4 · Related: #4157, #2788 (historic implementation), D-FOUND-OPMIX1=A
Body: CW4-PROJDRIFT's `P.sh check ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CW4-PROJDRIFT/mixed_rhs.jet` exits 1 with E0105 at :8:8 on two legal implementations: `impl Value.Add` takes Value and `impl Value.Add(Int) #Commutative` takes Int. The ratified A outcome requires one implementation per (left,right) pair, with a derived mirror; it does not prohibit two different pairs on one left type. The duplicate check at crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Items.rs:2502-2509 calls Registration.rs:1707-1727 based only on `m.name`. It tells users to rename/remove a lawful operator. foundations/exact's corrected Rational/ScaledDecimal/Money hooks expose the same failure. Do not replace operators with named methods or weaken the ratified law.
Criteria:
1. Registration distinguishes the operator's checked left/right pair; same pair still gets the registered duplicate diagnostic, while different RHS pairs register and resolve correctly.
2. The reduced mixed_rhs check and run succeed; both `value + 2` and `2 + value` print 5. A focused executable proof covers distinct RHS and the #Commutative mirror, plus a UI snapshot pins a true duplicate pair.
3. foundations/exact's lawful mixed operator headers no longer produce E0105; runtime/golden proof is recorded without hiding remaining independent defects.

cards.title: Default run tier SIGSEGV: struct literal field taking a two-loop U64 FNV callee result (MIR stable_id shape)
cards.body:
TITLE
Cranelift tier 1: SIGSEGV when a struct literal field takes the result of a two-loop U64 FNV callee (MIR stable_id shape)

BODY
Default `jet run` (Cranelift tier 1, D-JIT2=A) crashes with SIGSEGV (exit 139) on a 17-line program. `jet run --interpret` prints the correct value. The callee is the shape of `stable_id` in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/MIR/MIR.jet: two String parameters, a byte loop over each with `(hash ~| U64.from_u8(byte)).wrapping_mul(prime)`, and a separating `hash = hash.wrapping_mul(prime)` between the loops. The crash needs the result to be stored into a struct literal field (`Word{value: hash2(...)}`): calling `hash2` directly from `run`, or through a U64-returning wrapper, works.

This is what blocks the default-tier MIR Lint fixture run (#4125/#4126): every `mir_type_id`/`mir_function_id`/`mir_nominal_ref` builds `MIRTypeID{value: stable_id(...)}`, so the 38-case fixture unit (Compiler/JetOptimizer/Tests/run-lint-fixtures.mjs output) exits 139 during canonical fixture construction (first call into `fx_unit`/`fx_function`), before the verifier runs. The same unit passes 38/38 under `--interpret`.

Exact repro (cwd any; file ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/OW6-MIRLINT/stable/repro.jet, sha256 e2d544bbc7ada60ff0ff197e1b1b5d00a61a0714f78f9db88f575110311c0ac9):

    struct Word { pub value: U64 }

    fn hash2(namespace: String, identity: String) -> U64 Never! {
        prime :: U64{0x100000001b3}
        hash := U64{0xcbf29ce484222325}
        loop byte in namespace.bytes() -> hash = (hash ~| U64.from_u8(byte)).wrapping_mul(prime)
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(prime)
        loop byte in identity.bytes() -> hash = (hash ~| U64.from_u8(byte)).wrapping_mul(prime)
        hash
    }

    fn wrap(identity: String) -> Word Never! { Word{value: hash2("mir-type", identity)} }

    fn run() {
        print("wrapped: {wrap("Unit").value}")
    }

    jet run repro.jet              -> no output, SIGSEGV (exit 139)
    jet run --interpret repro.jet  -> "wrapped: 7299585414513572552", exit 0

Reduction ladder (all default tier, same binary; files in ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/OW6-MIRLINT/stable/):
- Works: hash2/stable_id called directly from run; hash2 through a U64-returning wrapper with forwarded parameters; struct-wrapped callees with one loop, two loops without the separating statement, loop+mul or mul+loop on one parameter, the same loop/stmt/loop shape with plain `+` instead of `~|`/wrapping_mul, a single-String-parameter variant of the full shape.
- Crashes: struct-wrapped two-parameter loop / wrapping_mul / loop (with or without the `if hash == 0 -> return U64{1}` guard, with a literal or forwarded namespace argument); verbatim MIR.jet `mir_type_id` + `mir_nominal_ref` (stable_wrap.jet).

Secondary observation, cause not established: the fixture's Foundation+MIR.jet prefix alone with a trivial `run` (no stable_id call; ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/OW6-MIRLINT/int/unit.jet) is SIGKILLed under a 3 GB cap (exit 137, no output) on the default tier, and passes under `--interpret`.

Source identity: release binary ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/jet-release-night12/jet sha256 464e83e21efc4ce5a68c3751a8fb702adc68c419a54fa4fa39aa3eba80e99d20 (built 2026-10-02 09:56); main 7bc7cc9d199451edf93e0183f6a6877904a8d127. Probes ran through ~/.cache/jet-luna/cards/cl2/P.sh (laneS 3 GB, 180 s).

CRITERION 1
repro.jet prints `wrapped: 7299585414513572552` and exits 0 on the default `jet run` tier, matching `--interpret`; a focused golden pins it on every tier (I5/I9).

CRITERION 2
The MIR Lint fixture unit assembled by Compiler/JetOptimizer/Tests/run-lint-fixtures.mjs runs under default `jet run` with `38 passed, 0 failed` and `all lint fixtures passed`, identical to `--interpret`.

cards.title: GC host trace IO checks paths with symlink_metadata then uses pathnames (TOCTOU); use held directory descriptors
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RuntimeLead-1). The GC host's trace file IO (crates/jet-codegen/.../__gc_host.rs:262-396) validates the parent directory and path with symlink_metadata and then creates, opens and renames by pathname. O_NOFOLLOW applies only to the temporary leaf (:337); ancestor traversal and parent identity can change between the check and the use (a time-of-check/time-of-use race), so a swapped symlink in an ancestor can redirect the write. The runtime port spec requires held directory identity and native no-follow leaves. Fix: perform the whole operation on a held directory descriptor with the existing descriptor/identity primitives (openat/mkdirat/renameat with no-follow), keeping the Jet error order and messages. The Jet port extracts the native leaf on those primitives, not on this sequence.

cards.title: Authority checked_file erases the native read cause, so E1331 cannot say why an entry file failed
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the Jetpack port (JP-ENTRY via JetpackLead-3). The checked entry loader cannot reproduce the Rust reference's E1331 'why' text (crates Loader.rs:245-253 includes the native read detail: ENOENT, invalid UTF-8, etc.), because the Jet AuthorityResolver.checked_file erases that detail into Missing/Invalid. cards.title: Fixed-decimal formatting rounds ties half-up; Rust {:.N} rounds ties to even (62.5 -> 62), so ported output differs
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the CLI port (CLI-44 coverage output via PortLead-8). Jet's fixed-decimal formatting (core.text.fmt.decimal and the :Fixed(n) selector, D-FMT-PLAIN1=A) rounds half-up/away from zero, while the Rust reference formats coverage percentages with {:.N}, which rounds the exact binary value to nearest with ties to even (5/8 = 62.5 -> "62"; Rust CmdCompile.rs:9185). Ported output that Rust prints through {:.N} therefore differs at ties. Decide (ballot if it changes a ratified formatter contract): either the ratified fixed-decimal rounding is ties-to-even on the exact value (matching Rust and IEEE formatting), or the CLI's documented output changes. The CLI port keeps the exact Rust expectation in its test, marked with this card.

log.text: Closed as DONE (burn-down 2026-10-17): every criterion met with evidence; see criteria. Evidence files: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/burndown/DoneEvidence/.

Ballot dropped 2026-10-04 (clarity pass): settled by ratified D-FMT-PLAIN1=A plus I9: fmt.decimal and the evaluator must follow the rule compiled code already ships (exact value, ties to even). Implementation work, no owner vote.

Observed on night12 (JetpackLead-4, real ArtifactStoreError renderer via canonical Duration.total_in(seconds) + :Fixed(3)): 62,500,000 ns renders exactly 0.062 (Rust's ties-to-even on the exact binary value), not 0.063; focused case exit 0 and a deliberate changed-expectation control fails (log ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/JetpackLead-4/StoreDuration/control.log). Together with CLI-52's 12.5 -> 12 and 1.25 -> 1.2, :Fixed(N) already matches Rust {:.N}. Remaining question only for the core.text.fmt.decimal half-up path reported by CLI-44; close this card if that path is also ties-to-even or is retired.

Third consumer (Jetpack Store, OpusRev-Jetpack-3/JetpackLead-4): StoreError Display formats Duration.as_secs_f64 with {:.3}; the Jet port had a bespoke integer half-up seconds formatter (Identity.jet:48-57), now to be replaced by the canonical Float :Fixed(3) path. Case: 62_500_000 ns = 0.0625 s, Rust 0.062 (ties-to-even on the exact binary value), half-up gives 0.063.

Counter-evidence (CLI-52 via PortLead-9, night12): :Fixed(0) and :Fixed(1) gave ties-to-even results in a real run (12.5 -> 12, 1.25 -> 1.2), so the selector may already match Rust's {:.N}; the half-up behaviour reported for CLI-44 may be specific to core.text.fmt.decimal or to the exact binary value. Recheck which entry rounds how on the rebuilt jet before deciding; close if both already agree with Rust.

cards.title: Core IOError has no InvalidData kind (Rust store index refusals); decide the public variant (ballot)
cards.body: Raised 2026-10-03 by the Jetpack port (JetpackLead-3, store index read_entries). The Rust reference reports two I/O refusal kinds Core's IOError cannot express: InvalidData (malformed entries, symlink where a regular file is required) and AlreadyExists (plus refuse-on-fsync). AlreadyExists is covered by the files-provider umbrella #3593; InvalidData has no home. Adding an IOError variant is public Core API, so this needs an owner ballot: (A) add IOError.InvalidData with a typed detail, (B) map these refusals to an existing variant with a typed reason field, (C) other. The port keeps the exact sites and tests (no fallback to Other) until decided.

cards.title: Default run tier: maps keyed by a struct with a nested struct field give wrong size and missing entries (JIT composite key)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the fix-lane Opus review (OpusRev-Fix-1). On the default run tier (JIT, night12), a map keyed by a struct that nests another struct (Key{subject: Subject, ...}) gives wrong results: after inserting two entries the size reports 3, and get() on a key just inserted stops with E3001 'map has no entry' (extended fixture Examples/features/generics/generic_composite_key_map.jet in .agent-worktrees/defect-fix, line ~85). cards.title: Core net: IPv4 is_reserved checks only 240 and 0 (should be 240.0.0.0/4); is_global misses special-purpose blocks
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the Jetpack port (JetpackLead-3, JP-NET-ADDRESS) reading Core/net/ip.jet. is_reserved (line ~75) returns true only for a == 240 || a == 0, but the reserved block is 240.0.0.0/4, i.e. every first octet 240..255 (Python ipaddress and the Rust reference treat it as a range); 0.0.0.0/8 is 'this network', a separate class. is_global (line ~81) also omits shared address space 100.64.0.0/10, 192.0.0.0/24, the TEST-NET blocks (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24), benchmarking 198.18.0.0/15 and 240.0.0.0/4. Fix the classification to the IANA special-purpose registry with a table-driven regression per block. The stricter outbound public-IP policy for Jetpack fetch is a separate Core API question tracked on #3595.

Examples/features/net/ip_special_profile.jet (26 IANA special-purpose rows + public/multicast controls at start/end/neighbours; all 256 first octets x 7 predicates): golden filter ok 1 passed; run / --interpret / --release rc 0, 30 lines MATCH, stderr empty (~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CloseLead/4413/).

Main disposition (CardLead-9 scouting, IANA registry 2025-10-09): is_reserved -> first octet 240..255; the existing 0.0.0.0/8 member is kept pending an owner decision on whether Core's is_reserved means protocol-reserved (incl. 0/8) or Python's 240/4; is_global -> explicit table from the IANA special-purpose registry incl. the 192.0.0.9/.10 global exceptions; multicast unchanged (Python treats it as global, Core does not); deprecated 192.88.99/24 (blank global field) unchanged and noted.

cards.title: abs: interpreter keeps the sign of -0.0/NaN and treats I64 as exact Int; F32 abs rejected (E0112 abs wants Int)
cards.body:
Found 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RtW4-MATH-PREFIX via RuntimeLead-2). Two defects in abs:
1. Interpreter sign policy (I9): Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/Core.jet:43-47 groups abs_i64/f64/f32 and computes `if number < 0.0 -> 0.0 - number else -> number`, so abs(-0.0) stays -0.0 and a negative-signed NaN keeps its sign, while Rust f64::abs / AOT clear the sign bit. The fixed I64 abs is also treated as exact Int (no overflow at I64 MIN). Repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/RtW4-MATH-PREFIX/RUNTIME-MATH-PREFIX-1/abs_sign_repro.jet.
2. F32 abs is rejected: the night12 full prefix corpus fails E0112 'abs wants Int' for an F32 argument (f32_abs_repro.jet in the same directory): the Core-owned signature masks the existing typed F32 path.
Fix: one canonical abs per numeric type in the Prelude/CoreLib that every tier calls (clear the sign bit for floats; I64 MIN behaviour per the Rust reference), and the sema signature accepting F32; regressions for -0.0, NaN sign, I64 MIN and F32 on all tiers.

cards.title: D-HTML-PARSE1: should Core parse HTML documents? (ballot)
cards.body: Owner ballot drafted in Docs/research/evidence-2026-09-29/3282-xml-markup-profile.md:56-61. Core has HTML escape/unescape and a span-based strip_tags but no HTML parser. Option A (recommended, not ratified): no Core HTML parser; core.text.html stays escape/unescape/strip; WHATWG parsing comes from an approved package. Beginner: html.strip_tags(text), html.escape(text); expert: the package; cost: scraping needs a dependency. Option B: core.text.html.parse(text) -> DataTree HTMLError! implementing WHATWG tree construction into the same tagged tree shape as XML, no script execution or fetching, bounded depth and nodes. Beginner: doc :: html.parse(page); expert: limits and events; cost: a large, changing algorithm in Core. Related defect regardless of outcome: html unescape renders plain characters as bracketed byte values (see the evidence file, criterion 3).

cards.title: E0340 'read_dir is not a method' fires on user-declared trait methods named read_dir (overbroad name ban)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the CLI port (PortW17-CLI-56 via PortLead-10) on the night12 jet. cards.title: Core http.parse_request copies the body (twice) before checking the 1 MiB limit
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the tools port (DEV-T1, ToolsLead-1), from source reading [inference, not executed]. Core http parse_request (Core http.jet ~516-517) slices the whole body with slice_b(raw, split, raw.len()) BEFORE checking the 1 MiB body limit, and slice_b (~1218-1226) pushes byte by byte into a new list and then copies it again (~out). An oversized request therefore costs proportional allocation and two copies before rejection, and every request copies its body twice. Fix: check raw.len() - split against the limit before any copy, and take the body as one borrowed/single-copy byte projection (one allocation at most), consistent with the byte-body surface decided on #4428.

Scope widened (Main, from the runtime Opus review): Core http parse_response has the same copy-before-cap shape as parse_request; apply the same length-before-copy fix there.

cards.title: A user struct named Unit collides with the built-in Unit type (wrong output on all tiers; AOT ICE)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by Main running Examples/features/memory/last_use_field_moves.jet (which declares `struct Unit {name, path}`) on the tonight's host overlay jet (rel-overlay3, target-rel3/release/jet). `jet run` (default tier) is correct; `jet build` crashes: 'internal compiler error: MIR non-unit return terminator has no value in `add_name` (MirType ... name: ".::last_use_field_moves.jet::Unit")' at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:19383. `fn add_name(graph: &Graph, name: String) { ... }` has no declared return type; its implicit unit return type is resolved by name and picks up the user's struct Unit. The night12 release jet builds the same file fine (rc 0), so this is a regression in the uncommitted host changes (PatternBorrow / MoveEmit / SplitBorrow / fix overlays). The implicit unit return must be the builtin unit type by identity, never a name lookup. Evidence ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/golden7/{last_use_field_moves.build.log,n12/b.log}.

Correction (Fix4432 root cause): not a host-overlay regression. night12 only looked fine because it uses the prebuilt jet-aot-rt runner; the rel3 build took the rustc path. cards.title: STATS-CANONICAL: which stats semantics is canonical, frozen Rust or current Core/math/stats.jet? (ballot)
cards.body:
Raised 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RuntimeLead-3). The frozen Rust Core stats and Core/math/stats.jet disagree on several functions; the port cannot blend them (one meaning, I8/I9).
- mean: A (Rust :265-267) naive sum/n, non-finite allowed; B (stats.jet:73-84) stable rescaled mean that rejects non-finite input.
- sum: A Rust stats.sum (:154-155) Kahan fsum; B stats.jet:87-110 Neumaier with explicit Inf handling.
- Same program: s.mean([1e308, 1e308]), s.mean([Inf]), s.sum([1e16, 1, -1e16]), s.sum([Inf, 1]) -> A: Val(Inf), Val(Inf), 0, NaN; B: Val(1e308), None, 1, Inf [inferred arithmetic]. Both: empty mean None, empty sum +0.
- rank: Rust (:222-229) competition ranks vs Core (:755-768) averaged ties: rank([1, 1, 2]).
- min/max: Rust (:477-483) ignores NaN vs Core (:528-543) rejects: min([NaN, 1]).
- kde_random: Rust (:467-475) deterministic density cycling (not random) vs Core (:493-505) Rand sampling with Gaussian kernel: kde_random([1, 2], 1, 3).
Recommendation (RuntimeLead-3): B throughout (beginner stability and validation, expert repeatable contract), with the frozen Rust changed in the post-stage-2 tandem batch and tier proofs; A means a clean cutover of the existing stats, tests and docs to Rust semantics. No new stats kernel until ruled.

cards.title: Core.text.is_control (Unicode Cc) public predicate for exact identity checks (ballot)
cards.body: Raised 2026-10-03 by the tools port (DEV-C2 devserver capture identity, ToolsLead-1). Rust uses char::is_control (Unicode general category Cc) for exact-identity checks. Core.text has only a PRIVATE is_control(cp: Int) grapheme helper that excludes TAB/LF/CR (a different meaning), and Foundation's private diagnostic control check also counts U+2028/U+2029 (not Cc). Proposed public surface, the same shape as the existing is_alphabetic / is_numeric predicates: Core.text.is_control(value: String) -> Bool, true when every scalar is in general category Cc, backed by the pinned UCD tables (#4426 work), with the private grapheme helper renamed to state its own meaning. Public Core API: owner ballot. Beginner: text.is_control(s); expert: the same predicate per scalar. Until decided, DEV-C2's exact-identity check stays gated on this card (no tool-local classifier).

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #4426; criteria carried there as [#4437]. Core text has_control (D-TEXT-CONTROL1=A; text.jet:888). Triage evidence: D-TEXT-CONTROL1=A ratifies has_control(any Cc), not title's all-scalar is_control; Core/text/text.jet:888 is still a private grapheme helper

Ballot detail (RuntimeLead-3): the consumer (devserver capture identity, Rust per-char char::is_control) must reject ANY Cc scalar in each of seven identity strings, so a whole-string all-scalars predicate (is_control("abc
") == false) would wrongly accept. Options to decide: (A) all-scalars predicate text.is_control(s) like is_alphabetic, with callers looping per scalar (needs a per-scalar iteration form that does not materialize one String per scalar); (B) a contains-any form, e.g. text.has_control(s) -> Bool (true if any scalar is Cc); (C) both. Exact cases: "" (A: false or true? state it), "abc" false, "a
b" (A false, B true), "
" (A true, B true), "	" Cc yes. Cost: no per-scalar String allocation. Either way the private grapheme helper is_control(Int) (GCB Control, excludes TAB/LF/CR) is renamed to its own meaning.

cards.title: Compiler-generated serde encode/decode collide with a struct's own encode/decode methods
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the Jetpack port (JpW6-STORE-SOURCE-2 via JetpackLead-4). A struct with explicit inherent encode/decode methods (Jetpack Hangar ProducerRecord, the Rust String wire codec) collides with compiler-generated serde methods: the Rust Serde layer (Serde.rs:373-375) only recognizes explicit Encode/Decode TRAIT impls as user-provided, and at :580-614 auto-generates encode/decode methods anyway, so the type ends up with two definitions of each. User-declared methods of the same name must suppress (or be the) generated codec, or generation must use a non-colliding internal name; check the Jet compiler's derive/serde path for the same rule (I9). Regression: a struct with its own encode/decode methods round-trips through its own codec on all tiers.

Absorbed #3755 records width0 stopping E3010 (interpreter earlier reported a different location/timing); these are historical observed receipts, not new runs.  },
 "options": [

   "key": "A",
   "name": "Keep the current nonfallible signature and caller-checked width",
   "technical": "Keep sign_extend(n: Int, bits: Int) -> Int Never!. The implementation continues mask/sign arithmetic without a local width check. Callers that need a protocol width of1..64 must validate before calling. Width0 retains the recorded invalid-shift stop; no typed Range result. Width65 is not rejected by a library guard and its result is governed by existing exact-Int arithmetic and shift rules; do not claim an observed result. Negative n is masked to low bits. No replacement API or compatibility alias.",
   "code": "// AUTHORED, NOT RUN. Same inputs for A and B.\nuse core.encoding.binary as binary\nfn show(n: Int, width: Int) {\n    if width < 1 || width > 64 {\n        print(\"invalid width\")\n        return\n    }\n    print(binary.sign_extend(n, width))\n}\nfn run() {\n    show(255, 8)\n    show(127, 8)\n    show(1, 0)\n    show(1, 65)\n    show(-1, 8)\n    show(128, 8)\n    show(-129, 8)\n    show(9223372036854775808, 64)\n}",
   "beginner": "Validate a caller-provided width before every call to avoid a process stop.",
   "expert": "A checked fixed-width parser calls directly after proving its width; no fallible outcome handling.",
   "tradeoffs": [
    "No public signature migration.",
    "Every dynamic-width caller repeats the width guard; forgetting it can stop the program."
   ]
  },

   "technical": "Cut over sign_extend(n: Int, bits: Int) -> Int BinaryError!. Before shifts or masking, bits<1 or bits>64 returns Err(BinaryError.Range). All widths1..64 compute v=n & ((1<<bits)-1), then return v-(1<<bits) when the sign bit is set and v otherwise. Negative n is legal and masked identically; no new restriction on Int magnitude, no implicit unsigned conversion and no clamping. Width1 yields0 or-1; width64 handles the signed minimum. Existing signed unpack internals propagate the typed error through their existing BinaryError contract. Migrate every callsite, registry/embedding signature, seed, example/golden and signature reference; no alias/shim. Ordinary unhandled-outcome diagnostics apply, no new diagnostic/API family.",
   "code": "// PROPOSED, NOT RUN. Same inputs for A and B.\nuse core.encoding.binary as binary\nfn show(n: Int, width: Int) {\n    value :: binary.sign_extend(n, width) ?? {\n        print(\"invalid width\")\n        return\n    }\n    print(value)\n}\nfn run() {\n    show(255, 8)\n    show(127, 8)\n    show(1, 0)\n    show(1, 65)\n    show(-1, 8)\n    show(128, 8)\n    show(-129, 8)\n    show(9223372036854775808, 64)\n}",

cards.title: Core strftime loses non-ASCII literal text (String.from_bytes per byte)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RuntimeLead-3), source reading. Core/time/time.jet strftime (~116-166) copies literal pattern text one byte at a time through String.from_bytes, so multi-byte UTF-8 literals in the pattern (e.g. "%Y年%m月") are corrupted or dropped. Copy literal runs as byte slices into the output buffer once (valid UTF-8 boundaries are guaranteed by splitting only at ASCII '%'). Regression with CJK and accented literals on all tiers.

cards.title: Jet sema never computes Func.diverges (Rust BodyCheck fixed point); API freeze reads it
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the compiler parity lane (CP-API-FREEZE via ParityLead-1). The Rust checker computes function divergence as a fixed point and writes it back to the AST (crates/jet-sema BodyCheck ~1367 and ~1379 set Func.diverges), and Rust ApiFreeze (~348, ~354) reads that AST field when freezing the public API. The Jet compiler has the Func.diverges field but no sema producer for it, so a Jet-built API snapshot would report every function as non-diverging. Port the divergence fixed point into Jet sema (same rules and iteration order as BodyCheck), with a regression (direct Never, transitive divergence, mutual recursion) and a report-parity case.

cards.title: Runtime: scoped allocation-accounting hook for the encoding max_bytes law (exact requested capacity, all tiers)
cards.body: Raised 2026-10-03 by the card lane (CW10-CBOR via CardLead-10). The ratified encoding max_bytes law (Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md ~1042-1071) counts input length AND the exact peak requested allocation capacity of a decode (arrays, maps, stack frames, error-path strings, arbitrary-precision Int counters) with a counting-allocator ceiling and no estimates. Portable Core has no allocation accounting, so no codec can enforce it today. Needed: a private runtime allocation-accounting hook scoped around a decode (prospective alloc/realloc/free charges including container frames, path strings and Int growth) that every encoding's decoder uses (CBOR, JSON, YAML, TOML, INI). It is a runtime/Core-internal mechanism (not public API) but spans all tiers (I9): JIT, AOT and interpreter must charge identically. Until it exists, every codec's allocation criterion stays BLOCKED on this card; input-length limits are enforced now.

log.text: Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: merged into #4472; criteria carried there as [#4448]. Encoding max_bytes law needs scoped allocation accounting (MemSentry.rs:386-391; cbor.jet:138-140). Triage evidence: crates/jet-foundation/src/MemSentry.rs:386-391 registers allocation provenance, not decode-scoped prospective capacity ceilings; Core/encoding/cbor.jet:138-140 only checks depth

Owner question (RuntimeLead-3 design): with max_bytes = 0 the decode cannot even allocate its Limit error (CBORError{path: String, reason: String}; string literals allocate), and the ratified law counts error/path capacities. Proposed reading: allocations made to construct and render the final budget-exceeded error AFTER the decode scope has failed and closed are outside the budget (the scope reports its own failure; path strings built during decoding still count). Alternative: a static/no-allocation error carrier for Limit. Main's provisional ruling: the post-scope Limit report is outside the budget, pending owner confirmation. Design notes: one private decode-scope ledger; every Core allocation/reservation charges exact capacity x layout via Int before the call (realloc: live - old + new), commit only on success, free subtracts, nested scopes checked atomically, failed reserve leaves live/peak unchanged; a GlobalAlloc hook alone cannot return an ordinary Limit, so the check lives in the fallible canonical growth leaves with a private typed BudgetExceeded transport caught at the codec boundary; native tandem covers every container/String/frame/Int growth path plus task/fiber context, unwind guard and post-scope free provenance, identical on all tiers.

cards.title: CONC-BACKGROUND-1: bounded non-blocking background worker in Core (Worker wrapper vs primitives) (ballot)
cards.body:
Owner ballot drafted 2026-10-03 by RuntimeLead-3 for the CLI receipt history worker (Rust ReceiptStore.rs 44-71, 1255-1280, 1915-1934: a bounded 8-job queue, one named worker thread, drop when full, per-job panic catch with a notice, synchronized dedup). Core today has channel<T>(capacity) with only blocking send/close (no try_send), task/detach without per-job panic isolation, and no synchronized mutable dedup cell.
Option A (beginner wrapper): core.tasks.worker<T>(capacity: Int, name: String, handle: fn(^T) -> Unit, on_panic: fn(PanicInfo) -> Unit) -> Worker<T> WorkerStartError!; Worker.try_send(^T) -> Unit TrySendError<T>! (Full(T) / Disconnected(T) return the owned rejected payload; never parks); Worker.close() -> Unit. Single named native worker, FIFO, disconnect after drain, each job's panic caught and passed to on_panic, then processing continues; no retries, no extra threads. Expert path = the same mechanism through primitives: Sender<T>.try_send(^T) -> Unit TrySendError<T>!, core.tasks.background(name: String, run: fn() -> Unit) -> BackgroundTask WorkerStartError!, core.tasks.catch_panic<T>(run: fn() -> T) -> T PanicInfo!.
Option B: only the expert primitives (no Worker wrapper).
Both: Shared<T>.with_mut<R>(update: fn(&T) -> R) -> R SharedAccessError! on the existing Shared permit (not a second mutex; no reference escape; Poisoned/Unavailable reported) for the dedup set. Send/owned static captures are checked; host abort/cancellation is not an ordinary panic. CLI policy (capacity 8, name jet-optional-history, drop + notice, dedup by fix) stays in the CLI; no Core telemetry.
Proof plan: capacity-8 FIFO, drop when full, disconnect, failed startup, per-job panic continues, concurrent dedup, owned-capture drop, deliberate wrong-Full control, all tiers. No implementation until the owner chooses.

cards.title: Core DataTree has no Bytes variant (Rust reference does): add DataTree.Bytes or keep it byte-free? (ballot)
cards.body: Raised 2026-10-03 by two lanes: the CLI port (CLI-44B, Rust CmdTest.rs 596-626 canonical_data_tree has a Bytes arm) and the card lane (#3271 CBOR: major type 2 byte strings cannot round-trip through DataTree). The installed Core DataTree has only Null / Bool / Int / Float / Text / Array / Object; the Rust reference DataTree also carries Bytes. Options: (A) add DataTree.Bytes([U8]) to Core (public API: encoders that cannot represent bytes, such as JSON/TOML/INI, define their mapping, e.g. reject or base64 per format law), migrating every exhaustive DataTree match; (B) keep DataTree byte-free and route byte payloads through typed codecs only (CBOR/MessagePack typed paths), so tree-based consumers like the test comparison corpus must reject or encode bytes explicitly. Same program: canonical_data_tree on a value holding [U8]{1, 2} gives A: Bytes([1, 2]); B: an error or a format-specific encoding. Until decided, ports keep the original Bytes branch/test marked on this card, excluded from scratch compositions only.

cards.title: D-DATATREE-ORDER: should DataTree objects keep insertion order (ordered payload), make all Maps ordered, or stay sorted? (ballot)
cards.body: Decision needed for #4306 (raised 2026-10-03 by FixLead-3 while preparing the fix). DataTree.Object's payload is the ordinary Jet map type, and Jet maps are sorted (frozen JetMap is an Arc<BTreeMap>), so insertion order is lost before any writer runs; the Rust reference's JSON/INI/test goldens expect insertion order. Options: (A) DataTree.Object's payload becomes an insertion-ordered entries type (e.g. an ordered map/entry list in Core), migrating every Object constructor, match, encoder, parser and tier mirror; language Map semantics unchanged. (B) Jet's Map becomes insertion-ordered everywhere (a language-wide semantic change: iteration order of all maps). (C) Keep DataTree objects sorted, and re-bless the Rust/Jet goldens and the INI/JSON writer contracts to sorted output. Same program: json.to_string(json.parse("{"b":1,"a":2}")) gives A/B: {"b":1,"a":2}; C: {"a":2,"b":1}. Recommendation (FixLead-3/Main): A (keeps Map simple and fast, matches the reference formats and user expectation for document order). Public Core API (DataTree.Object payload type): owner ballot. FixLead-3 may prepare the A cutover but lands nothing until ruled.

cards.title: Bootstrap assembly loses embed_file asset paths (assembled single unit has no asset staging or origin map)
cards.body: Raised 2026-10-03 by the tools port (DEV-A2 canvas assets, ToolsLead-1). `prep { embed_file("js/runtime-state.js") }` resolves relative to the source file's directory (escaping the source root is refused). The Bootstrap assembler (Compiler/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs ~185-199) concatenates every listed source into one scratch project/src/compiler.jet and copies no assets; check.sh passes only the unit, not the line map. So any listed source that embeds files will fail to find them once assembled. Decide the one canonical mechanism: (a) explicit per-file asset entries in the source manifest, which the assembler stages at the same relative paths, with the compiler resolving embed_file against the original file via the assembler's existing source markers/map; or (b) a compiler-level source origin map passed alongside the unit. Internal tooling (no public language change); needed before Bootstrap integration of JetCanvas assets (and any other embedding source). Until then, A2's standalone package proof stands and its Bootstrap integration is blocked on this card.

The Jet port needs a borrowed UTF-8 byte view of a retained String: a View<U8> over the String's own bytes, with no copy and no UTF-8 reconstruction. Today String.bytes() (Registry BuiltinMethods ~211 / BuiltinStatics) returns an owned [U8], and native codegen routes it to jet_string_bytes even with owned:false (~5589-5590). So hashing a source file (file.source.bytes().view) copies the whole file before SHA-256, where Rust uses .as_bytes(). Needed by the compiler-image source-authority digest (CompW18) and by every hash over retained source. If this is a new public String API, it needs a ballot; if an existing ratified spelling covers it, it only needs the implementation.

cards.title: Jet comptime evaluator lacks Rust MIREval capabilities: closure-call kinds, typed-text kernels, DMA simulation (E24-E26)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by a static function-by-function audit (SolDiverge, ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/SolDiverge/eval-operations.md) of Compiler/JetEval against the Rust evaluator. cards.title: Rust lexer: string-interpolation brace matching ignores comments, char literals and nested triple strings
cards.body: Found 2026-10-03 by the compiler port (CP-LEX-ESCAPE). The live Rust lexer (crates Strings/Scan, frozen) matches interpolation delimiters without lexical context: (1) `x :: """\n{f(\x27"\x27)}\n"""` reports E0002 (never-closing string) because the quote inside a char literal is treated as a string delimiter; (2) `"{a // }"` closes the hole at the brace inside a comment instead of reporting the unmatched `{`. The Jet lexer (Payload/Scan) skips comments, char literals and nested triple strings and gives the correct result. Fix the Rust reference to the Jet behavior (one meaning) with regressions for both shapes on every tier.

cards.title: Ballot: Unicode case predicates (istitle / is_lower / is_upper) canonical semantics
cards.body:
Found 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RtW20-TEXT-CASE). Today the Jet source and the frozen Rust disagree:
- Core/text/parse.jet:508 is_title is defined as text == title(text) and labelled Python str semantics.
- Rust Top/Text.rs:1649-1667 istitle accepts "AB" and "ABC abc", rejects the titlecase letter "ǅabc" and the uncased alphabetic "界"; its mapping-derived is_lower and is_upper both accept titlecase "ǅ".
Distinguishing inputs: ["AB", "ABC abc", "ǅ", "ǅabc", "界", "abc", "Abc"].
Options:
A. Adopt the literal frozen Rust predicates as canonical; migrate every public source caller.
B. Adopt standard Unicode/Python title, lower and upper predicate semantics (cased letters only; titlecase letters are neither lower nor upper; istitle requires uncased-then-uppercase/titlecase and cased-then-lowercase transitions), and repair the frozen/native/tier adapters.
Recommendation: B (the documented contract already names Python semantics; A accepts "AB" as a title, which no reader expects). Until ruled, the port keeps the public behavior unchanged and finishes the private exact policy and assets.

Triage evidence: D-UNICODE-CASE1=A ratified; Core/text/parse.jet:509-524 has ad hoc cased scanning rather than ratified UAX29 word semantics

Correction from the runtime port (RtW20, exercised source trace): the frozen Rust (is_title, is_lower, is_upper) table is: "AB" = (T, F, T); "ABC abc" = (F, F, F) (the space resets expect_upper, then lowercase 'a' is rejected; the earlier ballot text wrongly said istitle accepts it); "ǅ" = (F, T, T); "ǅabc" = (F, T, F); "界" = (F, F, F); "abc" = (F, T, F); "Abc" = (T, F, F). The remaining contradiction with Unicode/Python semantics: "AB" is a title in Rust, and titlecase "ǅ" is both lower and upper. Also noted: U+1D2C ᴬ is Other_Lowercase despite its CAPITAL name (asset correct).

cards.title: I9/parity: Jet sema Panic effect rows diverge from Rust (RequireStop/Never add Panic; lambda-body panic() never reaches the lambda or fn row)
cards.body: Found by stage-1 fixer FixL5-Lint2. (a) Compiler/JetSema Effects/Checks.jet:~1043 adds the __jet_panic__ edge for EVERY RequireStop and Never (require/require_eq/todo/no-else arm/missing fallback); Rust records Panic only for panic(...) and ?? panic(...) (check_panic_call; Effects.rs:3294 treats Todo/NoElse as effect-free leaves), so Jet rows carry Panic Rust doesn't. (b) a panic() inside a lambda body never reaches the lambda's row nor the enclosing function (the walker returns at .Lambda; lambda facts come only from call facts); Rust's record_effect adds Panic + edge to every open lambda accumulator and the function. Neither trips the MIR lint (effect.row is checked only at calls), so deferred until after stage 1. Fix both to Rust semantics with regressions.

cards.title: Owner gate: runtime native-port capability substrate (atomic word, typed storage/loans, raw owned C ABI, exact raw-owner, no-unwind callback/exit)
cards.body: Porting the Rust runtime natives into audited Jet (owner directive: all Rust ported, natives included) needs five internal capabilities Jet doesn't have today. Full request: ~/.cache/jet-luna/port/runtime/CAPABILITY-REQUESTS-8.json. (1) RT-CAP-ATOMIC-WORD: one private inline U64 atomic word (8/8 layout; load/store/swap/strong+weak CAS returning the observed value; Relaxed..SeqCst with checked legality; spin hint) for Atomic.rs 310-445, gc_portable.rs 14-145, Tools signal-safe AtomicI32. (2) RT-CAP-TYPED-STORAGE-LOANS: inline interior-mutable T with guard-retained loans and typed uninit T (write-once, init bit) for gc_portable + Uninit.rs 48-198. (3) RT-CAP-RAW-OWNED-ABI: policy-free raw alloc/free, typed placement/take/drop, opaque owned C-word String/cursor handles, raw ptr+len borrowed bytes, retained UTF-8 view, static string projection (CAbi.rs 49-81,105-213,336-383); depends on #4483. (4) RT-CAP-EXACT-RAW-OWNER: canonical owned raw exact-Int word retain/reload/hazard/ABA/drop/try_add (Atomic.rs, CAbi.rs, Foundation Numeric.rs). (5) RT-CAP-NOUNWIND-CALLBACK-EXIT: checked extern-C callback export/invoke, consume-once callbacks, panic catch/rethrow, output-free exit (CAbi.rs 28-47,96-103; gc_portable 156-175). These are expert-escape-hatch internals (I1 #Unsafe) and need a design decision on surface and target availability; until then the runtime writers port every independent policy and ledger these leaves as blocked on this card.

Requested acceptance — minted D-ACCEPT-4494.

The ArrowData port (wave packet 0004: ArrowData.rs 462-1050 and 1517-2098, plus its native tests) needs these native capabilities: unaligned exact-width native loads; a raw borrowed byte or text view tied to its owner's lifetime; calls through nullable C-ABI release function pointers; a process-global pointer-claim mutex or hash set that can recover from poisoning; and a process-local immutable reference-counted owner with a deterministic destructor and provider keepalive. Core/mem currently offers only address_of, from_addr and volatile access.

Correction to the CompW25 entry: a canonical condition wait already exists (SharedGuard.wait(Condition, predicate) in JetSema Calls/Memory.jet ~399-409 releases and reacquires the exclusive guard, and Condition.notify_one/notify_all are Core rows), so item (3) is withdrawn and the port uses that provider. Still missing: (1) an erased retained owner with checked downcast and unique extraction, (2) exactly-once final-alias cleanup and unwind ownership guards, and (4) task-local activation.

The compiler port's backend-resource packet (CompW25: Rust Foundation MIR.rs ~3954-3980, SourceResources ~669-687 and ~1681-1685, SourceCallbacks ReplyCell ~349-529 and session ~1619-1633) needs runtime capabilities Jet doesn't have yet: (1) an erased, identity-preserving retained owner with checked downcast_ref/downcast and unique-owner extraction; (2) a custom final-alias destructor that runs release_root and re-entrant finalizers exactly once, where a weak upgrade can't mint new roots; (3) a condition wait that atomically releases and reacquires the same permit, with owned abandonment and requeue on final drop; (4) unwind guards that restore a task-local stack on unwind. Shared<T> covers same, guard_read, guard_edit, downgrade and strong_count, but none of these. Core sync is CRDT, and TaskState.lock is value state, not a mutex or condition variable.

The Tools port of the compiled-workload peer launcher is blocked on these native capabilities (ToolW32; source and 24 tests are in port-tools Tools/ci): a borrowed SockFprog passed to prctl; LP64 variadic call lowering; reading errno immediately after a call; nullable, signal-safe C callbacks; a static AtomicI32 with Release store and AcqRel swap; spawning into a process group with pre-exec setup; null and inherited stdio; the raw wait status; a create-new status-file lifecycle; and native OS-path ingress. Windows AppContainer, raw output and environment come from the runtime lane.
Addendum (RuntimeLead-8): RT-CAP-ATOMIC-WORD also needs signed bitcasts/truncation between the U64 word and I64/I32/U32 atomic views.

questions.text: i still want expert control while providing the best safe, magic, and performant defaults
questions.answer:
Yes: the recommended option A now gives both, using CPU tools Jet already ratified instead of a separate SIMD mechanism (the old A kept a private kernel list with its own chip checks, a second mechanism beside #Multiversion).

Beginner default (no markers, no unsafe): plain loops and Core collection operations vectorize automatically; Lanes<T> uses the widest register of the targeted chip level; Core's hot kernels use AVX2 even in a portable build, because the chip is checked once at start-up and the best copy is used. Plain loops and Core operations give the same answers everywhere.

Expert control, each by explicit opt-in:
- exact width: Lanes<F32, 8>
- named instructions for one chip level: #Multiversion(x86_64, x86_64_v3) plus typed core.arch calls
- whole-program chip choice: jet build --cpu=znver4 --features=+avx2
- anything else: #FFI(asm) inside #Unsafe("…")
- keep a function scalar: #Scalar (already ratified)
- NEW, declinable: #Vectorized (build fails, naming the reason, if a marked loop stays scalar) and JET_CPU_MAX (caps the copy chosen at start-up)

Disclosed costs with mitigations: NaN payload bits can differ between copies; Lanes<T> sums across chunks can differ in the last bits between chip levels (Lanes<T, N> pins it); calls into marked functions are indirect; binaries grow per marked function; it waits on #Multiversion, core.arch and Lanes being built (#4168, #4167). Reviewed by a beginner pass and a separate adversarial pass; every code fact and cited decision was checked.

cards.title: Possible ABA in Rust Atomic<Int> CAS: compares initial bits A but clone_from_atomic may reload and retain owner B
cards.body: Found by the runtime port (RtW28-ATOMIC-NATIVE, source reading, not executed): crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Atomic.rs 349-355 / 379-390 / 413-424 compare-and-swap with the initially read bits A, but Numeric.rs clone_from_atomic 3182-3210 may reload and return owner B; the retained guard then protects B, not the expected A, so a recycled A address could make the CAS succeed against a different value (ABA). Expected: the retained-clone API returns the validated raw word together with its owner (or restarts when the raw word changed), and CAS uses that same validated word. The Jet port implements the correct version; keep the original schedule test and add an ABA witness.

cards.title: Runtime has no JetShow/JetDebug for tuples: auto-derived Show on a record with a [(String, [String])] field fails rustc E0599
cards.body: Found by the Jetpack port (JpW37 NixosImportRendering, repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/JpW37-NIX-IMPORT-RENDER/attempt3/original/unit.jet + generated .jet/build/unit.rs/unit.rustc.log): the Rust host emits an auto JetShow for a record whose field is Vec<(String, Vec<String>)>, but the runtime implements JetShow for no tuple type, so rustc fails E0599 before any test runs. Fix: add JetShow/JetDebug impls for tuples (up to the arity the language allows) in the runtime, with the same rendering as Rust's derived Debug of a tuple, on every tier (I9), then let both emitters derive Show for records with tuple fields.

cards.title: ICE (exit 101): 'checked TIR cannot lower to MIR: equal: distinct raw without its checked base type' on == over a distinct type
cards.body: Found by the compiler port (CompW13 REPORT-STATUS consumer). The Rust host's jet test --fresh on ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/CompW13-REPORT-STATUS/CP-REPORT-STATUS-API/consumer.jet (inputs listed with sha256 in positive.json there) stops with internal compiler error at crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:6603: 'checked TIR cannot lower to MIR at 2117..2120: equal: distinct raw without its checked base type'. Fix sema to record the base type for distinct equality (or reject with a registered diagnostic if the comparison is not allowed), and lower it; add the repro as a regression. Check the Jet compiler (Compiler/JetSema + JetLower) for the same gap.

cards.title: Sema: a pattern on a concrete generic enum (GCTryLockError<U64>.Poisoned(value)) leaves the payload typed T, giving E0108 T vs U64
cards.body: Found by the runtime port (RtW30 GC native, repro ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/RtW30-GC-NATIVE/RUNTIME-GC-PORTABLE-NATIVE-1/unit.jet line 252 + positive.log). Matching a value of concrete type GCTryLockError<U64> against .Poisoned(value) binds value with the declared generic payload type T instead of the substituted U64, so assert_eq(value, U64{MAX}) fails E0108 (T vs U64) even with an explicit concrete annotation on the helper. Fix: substitute the scrutinee's type arguments into variant payload types when binding pattern variables (sema, every pattern site: switch/if-let/let-else), with a regression; check the Jet compiler's pattern binding (Compiler/JetSema) for the same gap.

cards.title: One function arrow: retire the second body arrow (fn f() -> T -> …)
cards.body:
Owner ruling 2026-10-04 (chat, verbatim intent): "Jet has ONE function effect/arrow marking, never two for a function. There should be one arrow after the function inputs which can contain [Effects]; after the arrow comes the return type (if there is one), then the `{` for the function body."

This is already the ratified rule D-SIG-AFTER1=A (2026-09-18: "the return type follows the one arrow, and named function and method bodies always use braces"), and the owner said the same on 2026-09-16 (Docs/research/jai-vs-jet-fable-brief-2026-09-16.md:51). The code still violates it: the parser accepts `fn f() -> T -> expr` / `-> T -> { … }`, the formatter canonicalizes INTO that form (tests/fmt.rs:1173 expects `fn answer() -> Int -> 42`), and about 290 lines in about 100 files use it (#FFI(asm)/#FFI(c) bodies, Examples/features/lowlevel/inline_{asm,c}.jet, Compiler/JetBackend/Source/OS/Linux.jet, UI fixtures, parser/formatter tests, Core/web, Core/data). Stale prose: Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:232-241 (D-ARROW-CONTROL1 example `fn load(path: String) String -[FS]> {`) and D-ONELINE-BODY1 wording.

Greenfield cutover (one change):
- Rust parser and Jet-port parser: a named function or method head takes exactly one arrow (`->` or `-[E]>`) followed by the optional return/failure type, then a braced body. A second body arrow is a teaching diagnostic (registered code, what/why/fix "replace `-> expr` with `{ expr }`", UI snapshot).
- Formatter emits `fn f() -> T { expr }`; no double-arrow output.
- Migrate every caller, example, fixture, embedded test source, Compiler/, Core/, Jetpack/ and the spec prose.
- Out of scope (unchanged): lambdas `(x) -> expr`, control one-liners (`if c -> x`, loops, arm tables), computed fields `name: T -> expr`, function types `fn(Int) -> Int`.

Sequencing: land after the stage-1/stage-2 inputs are pinned, so the bootstrap chain is not disturbed.

cards.title: Add Char.from_u32 / U32.from_char and measured streaming chars() loops (D-CHAR-SCALAR1=A)
cards.body:
D-CHAR-SCALAR1=A (ratified 2026-10-04).

Scope:
- Char.from_u32(value: U32) -> Char? (Val for every scalar incl. 0 and noncharacters; None for surrogates and > 0x10FFFF) and U32.from_char(c: Char) -> U32 (never fails), following the destination-owned from_<source> rule. Rows in both compilers' builtin tables; every tier.

cards.title: Admitted target libraries and SQL rules libraries via authority.trust.compiler (D-LANG-IN-LIBS=A)
cards.body:
D-LANG-IN-LIBS=A (ratified 2026-10-04, ballot card #4503): ordinary packages unchanged; experts may admit a target library and/or one SQL rules library per package, by capability and lock hash.

Scope:
- authority.trust.compiler maps a direct dependency to {gives: [.Target | .SQLRules], hash} (+ schema: path for .SQLRules); hash must equal the lock integrity hash; mismatch = registered teaching refusal ("rv changed since you admitted it" with old/new hash and the exact field to update). Transitive registrations, overlapping target IDs and a second .SQLRules entry refused naming both entries; workspace policy may narrow, never widen. Providers gain no DB/FS/network/FFI authority.
- Target discovery: one data-only manifest (target ID, OS, arch, ABI, pointer size per D-USIZE-TARGET1, endianness, features) read before parsing target code; only the selected target's files load; output checked for shape and every claimed feature; built-in targets never use a library backend.
- SQL rules run after the built-in SQL check on every SQL{"…"} in that package, may only refuse (cannot change read/write class or paste holes); schema.sql changes recheck every literal; SQL.raw not run through rules; a dependency's literals use only its own admission.

Acceptance: decision checkInstructions (people program under all four options, riscv64 board run, hash refusal/accept, nmae typo refused at build time citing schema.sql, second .SQLRules refused, lying rule/backend refused).

cards.title: Implement core.mem.native (D-RT-NATIVE-CAP1=A): nine native tool groups plus the owner-admitted provider registry
cards.body:
D-RT-NATIVE-CAP1=A (ratified 2026-10-04, no group declined): private native tools for porting the Rust runtime into audited Jet. Gate card #4494 is cleared; this card carries the implementation.

Scope (Rust compiler and the Jet port together, one meaning on every tier):
- New module core.mem.native, importable only by bundled runtime/platform source units and by outside packages admitted by exact name + lock content hash in ONE compiler-embedded provider registry (Rust sema and Compiler/JetSema share the table). Unadmitted import = registered front-end error; changed hash = refusal naming the old/new hash; removed entry = refusal naming the revoked hash. Admitted packages still need policy.unsafe_deps.
- Groups: NATIVE-ATOMIC (inline 32/64-bit atomic words, load/store/swap/strong+weak CAS returning the observed value, ordering legality as a compile-time type error, signed views/bitcasts per the #4494 addendum); NATIVE-STORAGE (Cell<T> with guarded loans, Uninit<T> fill-once, typed place/take/drop over D-RAWPTR2); NATIVE-ABI (borrowed byte extents, opaque C handles, C layouts with real unions, unaligned fixed-width loads); NATIVE-EXACT (owned exact-Int word over atomics); NATIVE-CALLBACK (C callback export/invoke, once-callbacks, host-panic capture, signal handlers); NATIVE-LIFECYCLE (erased owners with checked downcast, final owner with one release, weak handles); NATIVE-TASKLOCAL (restoring task-local guards); NATIVE-OS (peer-launcher OS rows); NATIVE-ARROW (claimed Arrow C import, D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1).
- Every declaration adopts D-UNSAFE-EFFECT=A unchanged (land after or with that card).
- First consumers to migrate: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Atomic.rs 310-445, gc_portable.rs 14-145, CAbi.rs 20-46, crates/jet-foundation/src/MIR.rs 3954-3980, ArrowData.rs 408-1016, Tools/ci/compiled-workload-peer-launcher.rs (ToolW32), CompW25 backend-resource packet, ArrowData wave 0004.

cards.title: Runtime SIMD through #Multiversion and typed core.arch intrinsics (D-SIMD-NATIVE1=A)
cards.body:
D-SIMD-NATIVE1=A (ratified 2026-10-04 after the owner's expert-control question q0z7el6v was answered): one approved tool for newer chips; the runtime uses the same tools users get.

Scope:
- Hot Core/runtime kernels are ordinary Jet functions marked #Multiversion(x86_64, x86_64_v2, x86_64_v3) (D-CPU-DISPATCH1=A): one copy per level, start-up probe binds the best copy once, baseline copy is the fallback. Calls between marked functions stay at level and are direct; Core marks whole loops.
- Lane values stay in the level's registers inside each copy; Lanes<T> takes the widest listed width per copy; Lanes<F32, 8> pins width.
- Typed core.arch intrinsics inside #Multiversion copies, gated by `prep if $build.cpu.has(.AVX2)`; #FFI(asm) behind #Unsafe for anything else; no permits, no separate SIMD mechanism.
- JET_CPU_MAX cap honored; compile-time evaluation, interpreter and JIT run the baseline copy.
- Depends on card #4192 (release builds must stop passing target-cpu=native, or the baseline copy can use build-host instructions).
- Both compilers (Rust codegen and Jet backend) and the Jet port of the runtime kernels.

Acceptance: decision checkInstructions: every marked Core kernel and example under JET_CPU_MAX=x86_64, x86_64_v2, x86_64_v3 on real hardware and uncapped; same matrix in comptime/interpreter/JIT; bit-equality vs baseline for non-NaN results (signed zero, infinities, subnormals, exact I64 compares); NaN-ness rules incl. payloads, signaling NaN, 0/0, inf-inf, sign-bit negation; Lanes<T> width and identical sums per copy; AVX2 lane-permute intrinsic branch parity.

cards.title: Comptime: lower the comptime closure once per compilation; per-item cost O(item), not O(program)
cards.body: jet_driver_run_comptime (Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1856-2060), per pending item: re-checks every module under staged values when the value count changed (sema_comptime_modules_with_values), rebuilds the codegen session, recomputes package facts, lowers foreign artifacts, and assembles a whole temporary MIR program (jet_driver_assemble_mir) before evaluating. On L5: 538 items, 133.3 s, 248 ms per item (17.8% of the frontend). Rule R7 of Docs/research/fast-compiler-architecture-2026-09-30.md. Plan: $JET_STATE_ROOT/speed/SPEED-PLAN.md.
cards.plan:
1. One comptime program per compilation: lower every comptime-reachable function once into a shared, growable program; new closures append functions instead of reassembling.
2. Staged values are passed at run time (constant table indexed by item ID) instead of being baked into re-lowered fragments, so a landed value does not invalidate lowered code.
3. Declaration re-checks run only for items that name a newly landed constant (the driver already tracks this per item; make it per dependency, not per value count).
4. Package facts and foreign artifacts are computed once per staged set, not per item.
5. Cache each evaluated value by (item ID, argument digest) for the run. Do not extend JetEval (D-EXEC1 retires it); shape the shared program so SP17's native O0 path consumes it.
Acceptance: counters show 0 per-item jet_driver_assemble_mir / package-facts / whole-module re-check calls; L5 comptime <= 10 s (from 133.3 s); comptime value digests and out.rs bytes identical; Stage-2 outputs byte-identical before/after (the #815 fixed point is the oracle); UI snapshots unchanged.

cards.title: Remove copies at the self-hosted compiler's top clone and allocation sites
cards.body: Allocator (malloc/free/consolidate/unlink) plus memmove are 19-60% of self samples in every compiler phase (PhaseProf L2: register 60%, sema.check 48%, comptime 39%, sema.finalize 37%, lower 27%, load 27%, optimize 22%, emit 19%), with clone frames for Type, Expr, CtValue, TokenPayload, String, MIRType, MIRInstruction and Vec<JetInt>. Peak RSS on L5 is 23.2 GiB. This card attacks the compiler's own hottest sites through the general ownership routes (#4308 step 3, #3735, #4462), not compiler-local workarounds. Plan: $JET_STATE_ROOT/speed/SPEED-PLAN.md.
cards.plan:
1. Take an L5 perf profile per phase (fp call graphs, as PhaseProf/prof-l2.sh) and rank clone/allocation sites by inclusive cost.
2. For each top site decide: borrowed read, last-use move, or a source change in Compiler/ (pass by reference, consume with ^, stop returning rows by value).

cards.title: Memory safety: the JIT decodes raw U64/I64 map keys as exact-Int pointers (segfault on 1 in 8 stable IDs)
cards.body: Root-caused by NativeMono2 (2026-10-04): crates/jet-jit/src/functions_compile.rs:9365 routes IntN map keys (U64/I64 raw words) to MapKeyKind::Int, so jet-rt map_get_int/map_insert_int run exact_int_map_key + retain_exact_raw on the raw word; a U64 whose top bits are 01 and low 3 bits 0 is decoded as a JetInt node pointer and the process segfaults. Repro: `m := [U64:Int]{}; m.get(U64{5846639821254430312})` under jet run. About 1 in 8 stable IDs hit it, so every [U64:_] map in code run by the JIT is affected (I1). Fix: a word key kind (MapKeyKind::Word{unsigned} -> JetMapKey::Int/UInt, no exact retain) plus *_word runtime routes; regression test in the cross-tier suite. This is a bug fix in the retiring JIT, not an extension (I9).

cards.title: Pattern tests: `x == .Val(name)` binds a new `name` even when `name` is already in scope (silent shadowing instead of comparison)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-05 by Idiom-Compiler2 (#4588) converting port tests: in `x == Val(expr)`, the right operand is parsed as a pattern, so `== Val(name)` introduces a binding `name` rather than comparing with the variable `name`, and the comparison silently always matches. Equality must compare values; pattern tests use `::`. Done when `==` always parses expression operands (or a registered diagnostic rejects the ambiguous form), with UI snapshot and a regression example on all tiers, and corpus sites audited.

log.text: Closed as a duplicate of #4358: Same defect as #4358: in x == Val(name), the right operand parses as a pattern and rebinds name instead of comparing. #4358 is the survivor.

PortCodemod2 correction: only == takes a pattern right operand (jet-parser binary_unary.rs:489, BinOp::Eq only); x != Val(y) is a plain value comparison. So == and != disagree on the same right operand (== .Val(y) binds y; != Val(y) compares with y): include that asymmetry in the fix design. Confirmed port hazards: compiler 103, runtime 1 (scoped binding), main 0 (TSVs refreshed).

Reframed 2026-10-05: binding in == pattern tests is ratified (syntax-decisions: == pattern tests, D-IFGUARD1 bindings under &&), so this is not a parser bug. The hazard is silent shadowing: when name is already a local, == .Val(name) introduces a new binding and always matches, where the writer meant to compare. Port tests hit it. Fix direction: a registered diagnostic when an == pattern binding shadows an in-scope local (with the fix line showing how to compare the value), UI snapshot, both frontends; owner ballot only if the fix needs new syntax.

cards.title: Slot-IR safety net before Rust removal (replaces MIR Lint)
cards.body:
Before Rust leaves the toolchain, a Jet-owned checker re-proves the ownership and capture invariants on the slot IR (JetIR). It replaces the MIR Lint in the old body, since MIR is deleted by cutover A #5073. Each invariant gets a registered diagnostic and a UI test. Rust removal #4717 waits for this checker. No new language rules; only re-proofs of checked sema decisions.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Today rustc's borrow checker and Send/Sync re-check the Rust we generate (a rejection is an ICE, I2). The native backend has no such second check. Before Rust leaves the toolchain, Jet needs its own independent second proof. MIR Lint (Docs/spec/mir-lint.md) is already a second checker (types, ownership.move, effect rows) but has no exclusivity, view-validity or sendability rules.

Criteria:
1. MIR Lint gains rule families alias.exclusive (a write place is unique; no overlapping live read/write), view.valid (no owner move/resize/write while a view into it is live; no view outlives its owner set) and send.boundary (every value crossing task/channel/parallel boundaries is copied, moved, frozen or Shared; no Cell/view crosses). Linear dataflow, independent of sema's alias graph, failures are ICEs.
2. Mutation proof: a fixture set that deletes each sema check in turn (E0204, E0212, E0121, E1101, E1102, E1113, E2305) and shows MIR Lint catches every resulting program as an ICE.
3. Native-codegen trust: differential runs native vs Rust-path on all goldens until Rust is removed; ASan/UBSan-style instrumented native build of the golden corpus plus the compiler self-build with zero reports; a fuzz harness (generated well-typed programs) over sema + MIR Lint + native.
4. Runtime: every unsafe operation in the Jet CoreLib lives in an audited #Unsafe region in the safety.md baseline; bounds/overflow checks are emitted by the native backend identically on every tier.
5. Documented in Docs/spec (mir-lint.md and safety.md) as the post-Rust safety argument.
Gate: D-EXEC2's Rust removal waits for criteria 1-4.

cards.title: Beginner mistakes get diagnostics that name the cause and a fix that compiles (print vs return, ended-branch names, Int/Int, nested patterns, E0303, implicit multiplication, prose lines)
cards.body:
NEW repair card under ratified diagnostics law: philosophy 'errors that explain what happened, why, and how to fix it' toward user intent; D-REPORT-HOME1=A (typed rows own What/Why/Fix); D-TEACH-FOREIGN1=A (teach foreign habits at the mistake). Builds on done #3717/D-DISCARD1 (lost tails, pure drops) and #3713. Coordinates with ready #3720 (plain-words sweep): #3720 rewrites wording of existing rows; this card adds cause analysis (where the Unit came from, which binding went out of scope) that wording alone cannot supply. Not a duplicate of the 2026-09-28 learnability report's F17/F18 (different codes/cases).

Observed 2026-10-05 with the dev candidate jet (dev-05ea86f65, built 14:16) and the main checkout debug jet. Each case is a top beginner mistake demonstrated in a 7-hour beginner Python course (youtube 4M87qBgpafk) and each current report steers away from the fix.

## 1. Printing instead of returning (course 01:13-01:16, the classic print-vs-return confusion)

```jet
fn get_title(first: String, last: String) {
    title :: "{first} {last} the warrior"
    print(title)
}
fn run() {
    title :: get_title("Frodo", "Baggins")
    print(title)
}
```

Today: `E0112: print doesn't know how to show Unit ... Fix: Print one of its parts instead` (Calls/Direct.jet:318). Interpolating it instead gives `E0915: ``Unit`` has no Display implementation ... Fix: Add impl `Unit`.Display {...}` (Expressions/Literals.jet:896), which tells a beginner to implement a trait on a built-in and renders doubled backticks. Expected: when the Unit operand is a binding initialised from a call to a function with no written result type, the report says that `get_title` returns no value, points at the binding, adds a related location at the `print(title)` inside `get_title`, and offers the fix `-> String` with `title` as the last line.

## 2. A name made inside both branches, used after them (course 01:23-01:25, 03:01-03:07: Python scopes names to the function)

Today: `E0107: Nothing named name exists here ... Fix: Declare it first: name :: ...` even though `name` was declared in both `if`/`else` branches (Sema/Diagnostics.jet:214-220). Expected: when a same-named binding exists in a block that has ended, say so with related locations and offer the value form `name :: if { cond -> a  else -> b }` (verified to run, probe p10b).

## 3. Int / Int returned as Int (course 01:55-02:03)

Today: `E0113: This value is Fraction, but average returns Int ... Fix: Hand back a Int value: convert this value to Int` (grammar 'a Int'; no operator named). Expected: for an Int / Int operand where Int is required, offer `/%` (floor division) as the first fix and the explicit conversion second.

## 4. Qualifying a nested case in a pattern (course 06:59-07:00 handler-order lesson ported to Jet)

`.Err(ShotError.NoArrows) -> ...` gives `E0003: Expected , between pattern bindings, found .` plus a cascade at the closing brace. Expected: one report that says nested cases are written `.NoArrows`, with that edit.

## 5. E0303 fix text invents fields (folded in from web-data-net)

New defect in the same class as #3592 (done), which fixed a different E0303 text. Builds on D-LIT-DOT1=B.

Witness: `Err(MyError.Sized(limit: 3))` for `enum MyError { Plain Sized(limit: Int) }` on release jet dev-05ea86f65 gives E0303 "Variant `Sized` requires labeled fields", Why "Named-payload variants construct with the dot-brace form (D-UITREE1/D-DOTCTOR1)", Fix "Write `MyError.Sized.{ w: 1.0, h: 2.0 }`". The fields w and h do not exist, and E0320 says "D-LIT-DOT1 drops the constructor dot from every literal head". Core itself writes `.BodyTooLarge{limit: ...}` (Core/http/http.jet:426).

## 6. Two more cause shapes from the v3-P1 re-mine (4M87qBgpafk 0:00-3:35)

- Implicit multiplication: math notation `5/9(f - 32)` gives Python's 'float object is not callable', a symptom far from the cause (a missing `*`); the instructor never names the cause (PYA-040). Jet's report for calling a number literal or parenthesised numeric expression should say 'a value directly before ( looks like multiplication; write *'.
- A prose sentence left in code: Jet reports E0003 'Write the complete statement form named by this diagnostic'; when the line is several bare words with no operator, say it looks like text and offer to comment it out (PYA-017).
- Case 1 gains a cause signal: Jet already infers that `get_title` prints (IO effect) and returns Unit, so the report can say 'get_title prints its result and returns nothing' (PYA-048). Python reports the indentation error one line late; every Jet report must point at the cause line (PYA-069).

Distilled 2026-10-05 by DistillLang from the six mining batches; Tower snapshot rev 74843 (jet-state digest INCONSISTENT during collection: rerun before posting).

cards.title: I1: JetArena retains map values as exact-Int unless marked raw; remaining Float routes and the polarity inversion
cards.body: Root cause (SegvHunt, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/scratch/SegvHunt/ROOT-CAUSE.md): JetArena::map_insert* retains every map value as an exact-Int unless lowering marked the map's values as raw words; only U64/I64 were marked. Positive Floats >= 2.0 carry the exact-Int pointer tag bits, so jet_int_retain dereferenced the mantissa (SIGSEGV). Fixed for the main routes on fix/segv-scaling@f520ef1ef (going into tonight's dev gate). Remaining: jet_jit_map_map_values returning Float, Map.from_keys with a Float default, retain_value_roots for an embedded JetVal::Map. Criteria: (1) invert JetArena polarity so it retains only maps explicitly marked exact-Int (unsafe default removed); (2) fixtures for the three remaining routes on every tier; (3) MIR/host signature carries the value type so no route guesses.

cards.title: I1: CoreLib wrappers launder #Unsafe: safe code can call from_addr/volatile_read/volatile_write and posix sys wrappers with no gate
cards.body:
Found by SafetyNet2 on dev-05ea86f65 (repros $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/SafetyNet2/probe-mem/probe2.jet and probe3.jet).

Core/mem/mem.jet `pub fn from_addr`, `volatile_read` and `volatile_write`, and the Core/sys/sys.jet POSIX wrappers (umask, setpriority, fork, kill, setuid, stop, ...), are plain `pub fn`s with an internal `#Unsafe` block. So safe user code calls them with no gate: `volatile_write(from_addr<Int>(8), 1)` and `sys.setpriority(0, 6)` both pass `jet check`. `jet run` stops only at the runtime sentry R0801 on the Rust path, and native has no sentry.

Docs/spec/safety.md requires `#Unsafe` at the call site for pointer-from-address and volatile access, and sema's E3101 (#1465) and tests/conformance/corpus/core/sys/* expect a gate.

Criteria:
1. These wrappers are `#Unsafe("reason") pub fn`, so callers need an audited gate (E3103).
2. Every in-repo caller is migrated in one cutover.
3. UI snapshots and the core/sys conformance expectations hold.
4. A ratchet lint rejects any Core `pub fn` that wraps `#Unsafe` without being `#Unsafe` itself, unless it is audited as a safe abstraction with a recorded proof.

cards.title: Negative doubles cannot round-trip through core.encoding.binary; Float to_bits is signed; F32 bit casts missing
cards.body: Proven: binary.pack_f64le(-1.0) returns Err(Range) because math.to_bits returns a negative Int and pack_u64le rejects n < 0; unpack_f64le on the bytes of -1.0 stops with E3010 at Core/math/math.jet:185 despite a Float? Never! signature (p11_binary). to_bits(-1.0) = -4616189618054758400 (p03_math). D-FLOAT-BITS1=A is ratified but math.f32_to_bits is E1004 (p05_f32bits). Fix: implement the F32 pair; make the Float pair U64 in and out (owner nod on the signature change); golden round-trip of -1.0, -0.0, NaN payloads and subnormals.

cards.title: Stopwatch reads the wall clock: time.start()/elapsed() can go backward and saturate to 0
cards.body: time.instant() is monotonic and correct. But time.start() builds Stopwatch{start_ns: unix_ns()} and elapsed uses saturating_sub_ns(unix_ns(), start) (time.jet:23-27, 64, 199), so a wall-clock step backward reads as 0 and a forward step inflates timings. Probe b_atomic_time.jet. Fix: Stopwatch over the monotonic Instant; or delete Stopwatch and teach instant() differences (D-TIME-INSTANT1 owns time.instant).
