cards.title: Rust: reject() in a declared rule body reports E0956 instead of the registered diagnostic (UI snapshot regression)
cards.body:
**Rust: `reject(...)` in a declared rule body reports E0956 instead of the registered project diagnostic (UI snapshot regression).**

Repro: `jet check tests/ui/declared_text_block_check_failure.jet` (or `jet build`) with the release jet built from dev 595e0dca3.

Expected (tests/ui/declared_text_block_check_failure.stderr; D-META-USER1=A, D-META-DSL1=A): `Error [E0927]: Checked text is missing the required phrase` at 3:9 (`reject`), with Why/Fix from the rule.

Actual: `Error [E0956]: `__fragment: missing checked function target `reject`` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet` at the same span.

Suspected path: `Comptime::expand_derive_items` -> `Interp::exec_block` now evaluates the statement through the MIR fragment bridge (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs` `lower_mir_fragment`, module `__comptime`, function `__fragment`). The `reject` intrinsic lives only in the AST interpreter dispatch (`jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/dispatch.rs:917` -> `project_rejection`), so MIR lowering (`TIR/mir.rs:682`) finds no checked function `reject`.

Fix: route `reject` (labels code/what/why/fix, registered code) through the fragment bridge, as one compile-time mechanism (I8, I9); the Jet port (port/text-blocks@6182aa9e5) already follows the snapshot.

Proof: `cargo test --test ui -- declared_text_block_check_failure` passes; the same file through the Jet-hosted jet matches the snapshot.

Source: PortTextBlocks, $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/PortTextBlocks/HANDOFF.md (refs scratch/PortTextBlocks/ref-*.out).

cards.title: Union type switch: a struct literal passed to a union parameter reads zeros, and reusing a union argument is an ICE
cards.body:
Found while answering the owner's 'do we have a type-based switch' note (OwnerNotes1 digest section 2). Anonymous unions (D-UNIONTYPE1=A) are Jet's type switch, and two defects break it on the shared release jet dev-595e0dca3.

1. Silent wrong answer. `fn area(shape: Circle | Square) -> Float { if shape == { .Circle(c) -> { 3.0 * c.r * c.r } .Square(q) -> { q.s * q.s } } }` called as `area(Circle{r: 1.0})` prints 0.0 on `jet run`; expected 3.0. The same call with a named value (`one :: Circle{r: 1.0}; area(one)`) prints 3.0. Probes: union5.jet (literal, block arms, 0.0), union.jet (literal, one-line arms, 0.0 and 0.0), union4.jet (named, 3.0).

2. Internal compiler error. Passing the same named value to a union parameter twice (`print(area(one)); print(area2(one))`) fails `jet run` with: internal compiler error: checked TIR cannot lower to MIR ... MIR pass legality-verification rejected the program: function ... uses moved place ... at 41 (Source/lib.rs:264). `jet build` fails the same way (crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:6632). Probe: union3.jet. [INFERENCE] widening a named value into the union is lowered as a move even when the value is used again; the last-use rule (D-COPY-DEFAULT1) says a non-last use shares.

Probe files: $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/OwnerNotes1/probe/union*.jet.
cards.plan: Reduce both to TIR/MIR dumps; fix the union-widening lowering so a temporary struct literal's payload is materialized before the union tag is written, and so widening a non-last-use name copies or shares instead of moving. Add both programs as golden examples on every tier (I5, I9) and a UI/ICE regression test.

cards.title: DataTree.Object has two orders: decoded objects keep insertion order, but the public constructor sorts keys
cards.body:
Found by CorelibX3 (2026-10-07) while porting the JSON/JSONL stream folds to Jet. The native decoder builds DataTree.Object as an insertion-ordered Vec<(String, DataTree)>. The public Jet constructor takes [String:DataTree], whose JetMap is an Arc<BTreeMap> (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Core.rs ~2768), so keys come out sorted and each tree allocates. The same value kind therefore has two observable key orders depending on how it was built (I8/I9: one meaning).

The port keeps today's shipped behavior through a private raw carrier transfer (approved by Main, recorded in leaves.d) so nothing changes mid-port.

Needed: check the spec and ratified decisions for DataTree.Object's key order. If they define it, make every constructor follow it; if they don't, put the choice (insertion order vs sorted) on a ballot. Then remove the special carrier transfer if it's no longer needed.

log.text: Closed as DONE (burn-down 2026-10-17): every criterion met with evidence; see criteria. Evidence files: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/burndown/DoneEvidence/.

Also (CoreData1, 2026-10-07): native DataTree has a Bytes(Vec<u8>) variant (TOML.rs render_value ~215, YAML.rs render_scalar ~829, EncodingCodecs.rs CBOR ~394) and [U8].encode() can produce it, but Core.jet's DataTree declares only Null|Bool|Int|Float|Text|Array|Object. The port keeps shipped behavior via a compiler-private Bytes extraction (shared __tree_tag seam with JsonStreams2). Decide whether Bytes is part of DataTree's public declaration when fixing the carrier questions here.

Also: native JSONL/Data rows build an internal DataTree.TypedText(String) instead of the public DataTree.Text, and the JSONL writer rejects TypedText (State 'internal JSON carrier escaped typed decode'). The port keeps it via two raw leaves (String to TypedText transfer, carrier discriminant read). Decide whether TypedText should stay a separate carrier when fixing the order question.

cards.body:
Found by DevIntegrator11 (2026-10-07) when gate c69233829's 03-cand failed in the stage-zero Rust front end: 27 E0003 + 1 E0072 in Jet-only commits that never went through a stage-zero candidate: 1e4e3741e (Sema lifecycle, Edition.jet, 13 sites), 900d98c75 (CLI complexity/architecture lint port, 9), ef54390fd (CLI structure/Core projections, 3), b4056b4c6 (Resolution.jet:118, 1). Classes: `module`/`effect` used as names, inline arm tables (`if x == {.A(v) -> .. else -> ..}`), a `U8{48}` operand, a fn-lambda argument, a return arm, an inline `if` in a struct field.

For today's landing the sites were rewritten to forms stage zero accepts (TrainFix13, Jet-only). Still needed: for each class, check the ratified syntax. cards.title: Native lowering use-after-free: last_use_moves reads an inline List header from a freed Option<List<Link>> wrapper
cards.body: Found 2026-10-07 by SeedWork1 (determinism probe), diagnosed by NativeInteg2 from coredump 3579359 without rerun. On current dev, the freestanding native build of Examples stem last_use_moves SIGSEGVs deterministically: at 0x4015c0 lowered code calls drop.Option<List<Link>> (0x402240), freeing the 24-byte optional wrapper; the loop backedge then copies the inline List header (walk, RIP 0x401655) through an alias into the released wrapper (RCX 0x7ffff7fdb000, already unmapped). Root: native lowering's ownership lifetime for inline moved payloads / Option unwrap (the drop is emitted before the last use through the alias). The historical pack-linked pass was masked by malloc keeping freed bytes readable; the mmap-backed path exposes it. This is an I1 safety defect in generated native code, not runtime or nondeterminism. Owner: NativeTasks3 (inline moved-payload/Option-unwrap class) via NativeInteg2. Acceptance: last_use_moves passes natively with exact golden output; the safety net's native ASan/use-after-free run includes this stem and the whole moved-payload/Option-unwrap class; a fixture covering the backedge alias shape.

cards.title: Generic drop glue never calls Close: Close types inside generic containers are freed without Close (secrets not zeroized)
cards.body: In the Jet compiler, generic drop glue only drops fields and frees (Lower.jet ~2972-3027, Values.jet ~305-322); scope_end_close_function returns None for a generic T, and explicit close needs a nominal owner. So a value of a Close type held in a generic container (ExpiringSecret<T>, [Secret], Option<T>...) is freed without running its Close: crypto secrets are not zeroized on the native tier. The Rust tier relies on Rust Drop (ExpiringSecret.rs:27, CryptoEntropy.rs:170-173). Fix: monomorphization-time drop glue calls the instantiated T's Close when it has one; witnesses on every tier. Blocks the Core Clock/Expiring/vault source port (CoreReview7). Owner: native line (NativeLead13 assigns).

cards.title: Shared<T> payload Close is not run when the last reference is released
cards.body: Native Shared<T> is an opaque runtime handle, so releasing the last reference frees the payload without running its Close (the generic drop-glue fix #4792 can't reach inside the provider). Affects any Shared<X> where X has a Close. Fix: the Shared runtime release takes a payload drop-glue function pointer generated at monomorphization (the #4792 drop role) and calls it on last release. Owners: runtime provider ABI (RuntimeJet10's line) + Lower glue pointer (NativeSlice5). Doesn't block #4792 (ExpiringSecret uses a local wrapper Close). Found by NativeLead13.

cards.title: SOUNDNESS: Core/HostServices.rs jet_ui_host_scope erases the host lifetime (use-after-free) and re-entry aliases &mut
cards.body: Found by CoreProof1 in the #4851 unsafe-ratchet audit (write-up $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/CoreProof1/UI-HOST-DEFECT.md). Core/HostServices.rs jet_ui_host_scope(&mut dyn JetUiHost) (:1801) returns a JetUiHostScope with no lifetime / PhantomData (:1787-1789) and erases the host lifetime via transmute (:1806-1807), storing a raw pointer in TLS. Safe code can keep the guard after dropping the host; Core ui/host.jet:154 __capabilities → jet_ui_with_current_host (:1822) then dereferences freed memory. Separately, :1818 releases the RefCell borrow before body(&mut *ptr), so a recursive with_current_host creates aliasing &mut to the same host (UB). Minimal fix: tie JetUiHostScope to the host lifetime ('a + PhantomData<&'a mut dyn JetUiHost>), keep the borrow across body or refuse re-entry; regression tests for both (compile-fail for the escaped guard, runtime refusal for re-entry). Allowed under the native freeze as a defect fix. The Jet runtime port of this host scope must not copy the defect. #4851's ui-host regions are BLOCKED on this.

cards.body: From RuntimeJet19 via CoreReview4: the seed's jet_crypto_zeroize (generated CAbiRoutes:12825) wipes a COPY made by list_in, never the caller's storage. cards.title: StopCleanup scope internal ABI: one contract for #4881, MirStop and #4884
cards.body: Owner: RtUnwind1 (implementation); co-rulers NativeLead24-2 + RuntimeJet22-2 + RtTrapPub2-2. Internal ABI inside approved E2 scope (no public API, no owner ballot). Blocks #4881 (task panic stop rail), MirStop (MirStopFix2-2) and #4884 (native List.sort_by kernel). Current proposal (RuntimeJet22-2 update, 7 entry points, no 8th): stop_domain() -> I64 with NONE 0 / ROOT 1 / TASK 2, REPLACING root_active; derived from the actual TCB / control state plus proven task-cleanup provenance after body_leave, never a bare control / TLS flag. Root: begin / save (32), publish_rendered, take_stop(code_out), leave. Cleanup: cleanup_enter(delivered) -> saved flags, cleanup_leave(saved flags). Still to finalize (RtTrapPub2-2): the owned SaveToken and its drop; nested-root inheritance; double panic during cleanup aborts (unmasked); raw kind 1..4 reports; captured-root exit code 112 reusing SENTRY_RUNTIME_EXIT_CODE where it applies. Finalizer drain runs in REGISTRATION order (spec 879-883; Outcome.rs .rev() fixed under #4881): all callbacks registered before the first normal-finalizer Stop run under real StopCleanup; only work registered after the stop is excluded. Acceptance: NativeLead24-2 + RuntimeJet22-2 + RtTrapPub2-2 each log approval of the exact final signatures on this card; then consumers implement against it with no private ABI, Shield, fake flag or fallback; one meaning on every tier (I9).

log.text: Closed as DONE (burn-down 2026-10-17): every criterion met with evidence; see criteria. Evidence files: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/burndown/DoneEvidence/.

Root kind-1 ruling (RuntimeJet22-2 + NativeLead24-2, joint YES): kind 1 (cancellation) is UNREACHABLE for ROOT, as a source invariant. A fresh Root control is private and unregistered (flags 16 / 48 zero); canonical cancel targets Task / group children (+8) or registered Observe controls; Parallel uses fresh unregistered chunks; the CAbi publish helper's real callers (212-295) are only BudgetFuel 3 / BudgetDepth 4 / replay despite the broad enum match. Producer and publisher gates ASSERT that a Root never carries kind 1; Task and bare Session keep kind 1; ordinary outside-task cancellation keeps the cooperative None / false / Closed meaning; the generic FAULT Root catch is separated from cancel (Task / interrupt / test). An unexpected Root take of kind 1 is a HOST DEFECT: never exit 0 / 70, a fake report or a success default. Kinds 2 (E3003 -> 70) and 3 / 4 (private record -> 82 / 83) as approved. Exact source / gates / tests review still owed.

APPROVED by RtTrapPub2-2: YES to the exact 7 signatures + FIFO finalizers; adopts the binding layout ROOT 1 / TASK 2 / CLEANUP 4 / INHERITED 8 / ORIGIN 16 / MASK_KIND (kind << 8) & 0x700 and equal-kind masking; its earlier proposal is SUPERSEDED. ORIGIN 16 minted only from the actual body flag or a prior genuine Task cleanup; never a role from a bare control. SaveToken = owned opaque flags (zero is valid); its drop always calls cleanup_leave exactly once; the Rust MIR owns the wrapper; no heap allocation or runtime-record take. ALL THREE APPROVALS IN (NativeLead24-2, RuntimeJet22-2, RtTrapPub2-2): contract FINAL. Remaining before close: implementation (RtTrapPub2-2 = TCB / scheduler / scope side; RtUnwind1 = CAbi / Core bridge, Outcome.rs FIFO drain, #4881 composition), the Root kind 1..4 report / code 112 mapping (grounded in source, never default 0), and the native proof.

Final state (NativeLead24-2 APPROVED): binding layout ROOT 1, TASK 2, CLEANUP 4, INHERITED 8, TASK_CLEANUP_ORIGIN 16, MASK_KIND 0x700. ORIGIN 16 is captured from the actual body flag (64 = 1) BEFORE body_leave, kept through the real post-body capture drop, and the opaque old flags are then restored. RtTrapPub2-2's alternative (ROOT 1 / CLEANUP 2 / static Origin 4, and the mask covering all pending kinds) is REJECTED: only an equal genuine old kind is masked; 1 -> 2 and a new kind 5 stay visible. RtUnwind1's consumer doesn't read the bits. Same 7 approved signatures. RtTrapPub2-2 implements this.

APPROVED by NativeLead24-2 (exact signatures, 7 exports, owner RtUnwind1): root_begin(save32: I64) -> I64; stop_domain() -> I64 (0 None / 1 Root / 2 Task; replaces the unlanded root_active); root_publish_rendered(bytes: I64, len: I64, code: I64) -> Bool; root_take_stop(control: I64, code_out: I64) -> I64 (owned Stop); root_leave(control: I64, save32: I64) -> Void; session_cleanup_enter(delivered_at_entry: I64) -> I64; session_cleanup_leave(saved_flags: I64) -> Void. Existing stop_take_message / drop reused, no alias. Token = exact prior Control flags, LIFO on the same control / thread; no allocation, status clear or record steal. Flags ROOT 1, TASK 2, CLEANUP 4, INHERITED 8, MASK_KIND 0x700 (+ TASK_CLEANUP_ORIGIN 16 per the earlier refinement); the mask holds ONLY the genuine delivered kind present at entry (0 = the first new stop stays visible); a new kind stays visible; the publisher consults unmasked Shield-aware delivery / inherited unwinding, and a second panic aborts. Task role comes from actual constructor / cleanup provenance (no non-null or TLS spoof). Nested roots save / restore the 4 TCB words (control, shield, depth, body); parent records untouched; real ancestor delivery / inherited unwinding survives a fresh status 0. Finalizers per callback FIFO: all registered before the Stop, including late-queued; no RefCell held across a call / drop; captures after the Stop are dropped, not registered. Root kind 1..4 report / code producer proof still owed (not a signature blocker). MirStop and CopyPareto1 may implement against this now. Approvals: NativeLead24-2 YES, RuntimeJet22-2 (consensus author) YES, RtTrapPub2-2 pending (ruled: the logged contract binds unless it shows a concrete failing scenario).

Refinement (NativeLead24-2 via RuntimeJet22-2; signatures unchanged, still 7 exports): new Control flag bit TASK_CLEANUP_ORIGIN 16. stop_domain returns TASK 2 after body_leave only when TASK 2 + CLEANUP 4 + ORIGIN 16 are all set, never from a static Task flag, non-null pointer or raw kind alone. cleanup_enter sets ORIGIN 16 only when the actual TCB body flag (64) is 1, or keeps a genuine existing origin. The Task finalizer calls cleanup_enter(raw status) BEFORE body_leave, holds the opaque old-flags token through the genuine post-body capture drop, then cleanup_leave restores the old flags.

FINAL signatures (RuntimeJet22-2 consensus, NativeLead24-2 aligned on the domain; RtTrapPub2-2 approval still to be logged). cleanup_enter(delivered_at_entry: I64) -> I64 returns the exact saved Control flags; cleanup_leave(saved_flags: I64) -> Void restores exactly (no allocation, no record steal, no status clear). Control flag bits: ROOT 1, TASK 2, CLEANUP 4, INHERITED_STOP 8, MASK_KIND = kind << 8 (0x700). The mask holds only a genuine old kind 1..5; 0 = none; a new kind stays visible; publishers check unmasked, Shield-aware delivered / inherited double panic. Real Task creation sets TASK 2; a bare control role is 0. stop_domain() -> I64: NONE 0, ROOT 1 (real Root flag, body 0), TASK 2 (actual body, or real Task cleanup after body_leave); replaces root_active; export count stays 7. Root begin inherits the actual ancestor's Inherited, or Cleanup + nonzero Mask; parent record retained; save32 restores all 4 TCB fields. Finalizers run FIFO: everything registered before the Stop, including pre-Stop late-queued work; work after the Stop is excluded and its captures are dropped under real cleanup. Still held before a full run: Root kind 1..4 reports + whole-provider proof.

cards.title: Cleanup order differs between compiler halves: Rust TIR->MIR interleaves scope guards with defer closes (D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1 says explicit defers first)
cards.body: Found by GoldenSquad2 (golden stem cleanup_matrix). The Jet Builder (Codegen Builder.jet 1395-1401) runs explicit DeferredCall cleanups in reverse first, then the automatic DropPlace guard. The Rust TIR -> MIR path (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mir.rs 7237-7262) registers the ScopeGuard as DeferredCleanup::Guard, and 7078-7094 partitions only DropPlace as automatic, so guards INTERLEAVE with defer closes. D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1 (docs ~2573) states explicit defers run first. One meaning across tiers (I9): fix the Rust half to the ratified order (CoreReview5-2-2 confirms the exact law text first), with a regression asserting identical cleanup order on both halves. Owner: MirStopFix2-2 (editor of Builder.jet and TIR/mir.rs). No oracle changed toward baseline RAII.

log.text: Closed as OBSOLETE (burn-down 2026-10-17, owner rules). The divergent half was Rust TIR->MIR (mir.rs), deleted with Rust. The Jet Builder is the sole half; the ordinary-exit order is owner ballot #4902

Law check (CoreReview5-2-2): S63 / D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1/2 (syntax-decisions 2567-2582) say deferred closes run in reverse order at EVERY scope exit with automatic cleanup as the safety net, but do NOT say explicit defers run before ALL automatic drops / guards. Only the explicit process.exit / os.stop boundary is ratified: core-library 1683-1691 'Deferred closes run before scope guards' (each group LIFO; atexit FIFO after cleanup, spec 854-857), so the explicit-stop fixture order is close2, close1, guard2, guard1, then atexit. Scope of this card is therefore the EXPLICIT STOP path only (fix the Rust half there if it interleaves). The relative defer-vs-guard order on ordinary return / Err / panic / task cancel is NOT ratified: owner ballot filed separately; no oracle or code change for those paths until it's decided.

cards.title: Owner ruling: __ prefix allowed for compiler internals
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-09: I am totally fine with __ as a prefix for compiler internals. The current lexer reserves __-prefixed names (E0067) for ordinary user sources and already exempts embedded Core via parse_generated_source (JetParser Entry.jet:72-76). Scope of this ruling: compiler-internal sources (embedded Core, the Jet runtime pack Compiler/JetRuntime, and the compiler's own packages when the native compiler builds itself) may use __ names; user code stays reserved. Implementation: extend the existing source-class exemption, no new mechanism, no renames. Owner: CoreJetpackFix (driver/catalog side) with ParserSemaRestore (JetParser).

No exemption extension was needed. The ruling stands for future compiler-internal __ use; extend via the existing generated-source origin if it becomes needed.

cards.title: Owner decision: duplicating an already-held Directory handle (Jetpack resolver needs two owners)
cards.body: Blocks the self-host zero-error gate (r12 Jetpack group). Jetpack Resolver.checked_directory("."/"") returns CheckedDirectory{handle: self.root_handle.copy()} while the resolver keeps root_handle. checked_root_package/complete_checked_package return CheckedPackage carrying member.directory AND build a scoped resolver with a duplicate handle (PackageFacts.compose_configs_checked/checked_members_in). OverlayAuthority.open stores the resolver plus the checked root handle. The code has been written this way since 54f24a1 (#3590, then ~handle); 133d0d4 was only the .copy() codemod. Core Directory {path, handle: Int} is a non-copyable resource (closed on drop), so .copy() is rejected, correctly. Options: (A) a Core Directory.duplicate() -[FS]> Directory IOError! that duplicates the held descriptor (no new authority, no pathname reopen; Core already has an internal fd-duplication leaf for ProcessSpec, files.jet ~452); (B) redesign Jetpack's representation around one owner with borrowed Directory carriers through the PackageFacts compose/member APIs (larger change, outside Resolver/Overlay); (C) reopen by path (rejected: authority violation). Recommendation: A. Context: 2026-10-09 CliR12Fix.JetpackRepair, family of #4935.

questions.text: this is not at all clear to me, please rework. it seems like having a trait would be useful
questions.answer: Reworked (ballot updated, fresh beginner + adversarial reader passes folded in). Plain version: today a generic function can copy a value that owns a resource (a file, a secret) without any warning, so it gets closed twice; copying it directly is already an error. Recommended A is the trait you suggested: a built-in Copyable trait, derived automatically for every copyable type. A generic that copies T must say T: Copyable, and the error message offers that fix; generics that only move T still accept resources; #!Copyable lets a type refuse copying. It reuses the existing copy checker, so there is one rule. B (infer the need from the body) and C (Swift-style copyable-by-default with an opt-out) are compared side by side. Migration: the 3 bogus T: Clone bounds in Core/math/random.jet and 1 in Core/web/table.jet become T: Copyable.

cards.title: Lean native binaries: link only reachable JetRT and Core code; full release is the smallest possible binary
cards.body:
Owner order (2026-10-14): a native binary must contain only the JetRT (runtime pack) and Core functions it reaches. Using print must pull in print and its callees, not the whole Core library or JetRT. Today the compiler already lowers only the Core source bodies a program reaches (Pipeline.jet, #3980), but JetRT is one monolithic object (jet_runtime.pack.o), so the linker keeps all of it.

Plan: emit one ELF section per function and per data item (commit 9e3eaee8d, recorded in #4988) and link with --gc-sections, so the linker drops everything unreachable from the entry. Profiles: full release = smallest possible binary (gc-sections, no debug info, strip); dev and non-full release keep useful but lean debug info for reachable code only.

Acceptance: a hello-world native binary contains no JetRT/Core symbols it does not reach (nm diff against the reachable set), full release hello is measured and recorded as a paired size cell, and every golden still matches on every tier.

cards.title: Native backend miscompiles user Never calls in value positions (missing block, phi drop obligations)
cards.body:
## Defect
Found 2026-10-17 by ReviewCliPorts-2 while vetting round 4 (a0_004). Both a0_001 (r29 stage3) and a0_003 stage 1 miscompile:
- (A) a value-returning function whose last statement is a call to a user `-> Never` function, e.g. `fn f(n: Int) -> Out { if n > 5 -> finish(..); finish(..) }` or a value match whose arm tail is a Never call: `LIR lint bN: jump to missing block bM`; a Never call as the only statement: `LIR lint b-1: function has no blocks`.
- (B) `x :: opt ?? { d :: ...; finish(..) }` (a block with statements before the Never call): `E3001 panic: Jet codegen phi joins incompatible drop obligations` (jet_codegen_phi_ownership).
Working shapes: plain `x ?? finish(..)`, a match-expression arm `{ finish(..) }` when the function does not end in a Never call, statement-level finish after a statement match.

Repros and README: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/r4vet/never-shapes/.

## Expected
A Never call in any statement or value position lowers to a terminator with no fall-through block and no join; the type checker already accepts these shapes, so codegen must too (I3: codegen lowers what sema established).

## Bootstrap note
Round-4 source avoids shapes A/B (ExitTail rewrite) because every available seed miscompiles them; fix in round 5 and only then allow them in compiler source.

cards.title: Nested pattern payload is closed before it is consumed (`held == .Val(.Full(secret, label))` then `consume(^secret)`)
cards.body:
## Defect
Found 2026-10-17 by the a0_004 fixture gate (Examples/features/memory/move_match_payload, nested() case, id 5). The payload-take fix 68266af7c covers a top-level payload pattern: round 4 no longer double-closes secret 1 (a0_001 does). Under a NESTED pattern, `held == .Val(.Full(secret, label))` followed by `consume(^secret)`, the payload is still closed before `consume` runs: output shows `close 5` before `consume 5`. a0_001 has the same defect, so it is pre-existing, not an a0_004 regression.

## Expected
A payload bound through any depth of pattern nesting is owned by the binding when the subject is moved (D-CARET-MOVE / R6 rule): exactly one Close, after the consumer, never before. Fix the payload-take bookkeeping to follow nested patterns; the move_match_payload golden is the witness (its expected output already states the correct order).

cards.title: Checker: `^x` of a borrowed place in a call argument silently deep-copies (no diagnostic)
cards.body:
## Defect
Found 2026-10-17 by CopyHunt (copyscan.mjs census of fc711cef0, runtime probes): `^x` where x is a read/write parameter, a field or element of one, or a `::` view compiles with NO diagnostic when it appears as a CALL ARGUMENT, and lowers as a deep copy of the value. In binding position the same move reports E0201 as specified. This is the mechanism behind the round-3 comptime regression (200ad57c5: borrowed program tables + environment moved into thread state = deep copy every pass, 394 s + 11.5 GB). Census: 11 move-of-borrow sites in the compiler assembly.

## Expected
A move out of a borrow is rejected in every position with the E0201 family (registered code, what/why/fix teaching `.copy()` for an intended copy or `^` on an owned value), with UI snapshots; the compiler source has zero such sites; the receipt gate `copyscan.mjs --kinds move-of-borrow --min-weight heap` reports 0 hot rows. Fix location: Ownership/Checks.jet sema_ownership_mark_move_as (Jet side).

cards.title: Codegen: `if c -> panic(local)` drops the panic message before RequireStop uses it (use after free on panic paths)
cards.body:
## Defect
Found 2026-10-18 03:00 by the round-5 chain (first LIR lint over FINAL LIR at self-compile scale). MIR for `fault :: f(); if fault != "" -> panic(fault)`: `b1: v8 = read p2` (the message), then the scope-exit path `v9 = move-out p2; drop v9`, then `RequireStop [v8]` - the stop receives the dropped message. Reproduced identically on round-4 code (s1-r4d), the relinked O0 round-4 compiler and the round-5 seed (repro /tmp/r5lint/run.jet). Invisible to the pre-pass lint (v18/v17 are distinct block-param ids); O1 block-param forwarding merges them and the final-LIR lint reports `use of v9 after it was moved or dropped`.

## Expected
A diverging calls arguments stay valid: scope-exit drops before a Never call never drop a place the calls arguments read (move the last-use read into the call, or skip those drops on the diverging path), keeping D-PANICROOT1/#4881 Close order for other locals. Fixture: the repro builds lint-clean at O1 and prints the message.

cards.title: Self-host chain: 1-thread determinism (det1) check deferred until self-compile takes seconds
cards.body:
## Owner ruling 2026-10-18 06:58
The det1 check (s2 compiles the compiler at --threads 1; its jet.o must be byte-identical to s3 at --threads 16) is deferred: at current speed it costs ~35 min of a single core per chain (2,050 CPU s). Re-enable it as a release gate once a self-compile takes seconds (target a0_007 < 5 s), when it costs about a minute.

## What it covers that s2==s3 does not
- thread-count independence of every parallel merge (sema bodies, lowering workers, object waves) under a very different schedule;
- the serial single-thread code paths (compiler_threads_single) at full scale.

## Until then
s2==s3 compares two 16-thread runs. Cheap partial coverage: the fixture-gate determinism case (1 vs 16 threads on small units). a0_005 tagged without det1 (det1 frozen mid-run on r5-chain, not failed). Chain script: add SKIP_DET1 / re-enable when this card closes.

cards.title: Authority cutover: allow/deny directly under authority (D-EFFECTS-BLOCK1=B), one carrier, one vocabulary
cards.body:
## Outcome

A package states the effects it may use in one top-level block, `effects: { allow: [...], deny: [...] }`, instead of `authority: { holds: { allow: [...], deny: [...] } }`. The rest of `authority` (grants, needs, trust, providers) is unchanged.

## Source

Owner request 2026-10-20 (accepted and denied effects should not sit two layers deep under authority.holds). Ballot D-EFFECTS-BLOCK1 records the choice; it amends D-AUTHORITY-MANIFEST1 and restores the D-EFFBUDGET1 key.

## Scope once ratified

The Jet package parser (Jetpack/PackageModel), the syntax registry (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax), lockfile and ledger shape, jet init and jet fix templates, diagnostics text, spec and docs, and a mechanical rewrite of about 1,600 holds sites in 1,433 files (mostly tests/cases, Examples and Tools/agent-eval).

log.text: Follow-ups landed as 803195f620 (O0Load-3). Changes: the effect vocabulary is generated into Registry/EffectVocabulary.jet; E1803's registry row no longer carries both an edit and a no-fix reason, so jet fix no longer stops with E3001; the Golden harness strips the staged source root; jet fix --all no longer hangs on a file outside a package. FIXED_POINT 169e8ed5ed137503, t1 SAME, traps 0. Authority testkit: PASS 9 -> 11, FAIL 26 -> 24, 5 better and 0 worse against the dev-base run. The 24 remaining failures predate #5070 and are tracked on #5923.

2026-10-23 Main: Landed 9d9a2a1b73 (step 1 + D-AUTH-AMBIENT3 + D-AUTHORITY-DENYROW1) and dbc7532c47 (step 2) after seed a0_018 (FIXED_POINT ba404f357c73e9ad, 0 golden regressions). Main rerun: testkit cases --filter authority, at dbc7532c47 with its jet vs c324db24be with its jet: identical per-case statuses (9 pass, 26 fail, 19 known-failing, 3 refused, 2 error, 1 unexpected pass on both). The 26 pre-existing failures go to O0Load's #5070 follow-up patch.

Bootstrap note: the chain builds Compiler with the seed, which reads Compiler/JetCli/package.jet and refuses flat allow: (E1221). So the cutover lands in two stages: stage 1 migrates everything flat except the files the seed build reads, with one marked bridge in the driver and PackageModel that still reads authority.holds; Main then rotates the seed; stage 2 deletes the bridge and flattens JetCli/package.jet the same day. The bridge has no other callers.

D-EFFECTS-BLOCK1 ratified B by owner instruction (2026-10-24): allow/deny sit directly in authority; holds is removed. Proposal: Docs/proposals/authority-streamline.md (O0Load-3 audit, landing). The cutover also fixes these probe-confirmed defects: (1) the inline package {} block and package.jet must be one parser and meaning (package.jet = the package {} body, implicitly wrapped); inline is labelled 'package.jet default' and inline errors collapse to a generic E1362; the driver refuses authority.grants/trust/providers in both carriers. (2) Time.Wait in allow is inert and sleep needs Time, contradicting D-AUTH-AMBIENT2. (3) FS.Bogus is accepted, contradicting D-EFF2. (4) The root list has 5 hard-coded copies; Prelude/Effects.jet becomes the only table. (5) The --deny-wins rule is unreachable (E2102 fires first). (6) grants enforcement, trust.services and policy.effects have no production consumer. Pending ballots that shape the rest: D-AUTH-AMBIENT3 (allow adds to the ambient floor), D-AUTHORITY-DENYROW1 (package deny becomes a compile-time prohibition). Greenfield: migrate every example, test and spec section in one cutover.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.title: Rust exit E0: Rust→Jet parity ledger (the deletion gate)

log.text: Closed as a duplicate of #4717: Owner ruling 2026-10-22: the deletion lands once every Jet gate passes without Rust; that gate is #4717's acceptance.

Golden vs reference conflicts: the master Rust oracle rejects 3 examples whose goldens (unchanged in master since 09-30 and 10-08) expect success: loop_task_handles E0405 (Task of Int Never!), task_controls E0112 (print of Int Never!), variadics_eval_order E0764. Rule applied: the examples and goldens are the executable contract (AGENTS I5), so the Jet port follows the goldens (a total task body gives Task of Int; labelled calls through a function value keep its declared parameter names) and the Rust behavior is recorded as the defect. Oracle: rust-oracle-master debug build.

Owner decision 2026-10-21 (sequencing, Split): (1) freeze old-backend work (MIR/LIR/x64 lowering fixes and backend performance) except what keeps self-hosting and the release chain alive; backend golden failures (~85 of 1032 at m-7: MIR lint, optimizer, 58 E2104 lowering gaps) and backend performance are fixed in the new IR; (2) start the single-IR work now in parallel: detailed plan, then the spike (Core + examples through the new IR, go/no-go on speed and identical output, differential vs the old backend); (3) keep porting front end, Core, runtime and CLI to green goldens (837 of 1032 failures are front end, all carried over) - the green front-end corpus is the oracle for the IR move; (4) remove Rust after the goldens are green on the new IR (Rust stays as the reference until then); (5) script ports continue for correctness; the faster-than-original gate is measured on the new IR.

Owner priority 2026-10-21 ~13:15: finish ASAP - remove Rust and the other-language scripts, with Jet passing the goldens on the self-hosted compiler, then move to the single-IR architecture (#5073). Critical path: (1) full golden+UI corpus green on the self-hosted compiler (rerun on chain m-13 at HEAD now; m-7 had 1032 real failures); (2) every test package under jet test (B4); (3) Rust-only tooling replaced; (4) held cutover patches rebased. Proposed E gate (owner decision pending): corpus green + each remaining ABSENT parity row either ported or owner-approved obsolete in grouped lists. Backend/codegen parity is limited to what the goldens need, since D-ARCH-IR1 replaces that layer; full effort on sema, parser, Core, runtime and CLI.

Owner directive 2026-10-21: when porting the Rust compiler to Jet, port the compiler FUNCTIONALITY, not Rust memory semantics. cards.title: JetIR miscompile: heap corruption (wild write) after an unknown package.jet field
cards.body:
Repro environment: `JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY=$(cat ~/.local/share/jet-seeds/a0_010/IDENTITY) JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT=$JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Goldens/k/t5 prlimit --core=0 --stack=1073741824:1073741824`
- **Repro (1.4 s):** a dir with `package.jet` = `name: "x"` / `version: "1"` / `bogus: 1`, then `jet fmt --check package.jet` (or `jet check run.jet`).
  - Ready-made dirs: /tmp/g5ill/p2 (unknown top-level field, UnknownField), p3 (`policy: { bogus: false }`, BadMemoryPolicy), p4 (`policy: { auto_derive: false }`, RetiredPolicyField = tests/ui/auto_derive_policy_invalid).
  - Script: `/tmp/g5ill/fmt.sh <jet> /tmp/g5ill/p2`.
  - Same crash: Examples/features/packages/inline_deps/run.jet (it passes under JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1 because the heap layout changes).
- **These manifest errors do NOT crash:** MissingRecord (p5 `targets: [quantum]`), LintPolicyCode (p7), InvalidValue (p8-p10 `runtime: ...`). All of them go through pkg_e1206(detail). The crashing ones use pkg_e1206_unknown_field / the BadMemoryPolicy and RetiredPolicyField arms of pkg_manifest_parse_diagnostic (Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Manifest/Manifest.jet:286).
- **Kernel trap:** general protection fault in the JetRuntime allocator.
  - ip 0x34e8e79 = `alloc_slab_take`+0x269 (plain run).
  - ip 0x382deb8 = `alloc_try_validated`+0x248 (JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1, and inline_deps).
  - The main thread corrupts the free list. JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1 never traps at a free: it crashes in the allocation path first, with no "jet checked allocator" report. So this is an out-of-bounds or wild write, not a double free.
  - The crash happens after the manifest error, while Core sources load (strace: last read is core.files, then SIGSEGV).
- **First bad seed:** seeds a0_008 and a0_009 (Rust/Lower era) run p2 cleanly. a0_010 (the first JetIR-built seed) crashes, so this is a JetIR miscompile.
- **Reduction:** a standalone 130-line model of the parse, propagation and diagnostic (/tmp/g5ill/r1/run.jet) does not reproduce. The next step needs a jet_pkg_model-linked probe (medium build) or a debugger; no gdb/lldb on the box.

log.text: SpeedLane root cause (gdb on seed a0_010, p2 repro): this miscompile is seed-only and dev already fixes it. apply_field returns a 16-byte Result<(), PackageParseError> box (allocated at PackageParse.jet apply_field, UnknownField). pkg_parse_common propagates the failure by returning that same pointer as its own 824-byte Result<PackageFacts, PackageParseError> box (seed disasm pkg_parse_common+8118..8300: tag!=Ok -> mov %rbx,%rax; ret). jet_cli_fmt_package_manifest then drops it through jet_ir_drop_3519 -> jet_rt_free(ptr, 0x338=824, 8), which files a class-small block in the 824 class. A later 512-byte diagnostic_render_with buffer receives that 320-byte slot, and diagnostic_push_text overruns it into the next chunk header, which is the free-list head that holds " `build:". Fixed in dev by 7b183aa47 (#5095: ir_try_reraise passes an Err box through only when ir_box_bytes match, otherwise it reboxes). The current compiler reboxes at this exact site (s2 disasm: drop callee box, jet_rt_alloc(0x338,8), tag 0, payload). k/t5 s1 crashes because the seed compiled it. Proof (g5206/proof.sh, p2/p3/p4 fmt --check plus inline_deps check, plain and JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1): seed a0_010 = SIGSEGV 7/8; SpeedLane s2 builds of HEAD-era trees (runs/c11/s2, runs/c11/s2base) = clean E1206 diagnostics 8/8 each (inline_deps rc=1 E1253 offline, no crash). The crash goes away at the next seed rotation; until then avoid s1 binaries for crash repros.

criteria.text: The 1.4 s repro (/tmp/g5ill/fmt.sh on p2/p3/p4) and Examples/features/packages/inline_deps run clean, plain and under JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1, with the current dev compiler and with the next rotated seed
criteria.evidence: SpeedLane g5206/proof.sh: dev s2 (runs/c11/s2 and s2base) clean 8/8; seed a0_010 crashes 7/8. Root cause fixed by 7b183aa47 (#5095 ir_try_reraise reboxes when Result box sizes differ); the next seed rotation carries the fix.

cards.title: jet run (O0 in-memory) intermittent SIGSEGV: generics/typed_ast, crypto/crypto_error_run
cards.body: Found by O0Image 2026-10-23. jet run Examples/features/generics/typed_ast.jet segfaults intermittently (rc 139): seed a0_012 1 of 20 runs; HEAD-based s2 compilers about 1 of 6-9 (0 of 20 in another batch). crypto/crypto_error_run fails the same way, more often. A nondeterministic crash in the O0 run path, which blocks the 20:00 O0 completion. Suspects: the in-memory image loader (mapping/relocation/W^X race), thread shutdown/atexit ordering, uninitialized stack slots or pads at O0, address-dependent hashing. Repro: loop 50x, capture the fault address with R12 backtraces, compare jet build + run of the same file (does the AOT binary also crash?). Owner: O0Load.

log.text: Post-land proof on seed a0_015 (rotated from 148dd1ebf4, FIXED POINT s2==s3 a0ab10f18a344d8c, goldens 687->690 passed, 0 regressions): Examples typed_ast stress, 1000 runs (run-seq, run-par x6, check-seq, check-par x6, built binary par; 200 each), 0 crashes, all rc 0. The same harness on install-latest built by the old seed a0_014 crashed 42/1000, as expected: the fix is in codegen, so the compiler stays affected until a fixed compiler builds it. Fix: 73a48eba05 (ir_write_base gives every write place through a recursive edge its own wrapper) + a535df3110 (example covering every write-place kind).

ROOT FOUND AND FIXED (O0Load, out/rootfix.patch, queued): a JetIR miscompile. A write through a recursive-edge field (JetSema Binder.jet:299 sema_call_mark_written, value.flags.binder_label = ..) went into the wrapper box that every copy shares without a count; ir_write_base gave the place its own wrapper only when an index was on the path. Parallel sema threads then double-released the shared field (the SEGVs, allocator free-list corruption, derived Node.compare ICEs). The bug also shows single-threaded: the new example printed second/second. Proof: FIXED POINT s2==s3 c32d631904e0ab3c; stress on s2 0/800 failures (baseline 8/200, 6/200, 6/200 SIGSEGV and 5/100 checked-alloc ICEs); memory goldens run+build vs install-latest differ only in the new example (passed vs no-match); --release output == golden. Close after it lands and the post-land stress repeats clean.

Correction (O0Load): the JetIR write-window value bug is real and fixed (out/5480.patch, chain s2==s3 e6930d5d3ff6720e; example and repros correct on run/build/--release), but it is NOT the crash cause. With that s2: jet check typed_ast crashes 8/200, jet check r.jet 6/200 (allocator free-list null in sema_* allocations), jet run typed_ast 6/200, and checked-alloc still shows the derived Node.compare ICEs. A second cross-thread race remains. Next, in parallel: a checked-alloc owner-thread stamp to trap cross-thread frees; an all-atomic-RC diagnostic build; an audit of JetSema globals and caches. The value fix lands separately under its own proof.

Root cause (O0Load): a JetIR value-semantics bug, not a sema data race. A write window (if &e == .V(x) -> x = ..., or &payload passed on) writes into a shared payload box in place. The box was made unique only when the subject is an owned local, not for a write param, a field/index place or a nested recursive edge. User-visible: a :: Pair(Lit 1, 2); b := a; bump(&b) changes a, on seeds a0_010/011/012. In the compiler, sema's AST rewrites mutate shared derive-template AST across parallel body-check threads, which gives the SEGV and the checked-alloc ICEs. Fix in progress: out/5480.patch (ir_window_subject/ir_window_box make the subject's box unique at its place and store it back). Close needs: an example with goldens for every place kind on run/build/--release, a sibling sweep, and the repro looped 200× with zero crashes.

O0Load: typed_ast crashed in 9 of 150 jet runs (seq 2, par 3, JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=1 4) and 0 of 150 AOT runs; crypto_error_run 0 of 300. The core shows the SIGSEGV is in the COMPILER: jet_rt_string_drop(0xc8a) <- drop glue <- Binder_sema_call_mark_written <- sema_call_bind_args <- ... <- CheckProgram_sema_check_bodies_parallel, with 4 other sema body-check threads mid alloc/free. A heap-corruption race in parallel sema body checking, so it affects jet build/check of user programs too. Next: --threads 1 vs default on 100 runs; a compiler linked with the R12 runtime for self-backtraces; a poison-on-free/RC-header-check runtime mode for a deterministic first-bad-drop.

cards.title: Examples/features fn_dispatch_map aborts: 'memory allocation of N bytes failed' on every compiler incl. the seed
cards.body: Found by O0Comptime during the ctfail compiler-diff (2026-10-23): Examples/features fn_dispatch_map aborts with 'memory allocation of N bytes failed' on every compiler, including seed a0_012. Pre-existing. Likely a runaway size computation (a garbage length reaching alloc) or unbounded growth in function-value dispatch through a Map. Needs: the exact N, a backtrace (R12 fault reports are now available), the root fix, and the example golden passing on run/build/--release.

cards.title: Fixed-width compound assignment (x op= y) never checks overflow; it needs the #Arithmetic policy on the checked assign
cards.body:
Repro: Examples/features/safety/v_failure_cases/fixed_width_overflow. `x += 1` on a fixed-width integer at its maximum wraps silently, while the binary form `x + 1` stops with E3010. The golden expects the stop. Two spellings of the same operation have different safety meaning (I1, I8).

Root: JetIR lowers every `op=` (BuildExpr ir_assign_value / ir_assign_place / module storage / ir_list_index_assign, and BuildMaps index assign) as ir_binary(..., overflow=false). Turning overflow on for + - * / ** << >> breaks crypto/primitive_matrix and crypto/typed_crypto, because Core/Crypto/Expert.jet blake2b_mix is #Arithmetic(.Wrapping) and its `c += d` must wrap. Under #Arithmetic, sema lowers only the binary form, to an OverflowOpt node (Expressions.jet sema_expr_arithmetic_policy_value, from context.arithmetic_policy). TStmt.Assign{place, op, value, line, span} and FnBody carry no policy, so IR cannot tell a policy function from a plain one.

Fix (sema owns it, I3): either sema lowers a policy-governed fixed-width `op=` to `place = OverflowOpt(prefix, op, place-read, value)` at its three Assign sites in Statements.jet (local, module storage, expr place), or Assign/FnBody records the arithmetic policy. Then IR checks overflow for a plain `op=` and keeps wrapping, saturating or checked per the policy. Other #Arithmetic `op=` users to cover: JetRuntime CryptoArgon2id, CryptoBlake2b, Sha512, and Core/Crypto/ExpertCt.jet. Prove with fixed_width_overflow plus the crypto examples on both tiers.

cards.title: #5005 child A: link and target build options (output_dir, work_dir, link_args, libs, cpu, cpu_features, os, min_os, entry_symbol)
cards.body:
Child of #5005 (Jai build options), drafted by O0Image 2026-10-23.

Both cards build on the one option table that (a)+(b) land, `JET_BUILD_OPTIONS` in
`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet`. A row is written as a profile field
(`build: { p: Build{ name: value } }`), the flag `--name=value`, the method `b.name(.Value)` and the pin
`b.pin(.name, .Value)`. Resolution order: stock, then profile, then `fn build`, then the flag. Spellings
are the ballot names in `Docs/audits/jai-parity-2026-10-16.md` section E. Rows marked
**free-form value** carry a string or list, so the table needs a value kind beyond an enum: add
`kind: enum|text|list` to `BuildOptionRow`, with the flag taking the raw text and the method a
String / [String] argument. That is an internal API, owned by whichever card lands first.

Per-row acceptance (card criteria): a row in the table; set from profile, `fn build` and CLI through
`build_options_resolve`; the consumer named below reads `build_options_value(options, name)`; an
example under `Examples/features/tooling/` with a run golden plus a build-tier golden; every refusal is
a registered diagnostic (an E-code row with Why/Fix) with a UI snapshot in `tests/cases/build_entry/`;
CLI help/man/completion snapshots gain the flag (pattern: `$JET_RUN_ROOT/O0Image/snapbounds.mjs`).
A value that removes a runtime check is listed in `removes_check` (a `check_removal` gate, E3415 under
Forbid), as `bounds` does in (b).

## Card A: #5005 link and target options (audit rows 1, 3, 10, 11, 20, 23, 25)

| row | spelling | values | stock build / run | consumer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `output_dir` | free-form text (path) | `""` = today's output path | `jet build` artifact path in JetCli Host build step (where the image is written today); `jet run` ignores it (in-memory image) |
| 1 | `work_dir` | free-form text (path) | `""` = `.jet/` | the generated/cache directory root (`.jet/generated/`, syntax-decisions.md:5652) in JetDriver/JetBuildSession; the cache key excludes it |
| 25 | `link_args` | list | `[]` | native link step (`Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Host.jet:588-601`, JetBackend/Source/Image/StaticLink.jet): appended to the link of foreign libraries. Expert override under D-TARGET-LINKER1 (syntax-decisions.md:5971): a policy gate `link_override` refusable by Forbid |
| 25 | `libs` | list | `[]` | same link step: extra libraries to resolve foreign symbols against |
| 3 | `b.link(...)` command (D-JAI-EVENTS1 `build.link`) | `fn build` only | none | replaces the native link with a BuildAction-gated command. Gated on the D-JAI-EVENTS1 ballot; it is **not** a table row. If EVENTS1 is not ratified, the card refuses it with a law row (as null/casts are refused in (b)) |
| 10 | `cpu` | free-form text (`x86-64`, `x86-64-v2`, `x86-64-v3`, `native`) | `x86-64` / `native` | JetBackend instruction selection: gate the AVX2/BMI paths on the level [INFERENCE: isel feature paths not opened]; `native` reads cpuid at compile time; recorded in the cache key |
| 10 | `cpu_features` | list (`+avx2`, `-bmi2`) | `[]` | same, as per-feature overrides of `cpu` |
| 20 | `os` | `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, `web`, `freestanding` | host | joins `--target=<triple>` (Front.jet:651-659): `os` is the triple's OS part; a flag/profile disagreement with `--target` is E2104. Native backend refuses an OS it cannot emit with a registered diagnostic |
| 11 | `min_os` | free-form text (version) | `""` | ELF: none (refuse with law on linux: no versioned ABI floor); Mach-O `LC_BUILD_VERSION` minos when macOS output lands. Until then the row exists and a non-empty value on linux is a registered refusal |
| 23 | entry name | **no new row**: output `entry:` (spec.md:4065-4073) already selects the function; the card adds `entry_symbol` (free-form text) for the exported symbol name of a freestanding/library output | `""` = `main`/`_start` | JetBackend image writer's entry symbol (`Image/ELF.jet`) |

cards.title: Owner decision: a fast string hash for the compiler (String builtin or internal intrinsic)
cards.body:
Needed for the 2.5 s self-compile (#5479). Measured (RustOut, prof21 instructions:u): interning sema names as Int ids cut lookups by ~47 G instructions (string_compare -39 G), but hashing each name in a Jet FNV loop plus a bytes() copy per probe added ~68 G, so it lost 3.1%. With a native hash it nets about -21 G; full parser-time interning (the SoA AST) needs the same hash at intern time.
Compiler code cannot hash a String without copying: Strings expose only bytes() (copies) and count_bytes(); Core's in-place reader core.encoding.__string_byte is private; #Import(c) copies to a NUL-terminated C string and runs the FFI sentry. [String:V] is an ordered map (binary search on compare), so no hash exists today.
Options:
A. Public builtin: `s.hash() -> U64` (stable within one process run, not across runs or versions; not cryptographic). Beginners: an obvious way to hash; experts: build their own tables. Cost: a new public API to ratify and document.
B. Compiler-internal intrinsic: a jet_rt_string_hash routine reachable only from compiler/Core sources (like other internal runtime routes), not part of the user surface. No new user API; one more internal route.
C. Neither: keep ordered maps; R3a stays parked and interning waits for the SoA AST to carry ids from the parser without hashing (much slower to land).
Recommendation: B now (no user surface), A later if users need it.

cards.title: Named tuples compare in member-name order, not written order: sort() looks like a no-op (needs owner ruling)
cards.body: Repro (discovery jet at 904ffda357, jet run): xs := [(key: "c", index: 0), (key: "a", index: 1), (key: "b", index: 2)]; &xs.sort(); prints c 0 / a 1 / b 2 unchanged. The same list sorts correctly with sort_by(left.key <=> right.key), and [String].sort() works. Found by O0Speed-3: it made the IR claim-queue merge order thread-dependent (BuildWaves later.sort()), and BuildMerge ir_merge_function_run's &run.sort() on (key, local) tuples is likely affected too, so the self-compile's function order may not be what the code intends. Expected: lexicographic member-order sort (or a compile error if tuples are not Comparable, which needs a ruling); never a silent no-op. Check every tier (run and build) and audit compiler callers of .sort() on tuple lists. Repro file: $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/ts/t.jet.

log.text: 2026-10-23 Main: Main rerun at 900b4add9c (discovery jet from that sha): Examples/features/collections/tuple_order.jet matches expected/collections/tuple_order.out byte for byte on jet run (rc 0) and on the jet build binary (rc 0). Landed 4cb2b0d820 (static map order sort_by) and 900b4add9c (docs + golden).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

O0Comptime-3 root cause: not a no-op. S73 (syntax-decisions.md:1141) makes a named tuple's identity its fields sorted by name, so the derived order (JetIR ir_order_into, BuildTypes.jet:1898) compares 'index' before 'key'; the repro was already sorted by index. All tiers agree: run, build, comptime constant, <, sort_desc. Compiler callers: BuildMerge.jet:239 is correct by luck (key sorts first); BuildStatic.jet:460/467 (texts/words with key, at) is a latent bug: ir_static_map_order expects key-then-position, and O0Comptime-3 is fixing it with an explicit sort_by under any ruling. cards.title: Closures capturing a by-value record keep that memory for the rest of the run (+300-600 MB in self-compile)
cards.body: Found by O0Comptime-3 on 2026-10-24. ir_reachable_core_rows (CoreReach.jet:275-284) passes body_each_*_child a closure that captures tree: BodyTree by value. Peak RSS over that span: +326 MB at f2 and +629 MB with two extra Int fields on BodyTree. A rewrite whose closure captures only &children costs +56 MB, and the whole-build peak drops 8847 -> 8594 MB. The same pattern appears in Effects/Checks, FailureLaw, PureRoot, HttpMount, Services and the driver's unresolved_call, and is a suspect for #5889's +300 MB. Open question, being settled with a micro program: either the closure env is leaked or copied in codegen/runtime, or the allocator retains it. Fix at the root (one mechanism, every tier), not by rewriting call sites. Acceptance: the micro program shows flat RSS on every tier; self-compile peak RSS drops; FIXED_POINT; goldens.

log.text: 2026-10-23 Main: Landed 94d81c7d95 (O0Comptime-3: FIXED_POINT 26aa62b46313d809, t1 SAME, traps 0; goldens identical per stem to 277c99; same-generation A/B peak RSS 11-21 MB lower). Main rerun at 94d81c7d95 with the discovery jet built from it: testkit cases --filter closure_boxes_free -> PASS 1/1 (tests/cases/memory_semantics/closure_boxes_free_at_their_last_owner: 16 scenarios, built binary and jet run, peak 4,024 kB vs 4,927,044 kB on base). The cycle-struct capture leak remains under #5917; the tx.on_commit leak is #5918.

O0Comptime-3 patched compiler: the 16-scenario closure regression program runs flat on the built binary and on jet run, peaking at 4,024 kB against 4,927,044 kB on base 728ca37b91. With the patch, a closure capturing a cycle struct still leaks only the captured cycle value (~96 B per round); that leak is #5917's drop glue, and the closure box itself is freed. Boundary agreed: #5909 lands first, #5917 rebases; #5917 adds a cycle-capture case to the same regression fixture. Testkit case, then the HEAD chain, in progress.

Root cause confirmed by a micro program (O0Comptime-3, dev jet 728ca37b91): every closure box leaks. 10.5M closures: capturing a struct of 4 lists peaks at 2,573 MB (~245 B per closure); capturing only a write var, 658 MB (~63 B); the same walk with no closure, 4.5 MB. Mechanism: ir_lambda writes release helper 0; the Fn type row has no drop or clone, so no Drop or retain is ever emitted; named fn values and zip adapters leak the same way. Fix plan (one mechanism, IR builder): Fn rows become counted boxes (clone = closure_retain, drop = ir_closure_unref); each box gets a real release helper that drops its by-value captures; runtime hand-off sites are marked as moves. Required: same lifetime on the comptime and web tiers, and a testkit RSS-bound regression case covering every closure kind and move site.
Owner 2026-10-24: memory leaks and similar memory issues are P0.

cards.title: A struct inside a recursive type cycle leaks its value on every drop (~95 B each)
cards.body: Found by O0Load-3 on 2026-10-24 while chasing #5889. Minimal shape: enum Ty { Int; Other(items: [CycleOnly]) } with struct CycleOnly { ty: Ty }. Building x :: CycleOnly{ty: Ty.Int} 300k times reaches 30 MB RSS (about 95 B leaked per value). The same struct outside the cycle uses 2.3 MB and does not leak. Plain recursive enums, lists, maps, strings and Option matches do not leak. Repros: $JET_RUN_ROOT/O0Load/leak/m6r.jet and m6s.jet. The compiler has this exact shape (Type.Tuple(fields: [TypeTupleField]) with TypeTupleField.ty: Type), so every dropped tuple-field row leaks; #5889's extra type walks multiplied it (+330 MB, +7 s). CORRECTION (O0Speed-3, kernel log ip + nm + strace): spawn failure IS reported correctly through HostSpawn.jet's CLOEXEC error pipe, and case 9 passes with an IOError on every tier. The real crash is case 10, the empty command: process_execution_invalid passes a null path as the resource and compiler_fs_error calls jet_rt_string_clone(0). process.pipeline([]) crashes the same way. Plan, one patch: no resource for a null path; spawn errno mapped through compiler_fs_errno (ENOENT -> NotFound, EACCES -> PermissionDenied) instead of always Other; the witness checks the error before using it; a golden for missing program, empty command and empty pipeline; an audit of every compiler_fs_error caller that can pass a null path.

Root (O0Speed-3, strace on 277c996280): witness case 9 spawns /nonexistent/jet-no-such. The child exits 127 and jet_process_spec_run returns a receipt (ok=1, error NULL) instead of the spawn IOError, because the exec errno never reaches the parent and _exit(127) is treated as a normal exit. The witness then dereferences the NULL error (SIGSEGV at 0x10). Two defects: the runtime's spawn-failure reporting (the fix is the standard CLOEXEC error pipe carrying exec errno to the parent), and a witness that does not check the error before using it. Not related to #5920. Owner: O0Speed-3 after #5920.

cards.title: Core's vendored C (SQLite, soon mbedTLS) needs a system cc at build time; jet's self-compile fails E2105 without one
cards.body: Since 764097f6be (core.db on vendored SQLite), JetCli's native closure realizes SQLite C, so every jet build of the compiler, and every user program that imports core.db, shells out to the system cc/ar (ForeignLink.jet jet_cli_native_c_tools). Without one it fails with E2105 'the C compiler is not installed'. Found by RustOut-4: every s21ab self-compile A/B outside nix fails at the native link. Before this, building the compiler needed no C toolchain. Fix direction (Main): Core-owned vendored C is compiled once when the toolchain is packaged (Tools/packaging/prebuild-runtime.sh, keyed by the runtime key) and shipped beside the runtime pack, like jet_runtime.pack.o. A system cc is needed only for C the user declares. Acceptance: self-compile and the io/db* goldens pass with no cc on PATH; a user-declared C dependency still uses CC/cc; no RSS or build-time regression.

log.text: Post-close confirmation (O0Comptime-3, strace -f -e trace=execve): (1) 'jet build Compiler' with a HEAD-packager pack (foreign/{mbedtls,sqlite3}/lib*.a, no .c) makes 0 cc/cc1/gcc/clang/ar/as/ld/collect2 execs, 0 write-opens under jet-runtime and 0 .c opens. (2) With foreign/mbedtls removed from the pack, a core.net.tls build refuses with E2105 naming the missing libmbedtls.a, makes 0 cc execs and produces no binary; there is no link-time fallback. (3) Vendored C compiles only in prebuild-runtime's tmp dir, which publishes only the .a. The 40 s sys O0Speed-3 saw came from builders whose packs predate 77b18e4f00 (they ship .c files), as expected for those packs.

cards.title: Runtime process spawn uses plain fork(): a large multithreaded parent stalls every thread (78 ms for the 4.5 GB compiler)
cards.body: Found by O0Speed-3 profiling the HEAD self-compile: jet_process_spawn_raw (HostSpawn.jet) does a plain fork() of the whole process. For the ~4.5 GB compiler this freezes every thread for 78 ms per spawn (page-table copy), e.g. the cc -dumpmachine probe (that one goes away with #5936). Every Jet program that spawns from a large or threaded process pays the same, and fork in a multithreaded process is also a correctness hazard (locks held by other threads). Fix direction: spawn with posix_spawn, or vfork/clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK) with an async-signal-safe child path, keeping the current fd/env/cwd/abilities semantics exactly (I9: one runtime implementation). Acceptance: the process goldens and witnesses are unchanged; spawn latency from a 4 GB parent is under 2 ms; a paired cell compares the old and new spawn.

Fix LANDED 1102b9df03 (O0Load-3): jet_process_spawn_raw no longer does a plain fork() of the parent (vfork-style spawn). Spawn from a 4.5 GB parent goes from 148-162 ms (worst 207) to 0.50-0.67 ms (worst 3.4); from a 64 MiB parent, 748 -> 482 us. cards.title: `x == "...{name}..."` is a pattern that rebinds an in-scope name: silent always-match bugs, including in the compiler
cards.body: Found 2026-10-02 by the CLI port (CLI-12A via PortLead-5): under D-PARSESTR1, `subject == "jet {name}"` is a string PATTERN test whose holes bind fresh names, not equality with an interpolated string. When the hole names an existing binding (`x == "{root}jet_fraction_from_parts"` with `root` in scope) the author almost always meant equality, but the hole silently shadows the binding and matches any text. Live instances in the compiler itself (equality was intended, ported from Rust format! equality): Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:890-909 (`symbol == "{root}..."`), Compiler/JetEval/Source/Evaluator.jet:7842 (`== "jet_gc_{member}"`), Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/Prelude.jet:50, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions.jet:2390, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet:33, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Statements.jet:1570,1614; the port fixed two in Args.jet and DynamicCompletions. Two parts: (1) fix every such site in Compiler/, Core/ and Jetpack/ by computing the expected string first and comparing values; (2) language safety: a pattern hole whose name is already bound in scope must not silently shadow it: the precise rule (reject with a teaching diagnostic, or treat an in-scope name as an equality anchor) is an owner decision under D-PARSESTR1: prepare a ballot.

cards.title: Runtime E1003 range stop must exit 70 (fault), not 1
cards.body: Ruling (CoreReview5-2-2, ratified sources): a runtime E1003 raised via jet_runtime_stop is a program-side FAULT and exits 70 (D-FAIL-EXIT1=A, syntax-decisions on 0513 lines 1738-1745; S36 1787-1792 includes FFI producers). D-INTBIG1 (1285-1294) mandates the range check and code E1003 with NO exit-1 exception. The compile-time E1003 diagnostic (exit 1) and a real returned fallible entry error (exit 1) stay distinct. DEFECT: Core.rs (0513: 1374-1377) special-cases JET_C_INT_RANGE_CODE into jet_entry_error_exit -> 1, and Contracts.rs:35-37's comment wrongly claims a D-INTBIG entry diagnostic. The producer MathRandomTime.rs:78-82 (Stop) is CORRECT. Fix at the exact existing boundary on ALL tiers (remove the bypass so the uniform Stop law applies; fix the comment), with a regression asserting exit 70 + the Stop report for a runtime E1003 (e.g. rng beyond-64 bounds). No oracle edit needed (int_exact covers only the success path). Owner: CorelibInteg19-2 assigns within Core composition (Core.rs editor); NativeLead24-2 + CoreReview5-2-2 review. Unblocks GoldenSquad2's held RNG fixture expectation (70).

No Jet runtime or IR source raises E1003 at run time (git grep E1003 over Compiler/JetRuntime and Compiler/JetIR: none); the exit-1 path was the deleted Rust Core.rs stop.

The fix must also give E1003 canonical RUNTIME registry support through the EXISTING dual compile / runtime stage metadata mechanism (same code, one mechanism; what / why / fix text and snapshot per I4), plus the bypass removal and the Contracts.rs comment fix. No code-based fallback, no unknown-row-to-70 suppression.

Only compensation threads use a bounded 2 ms wait. No polling loop remains in the worker path.

cards.title: Parser divergence: Jet parser accepts typed literals in for-loop headers and Val(...) in conditions; Rust parser rejects (E0003)
cards.body: Found by gate 2's focused L4 field-owner fixtures (Stage0Sweep7, $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Stage0Sweep7/focused-11cc9a9ee/l4-field-owner-fixtures.log: 13 problems, all E0003). The trusted Jet parser accepts (1) for loops that iterate a typed collection literal directly, e.g. for x in [String]{...} { ... } (fixture lines 20, 39, 56, 80), and (2) an equality against Val(...) in a condition, == Val(integer_bounds_exact(number)) (line 61); the Rust parser rejects both with E0003 (it treats the literal's brace as the loop body, and enters condition-binding grammar). Two front ends must accept exactly the same language (one meaning). Decide the ratified grammar for both shapes (check Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md: brace-literal vs block disambiguation in headers), then make the losing parser match, with UI snapshots for the rejected form and corpus cases for the accepted one. Related: #4785 (Jet parser single-arm structural if). The gate fixtures were normalized (arrays bound before the loops, Val(...) parenthesized) so gate 2 isn't blocked.

cards.title: Core which/is_file do not follow symlinks: process.which and files.which return None on NixOS, every requires tool:X case is SKIP-HOST
cards.body: Core/Process/Process.jet:183 path_is_file and Core/Files/Files.jet:1810 is_file_impl call __stat_at(-1, path, false) (lstat). On NixOS every PATH entry is a symlink, so which("node"/"sh"/"git") is None and files.is_file("/etc/hostname") (a symlink) is false. cards.title: Comptime JSON renderer emits invalid JSON for non-finite Floats and non-text map keys (violates the encoding law)
cards.body: Found by NativeReview2 during the #4891 review. Rust CtFloat::to_json (crates AST/comptime.rs:423-429) and Jet AST/ComptimeJSON (lines 6-8) render NaN / infinity with a '.0' suffix, producing invalid JSON; CtValue Map (Rust and Jet, ~22-24) writes non-text keys directly as JSON object keys. The ratified law (Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:152, 165-168, 881-883; D-ENC-DYN1) rejects both as Unsupported (reason 'JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float'; non-text map keys never coerced). Fix at the root on BOTH tiers: return Unsupported per the exact law, migrate every fallible caller / report path, and fix Char / C0 control escaping (lowercase \u00xx) in the same renderer. No coercion and no new serialization law. Regression: NaN, +/-inf, a Map<Int, …>, Char and C0 cases on both tiers with identical results (I9).

log.text: 2026-10-27 Main: Checked on dev ca923f0fb3 s2. Comptime: Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/AST/ComptimeJSON.jet returns EncodingError Unsupported 'JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float' and 'JSON cannot encode non-text map keys'; jet test Compiler/JetFoundation/Tests/ComptimeJSON.jet reports comptime_json: pass (NaN, +/-inf, list of inf, Map<Int,...>, Char and C0 escaping). Runtime: json.dumps/dump are String EncodingError!; probe q/p4892 prints 'Unsupported JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float' for nan, inf and a list holding -inf on both run and run --release. The Rust renderer is deleted.

Scope ruling (Main): the public Core JSON text serializers are a DEFECT against the ratified law, not a new API decision. core/encoding/json compact / dumps / dump / pretty (json:97 / 99 / 101 / 104) and the JSONL writers (37 / 67 / 92 / 102) return String Never! although DataTree.Float admits non-finite values and encoding-decisions 165-168 require Unsupported ('JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float'); canonical (json:111) is already String EncodingError!. Cutover: every JSON / JSONL TEXT serializer becomes EncodingError! exactly like canonical, rejecting non-finite Float (and non-text map keys) per the law; events (json:191, [DataEvent] Never!) is not JSON text and is unchanged. Migrate every caller on all tiers in one cutover (I9), including the comptime renderer (plain_calls 968 / 974 old infallible render) and docs / examples / goldens whose output changes. If a frozen route file would have to change, that part waits for E2 green (report it, don't edit). Owner: ScalingGate6; reviewers NativeReview2 + CoreReview5-2-2; composed by CorelibInteg19-2 in NEXT.

cards.title: L0101 flags the implicit err of ?? when an #Unsafe fn is called inside an #Unsafe block
cards.body: Repro (dev 3aa6fe388c s2, 2026-10-27): #Unsafe("probe") fn mine(x: Int) -> Int IOError! { return x } and fn c() -> Int { #Unsafe("probe") { return mine(3) ?? -1 } }. jet check warns L0101 'Local binding err is never read' at the ?? span. The same ?? on a safe fn inside the #Unsafe block, or outside any block, gives no warning. Same false positive for Core calls such as sys.getpriority(0) ?? -1 and sys.setsid() ?? -1. The ambient err of a ?? fallback is declared in Control.jet sema_expression_or_fallback_route with no single-use duty and must never produce L0101. Acceptance: no L0101 for the implicit err in any ?? form; a UI case pins it.

log.text: 2026-10-27 Main: Fixed in dcc73c2b2b: the err a ?? fallback declares is marked compiler-made (sema_ownership_declare_ambient_binding in Ownership/Checks.jet, used by Control.jet and Statements.jet) and liveness skips it. Pinned by 5df38e06fb tests/cases/liveness_lints/fallback_err_is_never_an_unused_local.case (the card repro: #Unsafe fn in an #Unsafe block, plus a safe value fallback, ?? return, and core.math.factorial ?? -1): PASS on s1 dcc73c2b2b, FAIL on the compiler before it (L0101 at lines 8, 18, 19). A user err binding that is never read still warns.

cards.title: Named tuple ordering compares fields by label in alphabetical order, not declaration order
cards.body: Found by O0Speed (2026-10-23, runcap): sorting [(used: Int, name: String)] ordered the elements by name, not by used, as if named tuples compare their fields in alphabetical label order. Declaration order is the expected meaning (the first field decides). Check sema's derived compare/order for named tuples and every tier (run, build, --release, comptime), add an example golden with labels whose alphabetical order differs from declaration order.

log.text: 2026-10-27 Main: Not a defect: the ratified tuple-order decision (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, S73) says a named tuple compares its members in label order, so (used, name) orders by name first; sort_by orders by another member. Examples/features/collections/tuple_order.jet proves this and PASSES its golden on every tier on dev 42e6a05fa4. The warning for a mismatched written order is proposed separately on #5927 (needs owner approval).

2026-10-23 TowerSweep4 recheck on dev base/latest: STILL-FAILS: jet run 5522 probe (pair compare) => (used:2,name:a) < (used:1,name:z) prints lt true: members compare in canonical field order (name before used), not declaration order. Responsible: Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildTypes.jet:1568-1577 ir_tuple_members consumes canonical field order; ir_order_members:1971-1977 compares in that order.

cards.title: Fixed Float `fold acc + x` misses the add-fold route: fold_association prints 1.0, expected 0.0
cards.body:
Examples/features/collections/fold_association.jet: `fold acc + x` over a fixed Float list prints `fold acc + x: 1.0` where the golden (Examples/features/expected/collections/fold_association.out) has 0.0. Seen on the self-hosted compiler (CutoverLead4 chains kF on 62bc6918d and kG on d0499f032, both FIXED POINT). Every other line matches, including `sum: 0.0` (BuildRoutes ir_list_sum_fixed, 8 lanes and a pair tree) and `para_fold`.
Cause: the Rust checker recognized a `(acc, x) -> acc + x` closure over a fixed Float list as the closure op FloatAddFold{f32} and routed it to jet_list_fold_add_fixed_f64 (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs), which adds in a lane tree. Jet sema/TIR has no such op, so the fold runs as a plain left-to-right closure loop. Its rounding differs, and the example's inputs are chosen to expose that.
Fix: add the FloatAddFold closure op to Jet sema (or recognize the closure shape in the JetIR builder's ir_closure_method) and route it to an IR add-fold with the same lane order as jet_list_fold_add_fixed_f64 (compare ir_list_sum_fixed in BuildRoutes.jet). Proof: fold_association matches its .out.
