cards.title: shared_transact: wrong totals on jet run, a join panic on the interpreter, and an ICE on AOT
cards.body:
The shipped example Examples/features/memory/shared_transact.jet (golden: from=200 to=800 total=1000) gives three different outcomes. `jet run` (tier1 native per --trace-tiers) printed totals of 1000, 1100, 1100, 1100 and 1200 across five runs, so money was created. `jet run --interpret` stops with E3001 at the first `^t1.join()`. `jet build` fails with an internal compiler error (exit 101): `MIR nominal type "Stm" has no declaration row` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:2637). A second probe (eight tasks doing withdraw-if-funds in #Transact plus a shared counter) ICEs on jet run with `Shared constructor received an invalid checked type ID`.

Root cause for the wrong totals, from committed code: `edit_txn` (HEAD MathTaskMem.rs:1884-1918) stages a clone at first touch without a lock, and `JetSharedTransaction::try_commit_with` (SharedProtocol.rs:873-960) publishes it with no check that the value is unchanged. Two transfers can overwrite each other (lost update). Which fix to apply is ballot D-CONC-STM2 on this card; the ICEs and the interpreter panic are defects under either outcome. Probes ran on target/debug/jet built 2026-09-30 12:12 from a dirty tree (crates/jet-jit heavily modified); reproduce on clean HEAD first. Tower #2123 (done) fixed an earlier wrong answer in the same example. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.
cards.plan:
1. Reproduce all four outcomes on a clean HEAD build and record which are dirty-tree only.
2. Fix the AOT ICE (missing Stm declaration row) and the Shared-constructor ICE; both are internal errors under I2.
3. Fix the interpreter join failure so the interpreter agrees with the other tiers.
4. Apply the ratified D-CONC-STM2 commit rule in the shared Prelude so every tier inherits it.
5. Add a stress oracle example: 8 tasks x 1000 transfers with a conserved total, and a withdraw-if-funds variant that never goes negative.

log.text: 2026-10-27 Main: 2026-10-27, Jet compiler s1 (bd3, base caa6a2945c): Examples/features/memory/shared_transact.jet on jet run x5 and jet build --release x3 all print the golden from=200 to=800 total=1000; no ICE. Stress probe q/stm/s.jet (8 tasks x 2000 rounds of two conditional #Transact transfers between Shared accounts plus a Shared counter) prints total=1000 nonneg=true on jet run x3 and --release x5. The Rust-era interpreter/AOT paths named in the card no longer exist.
Burn-down consolidation 2026-10-04: absorbed #3978, #4201; their criteria are carried here as [#n] rows.

Ratified-state audit 2026-10-02 (D-CONC-STM2): Decision IDs: D-CONC-STM2

Active contract: Each transaction records the revision of every Shared value it reads or edits. At commit, under the ordered locks, Jet compares them.

Gap evidence (static source witness, not a passing test): Rust's current try_commit_with drains deltas and stages hooks under locks without comparing any read revisions or returning a retry disposition (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/SharedProtocol.rs:934-991). Jet lowers the body once then commits (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Statements.jet:1941-2001); no transaction retry loop is present. Both retain the superseded one-run algorithm, missing revision validation, complete local restoration, held output and escalation.

Coverage disposition: #3967 names D-CONC-STM2 and transfer totals but does not concretely prove revision-read conflict, restoration on every retry, held output or escalation. #3978 already owns mutating-call rollback; consume that repair and add validation/retry-boundary proof here.

Existing owner: shared_transact: wrong totals on jet run, a join panic on the interpreter, and an ICE on AOT; open-cards.json plan/criteria inspected.

All named tests/goldens below are REQUIRED delivery artifacts, proposed here unless an existing owner already names them; none was executed by this audit. Each runs the production Jet path, records compiler/source/provider identity, asserts exit/diagnostic/output or real side effects, and fails if the owning implementation is bypassed. Registry presence, mocks and fixed echo output cannot satisfy behavioral criteria. Unavailable hosts and inconclusive measurement cells remain open.

Retargeted to the Jet compiler under the Rust freeze, 2026-10-01 (owner): the Rust compiler only gets stage-zero blockers, deletions and C-ABI runtime exports. The AOT ICE (MIR nominal type Stm has no declaration row) and the transaction semantics are fixed in the Jet compiler; see #3978.

Board prep 2026-10-01 (D-EXEC1, #4013): Rewrite for new architecture: keep the AOT ICE (MIR nominal type "Stm" has no declaration row) and the transaction semantics (money created on jet run may be a Shared/#Transact law bug, see #3978); drop interpreter-only rows.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

D-TXN-WAIT1 is ready (full profile). Beginner pass (BeginnerTxnWait, rli5): terms, timeline, and the D-CONC-STM2 prerequisite were missing; repaired. Adversarial pass (AdversaryTxnWait): (1) tx.wait needed a control-flow contract: it now never returns, drops per-attempt hooks and output, and restarts the whole block; (2) escalated locks could deadlock a waiter: wait now releases every lock and rechecks revisions atomically like the Condition protocol, is a cancellation point, and wakes all waiters; (3) local restore was overbroad: filed #3978 as a prerequisite; (4) C was compared unfairly to channel tables, which choose channels only: C is now judged on combining helpers that wait; (5) current example used the retired `edit` closure: replaced with plain Shared access. Verdict: A survives with repairs.

Correction to the D-CONC-STM2 answer: the existing #Transact auto-snapshot restores assigned locals only; locals changed through method calls (list.push, &self methods) are not restored (env.rs:419-431). Filed #3978. D-CONC-STM2 option A now states it requires #3978 so a re-run never applies a local change twice.

Owner question on D-CONC-STM2 answered 2026-09-30: re-runs repeat computation, never changes; discarded attempts write nothing and locals are restored by auto-snapshot. Added to option A: after a few conflicts the next attempt pre-locks its previous participant set, so busy transactions always finish. Real failures already roll back and are handled by the caller (?? / result table / tx.on_rollback); a block-attached handler would duplicate that (I8), so it was not balloted unless the owner asks.

Full-profile ballot D-TXN-WAIT1 (transaction wait, the STM paper's retry) is drafted at ~/.cache/jet-luna/spj-tower/D-TXN-WAIT1.json. Tower refuses to store it until the beginner (rli5) and adversarial fresh-reader passes are recorded. It depends on D-CONC-STM2 choosing re-runs. Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-30-spj-papers.md.

questions.text: When you say busy block runs more than once, does that mean it is possible to apply more than one modification to the target? Or that something would be executed multiple times? Since this is inside a transact block, it is very likely that the user wants to ensure that if a failure happens, nothing occurs or if it does happen that they can handle. We may want to consider more advanced marker syntax, like putting an option to handle a result outside of the transact, almost like a lambda so that the user can handle an error and try rerunning on failure once or maybe print a statement on error but that way their critical data is rolled back?

cards.title: Tuple destructure binds by canonical (alphabetical) member order and ignores names: `(path, before) :: pair` silently swaps fields
cards.body: Found 2026-10-05 by Idiom-Main4 (probe $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Idiom-Main4/probe/tupord.jet): for `pair: (path: String, before: Int)`, `(path, before) :: pair` binds positionally in canonical member order, so path = 1 and before = "p", with no diagnostic. Binding names that are member names must bind those members (or the compiler must reject a destructure whose names are member names in another order); a beginner cannot see the canonical order. Done when the rule is defined (ballot if it needs a new surface rule), enforced in both frontends with a registered diagnostic or name-based binding, and covered by UI snapshot and example on all tiers.

Distill 2026-10-05 ('31 nooby C++ habits', youtube i_wDa2AS_8w habit 11): C++ structured bindings bind custom types in declaration order, so a reordered field silently swaps values. Ratified D-TUPLE-DESTRUCT1 (bind by member name only) is exactly the design that avoids this trap, which makes this card's defect (canonical alphabetical order, names ignored) the C++ failure mode Jet promised to remove. Add the habit-11 swap as a regression example.
Correction: the rename form is dotless, { before: name, after: value } :: t (D-LIT-DOT1 retired .{, E0320); the earlier log's .{ spelling came from S74's stale example, which this cutover fixes.

Owner ruling 2026-10-05: tuples destructure only by member name. `(before, after) :: t` is allowed when every binding name is a member name (binds those members); renaming uses the struct pattern form `.{ before: name, after: value } :: t`; any other positional tuple destructure is a compile error with a registered diagnostic whose fix line shows the named form. cards.title: Compiled workload superiority gate: Rust, C++, Go, and best peers
cards.body: Core API rows do not prove that Jet can replace a compiled language for complete work. Build a closed workload gate for systems, services, command-line tools, libraries, compute, embedded targets, and cross-platform applications. External trust and ecosystem age are out of scope. Every buildable Jet loss remains in scope.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the compiled-workload superiority gate. Every frozen task (systems, service, CLI, library, compute, embedded, cross-platform app) is compared with its best compiled peer on all ten metrics under the standing comparator, and every Jet loss is owned.

## Current state
- Criterion 1 is met: `tests/compiled_workloads/manifest.tsv` sits alongside peer_ledger, peer_adapter_ledger, adapter_ledger, metric_contract, measurement_policy, tier_matrix, canaries and domain_contract TSVs.
- The Linux runner and gate self-check pass: `Tools/ci/compiled-workload-gate.sh`, `Tools/ci/test-compiled-workload-gate.sh`, `Tools/ci/compiled-workload-runner.mjs` and `Tools/ci/compiled-workload-review.mjs`. Peer adapters are ledger-only.
- Contract tests exist: `tests/agent_workloads.rs:1577` and `tests/release_gates.rs:407`.
- The old plan cited the stale path `tools/ci/`; the scripts live in `Tools/ci/`.
- #2858 (measurement gate) is `ready` and owns the prerequisite runs.

## Changes (after #2858)
1. Keep all seven frozen tasks, one selected peer each, and every candidate row. Do not add a second benchmark framework and do not narrow the denominator.
2. Measure every applicable task/peer on all ten metrics: `source_effort`, `build_time`, `edit_time`, `runtime`, `memory`, `artifact_size`, `diagnostics`, `debugging`, `deployment` and `unsafe_burden`. Inputs, outputs, source boundary, toolchain, authority and tier identity must be identical across Jet and peer.
3. Record five samples/medians, monotonic timing, host peak RSS, immutable identities, per-tier artifacts, platform binding, normalized receipt hashes and every removal canary. The web row uses the Chromium CDP driver.
4. Apply the comparator per cell: Jet/non-Rust < 1.00 and Jet/Rust <= 1.05 (parity only). Missing, invalid or inconclusive cells fail. Embedded N/A is allowed only for the manifest's declared structural reasons (#2046/#2300 are done). Any hardware cell they left unmeasurable stays an explicit N/A with its reason, never a silent pass.
5. Link every buildable loss to a live Tower card or a ratified scope reduction, then run the fresh independent fairness review.

## Proof
Run in order:
- `bash Tools/ci/compiled-workload-gate.sh --contract`
- `bash Tools/ci/test-compiled-workload-gate.sh`
- `node Tools/ci/compiled-workload-runner.mjs --platform linux --report-dir "$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/compiled-workload-linux"`
- `bash Tools/ci/compiled-workload-gate.sh --check "$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/compiled-workload-linux"`
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test agent_workloads -- compiled_workload_contract_reuses_agent_schema_and_keeps_hosted_rows`
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test release_gates -- compiled_workload_release_gate_uses_frozen_contract_and_canaries`

Expected: the gate `--check` exits 0 only when every required cell passes the comparator. Otherwise the report lists each failing cell with its owning card. macOS/Windows cells are recorded as unavailable on this host, never as passing.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: evidence run with no compiler change. It measures emitted-program quality, so it stays valid under the Jet compiler.

## Dependencies
#2858 (measurement gate runs).

cards.title: Soundness: binding a list element (or its field) of a resource struct with :: silently copies the handle; the copy's drop closes the shared handle
cards.body: Found by O0Image-3 on 2026-10-24 (U7 Secrets tests). 'parent :: self.dirs[i]' or 'h :: self.dirs[i].handle', where the list element is a struct owning a Directory, makes a silent copy. When the binding leaves scope, the copy's drop closes the SHARED handle, and the list's original then fails with 'closed during read: the directory handle is already closed'. Passing self.dirs[i].handle directly as an argument, or calling a method on it, does not copy. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/repros/resource-element-binding-copy.jet ('jet run -A' on discovery ba20b4270f; variants 1 and 3 close the handle, 4 and 5 do not). Expected: E0209/E0211 (cannot move out of an indexed place), or an implicit borrow per the ownership spec; never a copy of a unique resource. Severity: a double close, and if the fd number is reused in between, a close of an unrelated fd. That is a memory/resource-safety (I1) violation. Impact: every Jetpack FoundationDirectoryAuthority method that binds 'parent :: self.directories[last]' closes the authority's leaf handle, which breaks every env_runtime_lock (Secrets: 4 lock FAILs). Acceptance: the indexed-place binding of a non-copyable value is either refused with a registered diagnostic and UI snapshot, or binds as a borrow, per the spec; a collect-all sweep of Compiler, Core and Jetpack finds every affected site and migrates it in the same cutover; the repro's variants all keep the handle open or are refused; the Jetpack '#5940(i)' workarounds are reverted.

log.text: 2026-10-27 Main: Landed 2330880e36. tests/ui/resource_copied_out_of_place.{jet,stderr} reports E0211 at 16:28 (Held element), 21:27 (Directory field), 26:22 ([Held] list). Repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/repros/resource-element-binding-copy.jet: jet check on s1 7dd3676506c5a2e8 gives E0211 at 15:22. Self-check Jetpack/Foundation, Jetpack/PackageModel, Compiler/JetCli rc=0, 0 rows (TreeHash rewritten, the 9 workaround comments removed). UI 1143 PASS, 0 lost.

2026-10-26 HANDOFF (owner order: no subagents; O0Load-3 stopped mid-work). Unproven WIP vs 2d9c75c319 saved as $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/O0Load/out/HANDOFF-w10-5942.patch (Sema Calls/Collections, Expressions/Literals, Ownership/Copy, Ownership/CopySites, Statements). Work tree $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/O0Load/w10 (chain state unknown). Not reviewed, not chained, no goldens: next owner must read the diff, run the repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/repros/resource-element-binding-copy.jet (variants 1,3,6 must not double-close), chain full+threads and goldens before landing.

Wider scope (O0Image-3, variant 6 in the refreshed repro): copying a whole List whose elements own resources also double-closes. 'dirs := self.dirs; &dirs.push(new)', returned as a new owner, shares the handles; when the copy drops, the original's fds are closed. Jetpack FoundationDirectoryAuthority.child works this way, so a parent authority used after its child drops is broken, and RuntimeLockScope (authority + marker_parent) double-closes on release. The root is the same: a value containing a unique resource is implicitly copied. Fix: any implicit copy of a non-copyable (resource-owning) value, whether element, field or whole collection, must be a move, a borrow or a refusal per the ownership spec. The sweep must cover collection copies too. A real duplicate needs an explicit dup API (#5935 gap 8).

cards.title: Jetpack ProjectLock locks the root DIRECTORY; ratified FILELOCK1 locks a regular lock file
cards.body: Jetpack/Foundation/Source/ProjectLock.jet:92/100/178 calls files.lock / files.try_lock on the managed root directory (mirroring Rust RuntimePolicy/Lock unix.rs:160 / windows.rs:249), but ratified FILELOCK1=A (card #3593) locks a REGULAR lock file (0600 create, no-follow, never unlink), so the call fails on a directory path under the ratified contract. Main ruling: option A: Jetpack locks a dedicated lock file inside the root (a Jetpack change that follows the ratified Core contract; no owner ballot needed). Same mutual-exclusion guarantee; tests for contention, try and timeout. Raised by CoreReview4 while implementing FILELOCK1 (#4697).

cards.title: #Transact: every non-commit exit rolls back the same way (panic, cancel, exit, stop)
cards.body: Owner approved 2026-10-23 ~10:40 (Main's recommendation after an industry survey: DBs, Haskell/Clojure STM, Rust Drop, C++ dtors, Go defer/os.Exit, Kotlin/Trio/Swift structured cancellation, Spring @Transactional). Semantics: (1) buffered Shared writes never commit on any non-commit exit: panic, cancel, process.exit, os.stop, ? failure, early return. (2) on_rollback hooks always run, in reverse registration order, in the same cleanup that runs guards and closes (D-FAIL-EXIT1); one mechanism. (3) A failure inside a hook during rollback is never fatal: it is attached to the primary report as a secondary failure ('while rolling back, this also failed'), and the remaining hooks and cleanup still run (beats Rust/C++ double-panic abort). (4) Hooks run with cancellation masked and under a per-hook deadline; a stuck hook is reported, not a hang. (5) A panic keeps propagating after rollback; rollback never turns a panic into a recoverable error (D-NOPANIC1). (6) A hard kill (SIGKILL, power loss) runs nothing, but consistency still holds: writes are buffered and irreversible effects are banned in the body (E0746) or deferred to on_commit. (7) Same meaning on run, build and --release (I9). Residual: a hook may run while the program is crashing; mitigated by hooks touching only what they registered for and by non-fatal hook failures. Work: spec.md #Transact paragraph update (spec.md:1364-1375), runtime/JetIR stop-edge restore of tx snapshots plus hook execution, examples per exit kind, diagnostics/report format for secondary failures (I4 snapshots), hook deadline value (internal default, documented). Owner: O0Load after R12 fault backtraces and the 3a temporaries fix.

cards.title: Soundness: a reordered or default-skipping call closes a whole `::` resource local passed as a read argument
cards.body: Found by SmallGoals3 on 2026-10-28 while tracing Examples files_store_primitives ('the directory handle is already closed'). It already happens on the base compiler, on both tiers. Trigger: a call whose arguments are not in declaration order, either because labels are reordered or because a skipped default is followed by a written argument. When such a call passes a whole `::` resource local as a read argument, it closes that local's resource, and a later use fails or double-closes. Examples: `swapped(name: "y", store: s1)`; `s2.rename("c", "d", if_exists: .Replace)` with `into:` skipped. A field place (`h.dir`) or an explicit `into: None` is fine. Repros: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/sg/vb/dirclose.jet and dirclose2.jet. Suspect, unconfirmed: the argument pin from sema_call_pin_binder_arguments (Checking.jet:568-597; receiver pin Methods.jet:748-763) reaches ir_bind_pin (JetIR BuildExpr.jet:626-652). If `b.fresh[value]` at :632 takes the owning path, the pin owns the local and drops it.

cards.title: jet run/jet build with a warm cache are slower than with no cache (hello: run 35 ms cold vs 80-510 ms warm; build 52 ms cold vs 316-1693 ms warm)
cards.body: Measured 2026-10-24 by Main with discovery jet 67726659c1 (s1). Harness: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/hello/bench2.py (perf_counter around each spawn, load ~10-12). With a fresh XDG_CACHE_HOME and .jet per run, hello takes 'jet run' 34.5 min / 35.3 median ms and 'jet build' 51.0 / 52.2 ms. Repeating with the cache kept: 'jet run' 79.6 min / 509.6 median ms, 'jet build' 315.7 / 1692.7 ms. Hitting the cache costs 2-30x more than compiling from scratch. Suspect: cache-hit verification re-hashes the 4.87 MB hello binary or the runtime pack with the slow Jet SHA-256 (measured earlier at ~14.5 MB/s, ArtifactStore verifies records twice), or a cache lock or contention. It blocks #5476 (hello <= 2 ms) and #5905. Acceptance: a warm 'jet run' and 'jet build' of hello are never slower than cold, measured in the same run; a per-stage trace of the hit path is attached.

cards.title: `jet test` bounds its default concurrency by cores and memory (testkit pool superseded by #6035)
cards.body: Profiled 2026-10-28 by Main on f30bffb323 (prof scripts and logs in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/sg/tmp/prof/). Tools/testkit/run.jet kit_execute_suites (:806-826) loops over the selected entries one at a time. A full golden run takes 23-27 min on the 32-core host while about 31 cores sit idle. The hidden `--shard I/N` option already splits the corpus: 8 shards at once took 372 s wall (load 15 from other lanes), with the same rows. Change: run entries on a bounded worker pool inside one testkit process (default from available cores with a memory-aware cap, and a `--jobs N` override). Keep each entry's scratch private, and print rows in corpus order so reports stay deterministic.

cards.title: Bare `jet` prints the command palette (today's `jet ?`), and `jet repl` starts the REPL (owner ruling)
cards.body:
Owner ruling 2026-10-28: bare `jet` runs what `jet ?` shows today, the command palette. Only `jet repl` starts the REPL; bare `jet` never starts it. This replaces the bare-`jet` part of D-DX-ENTRY1. Greenfield, one mechanism: `jet ?` is removed with no alias, and its palette moves to bare `jet`.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, CLI-02): bare `jet` reports `Error [E2104]: \`jet repl\` is not built yet`. `jet ?` fails with `failed to redirect to /dev/tty` when no terminal is attached. The palette must work without a terminal: print the static palette when stdin/stdout is not a TTY, and the interactive picker only on a TTY, if one exists. The greeting text exists already (jet_cli_greeting). Docs/spec first-hour.md and cli.md promise the palette. Related: #4720 (the REPL itself).

cards.title: Remove the temporary owner markup from syntax-surface.jet
cards.body:
Owner ruling 2026-10-28: the OWNER MARKUP notation (`//<<< Owner …`, `// HAVE:` / `// WANT:`, `//>>>`, `//!!`) was a temporary, ephemeral way for the owner to mark up code while working with an agent in early development. It is NOT part of Jet: not syntax, not a convention, and not something to rename or keep.
Remove it from Docs/spec/reference/syntax-surface.jet: the legend (lines 30-40) and every mark wrapper (lines 266/275, 366-371, about 650-662, 696-705). Every mark is already tracked (#32, #33, #34, #35), so keep only the current ratified spelling of each block, and drop HAVE/WANT duplicates and the `//>>> tracked` lines. Nothing in Jet, its tests or its tooling should treat `//!!` or `//<<<` specially.

cards.title: Self-hosted compiler: multi-file programs with cross-module types
cards.body:
Make the self-hosted Jet compiler (Compiler/) accept types, enums and traits declared outside the entry file. Today E0003 fires on imported types with no lowered owner type. Acceptance: a multi-module golden with cross-module types and enums compiles and runs.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

cards.title: One typed IR: backend failures are ICEs, sema hands IR every type, IR Lint checks every pass
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28 (highest priority): fix the backend now. The compiler has one typed IR, called IR (Compiler/JetIR). It must not grow extra layers that lead back to TIR/MIR/LIR. No new named IR (no 'Core' layer).

Audit evidence: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/typedir/ (INVENTORY.md, ICE.md, PLAN.md), dev bb12b96fe5.
- I2 is broken: every backend rejection exits 1 as E2104, not 101 (JetCli Host.jet:833, :862-863, :277; Emit.jet:71). Harness link failures report E2105 (Host.jet:1340-1346).
- Missing invariant: sema leaves a body incomplete with no diagnostic, which causes 75 of the 79 exit-101 rows (six driver sites from BodyComptime.jet:247).
- Facts lost between sema and IR: binders carry no type (Checked.jet:171-194); the builder re-derives types (BuildExpr.jet:582-584, :515; Build.jet:905, 123 call sites). This is the root of 80 of 158 single-defect cards.
- Nothing type-checks IR: the MIR checker was deleted, and ir_ssa_verify only panics under the verify option (Opt.jet:436-441).

The owner's direction settles the sema-to-IR boundary change (binder types and instantiated callee type arguments in sema's published facts). D-CHECK-DEPTH1=C stands: `jet check` stays sema-only, and IR Lint runs in build.

cards.title: Calling an inline C function needs no #Unsafe block in the self-hosted checker, and E3215 suggests a spelling E0999 rejects
cards.body:
The spec requires an `#Unsafe("reason") { … }` block around every call to an inline C function (D-FFI-INLINE1; E3103 in Docs/spec/safety.md). The self-hosted checker does not enforce it, so unchecked C runs from code that looks safe.

Found by CardDraft job 3 (2026-10-28), bd6 self-hosted compiler:

- `#[Unsafe("…"), FFI(c)] fn add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int { """…""" }` then a plain `print(add(20, 22))`: `jet check` reports no problems.
- An ordinary `#[Unsafe("…"), Inline] fn peek` called plainly gives E3103 "`peek` is an `#Unsafe` function", so the gap is specific to inline foreign functions (JetSema Effects/Checks.jet E3103 path).
- `#FFI(c) fn add` with no gate gives E3215 with Fix "Add the gate: `#Unsafe("…") #FFI(c) fn …`". That spelling, on one line or two, is refused by E0999 "Adjacent function markers belong in one bracket list". The accepted form is `#[Unsafe("…"), FFI(c)]`.

Related: #4524 (unsafe as an inferred effect), ballot D-FFI-ONE1 on #4174 (whether inline C stays).

The runtime sentry (Sentry.jet) exists but names every operation "read", and exits with SENTRY_RUNTIME_EXIT_CODE = 70 (enforced by Tests/Fragments SentryTests.jet:38). cards.title: Close the core.math gaps the Core surface ledger scores
cards.body: The Core surface ledger scores 72 gaps in core.math against eleven languages, read from primary sources. Highest-witness rows include log with eight witnesses, copysign, fma and the bit-count family. Size the work from the ledger cluster row, not from the raw row count: 582 losses are 491 distinct capabilities.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish the core.math ledger card. The gap functions already ship in Jet. What remains is one exact-`Int` ABI defect in `factorial` and the tier-parity proof (c1/c3) for `math_audit` and `more_math`.

## Current state
- The functions already exist in `Core/math/math.jet`: acosh/asinh/atanh (:93-98), cbrt (:99), expm1/log1p (:105,:116), `log(n, base)` (:117), copysign/fma/muladd (:131-135), is_normal/is_subnormal/is_canonical/is_signed (:154-157), nextafter/ulp/ilogb (:167-170), modf/frexp (:190-196), checked_* (:198-235), factorial (:258), binomial (:269), leading_ones/trailing_ones/cmp (:347-349). `Examples/features/math/math_audit.jet` and `more_math.jet` call them, and their goldens are `Examples/features/expected/math/{math_audit,more_math}.out`.
- Under D-INTBIG1=A (`Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1172`), `Int` is exact and unbounded. The Jet `factorial` body is correct for this, but the registry overrides it with a host call to `jet_std_math_factorial(i64) -> Option<i64>`. The override is at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:207-208`, mirrored in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:2001-2002` and the `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:455-456` dispatcher rows. The host function is at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathLibPure.rs:881`, whose doc says 21! is 'too big'. On 2026-09-15, AOT `math.factorial(25)` in `Examples/features/text/int_exact.jet:5` failed in generated Rust because JetInt was passed where i64 was expected. The core.math.combinatorics rows `binomial`/`perm`/`rising_factorial`/`multinomial` (:209-216) use the same i64 host symbols.
- Criteria 2 (ledger) and 4 (spec) are verified.

## Changes
1. In `CoreCallRows.jet`, delete the `core.math` `factorial` host row so the exact Jet body in `Core/math/math.jet:258` runs on every tier. Repoint `core.math.combinatorics` factorial/binomial/permutations_count/ncr/npr/falling_/rising_factorial/multinomial to the exact-Int Jet bodies in `Core/math/combinatorics.jet`, or widen the host leaves to JetInt. Pick one. There must be no i64 truncation path.
2. Mirror the same rows in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs` and the `Prelude/Core.jet` dispatcher rows (the shipped binary proves the fix). Retire the i64 `jet_std_math_factorial`/`jet_jit_math_*` leaves that no row uses any more.
3. Add `print(math.factorial(25) ?? -1)` and a combinatorics row with a result above 2^63 to `more_math.jet`, then bless its golden.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=math/more_math Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`, `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=math/math_audit …` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/int_exact …`: each passes.
- For each of math_audit, more_math and text/int_exact: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/<f>.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/<f>.out` and the same with `jet run --interpret`. Both must give an empty diff.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_surface_ledger` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-data: the fix is to Core math registry rows plus goldens. It lands with the other math/data rows before one build and one tier retest.

## Dependencies
None.

A fresh project should already be tidy. Today the files `jet new` writes are not what `jet fmt` would write, so a new user's first `jet fmt --check` fails. This card produces scaffold text with the formatter and adds a round-trip test.

Related: #5071.

cards.title: Two refusals of forms from other languages do not teach the Jet spelling: `Float(n)` and `impl Stack<T> {`
cards.body:
People arriving from other languages type a handful of forms that Jet refuses. Most refusals already teach the Jet spelling; two do not. This card makes those two teach. Its ballot D-SURFACE-COMMON1 was dropped before filing (reasons below), so the card no longer decides anything.

Checked by CardDraft job 3 (2026-10-28), bd6 self-hosted compiler:

| Typed form | Today | Teaches? |
|---|---|---|
| `side ** 2` | E0396, Fix: `base.pow(exponent)` | yes |
| `enum Shape { Rect(Float, Float) }` | E0003 "A positional enum variant can carry only one value", Fix: name each field | yes |
| `(tx, rx) :: channel<Int>(4)` | E0313, Fix: `(sender, receiver) :: …` or `{ sender: name, receiver: name } :: …` | yes |
| `loop i in 0..xs.len() { print(xs[i]) }` | E0364, Fix: `0..<xs.len()` | yes |
| `Float(n)` | E0102 "Nothing named `Float` exists here", Fix: "Define `Float` first" | no; the spelling is `Float{n}` |
| `impl Stack<T> {` | E0003 "Expected `{` to open the `impl` body, found `<`", Fix: "Write the expected token here", plus a cascade E0003 at the closing brace | no; the spelling is `impl Stack {` |

Why the language questions were dropped: `**` is settled twice (D-EXPOP1=A rejected it; D-SIGIL-ALGEBRA1=B, #4141, moved power to `.pow()`). Positional unpacking would undo D-TUPLE-DESTRUCT1=A (#4605), which fixed a silent swap. Multi-value variants already exist as named fields. Inclusive `..` with `..<` and E0364 was kept by #747. General `defer` is settled by D-JAI-DEFER1=A (#5026).

cards.title: Self-append through interpolation (s = "{s}...") is quadratic: make it an in-place append when s is unique, and sweep Core
cards.body: Found by RustTests: core.archive zip_names_json/tar_names_json built JSON with out = "{out}\"{escaped}\"" per name, which copies the whole String every time (214 s for zip_names near the 64 MiB limit; 5 s once rewritten). The plain spelling users will write is the same, so this is GENERAL: when the target of an assignment is the first segment of an interpolation and the String is uniquely owned, JetIR should lower to an in-place append (amortized growth), with the same meaning on every tier. Also sweep Core for the pattern (census + fix sites) until the lowering lands. Acceptance: a paired perf cell (the self-append loop vs an explicit builder) with linear time, and an example golden.

cards.title: Apply "The Language Is A Library": census of Core-only privileges and private compiler-rule copies
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-29: treat the language as a library and apply it holistically. The owner chose both meanings, which are now pillar 5 in Docs/spec/philosophy.md. First, the compiler is a small kernel and a public, versioned library that the CLI, the language server, fn build, compile-time code and outside tools all call. Second, every capability that can be a library is one: Core is ordinary Jet using only mechanisms any package can use, with no private compiler hooks, Core-only names, or Core-only diagnostics or optimizations.

This card finds every place the code breaks the pillar, then turns each finding into a fix card or an owner ballot. Module-private helpers inside Core (for example `__` internals, #5978) are ordinary package privacy and are not a violation. The violation is a privilege a user package cannot get.

Related: D-CORE-BOUNDARY1 (#4565, frozen), #5964 (GPU providers as a library), #5978 (Core naming), and the AI-out-of-Core owner direction (q2no5uew).

cards.title: clean-nix-tmp.sh deletes the TMPDIR of live jet-env shells (check.sh --tests panics 'scratch directory')
cards.body: Tools/agent/clean-nix-tmp.sh runs in every new jet-env shellHook. It deletes /tmp/nix-shell.* dirs it believes are dead. Its liveness scan has two passes: cwd/root/fd symlinks, and /proc/*/environ. It misses live check.sh runs. A shell that gets TMPDIR exported after exec (nix develop's rcfile) does not show it in /proc/PID/environ, and while no child happens to hold the dir open, nothing marks it live. RustOut7 observed this on 2026-10-29: a watcher inside jet-env logged 'TMPDIR missing at 08:17:48' during `check.sh --area Nix --tests`. That run gave 32 passed / 19 failed with 15 `panic: scratch directory` (files.tmpdir Err). The same tree gives 40/11 with 0 panics when TMPDIR survives. Earlier 'scratch directory' counts in check.sh evidence were partly this, not only the #6119 drop bug.
cards.plan: Make liveness robust at the root. Have the jet-env shellHook hold an open descriptor on its own TMPDIR for the shell's lifetime (for example `exec {fd}<"$TMPDIR"`), so pass 1's fd scan always sees a live shell and its children inherit the protection. Keep the batch scan fast (perf contract in the script header). Add a test that starts a jet-env shell, runs the cleaner from a second shell, and asserts the first shell's TMPDIR survives while a truly dead dir is removed.

log.text: Fix 020b890bb8 + 6131b d82ce61681 (NixIndex test key API, oracle sha). Old-tree chains: chain.sh and GoldC launchers set JET_NIX_TMP_CLEANED=1.

criteria.text: A live jet-env shell's TMPDIR survives clean-nix-tmp.sh run from another new shell, proven by a scripted two-shell test.
criteria.evidence: Landed 020b890bb8. Scripted two-shell test Tools/agent/clean-nix-tmp.test.mjs (node --test, 4/4 pass on the patched tree). In test 1, an idle shell whose own environ never names its TMPDIR (rcfile export after exec, waiting on the builtin read) survives a second shell running clean-nix-tmp.sh. Mutation checks: dropping the shellHook hold fails test 1, and dropping the userns guard fails test 3. Real nix develop E2E ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/NixTmp/e2e-run.mjs, patched flake): interactive shell A pid 1395762 had TMPDIR=/tmp/nix-shell.7nBRwa, its environ did not name it, and it held fd 10->/tmp/nix-shell.7nBRwa. After shell B's hook ran the cleaner, A's dir still existed. Userns: a live jet-env TMPDIR /tmp/nix-shell.6ZDAsS printed DEAD under the old logic in chain.sh-style `unshare -r -m; unshare --user --map-user=1000`; the patched cleaner run there removed nothing and the dir was still present.

criteria.text: A dead /tmp/nix-shell.* dir (no live process) is still removed, and the cleaner stays a batch scan (no per-process fork loop).
criteria.evidence: Landed 020b890bb8. The same E2E removed the exited shell's /tmp/nix-shell.Obg91q (it existed before B and was gone after). Test 1 asserts that an exited shell's dir is removed, and test 3 asserts that a host cleaner removes the dead dir the userns cleaner kept. Test 4 asserts no `for … in …/proc` loop and no readlink in the cleaner. Liveness is still one find over /proc/*/{cwd,root,fd} plus one environ cat|grep sweep.

criteria.text: `check.sh --area Nix --tests` run while other jet-env shells start shows 0 `panic: scratch directory` from a vanished TMPDIR.
criteria.evidence: Measured on dev 020b890bb8 + 6131b (landed d82ce61681). `check.sh --area Nix --tests` on dev HEAD 020b890bb8 + 6131b (NixIndex.jet:103 fix + oracle sha), run through Tools/agent/jet-env with no TMPDIR override, so nix's default applied: TMPDIR=/tmp/nix-shell.ZN2eQD, 09:25:43-09:27:01, and the dir still existed at the end. During the run, 8 other jet-env shells started (4 host, 4 chain.sh-style `unshare -r -m … unshare --user --map-user`, all rc 0), and each ran the shellHook cleaner. Result: 0 `panic: scratch directory`, 38 passed / 13 failed. RustOut7's pre-fix baselines on the same harness had 15 scratch panics (32/19), and their 40/11 run had none. The 13 failures and 14 Stop lines exactly match the 13 FAIL names and 14 panic messages of RustOut7's t31old run (signed resolution, test executable, …); none involve TMPDIR. JET: Main's chain s1 of dev 04fdfbde1d (sha cc6c5370…). The admitted seed a0_021 passes check, then fails run/aot with E2104/E2105 on Core/Http/Server.jet channel lowering. Guard: the run started only once no pre-fix chain.sh and no clean-nix-tmp.sh process was live, and found 0 blocking processes after. audit-cleaners.mjs logged every clean-nix-tmp.sh process in the window: 6 new-code cleaners, plus 1 old-code one (Main/q/sg/sg20) in the host user namespace, whose environ scan keeps live dirs. Logs: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/NixTmp/logs-b31/. Before chain.sh got JET_NIX_TMP_CLEANED=1, an unguarded run lost its TMPDIR at 09:17:56 to an old-tree cleaner inside a chain user namespace (GoldC rdbg, r14/snap).

cards.title: `::` bindings fold at build time as an optimization; `comptime` forces it
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-29: `::` should be an implicit request for build-time evaluation as an optimization, and the `comptime` keyword forces build-time evaluation. Immutables should be build-time constants. This matches D-VERDICT-1308-1 (implicit folding is the beginner default) and conflicts with the 2026-09-30 shipped note under D-PREP-SURFACE2 in Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:8214-8223, which says an ALL_CAPS `NAME :: value` is an ordinary runtime constant.

What the code does today (read-only audit, 2026-10-29):
- A module-level `NAME :: expr` is a soft constant. It is evaluated while building when the evaluation is pure and succeeds, and silently demoted to startup otherwise (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:3508-3530; Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:1189-1229, 1507-1514, 1918-1935).
- `name :: comptime { ... }` forces build-time evaluation. A failure stops the build (CheckProgram.jet:6881; Pipeline.jet:1515-1529).
- A block-local `name :: expr` parses as Stmt.Val with is_comptime false (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Statements.jet:1465-1493). Whether it is folded was not verified.
- The IR optimizer (ir_opt_simplify, Compiler/JetIR/Source/OptSimplify.jet:116-207) folds constant operands at O1 and above. Whether a user `::` constant reaches it as a constant was not verified.
- Docs/spec/spec.md:438-455 and syntax-decisions.md:8214-8223 disagree with each other and with the code.

log.text: Closed by Main: KitSpeed-6125 landed as f87cd39b78. All 5 criteria met with landed evidence (constant_identity case, E3010 ui, fold_constants golden o0/o1/o2, spec rule). criteria.text: A test proves that a block-local immutable `name :: expr` with a pure foldable value becomes a constant at every tier (O0, O1, O2), for example by an IR dump that shows no runtime computation at the use site.
criteria.evidence: tests/cases/constant_identity/immutable_constants_fold_at_build_time_on_every_tier.case PASS on s1 1e244182 (rb3/d6125 = dev 1106ae6da5 + patch): emit-ir shows the block-local `::` as `const s0 <- 34` / `const s2 <- 69` at O0 and `const s5 <- 70` at O1/O2, with no runtime add/mul at the use site; overflow past Int bounds and mutable bindings stay runtime (same case). The fold is Sema/CostTree.jet tree_expr_fold_int called from Sema/Statements.jet sema_stmt_check_binding; JetIR BuildExpr.jet marks an IntLit-initialised Let fresh so O1 keeps folding later uses. Gap reported in the msg: a `::` over a pure call or branch still folds only at O1/O2. Landed as f87cd39b78.

criteria.text: A test proves the same for a module-level immutable, and proves that an impure or failing module-level `::` value still runs correctly (computed at startup) with no user-facing error.
criteria.evidence: Same case: module-level `NAME :: value` folds to `const s0 <- 43` in the IR at every tier, and an impure module value is computed at startup (`GREETING#startup` in the IR) and prints `43 hi` / `43 hello` with exit 0 and no diagnostic. Landed as f87cd39b78.

criteria.text: A test proves that `name :: comptime { ... }` whose evaluation fails stops the build with a registered diagnostic and a UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: tests/ui/E3010_comptime_value_stops_the_build.{jet,stderr}: `name :: comptime { … }` whose evaluation fails stops the build with registered E3010; ui PASS on s1 1e244182. Landed as f87cd39b78.

criteria.text: Docs/spec/spec.md and Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md state one rule: `::` folds at build time when it can, as an optimization, and `comptime` forces it. The contradicting 2026-09-30 sentence is corrected.
criteria.evidence: Docs/spec/spec.md 440-455 states the one rule (`::` folds at build time when it can, as an optimization; `comptime` forces it). Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md has a new 2026-10-29 entry, the 2026-09-30 D-PREP-SURFACE2 note is amended to point at it, and the `comptime` lexical-ledger row (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/Spellings.jet, regenerated by Tools/agent/lexical-ledger.mjs) says the same; E0388's why text matches. cards.title: Port rounded and fallible unit conversion (X.from_y_rounded) to Jet

cards.body: Owner (2026-10-29): `pi`, `e`, `tau`, `infinity`, `nan` and the rest are declared as zero-argument functions in Core/Math/Math.jet (`fn pi() -> Float Never! { Float{3.14159...} }`), so callers write `math.pi()`. cards.title: Bootstrap resilience: rebuild Jet from the repo alone after Rust is retired (tag, seed binaries, portable wasm seed)
cards.body: Owner question 2026-10-01: how do we compile purely in Jet if this machine and its binaries are lost? Owner approved the plan ("yes"). Deliver all three: (1) tag the last commit that still contains the buildable Rust compiler (e.g. bootstrap-rust) when Rust is retired, with a documented chain: build Rust jet at the tag, build the Jet compiler at the tag, then build forward; (2) publish seed jet binaries per OS/arch with each release (plus a mirror) and a documented bootstrap that downloads one; (3) a portable seed checked into the repo, refreshed occasionally: the Jet compiler built to WebAssembly plus a tiny C wasm interpreter (like Zig zig1.wasm), so any machine with a C compiler can bootstrap from the repo alone with no downloads and no old binaries. Also a trusting-trust check: rebuild from the tagged chain and from the seed and compare outputs. Until then the rule is: push often; ~/.cache holds only rebuildable artifacts.

cards.title: Own wasm engine: run core.plugin and compiler-extension wasm through JetIR + our backend (replaces wasmtime)
cards.body: Owner decision 2026-10-23 (on #5482): replace wasmtime (RustBridge Runtime Plugin.rs, CompilerExtension.rs) with our own pipeline. A loader reads the Component Model guest's core wasm, translates it into JetIR with sandbox guarantees (bounds-checked linear memory, checked indirect calls, fuel/deadline, no ambient authority beyond the plugin policy), compiles it with the x64 backend, and runs it in memory via the native O0 loader. Design note first: the Component Model subset needed (the jetplugin and compiler-extension-v1 WIT worlds), the sandbox proof obligations, and the test corpus (spec testsuite subset plus existing plugin examples). Proof: the plugin examples and E1257-E1260 diagnostics unchanged; adversarial wasm (out-of-bounds, runaway loops) contained.

cards.title: Persisted package checks: interface records, red/green with early cutoff, diagnostic replay
cards.body:
ACTUAL: IncrementalSemaCache and CompilerQueries are process-memory only and enabled only for CompileMode::Check (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Pipeline/Completion.rs:242-247; crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs:274-350). jet build, jet run, and jet dev re-check every module every time. ReceiptStore keys a whole invocation on verb, cwd, argv, full environment, tool identities, and terminal mode, and two identical builds produced two different contexts (proposal I.5), so replay never happens.

EXPECTED (per the D-BUILD-NOCHANGE1 outcome; recommended option A): Check(module) results (interface record, body record with TIR, typed diagnostics record with spans, item digests) are store entries keyed on the module's raw source bytes + module path + imported interface digests + package policy/authority facts + lint settings + target/profile facts + compiler identity + digests of generated or external inputs read, for Run, Test, TestOverride, Check, and Eval modes. Canonical-AST, interface, and body digests are outputs for later nodes, not the Check key. Diagnostics are re-rendered per invocation (color, width, --json); --json records are byte-identical under a versioned schema. An input-audit test instruments every read a check performs and fails on an undeclared one; a node kind that fails the audit checks fresh until fixed. Reads go through stable handles with metadata compared before and after hashing, and every node of one invocation binds to one source snapshot. A Receipt entry keyed on the invocation closure digest (verb, argv, terminal mode, leaf digests) re-renders diagnostics and re-verifies the terminal artifact digest. Changed modules and importers of changed interfaces are always checked afresh. Source/ReceiptStore.rs, JET_RECEIPT_DIR, and JET_RECEIPT_BYPASS are deleted; --no-cache bypasses reads.

Writable paths: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs and Pipeline/Completion.rs, crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs and Driver/mod.rs, crates/jet-store (record kinds), Source/ReceiptStore.rs (delete), Source/CmdCompile.rs, tests/build_entry.rs, tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs.

Non-goals: units, emission changes. Invariants: D-INCR-UNIT1 layers 1-2; FrontEndCompletion gate unchanged; I4 (re-rendered diagnostics equal a fresh run's for the same terminal mode).
cards.plan:
## Plan

### Goal
Implement the owner's 2026-09-30 ruling. The package is the unit of
incremental checking. Package checks are persisted as versioned `jet-store`
records containing an interface record, typed diagnostics, per-item
fingerprints, and usages. Each record is keyed by:

- compiler and Core identity;
- the target facts sema reads;
- the package's source digest;
- its direct dependencies' interface digests.

An unchanged interface digest keeps importers green (early cutoff). A changed
interface rechecks only the importers whose usages name a changed item. The
batch-1 Receipt stays for whole-invocation replay.

Design:
`Docs/research/incremental-checking-design-2026-09-30.md`, sections 3–4 and 6–7.
Contract: `Docs/spec/architecture.md`, "Incremental Compiler Service".

### Scope of this card: stages S1, S1b, S2, and S2g

1. **S1, identity and records (days).**
   - Package identity for every `LoadedModule`, and the package DAG, in the
     Rust bundle.
   - Semantic-identity keys for effect, taint, memory, and failure maps.
   - Source, interface, and item fingerprints.
   - A std-only binary record codec in `jet-foundation`, with a trailing
     SHA-256. The Receipt payload moves to it.
   - `jet-store` record kinds `jet.pkg-check`, `jet.iface`, `jet.diags`, and
     `jet.program`.
   - `.jet/` priors pointer and stamp table.
   - `explain-build` rows per package showing green-by-key, green-by-usage,
     red, or cutoff.
   - Deterministic counters.
2. **S1b, sealed reader (days).** One audited reader for check-time file and
   environment reads in sema, comptime, and the loader.
3. **S2, Rust package checks for `jet check` (weeks).**
   - A green dependency enters registration as declarations with bodies
     erased (re-parsed; templates kept). Its summaries and constants are
     seeded from its record, and its registration diagnostics are replayed.
   - Each completion phase runs per red package, with the summaries listed
     in design section 4 crossing package edges.
   - The program-level phase covers:
     - outputs and the entry;
     - authority and effect budgets at dependency edges;
     - the web partition, app graph, and job graph;
     - unreachable exports;
     - the `used_core` closure;
     - ordering.
   - Root policy is removed from per-package keys.
   - Core modules become dependency packages.
4. **S2g, gates (days).** The design's section 6 scenarios on the
   `Compiler/` package graph, as corpus rows and focused tests; `--verify`;
   seeded edit replay.

### Out of scope (separate cards)
- S3R, Rust item reuse inside a red package. Measurement-gated on S2g.
- S4, per-package compiled output for build, run, test, and eval. Joins
  #2519 and #2520; until then those modes check every package and use the
  Receipt.
- S5a–c, the self-hosted JetDriver/JetSema port (identity and codec, package
  checks, item memo).
- Moving the ReceiptStore callers, which is still an owner question.

### Depends on
- #3862: `Compiler/` split into nine packages, with loader support for
  D-MOD-CYCLE1=A.

### Writable paths
- `crates/jet-foundation` (codec, fingerprints)
- `crates/jet-store` (record kinds)
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs`, `Bundle/Pipeline/*`,
  `Bundle/Validation.rs`, `Sema/mod.rs`, `Effects.rs`, `MemoryFacts.rs`,
  `WebPartition.rs`, `Bundle/Liveness.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs`, `QueryService.rs`
- `Source/CheckReceipt.rs`, `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, `Source/CmdInspect.rs`
- `tests/build_entry.rs`, `tests/cli_compiler_speed.rs`,
  `tests/receipt_store.rs`, plus a new `tests/package_checks.rs`

### Invariants
- The front end completes before any codegen.
- I4: warm diagnostics are byte-identical to `--no-cache`.
- A package check never reads dependency bodies beyond published templates,
  and never reads root policy.
- A corrupt or missing record is a miss with one `note:` line.

criteria.text: Retired by owner ruling 2026-10-30: no incremental compilation, period. The goal is 30M lines of code per second, at which point incremental recompilation is unnecessary; Jet should be so fast that incremental is obsolete. This card's cross-invocation reuse work is out of scope; the original criteria are kept in the card log.
criteria.evidence: Owner instruction in the Main session, 2026-10-30; answer recorded on question q0trf1ii.

questions.text: Ok with memoized default, but we should always have the expert hatch. I would like option a to be updated to include a force option/flag to force rebuild all if expert needs
questions.answer: Done, and the hatch turned out to be already ratified: D-BUILDCACHE1 names `--no-cache` as the expert flag that runs every executor, so option A now names `jet build --no-cache` instead of inventing a second flag. The rival pass caught one thing my first draft got wrong: action records are immutable per key, so a force build must not overwrite them. Rule now: --no-cache bypasses every read, writes records only for keys that have none, and when an existing key recomputes differently it keeps both artifacts, quarantines the key, and fails as a compiler defect, because that is exactly the nondeterminism evidence you want surfaced rather than erased. Beside it, `jet build --verify` recomputes everything without reuse and compares (identical, first changed input, or same-key mismatch), with one contract shared with D-RECORD1's --verify, for CI nightly. And the check phase now reads only through one sealed reader capability across the whole check-time closure including comptime, enforced by a source test, so the memoized path rests on structure, not trust.

questions.text: Ballot follow-through 2026-10-17: you ratified D-INCR-PARK1=C (retire item-level reuse) and said you do not want incremental compilation at this time. Does that also park this card (P0, package-level reuse / cached package results), or does package-level reuse stay in scope?

cards.title: Readable printing for everyday Core values: hex digests, database handles, date parts, hashing a String
cards.body:
Printing a value should show something a person can read. Today printing a SHA-256 digest shows raw bytes, printing a database handle shows nothing useful, and a date has no year or month accessors. This card fills these small gaps.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, CORE-05).

log.text: OWNER 2026-10-30: sha256 taking [U8] | String is fine (as landed in 921f1e48a6).
Landed 921f1e48a6 (BallotDesign-5960c2): crypto.sha256 takes [U8] | String (anonymous union, D-UNIONTYPE1=A) and a String hashes its UTF-8 bytes; case checked against sha256sum on o0/o1/o2 and AOT.

C2 (crypto.sha256 accepts a String) needs an owner call. Core has no overloading. A type table can't name [U8] (E0119, probed), and a union's [U8] member tag can't be spelled (M__U8_). The compiler itself calls crypto.sha256 with [U8], so new syntax in Core/Crypto needs a bootstrap. The options are a new name (e.g. sha256 over String via bytes()) or list-type arms in type tables (a D-TYPESWITCH1 extension); both are owner gates. (LiveUI finding.)

GoldC-g4 landed as a4e0e2f245: C1, C3 and C4 are met. C2 is still open: Core has no type overloading, and a String | [U8] union parameter cannot be matched (a union arm can name .String but not the [U8] member). This ties to D-TYPESWITCH1 (#6180).

criteria.text: `print(crypto.sha256("hello".bytes()))` prints the lowercase hex digest `2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824`; UI snapshot.
criteria.evidence: Core/Crypto/Crypto.jet adds `impl Digest256.Display` / `impl Digest512.Display` (the hex text). New golden Examples/features/crypto/digest_display.jet prints `2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824` for print(crypto.sha256("hello".bytes())), plus the sha512/blake3 empty-input vectors, identical on none/basic/full; `"{digest}" == digest.hex()` is true. (Snapshot is the golden .out; tests/ui snapshots are stderr-only.) Landed as a4e0e2f245.

criteria.text: `crypto.sha256("hello")` accepts a String (its UTF-8 bytes) and returns the same digest.
criteria.evidence: cases corelib/crypto_sha256_text_hashes_utf8_bytes PASS (jet run o0/o1/o2 + AOT): sha256("hello") == sha256("hello".bytes()) == 2cf24dba…9824, "é" == bytes C3 A9, "" == e3b0c442…b855; crypto/corelib/encoding_corpus filters lost 0; golden crypto at base after crypto_error_run.err.out 403->409; lane-check CHECK OK

criteria.text: `print(conn)` for a database handle prints one line with the database location and open/closed state, and no secrets.

A `jet check` of Examples/features/net/http_get.jet takes ~1.1 s with 16 threads (3.0 s at --threads 1). cards.title: Engineer away the whole-program (unity-style) build costs: reuse unchanged packages and Core across runs, edit-local rechecks, bounded memory
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: engineer away the issues of the current unity-style build, and ballot the proposed solutions.

Today every jet check, run and build loads the package, its imports and the reached Core into one program, then registers, checks and lowers it all (JetDriver Loader.jet, Pipeline.jet). Nothing is reused across runs: the CLI passes record_store None, and record_store, jet_driver_load_record and publish_record are dead stubs. Measured: jet check on a Core-http example takes about 1.1 s, of which about 470 ms loads 70-72 Core files (about 40 of them Unicode tables), against about 50 ms for a small example. Of the golden suite's jet time, 84% goes to such examples. The compiler self-check needs about 15 GB.

Ratified context: D-INCR-UNIT1=A (the package is the incremental checking unit, with interface records and dependent-only invalidation), D-LIB-REUSE1=B (sealed package objects linked statically, no public ABI), D-BUILD-STORE1=E (the store), D-EXEC2=A, D-DEV4/D-HOTSWAP1. Whole-program checks must keep their exact meaning: authority deny E0749, effect budget E1220, replay E0725, reflection, and generic instances.

#6032 stage 0 (lazy Unicode assets, register/finalize hot spots) proceeds meanwhile, since it is inside the ratified scope. The ballot decides the choices the owner reserved: unit granularity, persistence (on-disk records, resident compiler, or both), whether the toolchain ships Core prechecked, demand-driven loading, and the cache surface.

log.text: Retired by owner ruling 2026-10-30: no incremental compilation, period (goal 30M loc/s makes it obsolete)

Criteria before retirement: #1 [open] The ballot on the build model is ratified. || #2 [open] A warm `jet check` of the Core-http example after an edit to the user file alone rechecks only the user package, with the Core work reused, and the timings are recorded before and after. || #3 [open] Every whole-program diagnostic (E0749, E1220, E0725, reflection, generic instances) produces identical results with reuse and from a clean store, proven by a differential test. || #4 [open] Golden, UI and cases per-row compares lose no rows, with reuse on and off.

Main withdrew D-BUILD-CORELOAD1 as a ballot (owner rework order 2026-10-29). How much of the saved Core check a warm run reads is a cache internal with no user-visible surface; the implementer decides and records it here. Backup in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/backup38/.

questions.text: I dont understand the difference between verify, yes, and no. Why not just incremental=true false thing like rust?
questions.answer: You're right: it should be one on/off switch, like Rust's `incremental`. Off rebuilds everything from scratch. Verify meant "rebuild and compare with saved results", but Jet's agreed rebuild already compares each fresh result with any saved one for the same inputs and fails as a compiler bug on a mismatch. So off already verifies, and the third value is gone. The ballot now proposes `--cache=off` / `cache: false` / `b.cache(false)`, settable once from the workspace root.

cards.title: Arena/Bump .alloc: runtime storage_alloc with a drop function
cards.body: GoldC 2026-10-28: Arena and Bump `.alloc` need a runtime storage_alloc that records a drop function per allocation, so values with destructors are dropped when the arena resets or ends. The IR has no route for it. Until it lands, `.alloc` reports E2104 naming this card.

log.text: Landed 216cac590b (IrTypes-6109c3 + BallotDesign-6108).

C4 (environ read) removed: IrTypes-2 retracted it. alloc_check_requested reads /proc/self/environ in 2016-byte chunks and carries the match state across them, and strace confirms checked mode starts with a large environment.

IrTypes-2 2026-10-30: the C3 double drop does not reproduce. Tested with 5 payloads x none/basic/full/AOT under JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1, with no trap and exactly one close(fd) per FileWriter in strace; the Ok box copy goes through ir_copy_fixup. The C3 timing half is a real defect: a try_alloc Close value closes once, but at the end of the enclosing function, after the arena has been reset. A bare handle payload drops at reset while a struct payload drops at function end. C3 as written (exactly once, at reset/end, like alloc) stands; IrTypes-2 fixes it in ir_allocator_method.

cards.title: min, max and clamp are prelude built-ins: variadic, generic, no import
cards.body:
Owner (2026-10-29): Odin has variadic min, max and clamp built in, with no import; ensure Jet has the same.

Today: CorePrelude.names() (print, input, panic, assert, assert_eq, eprint, Clock, Instant, Date, Duration, Path, read_file, write_file, file_exists, embed_file, embed_bytes, find, fetch) has no min, max or clamp. Core/Math/Math.jet has only `min(a: Int, b: Int)`, `max(a: Int, b: Int)` and `clamp(x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int)`. They are Int-only and two-argument, and they need `math.` (36 sites in 19 files). Jet already has typed variadics (D-VARIADIC1: `name: ...T`), so this needs no new syntax.

Target surface, one mechanism (I8):
- `min(a, b, ...rest)` and `max(a, b, ...rest)`: at least two arguments of one ordered type T (Int, the sized integers, Float/F32/F64, Decimal, Duration, Instant, String, and any user type that implements Jet's ordering trait). The result is T.
- `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on the same T.
- All three are in the prelude, callable without import, and comptime-evaluable (`LIMIT :: max(4, CORES)`).
- Float: if any argument is NaN, the result is NaN (deterministic, documented).
- clamp keeps Jet's current lo > hi behavior unless the owner rules otherwise.
- Greenfield: `math.min`, `math.max` and `math.clamp` go away, and every caller migrates in the same cutover. List reducers (`xs.min()`, `iter.min()`, Stats/Data `min(xs)`) are a different meaning and stay.
cards.plan:
1. Define generic `min<T: Ord>(a: T, b: T, rest: ...T) -> T`, max and clamp in the one Core home the prelude exports (the CorePrelude entry table), with the real ordering-trait name. One runtime meaning on all tiers (I9); no codegen special case.
2. Add them to CorePrelude so they resolve with no import; keep a local or user definition named min shadowing as it does for other prelude names (check the shadowing rule and pin it in a test).
3. Delete math.min/max/clamp; migrate the 36 qualified sites and any bare user-defined helpers in Core and Examples that duplicate them.
4. Golden example Examples/features/basics/min_max_clamp.jet: Int, Float with NaN, String, Duration, a user ordered type, 2 and 5 arguments, spread `max(...xs)` with a 2+ list, a comptime constant, and clamp. UI snapshot for one-argument min (arity) and mixed types (E-code from the existing binder).
5. Update the LSP prelude test (Lsp03Tests CorePrelude.names) and the docs reference.

cards.title: Dispatch by type: `if T == { Int -> … else -> … }` in generics and bare member-type arms on unions
cards.body:
Owner 2026-10-29 (direct): Jai's dispatch by type 'just works' (`if param.value.tag == { Int -> … Float -> … else -> … }`); Jet must support it in idiomatic Jet.

Today (probed with chain s2 479d6936df, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/probe/typesw/):
- WORKS: runtime dispatch over a closed union `v: Int | Float | String` with `if v == { .Int(n) -> … .Float(f) -> … .String(s) -> … }` (D-UNIONTYPE1); prints `int 3` / `float 2.5`.
- MISSING: an arm without a binding (`.Int -> …`) is E0306; the arm must bind the payload.
- MISSING: compile-time dispatch on a generic type parameter. `if T == { Int -> … else -> … }` is E0107 (T is not a value); `T.$name` is comptime-only (E0302).
- RATIFIED NO: D-ANY-JAI1 rejects a general `Any` top type, so Jai's `Any` + type tag has no direct equivalent; heterogeneous values use unions or trait-bounded variadics.

The spelling is an owner gate: ballot D-TYPESWITCH1.
cards.plan: 1. Ballot D-TYPESWITCH1 (owner). 2. Implement the ratified form: generic type dispatch resolved at monomorphization (dead arms are not checked against the concrete type, or are, per the ballot), and union arms by member type with or without a binding. 3. Exhaustiveness: unions are closed sets and follow #6175 (no else); generic type dispatch is an open set and keeps else. 4. Goldens on O0/O1/O2, UI snapshots, registry, docs.

cards.title: Research: relative pointers and typed small indices, with types at compile time erased to a bare integer at run time
cards.body: Owner request (2026-10-29): research relative pointers and their benefits, and whether they can be used at comptime and erased for zero-cost run time. Owner's example: a Node {char text[32]; uint16_t left; uint16_t right;} in a fixed pool of 1024, linked by 16-bit indices. Prior art: Jai's self-relative pointers (`*~s16 T`), pool/arena index handles in C and game engines, generational handles (D-GAME-ENTITY1 in Jet), Rust index crates (typed_index_collections, slotmap), Zig and Odin practice, and position-independent data for mmap and serialization. Related Jet surfaces: @T links (D-MEMREF1), D-LINK-ITEM1, D-ARRAY-KEYED1 and D-ARRAY-LAYOUT1 (array package rework), and the implicit context and arena work.
cards.plan: Write a dated Docs/research document covering: self-relative versus base-relative (index) pointers; measured benefits (struct size, cache density, memcpy/serialize/mmap without fixups) with numbers from a C and Jet benchmark of the owner's Node pool; costs (range limits, the add on dereference, copying a self-relative pointer changes its target unless adjusted, null encoding, escape and aliasing); and how a typed index (element type, pool identity and index width known only at compile time) erases to a bare U16 with bounds checks proven away when the pool capacity equals the index range or indices only come from the pool. Map it onto Jet's existing surfaces and feed the array-programming package design. Owner-level surface goes to a ballot that meets the rework bar.

cards.title: ICE (exit 101): a package CheckedText literal with a run-time local in a hole goes to the comptime evaluator ('comptime.build unlowered: __comptime_item … checked-text')
cards.body: Found by ExtResearch and reproduced by Main at ec16c32d35 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/base/latest/jet run). Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/ExtResearch/probe/ice_hole.jet (`name :: "Ada"` then `accept(Token{"hello {name}"})`, where Token is a package CheckedText type). Output: internal compiler error: the comptime evaluator can't build `…Token checked text literal`: comptime.build unlowered: __comptime_item … checked-text. The repo examples pass only because their holes are constants ({7}). Core `SQL{"… {id}"}` with a local passes, because sema's hard-coded TypedHeadKind gives Core heads bound-hole lowering (#6208). I2 violation.
cards.plan: Lower package CheckedText literals with run-time holes the same way as the Core heads: validate the constant parts at compile time and bind the holes at run time, never sending the literal to the comptime evaluator. The root is shared with #6208. Add a golden with a local hole and a UI test if a hole type is rejected.

log.text: All criteria met; landed GoldC-maps c677a27e39.
Landed GoldC-rebase797 1edc185711 (C3 golden/ui/cases compare loses 0 rows pending): proof10 (goldc-n10* vs b6d and n9)

Main ruling (implementation within D-TEXTHEAD-TYPE1=A): a run-time hole is built as pieces + encode_hole(value), then check runs on the complete text at run time. A rejection is a registered stop naming the type and literal span, implemented once in the shared runtime (I9). Constant-only literals keep the compile-time check at zero run-time cost. A skeleton-only check was rejected because it is unsound when check depends on hole content: the contract is one pure complete-text checker, so every value of the type must have passed check (I1).

cards.title: Examples/features/ui/reactive.jet does not parse: `reactive.effect(...)` is E0003 because `effect` is a keyword after `.`
cards.body: Found by CoverPort's collect-all policy_check_gate (#5902). Examples/features/ui/reactive.jet:19 calls `reactive.effect(...)`. The dev parser (Compiler/JetParser … Expressions.jet:1783) rejects a keyword in member position, so the example has not parsed since at least 09-30, and G1 (every example passes on every tier) can't close while it fails. Two ways to fix it: member names after `.` accept keywords (contextual keywords, as Swift, Kotlin and C# do for member access), or the Core reactive API renames `effect`. Check the ratified reactive API name (Core/ui or reactive module) and the syntax registry: if `effect` is the ratified member name, the parser must accept it.
cards.plan: Determine the ratified name of the reactive effect API. If it is `effect`, make the member-name position accept registered keywords (one parser rule, with a UI test showing a keyword member works and that `effect` at statement start still means the keyword). Otherwise rename it in one cutover. Then make reactive.jet run on o0/o1/o2 with its golden.

cards.title: E1803 lists a parent effect beside its own children ("FS, FS.Read, FS.Write")
cards.body: Repro (BallotDesign probe q/bd/probe/proj tmp.jet, dev a9be739dae), run off a terminal: `fn run() { dir :: fs.temp_dir("t") ?? panic("x"); fs.write(fs.join(dir.path, "a"), "d") ?? panic("y"); print(fs.read(fs.join(dir.path, "a")) ?? "") }`. E1803 says authority is undecided for `FS, FS.Read, FS.Write` and that the program "reads and writes files, reads files and writes files". Under D-EFFTREE1 subsumption a parent covers its children, so the message should name the smallest covering set once.

cards.title: `?` refuses a NetError into a return union written with qualified members (`http.HTTPError | net.NetError | TaskFailure`): E2404
cards.body: LiveUI repro: Examples/features/net/http_route_markers.jet and the tests/cases/http auto_derived/mounted_* fixtures. `listener.local_addr()` fails with E2404: NetError can't propagate into `http.HTTPError | net.NetError | TaskFailure`. The union member written as `net.NetError` (module-qualified) is not matched against the NetError the call raises, so the qualified spelling of a member is compared by name, not by resolved type.
cards.plan: Resolve union members to their declared types before the propagation subset check, so a qualified and an unqualified spelling of one type are the same member.

log.text: Landed 5022832391 (GoldC-batch4).

cards.title: Speed of light: work backwards from hardware limits to what Jet must guarantee and generate, to beat Rust (tail calls and beyond)
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-30: "Work backwards from the speed of light as an engineering limitation to determine what the language should support or generate for machine code and binaries. Want to be faster than Rust, with tail optimizations etc." Owner: SurfaceDesign (design only).

log.text: All criteria met: research note landed (e784bb1ffe), ballots posted, gaps carded (#6357-#6363)

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's questions on speed-of-light code generation: for each hardware limit (instruction throughput, memory bandwidth and latency, cache, branch prediction, SIMD width, call overhead, code size) what the language must let the compiler know or guarantee (guaranteed tail calls, aliasing and exclusivity facts, layout control, bounds-check elimination, inlining, calling conventions, no hidden allocation), what Jet emits today (measured), and what Rust, Zig, C, Mojo and Odin guarantee, with every claim about Jet probed on o0, o1 and o2 or cited to file:line, and every peer claim cited.
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-speed-of-light.md (SurfaceDesign-docs3.patch): seven hardware limits from AMD Zen 4 SOG 57647 (dispatch, L1/L2/L3, branch mispredict, AVX-512, call bubble, op cache); Jet today vs Rust/Zig/C/Mojo/Odin guarantees; 14 kernels at Jet o0/o1/o2 vs Rust o0/o3/o3+overflow-checks in perf cycles and instructions (probes/pstat6343.tsv, dispatch row rerun with a rem_euclid peer); tail calls not jumps on any level (E3012), against D-DROP-ASAP1

criteria.text: Every owner choice the note raises is a Tower-ready ballot (readycheck READY, plaincheck PLAIN OK, recommendation.losses = []), with same-program alternatives and beginner and expert paths; implementation-only findings become criteria or cards, not ballots.
criteria.evidence: Ballot $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SurfaceDesign/ballot/D-TAIL-CALL1.json (A: every tail call is a jump on every level with a lint naming any blocker; B: explicit become; C: O2 only per D-RESOURCE-LIMIT1): PLAIN OK, READY, recommendation losses empty. Other owner-visible surfaces are already ratified (D-SIMD3, D-LANES1, D-INLINE-PARAM1, D-MEMREF-EXCL1, D-CACHE-CONTROL1, D-JAI-LAYOUT1); D-UB-BOUNDARY1 stays with MemDesign

criteria.text: Every measurable gap gets a paired perf cell plan against Rust under the Jet/Rust parity rule, and any compiler-only work is listed as criteria for the codegen cards.
criteria.evidence: Note sections 5-6: 13 compiler criteria for codegen cards, each tied to a kernel and the 1.05 gate; a paired Rust cell per kernel (sources probes/k6343 and probes/r6343/kernels.rs) plus two surface cells, tail_walk (tail call vs loop) and tail_interp (tail-call handlers vs loop+match)

cards.title: GPU: one cohesive way to run Jet code on the GPU, split CPU/GPU compilation and a portable kernel library, as in Mojo
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-30: "Mojo supports split compilation on CPU/GPU; how can Jet do that? Mojo has a portable GPU kernel library; can Jet use or support something similar to unlock maximum performance and let users more easily take advantage of the GPU? Right now the barrier to entry is massive. Need a cohesive experience to push code to the GPU: can we push code to run on the GPU? Sine is defined in Mojo so that it is portable; I want custom declarations where we can, to make Jet code more portable and accurate." Ratified GPU decisions already exist (D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1, D-GPU-SHADER-SURFACE1, D-GPU-F32-STORAGE1, D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1), and D-MATH-BITS1 (Jet-written math) is open. Owner: MemDesign (design only).

log.text: All criteria met: GPU note landed (f6eb2f2e08), D-GPU-DEVICE-OPS1 posted, gaps carded (#6347-#6349, #5454 log)

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's questions on GPU programming in Jet: Mojo's split CPU/GPU compilation and its portable kernel library (and CUDA, Triton, SYCL, Metal, WebGPU, Futhark, Halide), what the ratified D-GPU-* decisions give today and what is built (probed), how one Jet function could run on CPU or GPU with one meaning (I9), and how Jet-written math (sine and the rest) stays the same on every device, with every claim about Jet probed on o0, o1 and o2 or cited to file:line, and every peer claim cited.

cards.title: Early evaluation of :: values (D-COMPTIME-WORD1) is not built: BAD :: width(6, ...) stops at startup instead of failing the build
cards.body: Found by MemDesign-3 probes on dev 70b441a147 (2026-10-30); repros in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign-3/probes/. D-COMPTIME-WORD1 says a :: value whose inputs are known is worked out while compiling, so a failing rule should stop the build on that line. Today the program builds and stops when it starts.

log.text: Main 2026-10-30: filed against a superseded rule. The owner's newer direction #6125 (2026-10-29; syntax-decisions.md:8174-8183, spec.md:472-477) says a module :: value that fails while building is computed at startup, before fn run, with no build error; only comptime { } forces a build error (E3010). Today's behavior matches it, proved by the golden Examples/features/comptime/startup_trap.jet and tests/ui/comptime_reads_startup_constant (BugSweep check, 2026-10-30). The original criterion 1 (a build error for any known-input :: value) is replaced by the current rule. D-COMPTIME-WORD1's wording predates #6125.

criteria.text: A module :: value follows the owner direction #6125: it folds while building when its evaluation is pure and succeeds, and otherwise is computed at startup before fn run with no build error, the same on o0, o1 and o2; a golden example proves it. (Replaces the original criterion, which asked for a build error under the older D-COMPTIME-WORD1 wording.)

cards.title: Closing values are closed twice when returned or unwrapped with ?? (double free; self-built compiler deadlocks in jet check)
cards.body:
Root found by DeclTypes-3 (2026-10-30) on clean dev 03c64ad0c4. Since 78862972bd (ir_close_holds_handle), a struct holding a FileReader is a closing value, so Option and Result locals of it get close glue. Two IR paths then close the same payload twice:
(1) ir_return (JetIR BuildExpr.jet about line 4506) owns the returned slot through ir_own, which retains a held box into a new slot; ir_emit_return disarms only the new slot, so the variable close stays armed and closes the payload again at scope exit. This hits a tail `x`, `return x` and `^x` of an Option or Result local.
(2) ir_or_fallback: `found :: held ?? return ...` copies a held carrier payload into a result that the Let arms as its own closer while the carrier stays armed.
Resolver.jet:159-165 checked_manifest uses exactly that shape, so the self-built compiler (s2) frees the FileReader state twice and fd_lock futex-waits forever in `jet check <package>`; the seed a0_021 predates 78862972bd, so seed-built s1 is fine. This blocks every seed roll. A plain user `impl Res.Close` type prints "close" twice for a tail return, `^x` and `?? + bind` (repro m9), so the double close is user-visible and is a memory-safety defect (I1). Repros: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes/r8/close (m1, m5, m7 hang; m9 double close).

criteria.text: A closing value (a user `impl T.Close` type, and a struct holding a FileReader, inside Option or Result) is closed exactly once when returned as a tail value, by `return x`, by `^x`, and when unwrapped with `?? return` and bound; a case row per shape prints "close" once on o0, o1 and o2.

cards.title: Jetpack tests call APIs that were never built: expert zeroize and the JetOS install-identity helpers
cards.body:
