questions.text: i want to test jet's c ffi auto binding/codegen abilities with raylib bindings but I want a native jet version of raylib that we own that BEATS raylib. i dont know what value comes with fonts though so if theres a good reason for that then I guess we can card building our own, otherwise it can be ffi binding
questions.answer: Our own font engine is worth building, for four reasons. First, exact pixels: FreeType's output changes with its version and build flags, so with a binding the same Jet program draws slightly different text on different machines, and headless text goldens could never be exact on every tier. A Jet engine draws the same pixels everywhere. Second, nothing to install: a static Jet program cannot load FreeType or HarfBuzz at all without a dynamic loader, which is why the native tier shapes no text today. Third, safety: font files are untrusted input, and FreeType parsing bugs keep recurring. One of them, CVE-2025-27363, was exploited in the wild, and Chrome moved its web-font reading from FreeType to memory-safe Rust (Fontations) in 2025 for that reason. Fourth, one engine serves both the native game library and the gui toolkit, on wasm and embedded too. Raylib itself vendors a small font reader (stb_truetype) and does no shaping, so stage 1 of our engine (reading outlines, anti-aliased glyphs, kerning, ligatures) already beats raylib's text. Stage 2 ports complex-script shaping and is proven against HarfBuzz's own test data. The revised ballot therefore recommends three first-party packages: `raylib`, generated from raylib.h by the C binder as its showcase; `ray`, the native Jet library that beats raylib; and `font`, the Jet engine. Anyone who still wants FreeType or HarfBuzz can bind it through the C binder as an ordinary package.

cards.title: Jet test collect-all recompiles the whole program after every failing claim
cards.body: CoverPort finding (2026-10-30, g8): check.sh's collect-all default tier restarts `jet run` (a full recompile) after each failing claim, bounding each segment at 1800 s. A file with N failing claims costs N+1 full compiles; Engine (96 pass / 8 fail) and CLI (48 / 49) exceed a 3000 s cap. With observe faults fixed (g8) the runs keep going, so the cost now shows. This is the main wall-time bottleneck in ported test runs and blocks G11 (fast testing).
cards.plan: Compile once and keep going in-process: each claim runs under the test runner's trap boundary so a failing claim records a row and the next claim runs in the same process; restart (without recompiling, reusing the built artifact) only after a process-killing fault.

cards.title: A move out through a guard field (`^guard.value.stream`) is not recorded, so Shared drop glue closes the moved resource again (segfault)
cards.body: Found by DeclTypes-3 on 2026-10-31 (wave 10 tree) while fixing #6441. Moving a Close resource out of a Shared cell through its guard (`^guard.value.stream`) does not mark the field as moved. When the Shared cell drops, its drop glue closes the stream a second time, and the program segfaults. This is an I1 memory-safety defect: safe code must never double-close or use a freed resource. Ownership sema must record a partial move through a guard projection, and drop glue must skip moved fields (or the move must be rejected with a registered diagnostic, if the spec forbids it).

cards.title: Native compiler parallelism that actually scales: allocator caches, fewer allocations, lock-free shared reads, dynamic scheduling, parallel serial phases
cards.body:
Goal: native compiles actually scale with threads. Parallel phases reach >= 10x on 16 threads, serial phases shrink, and output is byte-identical for every thread count. This is the path from about 400 LOC/s toward the 1M LOC/s goal and to a self-rebuild measured in minutes.

Evidence (2026-10-16, r28 native stage-1 on the JetFoundation partition): 96.6% of sema.bodies CPU spins on the allocator's one global CAS lock (#5042). Runtime entries: alloc 27.7%, string_drop 22.8%, string_clone 21.6%, free 18.6%. Shared<T> reads take a mutex plus condvar on both acquire and release (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Shared.jet:44-77). Codegen lowering splits work statically (compiler_threads_partition). load, register (23 s on 67k lines), comptime, assemble, object and link run serially.

P0 Measure (before any change, and kept as the gate)
- The trace records per-span process CPU time (user+sys) next to wall time, so every phase reports parallel efficiency = cpu / (wall x threads).
- Scaling matrix: fixed partitions (foundation, sema, whole compiler) at 1/2/4/8/16 threads, wall time per phase. Recorded in the performance manifest as required cells.
- Determinism gate: the same compile at 1 and 16 threads gives byte-identical jet.o. It runs in CI-local and in the self-rebuild.
- Lock profile: perf share at the allocator lock and the Shared mutex per phase, reported by the census tool.

P1 Allocator (#5042), the biggest lever
- Per-thread caches: each thread keeps a small free list (magazine) per size class. alloc and free touch only the thread's own cache. Only a full or empty magazine exchanges one batch (e.g. 32 blocks) with the shared slabs under the lock, so the lock is taken about 30x less. A block freed on another thread joins the freeing thread's cache; the size class comes from the slab header. Slab live counts are updated per batch. Thread exit flushes its cache.
- The shared lock becomes futex-backed (sleep, not spin) like sync_mutex_lock, so waiting threads stop burning cores.
- Large blocks (> 4 KiB, mmap'd directly today): add size classes up to 64 KiB, plus a small per-thread cache of recent large mappings, to stop mmap/munmap churn (the kernel's mm lock is a second hidden serializer).
- Counting mode (ProgramAllocator policy lock): per-thread counters summed on read, so leak tracking stays exact without a global lock per allocation.
- Proof: runtime alloc tests; a cross-thread stress test (N threads allocating and freeing each other's blocks); the leak tracker floor on the probe set; the scaling matrix.

P2 Allocate far less (fewer lock trips and less work)
- #5041 no implicit copies: codegen borrow/move by default, plus the census gate (copies/census.mjs --baseline).
- Names as interned symbols: identifiers, keys and module names become interned IDs (one table, built in parallel per module and merged deterministically) instead of String clones.
- Immutable shared strings: cloning an unchanged String bumps a count instead of copying bytes, matching the list storage-sharing law.
- Per-module arenas for AST/TIR nodes that live and die together, released in bulk at phase end.

P3 Shared<T> read path
- Phase-frozen data (the module scope during the body pass, the registration graph after register) is handed to threads as an immutable snapshot with plain reads and no guard.
- Shared<T> gets a reader fast path: one atomic add when no writer is active or waiting, with the mutex and condvar only on contention. Writer preference stays as it is.

P4 Work distribution
- Dynamic scheduling: workers claim chunks from an atomic index (largest first by weight) instead of a fixed split, so one heavy chunk doesn't idle the rest.
- One persistent compiler thread pool reused by every phase (no spawn per wave), sized from the allowed CPUs.
- Results are always merged in canonical index order, never completion order, which preserves the determinism gate.

P5 Parallelize the serial phases (one at a time, each behind the determinism gate)
- load: lex and parse files in parallel.
- register: build each module's rows in parallel, then a short serial link step.
- sema finalize/effects and comptime bodies: per function where there are no cross-body dependencies.
- assemble and object: per function or section emission in parallel, concatenated in canonical order.
- link: stays single but becomes the only serial tail.

Order: P0 first. Then P1 and the P2 copy work run in parallel (independent owners), then P3, P4, P5. Each lands with its scaling-matrix row and the determinism gate green. No phase lands if it changes output bytes or regresses any cell.

cards.title: Core JSON decode of a huge exponent (e.g. 1e999999999) materializes an unbounded Int: hang/OOM from hostile input
cards.body: Reported by ToolsJet-2 (2026-10-31), [INFERENCE] from a probe: `decode<Int>` on the Dyn.Number lexeme "1e400" builds a 401-digit Int. Since Dyn.Number keeps the spelling and the integer read expands the exponent, a hostile document such as {"n":1e999999999} given to any JSON reader can hang or exhaust memory. Every reader of untrusted JSON is exposed. core-library.md:2816-2817 says .int(), .float() and typed decoding check the destination range; the check must happen before the digits are materialized.

questions.text: I told you to start from the language/library that does this best and improve on any downsides or make substantial improvements if you can. for this case why do we have a separate way to write int? why not make the json method int instead of integer? I told you to ensure the recommended option has all downsides engineered away
questions.answer:
You're right; there shouldn't be a second name. The ballot now recommends making `.int()` itself the strict read, the way serde_json's `as_i64`, Go's `Number.Int64` and C#'s `GetInt64` work. `.int()` accepts only a number written as an integer, and refuses `7.0` and `1e2`. Typed decoding into an `Int` field uses the same rule, so there is one rule and one name.

It also improves on those libraries in three ways:
- **No size cap.** Jet's `Int` is exact, so any written integer reads in full. serde returns None past 64 bits.
- **A real error.** A refusal is a field error with the path and the reason, not a bare None.
- **No slow inputs.** The spelling is checked before the value is built. Today the eight characters `1e999999` keep both `.int()` and `decode<Int>()` busy for more than two minutes, and that goes away.

The strict helper in the compiler library is deleted, and so are its two private copies.

The one cost that cannot be removed: a producer that writes a whole number as `2.0` (for example a Python float) is refused for `Int`. That value is a float at the producer, so the error message says to read it with `.float()` or to declare the field `Float` or `Decimal`.

cards.title: Map top_n(k) is O(n^2) over all entries; rank in O(n log k)
cards.body: top_n(k) lowers to an insertion sort over ALL n entries; k only limits the final copy. With the hashed Map at O2: wordfreq 10k costs +15% instructions; 200k distinct words take 68.13 s against 2.45 s for to_list + sort_by. The plain user spelling must not be a performance trap (owner order: faster than every peer for any program). Found by Codegen-1 (wave 14, Codegen-1-23.msg).

cards.title: Core regex runs an NFA simulation per match: add literal pre-checks and a cached DFA
cards.body: Profile (Codegen-1, 2026-10-31, bulkrename O2 release): the per-entry regex NFA simulation is about 26% of cycles (core_regex scan 12.9%, add 8.5%, filled 4.2%, ~5.5M of 21.1M; the ref.S is 85K). Ceiling pareto root 11. Fix in Core/Regex: a required-literal pre-check (memchr/memmem) before simulation and a lazily built DFA cached per compiled Regex, with identical match semantics (leftmost-first, captures via the NFA only when asked). Proof: regex cases and goldens unchanged on o0/o1/o2, bulkrename and regex-logscan cycles before/after.

criteria.text: core.regex answers existence with a DFA and skips text by its required literals, with identical match semantics: regex cases and goldens unchanged, and bulkrename and regex-logscan improve with no ceiling cell worse.

questions.text: Couldn't we just have a top-level package, and any nested packages would be subpackages? Having a separate project just makes it needlessly complex and confusing.
questions.answer: Yes. Option D is now on this ballot and recommended. There is only package.jet. The top one is the root package: it has its own code and holds the tree-wide settings (profiles, environments, toolchain pin, policy). Every package.jet below it is a subpackage, found automatically, so there is no members list and no project.jet. Only the root may set tree settings, and publishing strips them, so dependents never see them. A root can never skip its own code (bug B1). Test fixtures and vendored packages are kept out with exclude: globs and .gitignore. If D wins, D-PROJECT-WORDS1 shrinks to naming only: there is no packages:/members: list left to name.

cards.body: Owner request 2026-10-30 (evening batch for the reserved design slots; the owner is away, so the answer must stand alone in a report). Today fn dev serves web development (servers) and jet env handles environments. Weigh one construct against two and an env entry point, for consistency and scale. Relates to D-ENTRY-HOME1 (#6368), which must stay coherent with the answer.

questions.text: Since we are targeting being a replacement for not just nix but devenv we probably should lean toward a jet flavored devenv approach. I think having a separate env entry point might be useful but by default should just have great standard experience logic that runs the written env setup. This needs to be modular and scalable, everything from a simple devenv scope to a full nixos config (but our version as jetos)
questions.answer: Agreed. A redesign is in progress: one modular environment model, devenv-style. Environments are Jet values composed from modules (packages, services, processes, scripts, env vars, languages, hooks). By default jet dev or entering the folder just applies them, an optional entry point covers custom logic, and the same module system scales to a whole-machine JetOS config. It is consistent with D-PROJECT-ROOT1 D (environments: in the root package.jet). The reworked ballot will replace this one.

questions.text: i told you we should also have an env entry point. this should be an expert opt in for custom logic, not the default. default should stay the easy simple static configuration, but experts should be able to have full control via an env api and logic and entry point.
questions.answer: Agreed; reworking now. Default: simple static environments: data in the root package.jet. Expert opt-in: an env entry point (env.jet, a dev fn) with a full core.env API (packages, services, processes, scripts, variables, hooks, languages, JetOS systems). The static data is its default input, which the entry point can read and change. The ballot will be updated in place.

cards.title: Function-boundary performance: returns, allocation and buffers optimized by the compiler to beat C and Rust
cards.body:
Owner 2026-10-04 (with D-OUTPUT-RETURNS1=A ratified): "ensure we HIGHLY optimize the entire process around functions at the lowest possible level, optimizing allocation and buffers etc at the compiler level so we beat c/rust performance if physically possible".
Research baseline: Docs/research/output-parameters-vs-returns-2026-10-04.md (rustc 4 KiB array return 116-128 ns vs 51 ns out-param; fresh 4 KiB Vec per call 11-18% slower than reuse).
Scope: return-slot (destination-passing) lowering for aggregates so returning is never slower than an output parameter on any tier; automatic buffer/capacity reuse for returned collections in loops; escape analysis with stack placement and scalar replacement of non-escaping aggregates; allocation sinking/hoisting and elision; producer/consumer fusion that removes intermediate collections; small inline storage where it measures faster. Every surface or optimization arrives with paired cells against C and Rust under the AGENTS performance gate (Rust parity <=1.05, others <1.00), one meaning on every tier (I9), no semantic or diagnostic change.
cards.plan: 1 design + baseline cells (RetPerfDesign) 2 return-slot lowering 3 capacity reuse 4 escape analysis/SROA/stack placement 5 fusion 6 gate

questions.text: Im pretty sure we removed the shared keyword and replaced it with @ to "link"
questions.answer: You're right. On 2026-09-28 you chose `@` as the spelling for a live shared value (D-MEMREF1=A). The lexical ledger (syntax-decisions.md:34) lists `@` as the live link, and the memory-model proposal (:144) records that it replaces `Shared<T>`, `View`, `Cell` and `Pin`. The `shared` keyword is still in the registry (Spellings.jet:160, KW_SHARED) only because `@` links are not built yet; nothing in the ruling keeps it. The revised ballot uses `@`. Module state that functions change is declared `HITS :: @0`, and every write stays as written, `HITS += 1`. A fixed `::` link can never point anywhere else, so assigning to its name can only change the value it points at, and no wrapper struct is needed. The built `shared` holder does need one: `TICKS :: shared 0` with `TICKS += 1` is E0111 today (probe a26). Under D-MEMREF-TASK1=A, a link that no task reaches is a plain word with no lock, and a link that a task reaches takes one lock per statement. The rule lands with the module part of the link build. Until then, E0111's fix writes today's `shared` struct holder, and `jet fix` respells it as `@` once links land.

cards.title: A Close temporary passed to `.drop(...)` or `close(^make(...))` is never closed

cards.title: A function with a pack parameter (`...[Edit, Inspect]`) that is never called is not type-checked
cards.body: Found by DeclTypes-3 on 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): when a function has a `...[Edit, Inspect]` pack parameter and no call site, sema never checks its body, so `item.nothing_here()` (a call to a method that does not exist) passes `jet check`. Every declared function must be checked once against its declared bounds whether or not it is called; instantiation-only checking hides errors in library code.

cards.title: Eight required gauntlet entries do not build on dev 02f8130821
cards.body: Sweep by TestGreen-3 on the 02f8130821 compiler. Six fail with a false E1004 "exposes X, but not in this position" on qualified Core calls under a bare `use core.files` import (bulkrename files.rename, concurrency-service time.sleep, http-service server.response, logreport and regex-logscan files.open, taskfile-cli files.exists/process.args). The cause is sema: a bare Core import binds the module under its name, not the loaded Core identity, so the call route finds no source functions. Qualified access is legal (core-library.md:241-246). Two fail for other reasons: embedded-data (E0965 index 255 out of range for a 4-element list) and web-app (E0225 & mark on a read-only receiver). A required cell that does not build is a gate failure.

log.text: Closed on dev 163d4852ad: all eight entries build and print their expected output (criteria 1 and 2 evidence). The wider every-cell O0/O1/O2 proof stays on #6482.

OWNER QUESTION (TestGreen-3/Main 2026-10-31): C2-CLI (#Target(Web) inference + E-WEB-RUN on `jet run`) is held. Owner commit 727bd90801 (2026-10-20, "fn run() serves apps", D-ENTRY-RUN1) removed the App-return entry exemption and migrated app_hello, app_typed_args, forms_table, tanstack_start and web_app to `run() { … .serve() }`. But the ratified D-ENTRY-VALUE1=B (syntax-decisions.md:6853-6859) and spec.md:4353 still say a returned App is served at the runtime edge, and D-ENTRY-RUN1 is not recorded in syntax-decisions.md. Refusing `jet run` on #Target(Web) would turn the passing case web_app/app_hello_serves_home_and_save_action into a failure. Decide: (1) record D-ENTRY-RUN1 in the spec and exempt programs whose run() serves from E-WEB-RUN, or (2) restore `-> App` entries per D-ENTRY-VALUE1=B. TestGreen3-28 has drafts of both.

cards.title: Single-threaded programs emit unlocked reference-count operations
cards.body: UiGreen-1 2026-10-31 (card-request-size.md §1b): in sieve 773 of 773 and in wordfreq 836 of 836 inline RC sites use lock-prefixed inc/dec/xadd, yet neither binary contains pthread_create, __clone or a clone/clone3 syscall. When the whole program (user code + reachable Core + runtime entries) can never start a second thread, every RC op can be a plain inc/dec with identical semantics. Derive the fact from the program call graph before codegen (no reachable task/thread spawn route, no runtime-internal thread start) and select unlocked forms only then; any reachable spawn keeps today’s locked forms. http-service (links pthread_create) needs per-value escape facts and is out of scope here. Proof: sieve/wordfreq lock-site count 0, ceiling A/B cycles and bytes, a probe that adds one task spawn flips every site back to locked, FULL cases + s2 chain + doctor + check.

log.text: Closed on dev 163d4852ad with the criterion 1 evidence.

Landed on dev at undefined in UiGreen-34: program lock sites sieve 853->0, wordfreq 900->0 (runtime pack's 48/67 unchanged); tests/cases/single_thread_rc 6/6 PASS (base 4/6: the two unlocked cases fail); spawn/signal/async/unvetted-FFI cases stay locked; missing receipt stays locked; UiGreen-34.msg

UiGreen-34 landed in wave 19 (dev 45ab3b5ef5): a program that provably never starts a second thread updates inline RC counts without the lock prefix, gated by the runtime pack's thread receipt; single_thread_rc cases added. Close after the asm-parity census on the landed compiler shows the unlocked counts in sieve/wordfreq and http-service keeps locked forms.

criteria.text: A program that can never start a second thread emits plain (unlocked) reference-count inc/dec in user and Core code, and any reachable task/thread spawn, signal handler, async handler or unvetted foreign call keeps the locked forms.
criteria.evidence: UiGreen-34 (landed wave 19). On dev 163d4852ad all 6 tests/cases/single_thread_rc/* PASS in cases-w22-wave: never-starts, vetted libc, task spawn, signal, async handler, unvetted foreign. Their objdump steps run only 'when tool objdump', and objdump is not on PATH here, so IrTypes-3 checked by hand. Built gauntlet sieve and wordfreq with jet build --release --debug-info=true on the 163d jet, then disassembled with nix binutils objdump. Lock-prefixed RC sites in user/Core code: 0. The 2 (sieve) and 5 (wordfreq) remaining lock sites are inside runtime-pack helpers (jet_world_now, jet_string_from_bytes, jet_err_apply_conversion). Unlocked incq/decq sites: 721 and 783.

cards.title: Safe code can forge Core resource handles (SqliteDB, JetcFd, FileWriter) via struct literals
cards.body: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 on the w16 s2 jet: `use core.db.[SqliteDB]; SqliteDB{raw: 1}` type-checks and crashes with SIGSEGV (rc 139) at Close (Core/Db/Db.jet:1387); `use core.crypto.[JetcFd]; JetcFd{fd: 1}` closes stdout at scope end; `FileWriter{path: "/etc/passwd"}` checks clean and ICEs at run (rc 101, unlowered struct literal of FileWriter). cards.title: Backend shrink-wrapping: no callee-saved prologue on early-exit fast paths
cards.body: Codegen-1 2026-10-31: the list-uniqueness helper pays a full 5-register prologue/epilogue on its fast path (already unique, return at once), and that call cost is what made hoisting uniqueness checks a loss (uq +12.8% instructions). cards.title: BALLOT D-EXPLAIN-NORECORD1: what jet explain-build shows when no build record exists
cards.body: Owner decision needed (product behavior of a shipped command). Found by CLIParity3 porting the build-graph CLI rows. Today the two implementations disagree when no authenticated build record exists for the target. Rust (Source/CmdCompile.rs:807-856, schema jet.explain-build/v1) prints the checked static graph with duration_ms: 0.000 and why_ran: first-run for every node, indistinguishable from a measured run. The Jet port (Compiler/JetCli InspectBuild.jet:175-180, commit adba07463, no decision ID) refuses with E2104 and its fixture asserts no first-run output. D-BUILDQUERY1=A ratifies the shared CLI / editor graph and provenance but says nothing about the missing-record case. Options (same program: jet explain-build on a target never built): A) refuse with E2104 'no build record for <target>; run jet build first' (no graph). Beginner: clear next step. Expert: loses the static graph. B) print the checked static graph with each node marked not-run: no duration field (null), why_ran: never-run, plus a header line 'no build record: showing the planned graph'. Beginner: sees what a build would do. Expert: graph available, nothing fabricated. C) keep the Rust output (duration_ms 0.000, why_ran first-run). Presents 0 ms as if measured. Main recommends B (truthful and useful); A is the strict alternative. After the ruling, both implementations and the fixture migrate in one cutover.

log.text: Closed: D-EXPLAIN-NORECORD1 A is implemented (IrTypes-44, a34ef0affd). The other 5 explain-build cases stay known-failing under #6418, because jet build does not write a record yet (#6431).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-44: D-EXPLAIN-NORECORD1=A (ratified 2026-11-01, outcome A: always list the planned steps, list measured steps only when recorded) is implemented. Before any build is recorded, `jet inspect explain-build main.jet` exits 0 and prints "no build recorded for main.jet yet; planned steps:" followed by the check, compile and link rows (kind, key, subject, inputs). `--json` is jet.explain-build/v1 with nodes:[] and 3 planned entries that have no duration_ms or why_ran field. A record for another program keeps E2104 (asserted in Compiler/JetCli/Tests/InspectBuild.jet, which type-checks but was not executed). New case tests/cases/build_entry/explain_build_lists_planned_steps_before_any_build.case: PASS on s1 4a9bf4cdea5d72ac (q/sg/cases-irt44.txt), FAIL on base 163d4852ad (q/sg/cases-irt44base.txt). Also: compiler_speed_explain_build_reports_release_nodes goes KF to PASS. lane-check CHECK OK.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-EXPLAIN-NORECORD1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Scope addition (CLIParity3): the fabricated-zero problem is not only the missing-record case. In NORMAL receipts the Rust adapter (Source/CmdCompile.rs:15103-15152) maps every Check node to duration_ms 0.0, because there is no per-module check timer; compile / link durations come from real action timing. So the ballot also covers: what a Check node reports when its duration isn't measured. Options mirror the main ballot: A) omit Check nodes from timed output; B) keep them with duration null / 'not timed' (Main recommends, consistent with B above); C) keep 0.0 (current Rust; presents an unmeasured value as measured); D) add a real per-module check timer so the value is measured (implementation cost; no ballot needed if chosen, only scope). CLIParity3's Jet design already separates the static graph projection from actual Host action observations and publishes no BuildRecord from a query.

criteria.text: Per ratified D-EXPLAIN-NORECORD1 A: before any build is recorded, jet inspect explain-build exits 0 and lists the planned steps (kind, key, subject, inputs) with no time or reason; --json has an empty nodes list; with a record the measured rows print as before; a case pins text and --json.

cards.title: Owner decisions from the 2026-10-23 memory review (9 questions)
cards.body:
The memory review (Docs/audits/2026-10-23-memory-model-review.md) needs owner rulings before its larger items can be planned. Each needs a ballot with same-program alternatives:
1. Build the expert tier (arenas, raw pointers, sentries) now, or mark it unbuilt?
2. Start the @ link cutover, or reaffirm View/Shared/Cell/Pin?
3. Build a collector for #Policy(gc), or retire it and its sema code?
4. #Context(allocator:/logger:): build or remove?
5. Accept the layout and glue change to stop boxing Option/Result/enums (#5469, #4620)?
6. Non-atomic or biased reference counts by default (#5041)?
7. Secrets: own locked pages, or stop locking pages?
8. Long-lived host heap: reclaim between runs, or accept the leak?
9. Settle ballot #4935 (take/replace out of a borrowed field).

log.text: Closed: the card's action, getting the owner's rulings, is complete. Building them is tracked on the cards those decisions name (#4620, #4935, #4756, #5022).

cards.title: `s += x` copies the whole string: O(n²) string building
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R1 (cells: w12 all metrics (TIMEOUT)). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `s += x` copies the whole string each time: O(n²). `.Concat` lowers to `jet_rt_string_concat` (`Compiler/JetIR/Source/X64Select.jet:1742`), which always allocates a new exact-size buffer and copies both sides (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Text.jet:334-354`). No in-place append, no spare capacity.

Evidence: `bin/jet run probes/strcat.jet 100000` 2.42 s; `… 200000` 10.80 s (2× n → 4.5× time). Full w12 (2,000,000 appends) > 120 s. Paired probe `probes/strjoin.jet` (push parts, `join("")`, `jet build --release`; not a gate cell): `hyperfine -N --runs 10 --warmup 1`, cores 24-27: 476.6 ms ± 23.0, peak RSS 241,336 KB. That beats only LuaJIT (1,032 ms), Lua (1,764 ms), pwsh (1,722 ms) and Nushell (2,927 ms); Perl 69.7 ms, PHP 134.9 ms, Node 262.7 ms, Python 343.6 ms and Ruby 367.2 ms are faster (warm).

log.text: All criteria met with evidence; closed.

cards.title: A sleeping program wakes every 2 ms (idle compensation worker)
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R19 (cells: w15 jet-bin CPU). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: A sleeping Jet program keeps waking up. `time.sleep` parks through `scheduler_yield`, which marks a blocking wait (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Scheduler.jet:687`); an idle compensation worker waits on its condition in 2 ms slices (`:957`). About one futex timeout every 2 ms fits that loop [INFERENCE: strace does not name the thread].

Evidence: `strace -f -c build/w15_watch/main` (30 sleeps of 100 ms): 1,663 `futex` (1,299 timed out), 1,511 `clock_gettime`, 25 `clone`. Timed cells: jet-bin warm CPU 12.6 ms (sys 9.5) vs lua 3.7 ms, perl 10.6 ms.

log.text: Closed: c1 root fixed (783310b83f), c2 binary beats every peer on w15; jet-run launch cells are report-only (D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B) and logged on #6087.

cards.title: A kept stdin handle's lines() grows memory without bound at an invalid UTF-8 line
cards.body:
Found 2026-11-01 by CardClose-1; it OOM'd the build machine (44 GB).

Repro: `h :: io.stdin()` then `loop line in h.lines() { print(line) }` with stdin `printf 'ok\n\xff\xfe\nnever\n'`. On wave/24 s1, jet run, --release and the built binary print nothing, write no stderr, and grow until OOM (2 GB in about 4 s).

Root: jet_rt_native_iter_stdin_lines drains a borrowed handle eagerly (iter_collect_node -> iter_drain -> iter_pull -> iter_source_pull -> lazy.line_next). On the bad line read_line returns Err; line_next panics; the program body is a task, so rt_task_panic_publish turns it into a pending stop and returns. The stop check takes ir_stop_return, whose stop edge returns "no result written" (edx=1) but leaves rax=1 from the stop poll. iter_source_pull reads only rax (1 = moved), pushes an unwritten slot and pulls again. Every later read_line returns at once at its stdio_checkpoint, so the push loop never ends and the panic is never reported. Process line sources and file handles share lazy.line_next and are exposed the same way.

Fix direction: an IRBuilder.stop_status flag so ir_stop_return returns -1 on a stop edge of bodies the runtime trusts for a status word; ir_line_next_body sets it.

log.text: Closed by Main: criteria 1 and 2 met; CardClose-60 landed as part of dev 1620f05362 (wave 26 batch). Wave 26 cases include the new stdin_lines_keep_read_line_text_on_every_tier case.

Its 1.9-3.4 s and 660 MB are the compiler, and base matches that (655 MB, 3.7 s for the same program). On base the kept handle is OOM-killed on every tier (4G cap at 13.2 s; the 64M cap within 0.31 s). File line source (`files.open(p).lines()`): AsmPar-1's regex-logscan rebuilt with tsh exits 70 on /dev/shm/asmpar/rls/bad.log (default 94 ms, release 27 ms, 64M cap) with `panic: invalid input during read ...: stream did not contain valid UTF-8`, while its a34base binary is OOM-killed (rc 137, 455 ms; rc 124 at 10 s uncapped). cards.title: A foreign C host that never calls jet_rt_host_arguments runs with checked-alloc unenforced
cards.body: AsmPar-15 (2026-10-31) moves the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC environment scan out of eager startup and into the host argument path. A foreign C host that embeds the Jet runtime and never calls jet_rt_host_arguments is therefore not refused or checked under JET_CHECKED_ALLOC; it runs unchecked. Make the checked-alloc decision reachable on every entry (for example, on the first allocation, from envp captured once at a defined point) without restoring the eager whole-environment scan, and add an embed-host case.

log.text: The startup environment scan is deleted. A C host that links the runtime object with a system linker keeps the jet_rt_alloc_check_init hook, so it always runs checked: never unenforced, and never dependent on whether it calls jet_rt_host_arguments. The prelinked runtime image leaves out the hook and jet_rt_alloc_check_link (RuntimePack.jet LINK_IMAGE_UNROOTED_EXPORTS), so image-bound programs stay unchecked. alloc-parity embed-clean and embed-double-free PASS. Landed in wave 29 as dev 11cf095719 (AsmPar-26).
Main: superseded in approach by D-CHECKED-BUILD1=A (unchecked builds link no checked heap, so a foreign host can't run unenforced). Implementing as AsmPar-26.

AsmPar-25 (lazy check at the first allocation; hello 1,273 instructions in every environment) is held, not landed: it lets user code run before the exit-70 refusal, against D-SIZE-PAYUSE1 A ('stops with exit 70 before user code'). The scan's removal waits on D-CHECKED-BUILD1.

Main-1 (wave 24, landed as dev a34ef0affd; ui/cases rows from $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/sg/{ui,cases}-w24-wave.txt) moves UiGreen-37's case fixture from fn main to fn run; the checked_alloc_request case PASSES. The card stays open: the eager startup env scan it forbids is still in .init_array. See also D-CHECKED-BUILD1 (redesigned 2026-11-01 as a build flag, which would delete the scan).

Stays open; UiGreen-37's approach misses this card's own constraint. The card asks for the checked-alloc decision on every entry 'without restoring the eager whole-environment scan'. UiGreen-37 (wave 22) adds jet_rt_alloc_check_refuse_init (Compiler/JetRuntime Alloc.jet:266, 301 B) to .init_array. At every startup it walks all of envp and byte-compares each 'J…' entry against JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1. AsmPar-1 bisected hello's instructions:u: 45ab = w19 = w20 = w21 = 2682, w22 = w23 = 3235 (+553, more with more JET_* vars; asm-parity measured +725), at default and release. Rows: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/AsmPar/selfab/hello-bis.tsv. Needed: decide lazily, as the card suggests (envp captured once, read on the first allocation or the first host-argument call), so a program that never allocates pays nothing; then re-prove run-alloc-parity embed-* and the checked_alloc_request case.

wave 22 landed as dev 163d4852ad (wave s2 FIXED_POINT; goldens 1203=1203 0 lost; ui +1 0 lost; cases 2335 -> 2458, 1 lost = blocks_shared_by_two_tasks_are_freed_once E2105 build-write error under suite load, PASS alone via suite.sh --filter on the same s2). cards.title: jet refuses to start under JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1, so no checked program can be built
cards.body: Found by CardClose-1 on 2026-11-01 (log $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/smr.out). Docs/spec/reference/environment.md and Host.jet:420-425 (jet_cli_checked_alloc) say JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1 is set when jet builds a program, and only such a build links the runtime's checked heap. But jet is itself a Jet program built without the checked heap, and the runtime's refusal (a program built without the checked allocator exits 70 when the variable is set) fires in jet's own startup. a0_022, the wave-21 s1 and tsb s1 all exit 70 with 'jet checked allocator (JET_CHECKED_ALLOC=1): this program was built without the checked allocator'. cards.title: jet build overwrites its output in place: E2105 Text file busy when the previous binary is still running or held
cards.body: IrTypes-3 and Main, 2026-11-01. tests/cases/memory_semantics/blocks_shared_by_two_tasks_are_freed_once fails intermittently on chain-built compilers: 2 of 11 runs on the IrTypes stack s1, 1 of 12 on a base 1620f05362 chain s1, and once in the wave 25 suite. Step 3, jet build main.jet, reports E2105 'Couldn't write …/.jet/build/main: Text file busy (os error 26)' right after the release build step passed. jet build opens the existing output path for writing. Linux refuses that while any process is executing the file, or while a forked child still holds an inherited descriptor. Root fix: write the image to a temporary file in the same directory (O_CLOEXEC) and rename() it over the destination. That is atomic, never ETXTBSY, and never leaves a half-written executable. Same meaning on every tier.

cards.title: `jet fix` applies a deprecation rename that breaks the call, and the warning promises an automatic migration
cards.body: Found by MemDesign-5 for #6376 (release-notes research: Go 1.26 `go fix` inliner, Mojo 1.0 fix-its, Zig 0.15 hand migrations). Repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign-4/probes/rel/r11_deprecated.jet on jet 03c64ad0c4: `#Deprecated(since: "1.2", use: "scaled") fn double(a: Int) -> Int { return scaled(a, 2) }` where `scaled(a: Int, by: Int)`. `jet check` prints L2001 with Fix "Use `scaled` instead, or run `jet fix` to migrate automatically." `jet fix` on a copy prints "applied 2 fixes", and the fixed file then fails with E0766 "This call to `scaled` is missing `by`" at `print(scaled(4))`. D-STRUCT-LIFE1=A says `jet fix` applies the replacement only "when the replacement is a plain rename". The owner choice about non-rename migrations is ballot D-DEPRECATE-INLINE1; this card is the defect under any outcome.

Finding to resolve: core.args.decode_argv(argv) still skips element 0, so decode_argv(process.args()) would drop the first user word.

Start-name dispatch needs no ballot: releases ship the aliases as hard links (cc-driver.md), and through a hard link sys.executable() returns the alias path (probe: hard link prints .../hard-cc, symlink resolves to the target). The compiler and Jetpack entries dispatch on the basename of sys.executable(), matching the ratified rule that the program path comes from sys.executable(); the alias case moves from symlinks to hard links. Card question q0khv0gh withdrawn.

c2 second blocker, found by building it: stage 1 is compiled by the pinned seed a0_025, which type-checks the tree's Core with its own export table. That table knows only the public intrinsic core.process argv (dispatcher row jet_std_io_args), so a Core that calls the private core.process.__argv() fails with E1004 (.chain s1 key 88029e078107b565), and a non-Core caller of __argv fails with E0067. Removing the public name therefore needs either a seed cut or a two-step bootstrap: (1) land a compiler whose registry also routes core.process __argv, (2) cut a seed, (3) land the Core switch that removes argv. No seeds tonight, so c2 is parked. Full parked patch (100 files, placeholder entries marked do-not-land): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/unitarg/argv-one-parked.patch on base 2ba0d540c4.

c2 (D-ARGV-ONE1=A cutover) is implemented in export tree $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/argv (base 2ba0d540c4) and NOT landed. Done there: public process.argv() removed (Core.jet exports and owns, StructureRegistry, CoreSurfaceInventory, CoreHostSignatures, CoreCalls ambient row, ledger script); private core.process.__argv() for Core's own help and #CLI entry; ArgsSpec.parse and parse_or_exit take process.args() with 0-based indexing; E1304 what/why/fix name the argument list and process.args(); L0515 retired (sema check, registry row, coverage row, ui_lint snapshot, diagnostic_snapshots step and fixture removed; TSV row marked retired); corpus policy rules retargeted to process.args, with the argv().skip(1) builder-view rule retired and finding Fex-core-2 kept under raw-cli-fixed-shape; Examples, agent-eval programs, about 40 test fixtures and their outputs, Tools/perf/olevels/sweep.mjs, LintPlanted.jet and the spec prose migrated. decode_argv (explicit vector) is intentionally unchanged. BLOCKED on owner question q0khv0gh: the compiler's jet-cc/jet-cxx aliases and Jetpack's jetpack-nix-index/jetpack-trust-root personalities dispatch on the start name via symlinks, and sys.executable() resolves the link, so the two entry files (Compiler/JetCli/run.jet, Jetpack/run.jet) and tests/guards/cc_driver_hosts.jet carry a do-not-land placeholder until the ruling. Still owed after the ruling: stage-1 build, regenerate CoreSourceOwned/CoreCallRows, args_spec_bad_parse_arity.stderr re-bless, lane-check, focused cases/ui/golden runs, one wave.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

c7 census 2026-11-03 (base 5eeacdd26d). Item 1 is fixed: an external header 'fn Point.debug_string(self)' beside 'derive T.DebugText' now gives E0105, not the ICE. Its own fixture, tests/ui/derive_generated_collision_external_header, lands in Main-20. Per commit a79059cd4e, the other snapshots are cffi_callback_bound_method, cffi_callback_effect, cffi_callback_generic and cffi_callback_nullable. All four still carry retired-syntax expectations: E0065/E0068 lines, fn(I32) I32 -[]> spellings, E-ERR-SUFFIX. Actual today: (a) bound_method gives E0302 only. Jet has no method values: 'inc.apply' and 'Incrementer.apply' are both E0302. The snapshot's E3216 followed a value that never formed. (b) effect gives E0112 'wants fn(I32) -[]> I32, but this is fn(I32) -> I32'; the snapshot also wanted E3203 at the same span. (c) generic gives E0112 with fn(T) -[]> T; the snapshot also wanted E3203. (d) nullable gives E3203 for (fn(I32) -[]> I32)?; the snapshot holds only the retired E-ERR-SUFFIX. No spec line decides whether E3203 must follow E0112 for a callback, or whether a nullable C callback is legal. So these need the #6425 E3203 port or an owner ruling before any re-bless.

c5 probe 2026-11-03: the false E0904 (caller T spelled like callee T) is gone on base 5eeacdd26d. The solver renames a shadowed callee parameter to T#callee. 'y :: f(x?)' inside g<T>(x: T?) gives 4/0 on O0 and --release. A tail call 'f(x)' into a T? slot still gave E0113 'This value is T?, but g returns T?', also for concrete Int?. The cause: sema_stmt_return_probed_carrier routed by the callee's declared result T (not a carrier), which took the payload route. Fixed in Main-20 by probing direct calls whose declared result is not a carrier; the new golden generics/caller_parameter_same_name passes on o0/o1/o2. Remaining finding: the T E! slot, 'fn h(x: Int Err!) -> Int Err! { f(x) }', is still E0113 'This value is Int, but h returns Int'; sema_stmt_return_call_widening takes over first. Separate finding: 'fn id(value: Int?) -> Int? { value }' is E0120 (not moved).

Why: c8's ICE is fixed, but those seven UI rows stayed known-failing under it. With the ICE gone they show the real gap: E2806 and E2807 are registered but never emitted (the Rust App.rs graph extraction was never ported), and tanstack_start stops on an E0102.

Body: Found 2026-10-23 by the Regex lane. The IR build resolves a private struct by its leaf name across modules. Folded #4975 "sema: generic binding occurs check diverges from Rust unify_types" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5990 (Map: Sema: unknown names, cross-module identity and generic); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Jet sema_inference_bind (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Inference/Solver.jet) rejects a binding whose value mentions the parameter's own name; Rust unify_types (crates/jet-foundation/src/Generics.rs) has no occurs check. A caller parameter spelled like the callee's is concrete evidence, not a cycle: inside g<T>, f(x?) for f<T>(value: T) gives a false E0904. Caveat shared with Rust: without the check, T bound to the caller's T? plus later evidence for T recurses forever (E3012 in Jet). Proposed: drop the occurs check (branch coremathsema4, d0dd8c47d) and guard sema_inference_unify_inner so only the expected (callee) side is substituted; land the same guard in Rust. cards.title: #CLI Int argument past I64 runs forever instead of failing; ' 5' and '+5' are accepted
cards.body: Found by AsmPar-1 on 2026-11-01 while building the embedded-data asm reference. For a typed CLI Int argument, --ticks 9223372036854775808, 18446744073709551617 or 99999999999999999999 makes the program run forever. It should exit with the usage error saying --ticks expects an Int. Leading-space ' 5' and plus-sign '+5' are also accepted, where core.args should parse Int with the same strict rules as Int.parse. The root is in the core.args Int conversion, which is shared by every tier.

criteria.text: A typed CLI Int argument outside I64, or with leading/trailing space or a plus sign, exits with the core.args usage error naming the flag, the same way on O0/O1/O2. A cases row covers the three overflow values plus ' 5' and '+5', and the in-range values still parse.
criteria.evidence: Retargeted to c2: the premise is false. Int is exact (no I64 bound), Int.parse trims Unicode whitespace and accepts '+' by design (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/IntParse.jet numeric_trim_start/end), and core.args already decodes Int flags with Int.parse (Core/Args/Args.jet __cli_is_int, __cli_int_of). A huge --ticks is a valid exact Int, so a program that loops that many times is correct, not hung. Giving CLI flags stricter rules than Int.parse would create a second Int text grammar (I8).

criteria.text: A typed CLI Int flag decodes with exactly Int.parse's rules on O0, O1 and O2. Int is exact, so 9223372036854775808, 18446744073709551617 and 99999999999999999999 decode to those exact numbers, and ' 5' and '+5' give what Int.parse gives (5). A cases row covers the three big values, ' 5', '+5' and a negative value.
criteria.evidence: Commit 83c4c6521b (Main-32): tests/cases/cli/cli_int_flags_decode_with_int_parse_rules.case PASS (cases --filter cli_int_flags: 1 PASS, 0 FAIL). It covers 9223372036854775808 at O0, 18446744073709551617 at O1, 99999999999999999999 at O2, ' 5' at O0, '+5' at O2 and -12 at O1, each printing the exact decoded value. A direct probe shows Int.parse gives the same values for the same inputs.

cards.title: Shared store broker socket fails when the Jetpack root path is long
cards.body: The non-admin shared store puts its broker socket at <private Jetpack root>/shared-store/broker.sock (Jetpack SharedStoreInstall.jet:49-50). cards.title: Markers inside a declaration body: #X :: value lines (D-MARKER-INBODY1 A)
cards.body:
Ratified D-MARKER-INBODY1=A (2026-11-04). Any marker on a declaration with a braced body (struct, enum, trait, impl block, inline module, function, method) may be written inside that body as `#X :: value`. It means exactly what `#X(args)` above the declaration means; both fill one marker list. Values: `true` applies with defaults, `false` refuses where `#!X` is allowed, one name, string or number needs no parentheses, and any other argument list is written in parentheses with the marker argument grammar. A Bool argument is always parenthesized.

Owner amendment at ratification: the lines may be ANYWHERE in the body, not only at the top. The owner's reasoning: the member declarations are the most important part of a struct, so markers need not come first. The ballot's 'leading lines' rule is therefore void. Consequence (adversarial finding 7): type-marker facts that the parser applies before the body today (Items.jet:1901-1904 layout and type markers, :2019-2020 enum markers) must instead apply after the whole body is read, wherever the line sits.

Kept rules: a declaration writes its own markers all above or all inside; mixing is refused with a jet fix that moves the whole set either way. Markers added by tools or templates go where the declaration's markers already are, and above when it has none. A wrong site gets the same site error as above. Blocks, lambdas and tests keep `#X` at their head. jet fmt keeps the author's placement and drops parentheses around one simple argument.

Depends on nothing for most markers; `#FX` on types additionally needs D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1's site change (c09kjhit).
cards.plan: 1. Parser: in every braced declaration body, a member starting with `#` Path followed by `::` is a marker line; parse the value with the marker argument parser (plus true/false); collect them and append to the declaration's marker list after the body. Move the parser-time type-marker facts (layout, derives, SingleUse, MustUse, enum markers) to after the body. 2. Sema: refuse mixing above and inside, a wrong site, `false` where `#!X` is not allowed, and an unparenthesized Bool. Each refusal is a registered code with what/why/fix and a UI snapshot. 3. jet fix: move a declaration's whole marker set inside or above. 4. Formatter: print the lines in place; one simple argument without parentheses. 5. Registry, editor grammars, highlight guard and docs. 6. Examples with goldens on every tier.

log.text: D-MARKER-MOVE1 A (ratified 2026-11-04) is implemented in 37eae4f5d6: jet fix --markers inside|above (FixCommands.jet, InBodyMarkers.jet), and plain jet fix moves a mixed set above. Cases marker_inbody x6, including ui_fixes/marker_inbody_moves_whole_set, pass on 125e2e8f89 (Prep-2 check). The editor code actions have no test yet, tracked as #4917.

Main 2026-11-04 (derived rule, recorded so the owner can overrule): in a FUNCTION body, # X :: lines are accepted only at the body's top statement level. Inside a nested block or a lambda they get E0355 (Block site), because a nested position would suggest a scope the marker does not have. In type, module and impl bodies they go anywhere among the members, per the owner's ANYWHERE.

Main 2026-11-04: Prep finding. Markers written above a trait, a top-level impl or an inline module are dropped silently today: no AST field holds them (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/inbody_sites.jet). This card adds those carriers, and markers on those declarations are then checked (site errors) both above and inside. The jet fix move in both directions waits on ballot D-MARKER-MOVE1; every other criterion proceeds.

cards.title: `os.executable()` under `jet run` names the jet binary, so a program that relaunches itself runs `jet <arg>` instead (I9)
cards.body:
Title: `os.executable()` under `jet run` names the jet binary, so a program that relaunches itself runs `jet <arg>` instead (I9)
Kind: bug · Track: sidequest · Priority: P2 · Tags: I9, process
Body: Found 2026-10-02 (CW2-GOLD-A). Examples/features/io/cleanup_matrix.jet:85-93 relaunches itself per case with `process.cmd([os.executable(), path])`. Under `jet run` (night12), `os.executable()` returns the jet binary (scratch probe printed ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/jet-release-night12/jet), so each child runs `jet return`, `jet error`, … and all six exit 2 with no cleanup trace; the example exits 0 with wrong output. After AOT the same call names the program itself. One source, two meanings. Decide the contract (core-library.md:1499 says only "Return process … facts"): either `jet run` gives the program a relaunchable executable identity (os.executable() names something that reruns this program with the same tier), or self-relaunch gets its own explicit API and os.executable() is documented as the host process binary on every tier, with cleanup_matrix migrated.
Criteria:
1. The chosen contract is written in Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md beside `executable()`.
2. cleanup_matrix prints the six case traces on the default tier and after AOT, identical; a golden is added.

cards.title: One meaning for date and time format patterns (D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1)
cards.body:
Implement one meaning for Core time format patterns, as ratified in D-TIME-FORMAT-CANONICAL1. Remove the second meaning. Acceptance: format goldens use one pattern grammar, and each pattern has one documented result.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Raised 2026-10-03 by the runtime port (RuntimeLead-3). Two time formatters disagree: frozen Rust Time.rs:1760-1868 jet_time_format_pattern (ordered replace with legacy tokens; %%Y renders the year; %f = 9-digit nanoseconds; %Y zero-padded to 4 digits including negative years), used by native Date/LocalTime/DateTime.format; and Core/time/time.jet:116-166 strftime (one-pass byte parser; %%Y renders a literal %Y; %f = 6-digit microseconds; %Y unpadded; also supports %c/%U/%W/%w), a separate public entry. Same program: format(date(-5, 1, 2), "%Y %%Y %f") differs. Options: (A) keep two distinct documented formats (Date.format pattern vs strftime) over ONE private configurable engine; (B) ratify one uniform semantics and migrate all callers (native Date.format + Core strftime + docs + tests). Recommendation: B with strftime semantics (one meaning, POSIX-familiar), unless legacy pattern compatibility is wanted. Independent defect regardless of outcome: card filed for strftime's non-ASCII literal loss.

cards.title: Every closed card is durable: no work lives only on the scratch disk
cards.body: On 2026-11-04 Main's $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT cleanup deleted lane work that open cards still cited (for example #6442's held patches). A closed card or met criterion is a promise that its change is on dev or master. Evidence that names only a scratch path, ~/.cache, /tmp or a commit outside dev/master/rust breaks that promise, and card merges carry such evidence forward unchecked. Owner order: durable work lives in the repo, and only throwaway output stays on disk.
cards.plan: 1) Audit every done card and met criterion, live and archived (audit-closures.mjs): DURABLE, SHA-NOT-IN-BRANCHES, SCRATCH-ONLY, NO-COMMIT. 2) Re-verify each non-durable code closure against dev content, and reopen any whose change is absent, with the reason. 3) Move durable out-of-repo work into the repo: unlanded patches under Tools/tower/held/<card>/ (base commit, state, next step), research and proposals into Docs/research and Docs/proposals, ballot drafts into Tower. 4) Tower refuses card close and criterion meet unless the evidence names a commit reachable from dev or master; scratch-only evidence is rejected. 5) Commit the board to master regularly.

Work not yet on dev is committed, or recorded on its card, before its scratch is removed. cards.title: Moving a handle field out of an aggregate (^x.f) does not transfer ownership
cards.body: Reported by JetpackStore. Expressions like close(^outer.owner), ^verified.lease.release() and lease: ^parts.lease consume a field. The consumer's drop is a no-op, and the fd or flock closes only when the source aggregate drops. Repro: struct Outer{owner: Holder{lock: FileLock}}; close(^outer.owner) leaves the fd open until outer's scope ends. Closing the whole value works. Hits Jetpack Store leases (LeaseSnapshot.jet:243: the owner lock dies with prepared). Related: #6581 (a clone:false handle in a struct double-drops). Fix: a partial move transfers drop responsibility to the consumer, and the source aggregate skips that field's drop on every tier.

cards.title: A BuildError from an implicit-contract fn build loses its identity and reports E3502
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine on dev 7de2280131. A BuildError returned from an implicit-contract fn build reports 'fn build returns nothing' (E3502) instead of the typed build error. JetIR BuildTypes.jet .Typed conversion calls the Prelude impl BuildError -> Err { Err("{self}") }, dropping typed_identity and details, so jet_eval_build_failed_diagnostic (BuildServices.jet) returns None. Three non-known-failing cases fail on base because of it: criterion9_programmable_build_cli_human_and_json_reports_match, ..._implicit_failure_preserves_build_error_identity, ..._error_union_widens_build_error_without_losing_identity. Fix at the conversion so the typed identity survives on every tier.

criteria.text: A BuildError from an implicit-contract fn build reports its typed identity and details, proven by the three criterion9 build_entry cases
criteria.evidence: dev d6c1a293bc (JetpackEngine): the IR .Typed conversion takes the BuildError's own Err record via BuildError.into_err and the evaluator writes it as a native JetErr (the inverse of jet_eval_ir_err_data), so typed_identity and details survive. On s1 of HEAD+patch, cases build_entry/criterion9_programmable_build* pass 6/6, including cli_human_and_json_reports_match, implicit_failure_preserves_build_error_identity and error_union_widens_build_error_without_losing_identity (all FAIL on base). cards.title: A child's stdout line reaches the parent only after the child exits
cards.body: Found by CoreOwnership on dev d1e6c214e1: in golden foundations/storage, crash_recovery waits for a child to print 'ready' while it keeps running, but the parent receives the line only after the child exits, so the program panics. Streaming a running child's stdout must deliver each line as it is written (no buffering until exit), on O0/O1/O2. Add a case where the parent reads 'ready' from a child that then waits for the parent.

log.text: Restated (CoreOwnership, Main): the runtime follows ratified D-STDOUT-BUFFER1=A (spec.md:321-325: pipe stdout is written when its buffer fills, or before a stderr write, stdin read, child start or stop; Host.jet host_stdout_write). The foundations/storage child printed 'ready' into a pipe and slept without flushing, so the example is wrong, not the runtime. Fix: the example flushes stdout after 'ready', plus a case where the child prints ready, flushes and waits, and the parent streams the line on O0/O1/O2. Line-buffered pipes would need an owner re-ballot of D-STDOUT-BUFFER1.

criteria.text: Under D-STDOUT-BUFFER1=A, the foundations/storage example flushes its ready line and passes on O0/O1/O2, and a case proves a flushed child line reaches the parent while the child waits
criteria.evidence: dev bd4d5bb844 (CoreOwnership): the storage crash writer flushes its ready line; golden foundations/storage added, o0/o1/o2 PASS; new case process_sessions/flushed_child_line_reaches_the_parent_while_the_child_waits PASS on O0/O1/O2 and the built binary.

cards.title: Compiler segfaults in codegen on &opt_handle == .Val(x)
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine on dev 12da3c76b5: compiling a comparison of a borrowed optional handle against .Val(x) (&opt_handle == .Val(x)) crashes the compiler with SIGSEGV in codegen. Two #3590 c190 known-failing Store rows hit it. I2: checked code the backend cannot lower must be an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a crash, and this shape should lower. Fix the lowering and add a reduced case that runs on O0/O1/O2.

log.text: c2 partial (GoldenRoots3): Engine --tests on 137704d910 sources still null-derefs in both named claims. Claim 83 'store profile receipt copy and proof preserve native io errors': SIGSEGV at 0x0 in compiler_fs_error <- store_reuse_executable_lease_members <- store_snapshot_lease. Claim 69: SIGSEGV at 0x0 in jet_rt_mem_move <- jet_string_bytes <- Files.join_impl <- store_lease_member_path_matches <- executable_index_at. Safe code reaching a null pointer is an I1 defect; it stays on this card. Logs under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/GoldenRoots3/state/jetpack-bootstrap/GoldenRoots3-c75109d407/run-from-{81,4}.log. The AOT tier is still running.

Repro (JetpackEngine): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/JetpackEngine/repro6590/v2.jet, the match form from CacheLease.copy_profile_executable: if &members[index].file == { .Val(input) -> { input.stat() ... } .None -> ... } over [Member{file: FileReader?}] borrowed as &[...]. jet build --optimize=none of it produces a binary that hangs in a futex (fault-handler deadlock, exit 124 under timeout 10). The statement form if &...file == .Val(input) { and the variants with seek/read and an == None precheck pass. The LeaseSnapshot.jet:314 SIGSEGV is not reduced yet; the in-Engine claim reproduces it. So: wrong code from the match-on-borrowed-optional lowering, plus a fault handler that deadlocks instead of reporting.

criteria.text: A switch on a borrowed optional no-clone handle in a list element closes it exactly once and exits, proven by a case on O0/O1/O2 (an I1 safety fix: no double close on freed state)
criteria.evidence: dev 137704d910 (GoldenRoots3): root cause was a double close. Sema hoisted the switch subject into a generated Let that moved the no-clone handle out of its List element, and ir_bind_pin's box alias also armed a close, so the second close locked freed FD state and hung in a futex (no signal, one thread). Fix: a hoisted generated Let over a place whose value has a drop and no clone reads the place in place, and an ir_bind_pin box alias never arms a close. Case core_files_opaque_handles/switch_on_listed_optional_reader_closes_it_once passes on O0/O1/O2 and release and times out on base; 16 repro variants that hung now exit 0; A/B vs 6bee890a10 ui, golden and cases 0 lost.

criteria.text: The Jetpack Engine claim 'store profile receipt copy and proof preserve native io errors' (LeaseSnapshot.jet:314 crash) and the Engine AOT test binary run to completion with the fixed compiler

Stream line leaves handed out align-1 buffers with no count word as owned [U8], so trim_pipe_line's pop uniqueness check decremented the neighbouring String? box; the leaves now allocate with jet_rt_alloc_8. New case process_sessions/streamed_child_lines_leave_neighbouring_values_intact passes on O0/O1/O2 and a built binary; the other process_sessions cases pass. With jetpack rebuilt, Engine claims 69 and 81-92 (including 83) pass; the Engine AOT tier on c75109d407 runs to completion with 530 passed, 30 failed and no hang (its failures include claim 69, fixed by this commit).

cards.title: Runtime witness harnesses rotted against the current runtime ABI: text header, shared clones, renamed exports, missing fixture doors
cards.body: Found by Builder5 under #6595 after the free-observer route landed. Of the 75 *Witness.c harnesses, 26 still FAIL and 30 fail to compile or link, both before and after the route. Causes: (a) Text is refcounted with a 40-byte header at t-8 and clone shares the pointer, but the witnesses assert a 32-byte header and distinct clone pointers (Authority, EventResult, IpAddrShow, MathGlue, ScalarReflect, TextDebug, HTTP*, Plugin*, ServiceValues, UiEvents/Metadata/Raylib, XMLGlue, …). (b) Exports were renamed (jet_rt_handle_clone_vec2 is now Vec2, and others), fixture doors (ui_*_witness_*) are missing, and jet_rt_string_new is gone. Bring every witness to the current runtime ABI. Never weaken an assertion to pass: each witness keeps proving its ownership claim (no leak, no double free) against the real layout.

cards.title: jet front accepts any registered flag on any command: jet init --check silently writes
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine (#6418 c9). The CLI registry scopes --check to fmt ("With fmt:"), but the JetCli front accepts any registered flag on any command. So jet init --check ignores the flag and writes package.jet. A flag outside a command's registry scope must be a usage error that names the commands which do take it. Silently ignoring a flag that promises no writes is a safety bug.

criteria.text: Every jet command refuses a registered flag outside its registry scope with a usage error naming the commands that take it; jet init --check writes nothing; a cases row covers init --check and one other mis-scoped flag
criteria.evidence: 89f28e76af and 0c07bee511 (JetpackEngine). A registered flag outside a command's registry scope is E2102 naming the commands that take it, from one scope rule that also drives jet help. jet init --check exits 2 and writes nothing. Row cli_commands/misplaced_flag_is_e2102_naming_the_commands_that_take_it PASSES. A one-pass census of every jet <cmd> --flag in tests, Docs/spec, the site and harness argv against the scope finds only the intended refusals. Fixed per spec: the stale gate_law check --allow/--force case now runs through jet inspect gates and PASSES; the --preview/--accept scopes are widened for build --import and bind --update (D-FFI-BUILD1, cli.md); help, man and completion snapshots re-blessed for those lines only.

cards.title: Test kit runs cases with the real HOME: suites write ~/.jet (registry index, keys)
cards.body: The cases kit does not isolate HOME per case, so suite runs (pkg and vendored filters) modify the owner's ~/.jet: registry-index was modified on 2026-11-06 at 04:11 during agent suite runs. A probe with the real HOME also overwrote ~/.jet/keys/jet.ed25519 at 04:23. Every case must get its own fresh HOME (and JET_HOME, XDG_* dirs) under its scratch directory, unless the case explicitly declares a home fixture. The kit must also refuse to run when the resolved HOME equals the invoking user's real home.

log.text: Suspect runs that modified the owner's ~/.jet on 2026-11-06: DeclColon's ui suites, jetpack builds and generators (03:30–04:45); GoldenRoots3's tests/cases/pkg A/B (04:00–04:36); JetpackEngine's pkg/vendored filters and its registry keygen --force probe (04:23). GoldenRoots3's pkg profile also deadlocked on the base compiler (all threads in futex waits, no children), probably contention on the shared real ~/.jet/.jetpack.lock across agents. Re-check under per-case HOME. Every lane now runs with a temp HOME and JET_HOME.

A planted case that writes $HOME/.jet/probe leaves the real home untouched (proven by stat before and after a full pkg-filter run). The kit refuses a run whose HOME resolves to the real user home.

The quick profile's JetTestKit/Tests pass 'cases run each row with its own HOME, JET_HOME and XDG roots under its scratch' and 'cases refuse a row whose HOME or JET_HOME is the invoking user's before it runs'. Two full --filter=pkg cases runs with HOME, JET_HOME and XDG_CONFIG/DATA/STATE pointed at a stand-in home holding .jet/lock, .jet/keys/jet.ed25519 and a registry-index row: a recursive lstat+sha256 digest is identical before and after both runs (4be57bd3..., f99c92c7..., 13 entries each), so package cases that write HOME/.jet leave the invoking home untouched.

cards.title: Witness harnesses that count frees through --wrap=jet_rt_free never see runtime frees
cards.body: Found by GoldenRoots3 on dev e8bf2c763d: the runtime object binds its internal calls section-relative (objdump shows R_X86_64_PC32 .text-4), so -Wl,--wrap=jet_rt_free never intercepts frees made inside the runtime. About 50 *Witness.c harnesses count frees that way, so their leak and double-free assertions prove nothing; TerminalProcessWitness fails its free-count assert because of it. Give the witnesses a counting route that sees every runtime free (for example a runtime test hook or symbol-relative calls in the test build), keep one mechanism, prove it with a negative control that leaks one buffer and fails, and rerun every witness.

cards.title: Native-era collect-all launch gate: check in the preflight that AGENTS.md requires
cards.body: AGENTS.md (Find every issue at once) says expensive launches start only through tooling that refuses to launch without a collect-all preflight receipt for that exact commit, naming $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Main/preflight.mjs enforced by prepare-sharded-chain.mjs. Neither is usable: prepare-sharded-chain.mjs does not exist in the repo or scratch, and preflight.mjs depends on the retired Rust-era jetc0 factory, hostJet and proof-source.mjs. In practice the gate today is chain full reaching FIXED_POINT plus the keep-going census, but nothing enforces it, and a fresh clone can't follow the contract. Fix: check in Tools/agent/preflight (Jet or the existing tooling convention). For a commit it runs, in collect-all mode: parse, imports, sema (JET_KEEP_GOING=1), the lowering sweep (JET_DEBUG_LOWER_ALL=1), the generator checks and the comptime-host count against the last admitted compiler. It writes a receipt keyed to the commit in which every row is clean or carries a written disposition. The seed-cut and release launchers refuse to start without a matching receipt. Then point AGENTS.md at the checked-in path in the same cutover.

cards.title: Publish-time SemVer gate (E1218): sema produces the public API snapshot that jet registry publish compares
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine on #6418 c7 (a6b917e72e). cards.title: core.ui host types and services lower on native tiers from Jet source
cards.body: Found by CoreOwnership on dev 668a296d5c (#4717 c8, goldens ui/battery and ui/surface, 14 lowering faults on checked code, an I2 and I9 defect). (a) bb9c74e522 made UIHostError, UIClipboardText, UICapabilityFacts, UIShortcut(Binding), UIFileDialogRequest, UIFSGrant and UIAccessibility Jet structs and enums in Core/Ui/Host.jet, but the JetIR RuntimeRoutes rows and the JetRuntime Ui*.jet carriers still treat them as opaque JetUi* handles, so ir_is_handle refuses them (BuildRoutes.jet:4263/4493/4609; 9 faults). (b) The native runtime exports no jet_ui_host_* service (clipboard, drag, IME, shortcuts, capabilities, open/save file) or jet_ui_text_input; only Prelude/Web/Core/Ui.js implements them, while the CoreCall rows mark them aot_direct (4 faults). (c) The UINode handle has field routes only for label, width and height, so .accessibility has none (1 fault). Fix at the root by finishing the Jet-source cutover: remove the handle carriers and Handle route rows for these types, and implement the native host services as source-owned Jet over a headless provider that returns CapabilityUnavailable, with the same meaning on every tier (I9). A native-tier rejection would split meaning by tier and is not the fix. Proof: ui/battery and ui/surface pass on o0/o1/o2 and web, and no lowering fault remains in a core.ui sweep.

log.text: ac563303ea (CoreOwnership): the Core helper __provider_fields becomes provider_record_fields, since __ names are reserved for registry host leaves. Prepush's Core check had reported 4 ReservedDunderName errors. Views regenerated with check-core-surface-ledger --write. On 89f28e76af+patch, chain check shows 0 rows, ui_host_provider and ui_default_browser PASS.

60adfbb42a (CoreOwnership): a default browser provider, with provider records as length-prefixed fields; the clipboard reads from the page's paste, copy and cut mirror with no implicit readText; core-library.md updated. Main's review keeps c2 open: the provider still computes the IME caret, maps DOM event types to phases (including compositionend with an empty string → Cancel), and keeps unbounded queues. The fix: send raw fields, let Core own the mapping and caret, and report overflow as Core's existing QueueFull. Ballot item B3: the browser's dragleave dropEffect 'none' has no UIDragOperation, so today it is a HostFailure; the choice is a None case or an optional operation.

Ballot prep (CoreOwnership). B1, browser file dialogs: (a) keep FileDialog absent on web (current); (b) a pending dialog plus a public poll or dialog event, with a UIBrowserFile{name, bytes/handle} carrier; (c) OPFS/File System Access handles in a synthetic grant root, Chromium-only, which changes what a grant means. B2, web shortcuts: (a) keep Core-only register/dispatch, with the app feeding keys itself; (b) a keydown queue plus a public shortcuts.poll(). Main's adversarial notes before this goes on a ballot: B1(b) must not create a second 'chosen file' carrier beside UIGrantedPath (I8), so one selection type has to serve native and web. B2(b) must not need app polling; keys should arrive through the UI event delivery the app already handles. Both need same-program alternatives with these downsides engineered away before the owner sees them.

A3 seam landed, ae8271e354 (CoreOwnership). Ui.js (1414 lines of dead JS policy) is deleted. Core/Ui/Host owns every rule over six marshal-only C-ABI provider leaves: headless on native, and on web forwarded to globalThis.jetUiProvider. Proof: tests/cases/web_build/ui_host_provider_answers_are_core_owned. Native reports every capability absent with the same validation answers; the web run with a stubbed provider gets Core-decoded events and errors. Full chain s2==s3 (4633942b); golden ui/ 57/57 on o0/o1/o2. Open before closing: the web runtime installs no default browser provider, so a shipped app reports all capabilities absent. A default marshal-only provider is still needed, including a sync/async bridge for the clipboard.

Partial, 9ce77ac519 (CoreOwnership): the node-slot half. UIAccessibility and UIShortcut are runtime records; the .accessibility, .shortcut and .ime field reads and the native jet_ui_text_input lower. Remaining: the A3 primitive provider seam for the host services.

Ruling (Main) on the web host services: A3. Core source owns the UI host service logic (validation, queues, the binding registry, UIHostError meaning) over a primitive-only provider seam: capability flag, clipboard get/set text, event pop, dialog request/result. Web implements the seam with the browser; native implements it headless and reports the capability as absent. Rejected: A1, deleting the web JS provider, because it would drop shipped web clipboard, shortcut, IME/drag and file-dialog behaviour, which is a product change for the owner; and A2, keeping the logic in Ui.js with native record carriers, because hosts would re-encode policy, which violates I9. The node-slot half (UIAccessibility and UIShortcut records, field reads, native jet_ui_text_input) lands first and separately.

CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. Owner directive (2026-10-06 06:20): everything is ported to Jet so Rust can be removed from the toolchain; Jet-only native must contain no Rust remnants, not even policy-free provider leaves (host/OS access through Jet FFI/syscalls inside vetted #Unsafe Core internals). Timing may slip past the 15:00 goals; nothing may be designed to keep Rust.

Inventory of Rust on integ/next6 (2026-10-06 06:25, git ls-tree sizes):
- crates/jet-codegen 19.4 MB (Prelude runtime 10.7 MB embedded in every generated program; Codegen 8.7 MB)
- tests 11.1 MB (Rust integration tests: must move to Jet test harness)
- crates/jet-sema 6.7, crates/jetpack 6.2, crates/jet-foundation 5.9, Source (CLI front door) 5.6, jet-pkg-model 3.4, jet-comptime 3.2, jet-devserver 2.2, jet-parser 1.9, jet-evalhost 1.4, Compiler/Bootstrap host .rs 1.0, jet-driver 0.9, jet-repl 0.6, jet-env-model 0.5, jet-debug 0.5, jet-cli 0.5, jet-semindex 0.4, smaller crates ~1 MB.

Existing Jet ports: the self-hosted compiler (Compiler/, fixed point) covers the compiler crates; origin/port/compiler (3aab69fde) holds an unverified 1:1 Jet port of crates/ (38 MB); Jetpack/ has Jet ports of the package manager. In flight 2026-10-06: CLI front door (SolCLI1-5 via PortInteg2), Prelude/CoreLib cutover (SolCore1-5 via CorelibInteg; Rust leaves tracked in $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/CorelibInteg/RUST-LEAVES.tsv), native backend replacing rustc (NativeLead2 line).

Criteria: (1) every Rust file above has a Jet replacement or is deleted; (2) the toolchain builds and runs every tier with no rustc/cargo; (3) tests run on the Jet harness; (4) RUST-LEAVES.tsv is empty.

questions.text: Not sure that shared keyword is valid jet.. Ensure accurate
questions.answer: shared is valid Jet. It is the registered keyword that builds a shared cell (D-CONC-SHARE1, Syntax.rs KW_SHARED). The example shared_config.jet uses it, and it parses and runs. Checking the ballot's examples against the compiler did find four other mistakes, now fixed. [:] is not Jet; an empty table is [String: String]{}. Semicolons between statements are not Jet. The module-level binding must be capitals, STORE. The setter must store value.copy(). With those fixes, option A's declaration fails today with exactly one error, E0622, "a module binding's value must be a literal", which is what this vote would change. The options and the recommendation are unchanged. Separately, the probes found a compiler bug: writing a table entry through a shared cell is silently lost today.

questions.text: G3 No Rust anywhere: VERIFIED and marked achieved (dev a9be739dae). The only Rust left is the benchmark peers (Tools/gauntlet, Tools/perf, tests/compiled_workloads), the Zed extension, the Rust host in the FFI example Examples/ffi/projections/rust/host.rs, and Cargo fixture files Jetpack's tests read as data. This card's remaining proof rows ride on G1 (goldens). — Main
Just because something isn't used directly in this specific repo doesn't mean we shouldn't have it or it isn't useful. Why would we act like that?
questions.answer: We would not, and no option removes or devalues any Core function. The old wording (uncovered, gaining a use) was misleading. The check asks one thing: does some test, example or doc example run this function, so we know it works? 4639 public functions have no test yet. That is test work owed, not a sign they are unwanted. The ballot now says untested throughout. Recommended A records today's untested functions by name. Each new function must arrive with a test, and the list shrinks as the missing tests are written.

Owner 2026-10-30: ballot the namespace question for C6 instead of Main's ruling. Options: one shared namespace where a re-export takes over the child module name, versus separate module and value namespaces as in Rust. C13 (E0610 fix text) proceeds independently.

C6 root cause (BallotDesign at d90660da90): the bodyless child declaration 'module wrap' registers a Module symbol wrap (Registration/Items.jet:1989); 'pub use wrap.wrap' then binds the function wrap in the same namespace, and the duplicate check at Items.jet:3657 reports E0105. Dropping 'module wrap' gives E0610, so the spec's canonical form (spec.md:2232-2243, D-MOD4) cannot compile. Main's ruling, within D-MOD4: a parent's re-export of a child item that has the child module's name replaces the child module name in the parent namespace. The child stays reachable as a path prefix inside use declarations. No separate module and value namespaces.

cards.body: Found by GoldenRoots3 on dev 41ad578550 and present on the base too: linking the program built by run-process-witnesses.mjs fails with an undefined reference to jet_rt_fault_report. Every runtime symbol a generated program calls must come from the one shared runtime (I9). Find where the reference is emitted without the runtime pack providing it, fix the pack or the route, and prove the witnesses link and run.

log.text: Owner 2026-11-06: script porting, the pairing bars and full removal of non-Jet languages are G4 work (#5072), not G1/G2; c5 keeps its original goal.
Owner 2026-11-06 refinement: runner ports follow #5072's pairing rule; the .mjs keeps running until the Jet twin wins every bar.
