HANDOFF 2026-11-06 (Main restart after the session crash): TestSystemLead takes over from TestRot: c5 runner registration; c3 fixed point and c4 s5 loop are in batch vb5.
c3 and c4 added from TestRot's #6595/#6609 findings (no new card): runtime import ledger drift and 6 s5 witness-loop rot rows.

Finding (Builder5): with the process-wide atexit queue built, main-run worker-fatal still loses every handler. A worker's fatal stop runs in stop domain 2, and Trap.jet trap_exit routes only domain 1 through the root. Every other domain takes trap_defect_exit, a raw exit_group with no main_exit_claim, no cleanup and the report written straight to fd 2. This looks like a regression since 114e150cba. Ruling (Main): a fatal stop in any domain under a live jet_rt_main claims the process exit (single winner), runs main_exit_cleanup, then writes the captured report. Report text and exit code 70 are unchanged; a stop during cleanup aborts; hosts with no live jet_rt_main keep the defect exit. The golden is re-recorded to all four handlers in registration order, then the report, once the fixture's registration order is deterministic. Builder5 owns Trap.jet and Scheduler.jet for this fix.

Ruling (Main) on run-main-fixtures worker-fatal: make the os.atexit queue process-wide. Today it is per-thread TLS (Task.jet task_exit_queue), and main_exit_cleanup drains only the main thread's queue, so a worker's handlers are dropped. core-library.md:1875,2073-2079 and spec.md:1069-1077 define atexit as a process-boundary registration run in registration order, so that's a runtime defect. Same change: core-library-native-contract.md:573-575's thread-exit drop is rewritten; the scheduler fixture asserts survival; a new case covers a handler from a worker that exits normally; the lock covers only append and claim. The LIFO goldens (exit2exit1) are re-recorded as exit1exit2 to match spec registration order.

cards.title: Imports: Go-style `use { … }` blocks with `alias: path` rows; retire `as` and member lists
cards.body:
Owner instruction 2026-11-01 07:40 EST (chat): imports use Go-style blocks; aliasing uses `name:` (D-DECL-COLON1=A), not `as`; more than one use block per file is allowed (single-file multi-module setups, `comptime use` for custom linking logic). Owner answers the same morning: a single import may stay on one line (like Go); member lists (`use math.{double}`) are retired in favor of alias rows.

Canonical form:

```jet
use core.term

use {
    jetfoundation
    unicode: core.text
    double: math.double
    "./lib"
}
```

Rows: a module path, `alias: path`, a string file path, or `alias: "path"`. One row per line. `use alias: path` is the single-line alias. `as` in imports and the `.{…}` member list are removed (they are no longer Jet syntax and get no teaching diagnostic).

Bootstrap order: (1) the parser, formatter, registry and LSP accept the block and the `::` alias beside the old forms; a seed is cut from that commit. (2) One cutover migrates every in-repository `use` (Compiler, Core, Prelude, Jetpack, Tools, Examples, tests, .case sources, docs, editor grammars, snapshots) and deletes the old forms.

cards.title: Alloc cache gating disagrees between alloc and free (Alloc.jet:1012 vs :1056)
cards.body: Found by MechD 2026-11-06 while fixing the JetRuntime plain transport (#6594). Compiler/JetRuntime Alloc.jet:1056 gates the cached free on alloc_root+200 (the tracked count) while the allocation fast path at :1012 gates on alloc_root+144 (mode). When anything is tracked, frees bypass the cache but allocations still pop it. Confirm with a runtime test that tracks one allocation and then cycles cached sizes; fix so both paths read the same gate.

criteria.text: A runtime test tracks an allocation and cycles cached sizes; alloc and free gate on the same root field, and the test passes on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Not a bug: the two gates differ on purpose. Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Alloc.jet:1012 jet_rt_alloc takes the cache only when the counting mode word (alloc_root+144) is 0, so every allocation in counting mode is tracked. :1056 jet_rt_free takes the cache only when the tracked count (alloc_root+200) is 0. Policy restore (:887) turns the mode off while tracked blocks stay in the side table, so each of those frees must still reach alloc_untrack. Gating free on the mode would skip the untrack and leave the ProgramAllocator facts stale. Gating alloc on the count would skip tracking the first counted block. The comment at :995-997 documents the split. Verified by Main from MechD-3's analysis.

cards.title: Port the C binding generator to Jet: jet inspect bind <header.h> and the cache-miss refresh
cards.body: Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/InspectB.jet:968 returns not-ported for `jet inspect bind <header.h>`, and there is no Jet implementation of the #Bindgen cache generator that the usage text says the compiler runs automatically on a cache miss. Only the data-schema binders (json, csv, sql, xml, proto) are ported. As a result, the checked-in `c.<lib>.__bindgen__` caches can't be regenerated under today's FFI rules. Examples/ffi opaque_handles fails E3203/E0702 because its cache predates them: `struct GzFile {}` is not C-ABI, and #Close needs a close that returns nothing, but run.jet reads gzclose's status. This blocks #4717 c8 item 3. Scope: the same header subset the retired Rust binder accepted (this is not #4174's full C front end); output a #Bindgen module that follows today's C-ABI and #Close rules; implement the manual verb and the cache-miss refresh as one mechanism; regenerate every checked-in cache and its golden in one cutover.

cards.title: jet fix renames a used loop variable to _n and skips the real := fix (E0111)
cards.body:
Repro on a0_029 (release binary, empty HOME): oops.jet is
run: fn() {
    total: 0
    loop n in 1..3 -> total = total + n
    print(total)
}
`jet run` correctly reports E0111 (total was made with `:`; Fix: declare it with `total := ...`). `jet fix oops.jet` then says 'applied 1 fix, skipped 1 suggestion for review'. The applied fix renames `n` to `_n` as if unused, although `total + n` uses it, so the program is now wrong. The real E0111 fix (`:` to `:=`) is the skipped one. Probe: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/readme-probe/fresh/oops.jet.

cards.title: Hand-off anywhere: a fresh clone is enough for any agent to continue work
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-04: work must be able to move to another machine or a remote/cloud agent at once. Today, landing, building, suites, ballots and preflight depend on files outside the repo: the lander and queue (lanes/Main/q.mjs, stackcheck.sh, pareto-approved.txt, $JET_RUN_ROOT), the chain (chain.sh, chain-lib.mjs, build-slot.sh, publish-base.sh, publish-latest.sh, SeedRotate/norust.sh, gsel.mjs), the suites (q/sg/suite.sh, TestGreen/tk-build.sh), the ballot validator (lanes/Main/ballots/validate.mjs), the preflight ($JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Main/preflight.mjs), $JET_STATE_ROOT/cheap.sh, and the admitted compilers in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/discovery/base. Repo files also hard-code machine paths (Compiler/JetRuntime/Tests/check-runtime.mjs, CryptoEd25519SignatureFixtures.json, AGENTS.md, skills).
cards.plan: 1) Inventory every out-of-repo script, config and path that agent work relies on (briefs, skills, AGENTS.md, Tools, lane scripts). 2) Port each into Tools/ (agent/, ci/ and so on), with roots taken from environment variables (JET_SCRATCH_ROOT, JET_TARGET_ROOT, JET_SEED) and machine defaults set only in jet-env. 3) Make the seed path explicit: a fresh clone names where its admitted compiler comes from (D-SEED-DIST1), plus a bootstrap doc. 4) Prove it: a fresh clone in a new HOME with a new scratch root runs jet-env, builds, runs one suite slice, lands a trivial patch and runs the ballot validator.

c23 follow-up (Builder5). Pre-fetch: with fresh HOME, env -i and no host compiler, jet env fetch-toolchain fetched and unpacked the pack (clang 21.1.8, musl 1.2.5, glibc 2.42; 289.8 s, rc 0); after the source copy was deleted and JETPACK_DENY_NETWORK=1 set, jet cc --target x86_64-linux-gnu (PIE) and aarch64-linux-musl (static, musl built on first use, run under qemu) both built and ran. CcDriver has no Nix-index route: its ProviderCtx sets nix_index None and allow_local_nix_catalog false, and the cc provider reads only the Hangar, the JETPACK_FIXTURES test double, then the pack. 80e3ee6251 removes two decision citations from comments (I7). CLI cc claims 6/6, Engine cc and Closure claims, testkit help/completions/man/cc cases and guard cc_driver_hosts 3/3 pass. Known limits: glibc 2.42 sysroot (binaries need glibc 2.34+), no C++ standard library, 8 case-colliding iptables headers dropped.

Owner ruling 2026-11-05: unbuilt work is built to the spec and the owner's requirements for that feature, not to the Rust compiler's output. Rust is removed and is not an oracle; Jet will differ from Rust and is meant to be better. A ui row whose Rust-era snapshot differs from Jet's spec-conforming output (registered code, what, why and fix) gets its snapshot regenerated from Jet, not Jet bent to match Rust bytes. KF-UNPORTED rows mean 'build to spec'.

The live migration (archive shard --apply) waits until master advances past this commit, because tower.mjs and tower serve load master's Tower code and old code refuses a sharded board.

Owner order 2026-11-04 (branch policy): everything lives on dev. Board commits, which Tower makes on local master, are fast-forwarded into dev at once, and only dev is pushed. master (local and origin) advances to a dev commit only after Tools/agent/verify-full.sh passes on that exact commit. origin/master stays at 2b060094ec (pushed earlier today before this rule; no rewind, per the owner).

c3 depends on c4 (SelfMem, 2026-11-04): the published a0_025 seed's runtime pack does not match dev (46 runtime and 42 backend files differ), so a fresh clone can reuse its pack only from a seed cut at a matching commit. Ruling: a Jet tool step (Tools/packaging/reuse-runtime.jet) checks the pack's provenance inventories against the checkout and refuses a mismatch, naming the latest published release (c4) or the rebuild route (#5072 c11). c3 is proven with the latest base as a stand-in seed until c4 publishes a matching release.

G4/G5 landed (SelfMem-6564a): testkit scratch comes from JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR, then JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/testkit, then ~/.cache/jet/testkit; lane-check runs $JET check directly with no jet-env. Testkit self-tests match base (212/6), lane-check CHECK OK for Tools/testkit, lane-check-regression green (red on base).

Gaps: G1/G2, jet requires both variables (ruling: jet defaults them, env > the input's Jet-checkout ancestor > the install beside the binary; identity from IDENTITY beside the binary); G3, s1 reuses the seed runtime pack (ruling: reuse when the recipe hash matches, else a registered error; the Jet port of prebuild is on #5072); G4 testkit scratch under HOME; G5 lane-check via jet-env; G6 verify-full is node and hard-codes the scratch mount; G7 docs route through jet-env/Nix.

Owner 2026-11-04 on c6: environment setup may belong to Jetpack rather than the jet compiler; the line is blurry. Read c6 as: with a Jet toolchain present (jet + Jetpack), the environment comes from it, not Nix. Which component owns it follows the existing Jetpack environment work (D-DEPS-ENV1; #5969).

Owner answers 2026-11-04: (a) seeds are GitHub releases of each valid, proven latest compiler; (b) scrub personal info, no allowlist; (c) jet-env bash is temporary only; with jet present, jet is the environment, and Jet replaces Nix over time. Added as criteria c4-c6.

Handoff from the stopped Infra agent (2026-11-04). Inventory: Docs/audits/2026-11-04-handoff-inventory.md (70 rows: 47 external paths + 23 committed hard-code groups, ~270 files), queued as land job 1793810639-Infra. Proposed: (1) preflight.mjs, preflight-gate.mjs and prepare-sharded-chain.mjs are dead Rust-era stage0 tooling (last receipt Oct 21): retire to held/, and AGENTS.md's preflight becomes Land.jet census + Chain.jet --dry-run. (4) Root variables with defaults only in jet-env: JET_STATE_ROOT, JET_SCRATCH_ROOT, JET_RUN_ROOT (default $JET_RUN_ROOT here), JET_BASE_ROOT, JET_TARGET_ROOT, JET_SEEDS/JET_SEED, JET_DEV_WORKTREE, JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB. (5) The only Core gap so far is #5072 c2 (worker pool); it blocks parallel prescreen and the sharded suite, which run serially until then. Open owner questions: (a) where the D-SEED-DIST1 seed is published (fetch command for the bootstrap doc); (b) leave recorded evidence paths (Tower json, agent-eval transcripts, gauntlet evidence json, proposal quotes) as written and allowlist them in the lane-check guard; (c) jet-env must stay a bash bootstrap (it enters the Nix shell that provides jet), which amends #5072 c9.

questions.text: the end shape alone does not look like the best version compared to any language, i think zig just works
questions.answer: Agreed. The ballot is redone around the Zig shape. Recommended A: each jet release ships a C toolchain pack (static clang and lld, plus C library sources for every supported target) as a file beside jet. Its hash is built into jet. The first jet cc fetches it from the same release, checks the hash and keeps it. After that, jet cc works on a clean machine and builds for any supported target. It needs no Nix, no package index and no signing key. Pure-Jet programs never download it, and jet env fetch-toolchain prepares an offline machine. B keeps the old Nix and signed-index route; C uses the machine's own cc, like Go.

cards.title: Soundness: a struct holding a clone:false handle (WsConn) copies implicitly and double-drops (SIGSEGV)
cards.body: Found by BallotLead on dev 070ba19ad7 while porting core.web.browser. A struct whose field is a non-cloneable handle (clone: false, e.g. WsConn) is copied implicitly instead of moved or rejected, so both copies drop the handle and the program segfaults. Browser works around it with Shared<__BrowserWire>. Fix in sema: a type that holds a clone:false field is itself non-copyable, so an implicit copy is a move or a registered diagnostic. Add a case that segfaults today, then remove the Shared workaround.

criteria.text: A value holding a WsConn is non-copyable: an implicit copy is a move, and copying it from a read param or self is a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot (tests/ui/ws_conn_holder_is_not_copied). Golden tests/run/Net/WsConnHolderMovesItsSocket passes on O0, O1 and O2, and core.web.browser no longer has Shared<__BrowserWire>.
criteria.evidence: 34290833a9 release candidate kit (chain s2 613ff4f17287d935): tests/ui/ws_conn_holder_is_not_copied.jet PASS. This row is the proof the precut audit named for this criterion.

criteria.text: One rule for every clone:false handle, not a WsConn special case: every type holding a clone:false field is non-copyable in sema, with the WsConn-specific check removed. Receiver is classified by its real semantics: if its copies soundly share one reference-counted queue, it is not clone:false and its registration says so; otherwise Core/Tasks moves it instead of copying. The Core runtime pack builds, and every clone:false holder in Core either moves or is rejected.
criteria.evidence: release kit a0_032 (dev 2ec700da30, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/../release/2ec700da303b/kit): ec67763e26 replaced the WsConn-only check with one clone:false handle rule (handle table in Compiler/JetFoundation Registry/RuntimeHandles.jet); ui tests/ui/ws_conn_holder_is_not_copied.jet PASS, golden tests/run/Net/WsConnHolderMovesItsSocket.jet PASS o0/o1/o2.

criteria.text: Equality on a clone:false handle (for example a.wire == b.wire on WsConn) is a registered sema diagnostic with a UI snapshot, or a defined comparison that lowers on every tier; it is never accepted by sema and then an internal compiler error in the backend.
criteria.evidence: release kit a0_032 (dev 2ec700da30, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/../release/2ec700da303b/kit): ui tests/ui/ws_conn_is_not_comparable.jet PASS (equality on a clone:false handle is a registered sema diagnostic with its snapshot; no backend ICE).

cards.title: Released jet needs host cc/ar for C dependencies at O1/O2 (O0 builds them)
cards.body: Fresh-clone full-profile dry run ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/fresh-c65.sh, seed a0_032, dev b2a5bd22a2, PATH has git, coreutils and archivers but no cc, ar or Rust). Examples/Interop/FFI/InlineC.jet and NativeC/run.jet pass at o0 but fail at o1 and o2: 'Couldn't realize C dependencies …: the C compiler is not installed'. tests/cases/ice_regressions/b12_c_module_import_keeps_plain_c_return ERRORs with 'spawn: not found during resolve ar'. cards.body: From #6638 c3 (MechD-3, ffff735682). tests/ui/build_generated_collision pins E0603 because nothing emits E3510 GeneratedModuleShadows. cards.title: LaneCheck cannot check Compiler/Prelude or Compiler/JetRuntime files: it checks them as standalone units
cards.body: Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet checks a touched file's package as a normal unit. Compiler/Prelude is embedded, so checking it alone gives 1539 ReservedDunderName errors in Core.jet, including on untouched files such as CoreSurfaceInventory.jet. Compiler/JetRuntime is assembled by the chain, so checking it alone gives 2874 UnknownFunction os_store_i64 errors across 153 files. Workers editing either tree therefore get CHECK FAILED whether or not their change is good, which makes the receipt meaningless for the two most sensitive trees. Found by TestSystemLead-2 in 332eb41d18 and 83859ebe1c. d16f96e61e skips both in the packages suite for the same reason.

log.text: c4 isn't met yet: at dev HEAD 963f74b975 the lander's precommit (looping over Land.jet ratchets with seed a0_033; 10 checks in 23 s) fails Tools/agent/DiagnosticRows.jet --check on Docs/site/dist/e/E-ERR-PROPAGATE and E1206. Diagnostics.jet hasn't changed since 78aa137994, so the output depends on the jet running the generator. TestSystemLead-2 is fixing the root. The other 9 checks pass.

Ruling on c1: option B. The compiler gains a check mode that checks Compiler/Prelude files as generated prelude source (lex_generated plus the same unit context the compiler embeds them in), and LaneCheck uses it once a seed has it. Until then LaneCheck reports a touched Prelude file as unchecked ('needs a seed with the prelude check mode'), never as CHECK OK. The row-DSL inputs (Core.jet, CoreSurfaceInventory.jet, CoreSourceParts.tsv) are checked by their generator --check, which is their real consumer. No baseline-diff gate. c3 added for the duplicated raw-string copies.

criteria.text: LaneCheck checks a touched Compiler/Prelude file in its embedded mode: an untouched Prelude file gives CHECK OK on dev, and a seeded type error in a Prelude file gives CHECK FAILED naming it.
criteria.evidence: 78aa137994: jet check --prelude checks a Compiler/Prelude source as the embedded prelude, and LaneCheck routes Prelude files to it. With s1: clean Facts.jet and Traits.jet give CHECK OK. A seeded Facts.jet gives 'CHECK FAILED — 1 error(s)' with 'Facts.jet:71:5: Error [jet.ReturnTypeMismatch]'. A seeded Traits.jet reports both its errors (the OwnedTraitRows --check failure and the type error). A seeded marker gives 'Marker #ZzBroken builds no marker rule', and a seeded conversion 'impl ZzNotFamily -> Err is no Core error family conversion'. On a seed with no prelude mode it prints PRELUDE UNCHECKED with rc 1, never CHECK OK. jet test Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet 4/0.

criteria.text: LaneCheck checks a touched Compiler/JetRuntime file in its assembled mode: an untouched runtime file gives CHECK OK on dev, and a seeded error gives CHECK FAILED.
criteria.evidence: 8e5de05f9e: Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet checks a Compiler/JetRuntime path as the unit assembled from sources.list, in Jet with no node step, and maps errors back to source lines. Clean: LaneCheck Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Alloc.jet gives CHECK OK (rc 0); the shared Compiler/JetBackend/Source/OS/Linux.jet gives CHECK OK in both its package and the unit. Seeded: a ReturnTypeMismatch appended to Alloc.jet gives CHECK FAILED, 1 error in 1 file, at Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Alloc.jet:1851:5 (rc 1). jet test Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet: 3 passed.

criteria.text: Each Compiler/Prelude file the compiler embeds has one source: the compiler reads the Prelude file itself at build (or generates the embedded copy with a freshness check), not a hand-kept raw-string copy (today PreludeMarkers.jet MARKER_SOURCE, Registration/PreludeDerives.jet, PreludeUnits.jet and JET_CLI_EFFECT_SOURCE duplicate Markers, Derives, Units and Effects byte for byte).
criteria.evidence: d44f8a7b0b: the 4 hand-kept Prelude copies (MARKER_SOURCE, SEMA_PRELUDE_DERIVE_SOURCE, SEMA_PRELUDE_ERROR_SOURCE, SEMA_PRELUDE_UNITS_SOURCE) are generated from Compiler/Prelude/{Markers,Derives,Errors,Units}.jet by Tools/agent/PreludeSources.jet --write; CoreSourceRows owns the Effects copy. jet test PreludeSources.jet 2/0; --check: 'prelude sources check passed: 4 copies in 3 files match'. ba015c8b05 puts it in Land.jet's RATCHETS, which precommit runs. Refuse row: a drift line in Units.jet without --write gives 'prelude sources: …PreludeUnits.jet differ from Compiler/Prelude' and PRECOMMIT FAILED (rc 1); reverted, PRECOMMIT OK (rc 0).

criteria.text: Every generator whose output is committed has its --check run by Land.jet precommit: CoreSourceRows, OwnedTraitRows, DiagnosticRows (and any other generator with a --check). A seeded drift in each generator's source without --write is refused at landing, and the restored tree passes. The lander runs Land.jet's own list rather than a second copy.

Tools/agent/Land.jet ratchets lists 10 tools (UnsafeRatchet, CoreCoverage, PreludeSources, DiagnosticRows, CoreSourceRows, OwnedTraitRows, VocabularyRows, LexerKeywordRows, CollationTable, RuntimeGenerators). cards.body: A serial jet test of every package under Compiler/ and Jetpack/ (a0_031 on dev e4756389a9, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/pkgrerun.sh) finds failing tests in 10 test packages and 8 test packages that no longer compile. They pass unnoticed because no gate runs them. Compiler/JetCli/Tests (18 failing) is tracked on #6631 c7. Fixture packages (*.fixture) and packages with no #Test blocks are excluded.

log.text: All 9 criteria met: jet test Compiler --profile full runs every package's #Tests, and the red packages pass or are deleted.

c1 green half (PortsLead-2, 11-07): jet test Compiler --profile packages on a clean clone of dev 5202bd0699 gives rc=0 in 1654 s with 2982 rows: 2942 PASS and 26 FAIL, all known-failing (#6649, #3590, #6650). The #Test coverage row passes on the unseeded tree. Evidence: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/PortsLead/p6649/cov-green.{log,json}.

c9 progress: a1a6c69d62 (CoreCliLead-2) adds kit_require_tool in Compiler/JetTestKit/Source/RequireTool.jet. It reuses the runtime's one skip path (jet_rt_test_skip_scope) and has no spelling outside TestKit; 11 host-tool claims call it and their 11 KF lines are gone. Bare PATH (git+coreutils): JetCanvas 8 skipped, JetDebug 36 passed and 1 skipped, Integrations 92 passed and 2 skipped. Dev PATH: all 11 pass. The packages profile exits 0 bare. Still open in c9: the 7 dev rows (JetBackend/Tests, JetImpact, JetRuntime, Prelude, and 3 Publication api_diff), KF under this card, which need an owner.

Rerun in the batch environment: JetWasm/Tests 16/0, JetCli/Tests 97/0 (+1 expected-fail), EnvModel/Tests 148/0, Integrations/Tests 94/0, Foundation/Tests 93/0, JetDebug/Tests 37/0. Still red: JetParser/Tests 13, JetLexer/Tests 3, JetFoundation 1, PackageModel 1, PackageModel/Tests 1 (ada), and the 8 non-compiling test packages in c6. c3 met; c4/c5 corrected; c7 added (quick-profile baseline hides failures).

Rows c2-c6 came from a census run without JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY, JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT or jet-env (MechC found it: the 18 JetCli failures pass in the batch environment). Rerunning in the batch environment (pkgrerun.sh, fixed); rows will be corrected to its result before work starts.

criteria.text: A gate runs every package test: jet test Compiler --profile full runs the #Tests of every package under Compiler/ and Jetpack/ that has them (Tests subpackages included), so a red or non-compiling test package fails the profile. A package that no gate should run is deleted, not left unrun.
criteria.evidence: bd42ba0383 (PortsLead-2): Compiler/test.jet's packages profile adds a #Test coverage row that fails on any tracked #Test file outside a run package; Jetpack/JetOS is a named frozen exclusion. Red: a HEAD f5b313c304 clone plus the patch plus a seeded Compiler/Seeded/Unrun.jet with one #Test gives rc=1 under jet test Compiler --profile packages (2982 rows, 2941 PASS, 27 FAIL with 26 KF). The one new row is '#Test coverage: 1 #Tests no suite runs: Compiler/Seeded/Unrun.jet', and it names only the seed, so every tracked #Test on HEAD is covered. The gaps it exposed are fixed in the same commit: StopWitness.jet and UiWitness.jet (#! scripts) now run and pass. JetDevserver/Tests and JetLSP/Tests don't compile, and their KF rows are owned by #6650 (known-failing.tsv:1025 and :1027). LaneCheck: CHECK OK on Compiler/test.jet.

criteria.text: The quick profile can't hide a failure: today jet test Compiler compares against Compiler/.jet/test/quick/tests.rows, a git-ignored baseline that the first run records, failures included (it holds the jet_foundation failure and still exits 0: '236 rows ... 0 lost, 0 changed, 0 new'). A failing row fails the run whatever the baseline says, so a fresh clone's first run and every later run are red while any member test fails.

criteria.text: The Jetpack engine areas' #Tests (Jetpack/Store, Provider, Recipe, CLI, Services and Image Tests; these areas have no package.jet, so package_dirs in Compiler/test.jet skips them) run as per-claim rows in jet test Compiler --profile packages, which full includes. Each failing claim passes or carries a known-failing line naming its owning card. Their only runner today is Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --tests (shell plus assemble.mjs), and no gate calls it: release admit runs check.sh without --tests. That runner is ported to Jet or replaced, in one cutover.
criteria.evidence: 4af5a352ef: the Jetpack engine areas' #Tests run as per-claim rows in jet test Compiler --profile packages, and the check.sh --tests runner is cut over. MechD-3 lane run, s1 at 4af5a352ef with the hosted jetpack: 2974 rows, PASS 2919, FAIL 0, KNOWN-FAILING 33 (engine 13: 9 under #3590, 4 under #6649; CLI 9), UNSUPPORTED 11, ERROR, REFUSED and TIMEOUT 0. Jetpack/Store, ArtifactStore included, has no non-pass row. The only other non-pass rows were the 11 UNEXPECTED-PASS host-tool rows, whose KF lines a1a6c69d62 removed (they skip without the tool and pass with it). JetOS is frozen by owner order and not run. Confirm in the next Main batch's packages profile.

criteria.text: The package rows that fail on dev a499bfc612 in jet test Compiler --profile packages (CoreCliLead-2 bare run, 2146 rows) pass or are deleted when dead. Rows: Compiler/JetBackend/Tests (no run.jet or #Test: delete), Compiler/JetImpact (PathDependencyEscape jet_env_model), Compiler/JetRuntime (UnknownFunction os_store_i64; the runtime has to be tested in the mode it is built in), Compiler/Prelude (ReservedDunderName __live_arg; likewise), and Jetpack/Publication/Tests (api_diff_detects_removed_fn, api_diff_detects_changed_signature, 'api snapshot rows keep each line as its signature'). Package rows that need a tool outside the release environment (node, ssh) either stop needing it or declare it as a host requirement and SKIP-HOST, like the cases suite's tool: rows.
criteria.evidence: d16f96e61e (PortsLead-2): JetImpact declares jet_env_model (jet test exits 0). JetRuntime and Prelude are ASSEMBLED_PACKAGES in Compiler/test.jet and report skipped rows: JetRuntime is assembled by the chain and its registries run in the registries profile; Prelude is embedded and has no #Test. The dead JetBackend/Tests run-script is replaced by a real #Test, NativeOutputDiagnostic.jet, whose failure is a product defect now on #6669. Publication's 35 API-row literals are restored to the rows sema emits, and the 3 target rows PASS (298/1; the 1 needs JET_BIN, which the suite sets). 7 KF lines dropped. LaneCheck CHECK OK. Confirm in the next batch's packages profile.

cards.title: Native ELF writer emits no .text section header, so objdump -d shows nothing
cards.body: From #6651 (MechD-3, row simd_witness/default_and_scalar_float_witnesses_print_identical_values_on_every_tier, KF #6414). objdump -d prints nothing for a jet-built binary because the native ELF writer emits no section headers for code; tools that disassemble or symbolize by section (objdump, perf annotate, gdb disassemble) see no .text.

log.text: The ELF writer emits .text; the case pins it.

criteria.text: objdump -d on a jet-built hello binary lists a .text section with disassembly of main; a case pins it.
criteria.evidence: a41d925827 + cd023c35d1: tests/cases/debug/objdump_disassembles_main_from_text_section.case builds hello; objdump -h lists .text (PROGBITS AX at 0x401000) and objdump -d disassembles <main>:. jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter objdump_disassembles_main (seed a0_033, llvm objdump) PASS 1/1.
